## A3 cost-modifier pipeline (2026-07-17)

The LATE phase of `Hook::ModifyEnergyCostInCombat` — the four Free*Power
"next card of kind K costs 0" powers (#332) and their four `untouched`
attack sources (Unrelenting/Pounce/Synthesis/Veilpiercer). Batch-4
serialized `area:engine-core` slot, sequenced after A2-TANGLED (which
landed `card_cost_in_state` and the Early Tangled walk this builds on).
**Every RVA re-dumped this session from the installed build v0.109.0
(commit c12f634d)** via `tools/dump_il.py`; async BeforeCardPlayed
bodies read from the nested `<BeforeCardPlayed>d__N::MoveNext`. Walk
`invariant-walks/2026-07-17-65-a3-cost-modifier.md`.

### The Late cost hook (`TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate`)

One override per power, all four the SAME body shape (verified to the
`*cost = 0` / return-true site):

- `FreeAttackPower::TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate` 0x24e9bc
- `FreeSkillPower::...` 0x24eb74
- `FreePowerPower::...` 0x24ea98
- `VeilpiercerPower::...` 0x256510

Body: write the incoming cost through (IL_000e `stobj`), then three
gates in order — (1) `card.Owner.Creature == power.Owner` else
`ldc.i4.0; ret` (false, unchanged); (2) the KIND gate:
`card.Type == 1` (Attack) / `== 2` (Skill) / `== 3` (Power) for the
three Free* powers, or `card.Keywords.Contains(2)` (Ethereal) for
Veilpiercer, else false; (3) the pile gate: `card.Pile != null` and
`pile.Type ∈ {2 Hand, 5 Play}` (a nullable-CardPileType local; null or
any other pile → false). On all three passing: `ldarg.3; initobj
System.Decimal` (`*cost = Decimal.Zero`, an ABSOLUTE set — the incoming
value is discarded, NOT a delta) then `ldc.i4.1; ret` (true). This is
the LATE listener pass of `Hook::ModifyEnergyCostInCombat` (0x2b13e8),
which runs AFTER the Early pass (TangledPower's
`TryModifyEnergyCostInCombat` 0x25536c) — so a live free power OVERRIDES
a Tangled surcharge to 0.

The pipeline position (from A2's `CardEnergyCost::GetWithModifiers`
0x2c9ea4 read): `_base` → **CostsX or base<0: return, hooks never run**
(IL_002d/0022 — X-cost attacks are exempt from the free walk too) →
local rewrites (TOI/Ember) → Early hook walk (Tangled) → **Late hook
walk (this family)** → `Math.Max(0, ·)`. Both the afford gate
(`HasEnoughResourcesFor` 0x2c4144) and the spend (`GetAmountToSpend`
0x2c9fc2 / `GetResolved` 0x2c9ff5) reduce to `GetWithModifiers(-1)`, so
enumeration and payment see the SAME value (I4). Sim: the Late walk is
`_free_cost_applies(s, spec)` inside `card_cost_in_state`; a match
returns 0 unconditionally.

### The BeforeCardPlayed consumers (`PowerCmd::Decrement`)

`FreeAttackPower/<BeforeCardPlayed>d__5::MoveNext` 0x3841ec (and the
sibling nested bodies; Veilpiercer's is `d__7`). Same three gates as the
cost hook — owner, kind (Type or Keyword-2), pile ∈ {2,5} — then
`PowerCmd::Decrement` (IL_00ad): ONE stack removed per matching card
PLAYED, not a whole-power Remove. So a power at amount N frees the next
N matching cards. `get_Type` = 1 / `get_StackType` = 1 (Intensity) for
all four, so re-applications add stacks. Sim: the four `if s.free_* and
spec.<kind>` decrements at the end of `_powers_before_card_played`
(fires per CardPlay iteration, AFTER the spend — mirrors SpendResources
→ BeforeCardPlayed).

**Independence / no refusal needed.** The four are independent
listeners each writing the same absolute 0, so any co-active pair is
order-free (the brief's "multiple simultaneous free-powers" candidate
refusal is fully resolved, not guessed — see the walk's I5). A card
matching two powers (an Ethereal attack under FreeAttack + Veilpiercer)
decrements BOTH. **Duration.** None — the four types override no turn
hook (PowerModel base has none), so each persists the whole combat
until consumed; they ride the State default, not the turn-end reset.

### The four consumer cards (ctors, v0.109.0 c12f634d)

All `CardModel::.ctor(cost, …)`, DamageVar + `Apply<power>(self, 1)` in
OnPlay, one hit:

- **Unrelenting** 0x29b991: cost 2, DamageVar base **14**, OnUpgrade
  `UpgradeValueBy 6` → **20**; grants `FreeAttackPower(1)`.
- **Pounce** 0x293f40: cost 2, base **14** → **20** (+6); grants
  `FreeSkillPower(1)`.
- **Synthesis** 0x299ed0: cost 2, base **14** → **20** (+6); grants
  `FreePowerPower(1)`.
- **Veilpiercer** 0x29bcbf: cost 1, base **10** → **13** (+3); grants
  `VeilpiercerPower(1)`; `get_ExtraHoverTips` = `FromKeyword(2)`
  (Ethereal), the same keyword the power's Late gate reads.

All four match `card_templates.json` and the I1 census. Sim mapping in
`_TEMPLATE_POWER_STEPS`: FreeAttackPower→`free_attack`,
FreeSkillPower→`free_skill`, FreePowerPower→`free_power`,
VeilpiercerPower→`free_ethereal`; each `s.free_* += amount` in OnPlay.
The applying card pays its own cost and takes its BeforeCardPlayed latch
BEFORE OnPlay grants the power, so it never frees or consumes its own
grant.

### Harness pin (local-only; build v0.109.0 c12f634d)

Seed TESTSEED, Ironclad A10, deck [UNRELENTING, 4× STRIKE_IRONCLAD], no
relics/potions, ENCOUNTER.VINE_SHAMBLER_NORMAL, line
`[("play",1,1),("play",0,1),("play",0,1)]` (Unrelenting then two Strikes

### Issue-text corrections (I5 refuse-don't-guess; the A1/A2 discipline)

The coordinator flagged issue #284 as carrying interpretation rot. Both
of its central claims are wrong on the v0.109 IL, and the coordinator's
own pre-derivation ALSO missed one effect — all three re-derived here:

1. **`OnHpChanged` does NOT drive the charge/un-burrow reaction — it is
   pure SFX.** `CubexConstruct::OnHpChanged` (0x25e014) is: `if after <
   before: SfxCmd::SetParam('…cubex_construct_charge_attack',
   'enemy_hurt', 1.0)` and nothing else. `BeforeRemovedFromRoom`
   (0x25dfeb) is `SfxCmd::StopLoop` + `remove_CurrentHpChanged`. No
   gameplay state flows through the HP-changed subscription; **no
   reactive-HP-hook primitive is needed.** The un-burrow is
   MOVE-driven (see CHARGE_UP below).

2. **`_isBurrowed` / `_isCharging` are ANIMATOR-ONLY — a burrowed
   construct is FULLY targetable on turn 1.** `scan_calls.py
   IsBurrowed IsCharging` over the whole DLL returns exactly four hits,
   all in render lambdas: `<GenerateAnimator>b__34_0` and
   `b__34_1` read `get_IsBurrowed` + `get_IsCharging`; the only WRITERS
   are `<AfterAddedToRoom>d__27` (`set_IsBurrowed(true)`) and
   `<ChargeUpMove>d__31` (`set_IsBurrowed(false)` + `set_IsCharging`).
   Nothing in targeting, AoE, dispatch, or damage reads either flag.
   This is stronger than a harness run (which can only observe one
   single-turn outcome); the call-graph is exhaustive, so **no
   untargetable / AoE-exempt primitive is modeled** and no harness run
   was required to settle the open question.

3. **[MISSED BY BOTH ISSUE AND COORDINATOR] the construct gains 13
   Block at spawn.** `<AfterAddedToRoom>d__27::MoveNext` (0x3a0d74),
   read to SetResult, is: `await base.AfterAddedToRoom` (`<>n__0`) →
   `CreatureCmd::GainBlock(new Decimal(13), BlockProps.monsterMove=8)`
   → `Apply<ArtifactPower>(Decimal.One)` → `add_CurrentHpChanged
   (OnHpChanged)` → `set_IsBurrowed(true)`. The coordinator's
   pre-derivation listed only Artifact + subscribe + burrow; the
   `GainBlock(13)` (a flat literal, NO `AscensionHelper`) was omitted.
   It is ordinary monster block: it shields the construct through
   player turn 1 and clears at the construct's own first side start
   (no `BurrowedPower` — `_isBurrowed` is NOT the tunneler's block-
   persisting `BurrowedPower`). Modeled as `Monster(block=13)`.

### Move machine (GenerateMoveStateMachine 0x25e030)

Deterministic (census `random_branches 0`, `move_states 4`). Initial
state is **CHARGE_UP_MOVE** (ctor gets loc1); FollowUps wire
loc1→loc2, loc2→loc3, loc3→loc4, loc4→loc2. So CHARGE_UP fires ONCE,
then REPEATER → REPEATER_2 → EXPEL loops forever (EXPEL back to
REPEATER, never to CHARGE_UP — the HAUNTED_SHIP once-then-cycle shape;
in `CUBEX_LOOP` the EXPEL entry's 4th element pins its follow to
loop_pos 1). Move bodies (A9+/below; every getter re-dumped):

- **CHARGE_UP** (`<ChargeUpMove>d__31` 0x3a0f54): `set_IsBurrowed(false)`
  + `set_IsCharging(true)` (animator-only), SFX + `TriggerAnim('Charge')`
  + `Cmd::Wait(0.75)` (cosmetic), then `Apply<StrengthPower>(new
  Decimal(2))` self. BuffIntent only, no attack → `buff_strength (2,)`.
- **REPEATER_BLAST** and **REPEATER_BLAST_2** (`<RepeaterBlastMove>d__32`
  0x3a13a8): `DamageCmd::Attack(get_BlastDamage).FromMonster` — a SINGLE
  hit (no `WithHitCount`) — THEN `Apply<StrengthPower>(new Decimal(2))`
  self. `get_BlastDamage` (0x25defb) = `GetValueIfAscension(9, 8, 7)` →
  **A9+ 8, else 7**. Machine intents `[SingleAttackIntent(BlastDamage),
  BuffIntent]` → `attack_strength (8, 1, 2)`.
- **EXPEL** (`<ExpelBlastMove>d__33` 0x3a1144): `Attack(get_ExpelDamage)
  .WithHitCount(2)` (MultiAttackIntent x2), no rider. `get_ExpelDamage`
  (0x25df06) = `GetValueIfAscension(9, 6, 5)` → **A9+ 6, else 5** →
  `attack (6, 2)`.

Strength accumulates across the fight: CHARGE_UP +2, each REPEATER +2
(applied AFTER its own attack), so the observed damages at A9+ are
CHARGE_UP 0 (Str→2), REPEATER 8+2=**10** (Str→4), REPEATER_2 8+4=**12**
(Str→6), EXPEL (6+6)×2=**24** (no self-buff), then REPEATER 8+6=**14**…

HP `get_MinInitialHp` (0x25dee7) = `GetValueIfAscension(8, 70, 65)` →
**A8+ 70**; `get_MaxInitialHp` (0x25def3) tail-calls Min → fixed. Census
`hp_min_consts [8, 70, 65]`, `powers_applied [ArtifactPower,
StrengthPower]`, `card_effects []` (the GainBlock is not a power/card).

### Encounter generators (both deterministic, zero Rng)

- **CubexConstructNormal::GenerateMonsters** (0x27f250): ONE
  CubexConstruct, no Rng call → `ctx.fixed` (one Niche single-value draw
  for the fixed HP).
- **ConstructMenagerieNormal::GenerateMonsters** (0x27f048): a
  deterministic 3-element array — slot 0 PunchConstruct, slot 1 & 2
  CubexConstruct (no Rng call). Creation = slot = Niche-roll order; all
  three HP getters fixed (one single-value draw each). Both machines
  reused unchanged (PunchConstruct #148, CubexConstruct #284); each
  construct carries its own spawn effect (Punch Artifact 1; Cubex 13
  Block + Artifact 1).

### Pins + scope

Suite **396 → 398 passed / 3 skipped** (+2):
`test_cubex_construct_charge_repeater_expel_cycle_and_spawn` (spawn
Block 13 + Artifact 1, the 13-Block-clears-at-own-side-start check via
`end_player_turn`, the once-CHARGE-then-3-cycle rotation with
Strength-scaled damages, census cross-check) and
`test_construct_menagerie_composition_and_spawn` (slot/uid/creation
order, per-construct spawn effects, both openers). No `fight_states*.json`
pin touched; coverage matrix regenerated (encounters modeled **37 → 39**,
untouched 13 → 11). The two `content/encounters/normal.py` prose-refusal
comments (W3 wave, EW1 wave) were updated to point here.

### Harness

**None run — not needed.** The single open question the coordinator
raised (is burrowed = untargetable?) is answered exhaustively by the
`scan_calls.py` call-graph (correction 2 above): no gameplay site reads
`_isBurrowed`, so targetability is not a single-turn-observable question
a harness could better answer. Every other value is an integer IL
constant read to SetResult. No in-game capture pins either construct
encounter (HQPAXCBS6P has none); census + exhaustive-IL is the ground
truth. A future capture should pin the turn-1 13-Block shield and the
Strength-scaled EXPEL double-hit.

## CW7 card read wave (2026-07-17)

Seventh CARD wave (#138), the batch-4 `area:content` read track (Track-B):
15 `untouched`-pool cards, ALL IL-read against the installed **v0.109.0 /
commit c12f634d** DLL (`data_sts2_macos_arm64/sts2.dll`, dump_il.py; async
`<Hook>d__N::MoveNext` bodies pinned to their enclosing types via the
NestedClass table). **0 modeled, 15 refused (I5).** Distinct from the CW6
pool (no overlap). Every card either hosts an ongoing power whose hook the
engine does not fire (a `combat_sim.py` handler this track may not add), or
carries the `Sly` keyword outside the modeled vocabulary. Selection was
routing-driven: all 15 map onto ALREADY-OPEN primitive issues (#171, #332,
#333, #334, #335, #336, #349) — no new issue filed, no `#138` blocked-by
edge added. `CardType`: Attack=1 Skill=2 Power=3; `CardKeyword`: Retain=5
Sly=6. Absence of all 15 pinned by
the #171 Sly positive-admission pins. Full
I-registry walk: `invariant-walks/2026-07-17-66-cw7-card-reads.md`.

**Post-wave note (same batch):** Cluster C1's four cards (UNRELENTING /
POUNCE / SYNTHESIS / VEILPIERCER) were MODELED mid-batch by the A3 cost
pipeline (PR #361, "A3 cost-modifier pipeline" section above) — this wave's
independent reads of the four Free*Power bodies agree with A3's and served
as the review's second derivation. Their absence pins were converted to
positive admissions; the other 11 cards' refusals stand as written.

### Cluster C1 — "next card of type/keyword T costs 0" (#332)

Four attack+power cards. The attack step maps (`attack`), but the applied
power hooks `PowerModel::TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate` — the
card-cost-modifier pipeline the sim does not run (there is no per-card
in-combat cost mutation; `card_cost_in_state` reads the static census cost).
Refused whole (I5): admitting only the attack would silently drop the free-
cast, corrupting the energy/legal-action search (I2/I4).

- **UNRELENTING** (ctor 0x29b991, cost 2 attack; `attack 14→20`) —
  `Apply<FreeAttackPower>(1)`. `FreeAttackPower::get_Type` 0x24e9b3 (=1),
  `TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate` 0x24e9bc: owner-gated, `CardModel::
  get_Type == 1` (Attack), pile ∈ {2 hand, 5 …} → set cost `1`(Decimal, the
  "free" floor); `BeforeCardPlayed` d__5 0x24ea3c consumes/decrements.
- **POUNCE** (ctor 0x293f40, cost 2 attack; `attack 14→20`) —
  `Apply<FreeSkillPower>(1)`. `FreeSkillPower::get_Type` 0x24eb6b, cost hook
  `TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate` 0x24eb74 (same shape, `Type==2` Skill).
- **SYNTHESIS** (ctor 0x299ed0, cost 2 attack; `attack 14→20`) —
  `Apply<FreePowerPower>(1)`. `FreePowerPower::get_Type` 0x24ea8f, cost hook
  0x24ea98 (`Type==3` Power).
- **VEILPIERCER** (ctor 0x29bcbf, cost 1 attack; `attack 10→13`) —
  `Apply<VeilpiercerPower>(1)`. `VeilpiercerPower::get_Type` 0x2564fb, cost
  hook `TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate` 0x256510 gated on
  `CardModel::get_Keywords.Contains(...)` (a keyword, not a CardType) AND
  pile type; `BeforeCardPlayed` d__7 0x256598. Same pipeline as the three
  above — issue #332 names it explicitly.

### Cluster C2 — enemy powers modifying the player's outgoing damage/debuff multipliers (#333)

Two attack+debuff cards. The attack maps; the power lands on the ENEMY and
hooks a `Modify*Multiplier` on the enemy's own damage-received pipeline —
an insertion into the decimal pipeline I7 governs that the sim does not
carry. Refused (I5, #333).

- **KNOCKDOWN** (ctor 0x28fd4b, cost 3 attack; `attack 10→14`, enemy power
  `2→3`) — `Apply<KnockdownPower>(enemy, 2)`. `KnockdownPower::get_Type`
  0x2504d9; `ModifyDamageMultiplicative` 0x250548: `IsPoweredAttack` gate,
  applies `Amount` as a damage multiplier on hits the owner (enemy) takes;
  `AfterSideTurnEnd` d__11 0x250584 decrements (temporary).
- **DEBILITATE** (ctor 0x288ee3, cost 1 attack; `attack 10→12`, enemy power
  `2→3`) — `Apply<DebilitatePower>(enemy, 2)`. `DebilitatePower::get_Type`
  0x24d641; `ModifyVulnerableMultiplier` 0x24d682 + `ModifyWeakMultiplier`
  0x24d6aa (both `IsPoweredAttack`-gated, Decimal add/sub of `Amount` into
  the Vulnerable/Weak multiplier the target applies); `AfterSideTurnEnd`
  d__8 0x24d6d4 → `PowerCmd::Decrement`. Not the STS1 mega-debuff — a
  Vulnerable/Weak amp on the marked enemy.

### Cluster C3 — temporary NEGATIVE Strength on an enemy (#334)

- **MANGLE** (ctor 0x290dbf, cost 3 attack; `attack 15→20`, power `10→15`)
  — `Apply<ManglePower>(enemy, 10)`. `ManglePower` is a `TemporaryStrength
  Power` subclass (`.ctor` 0x250929 → `TemporaryStrengthPower::.ctor`) with
  `get_IsPositive` 0x250926 = **false** and `get_OriginModel` 0x25091f =
  `Card<Mangle>`: applies negative temporary Strength to the target. The
  sim has no enemy TEMPORARY-strength field and no negative-strength-vs-
  Artifact sign read (the `strength_enemy` step already raises on `< 0`,
  combat_sim ~L7344). Refused (I5, #334 names Mangle).

### Cluster C4 — enemy-applied attack play-count doubling (#335)

- **TAG_TEAM** (ctor 0x299fea, cost 2 attack; `attack 11→15`, power `1`
  both levels) — `Apply<TagTeamPower>(enemy, 1)`. `TagTeamPower::get_Type`
  0x2550b5; `ModifyCardPlayCount` 0x2550c4 gated on `CardModel::get_Type`
  AND matching `get_TargetType` (owner vs applier) → adds `Amount` play
  count; `AfterModifyingCardPlayCount` d__9 0x255128 → `PowerCmd::Remove`
  (one-shot). The `ModifyCardPlayCount` pipeline exists for player powers
  (Burst/EchoForm, combat_sim ~L387) but there is no ENEMY-applied,
  target-matched play-count consumer (I2 new keyed field). Refused (#335).

### Cluster C5 — per-card-INSTANCE dynamic var on AfterCardDrawn (#336)

Two attacks whose numbers mutate a PER-CARD-INSTANCE dynamic var each time
the card is drawn. The sim's cards are value tuples `(id, upgrade, …)` with
no per-instance mutable state — modeling the scaling needs a new instance-
var dimension the memo key must carry (I2). Refused (#336 names both).

- **KINGLY_PUNCH** (ctor 0x28fb11, cost 1 attack; `attack 8→10`) — OnPlay
  d__8 0x3f19e8; `AfterCardDrawn` 0x28fbb8: when THIS card is drawn
  (`ldarg.2 == this`), read `DynamicVars['Increase'].BaseValue` and ADD it
  to BOTH `Damage.BaseValue` and `ExtraDamage` (`get/set_ExtraDamage`
  0x28fb1e/0x28fb26) — permanent per-draw damage growth on the instance.
- **KINGLY_KICK** (ctor 0x28fa64, cost 4 attack; `attack 27→35`) — OnPlay
  d__3 0x3f18c4; `AfterCardDrawn` 0x28faf3: `CardModel::get_EnergyCost.
  AddThisCombat(...)` — mutates its own `CardEnergyCost` per draw (the
  cost-scaling sibling of Kingly Punch's damage scaling).

### Cluster C6 — the `Sly` keyword: auto-play on discard (#171)

`Sly=6` is combat-relevant, not cosmetic: `CardModel::get_IsSlyThisTurn`
0x227ba1 collects Sly cards, and `CardCmd::<DiscardAndDraw>d__4` 0x4291a8
(IL_02fd) **auto-plays** each discarded Sly card rather than exempting it
(the v0.109 semantics the CW6 wave corrected on #171). #171 models the
shared hook, so the five consumers whose OnPlay steps map are admitted.

- **ABRASIVE** (ctor 0x2833f1, cost 3 power, `Sly`) — OnPlay
  `Apply<DexterityPower>(1)` + `Apply<ThornsPower>(4→6)` — BOTH map
  (`dexterity`/`thorns` steps); modeled.
- **FLICK_FLACK** (ctor 0x28c4cf, cost 1 attack, `Sly`) — `attack_all 7→9`
  — maps (`attack_all`); modeled.
- **REFLEX** (ctor 0x295497, cost 3 skill, `Sly`) — `draw 2→3` — maps
  (`draw`); modeled. Its own draw can relocate a later collected Sly card,
  which AutoPlay follows by exact instance.
- **UNTOUCHABLE** (ctor 0x29ba1f, cost 2 skill, `Sly`) — `block 6→9` —
  maps (`block`); modeled.
- **TACTICIAN** (ctor 0x299f5f, cost 3 skill, `Sly`) — OnPlay `energy 1→2`
  — maps (`energy`); modeled (its real value is the Sly
  auto-play/discard payoff — cost 3 for +1 energy is strictly a downside
  played, confirming the discard mechanic carries the card).
- **SNEAKY** (ctor 0x297a93, cost 2 power, `Sly`) — DOUBLE-gated:
  `Apply<SneakyPower>(1→2)` + `Sly`. `SneakyPower::get_Type` 0x254103 (=1);
  `AfterCardPlayed` d__6 0x25411c: own card && `Type==1` (Attack) → block —
  the exact RagePower shape, so its POWER routes to **#349** (played-attack
  block on the AfterCardPlayed layer) while its keyword routes to #171.

0 modeled, 15 refused. All 15 stay `untouched` in the matrix (loader-

## E1-OBSCURA wave (2026-07-17) — The Obscura + shared Illusion lifecycle (#297, #150)

All reads in this section are from the installed **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**
`sts2.dll`. Each async move/power body was followed through its nested
`<...>d__N::MoveNext` to `AsyncTaskMethodBuilder::SetResult`; this section
supersedes the older EW2/E2 refusal notes. The shared Illusion primitive made
`FOGMOG_NORMAL` an exact, natural bundle rather than a speculative neighbor,
so this wave removes its `content_refusals.json` entry as well as modeling
`THE_OBSCURA_NORMAL`.

### TheObscuraNormal and Parafright

- `TheObscuraNormal::GenerateMonsters` **0x28144a** creates only one
  `TheObscura` in slot `obscura` (modeled slot 1). `Parafright` occurs in
  `get_AllPossibleMonsters`, not the initial roster; the opener summons it
  into slot `illusion` (slot 0). `TheObscura` HP getters are fixed 129 A8+ /
  123 below (`hp_min_consts [8,129,123]`); fixed creation still consumes one
  Niche draw.
- `TheObscura::GenerateMoveStateMachine` **0x26d970** opens
  `ILLUSION_MOVE`, then enters one `RandomBranchState`. Its three direct
  branches are `PIERCING_GAZE_MOVE`, `SAIL_MOVE`, and
  `HARDENING_STRIKE_MOVE`; all use the default-weight `AddBranch` overload
  **0x225725** (delegating to **0x225706**) with
  `MoveRepeatType.CannotRepeat`. Thus the post-opener roll is uniform among
  eligible moves, consumes exactly one MonsterAi `NextFloat(sum)` draw, and
  never repeats the immediately preceding move. Generic random selection is
  `RandomBranchState::GetNextState` **0x225734** /
  `GetStateWeight` **0x2257f0**. `HasSummoned` does not gate this graph: its
  remaining readers are animator lambdas **0x26dd0c–0x26dd27**.
- `IllusionMove` **0x3b9ae8** calls `CreatureCmd::Add<Parafright>(...,
  "illusion")`, then sets `HasSummoned=true`. `PiercingGazeMove`
  **0x3b9c4c** attacks for 11 A9+ (10 below). `WailMove` (move id
  `SAIL_MOVE`) **0x3b9d50** applies Strength 3 to
  `CombatState::GetTeammatesOf(self)`; that helper **0x2e23bb** returns the
  creatures on the same side, including the caster. `HardeningStrikeMove`
  **0x3b9960** attacks for 7 A9+ (6 below) and then gains 7 Block (6 below).
- `Parafright` has fixed 21 HP (**0x2670e7**) and one self-looping
  `SLAM_MOVE` machine (**0x26714c**). `SlamMove` **0x3af2b4** attacks for 17
  A9+ / 16 below. `AfterAddedToRoom` **0x3af174** awaits the base hook and
  applies `IllusionPower`.

### IllusionPower: summon, death, revival, and primary cascade

- `IllusionPower::AfterApplied` **0x24fabb** applies `MinionPower` if it is
  absent. `ShouldAllowHitting` **0x24fb3b** rejects hits only while the owner
  is reviving; `ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath` **0x24fb53**
  returns false for the owner, retaining the corpse.
- `AfterDeath` `<...>d__18::MoveNext` **0x386024** owner-gates, sets
  `isReviving=true`, builds a `REVIVE_MOVE` with `HealIntent`, chooses the
  configured follow-up or the last logged move, marks it `MustPerformOnce`,
  and calls `SetMoveImmediate`. `ReviveMove` `<...>d__22::MoveNext`
  **0x3861a0** wakes the animator, clears `isReviving`, and heals
  `MaxHp-CurrentHp`: one full-heal move with no attack. The modeled
  Parafright/Eye machines self-loop, so the restored follow-up is their sole
  normal move.
- Death cleanup is not "remove every power." `IllusionPower::
  ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath` **0x24faa2** removes a power when its type is
  2 and it is *not* `ITemporaryPower`, preserving other powers. An exact
  v0.109 metadata `InterfaceImpl` sweep found only
  `TemporaryDexterityPower`, `TemporaryFocusPower`, and
  `TemporaryStrengthPower` implement `ITemporaryPower`; the concrete
  `WeakPower`, `VulnerablePower`, `PoisonPower`, and `ShrinkPower` types do
  not. Therefore an illusion death clears all four modeled enemy debuff
  fields, while retaining Strength, IllusionPower, and MinionPower. The
  generic exception walk is `Creature::RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath`
  **0x2c9a0c** (lambda **0x423d54**).
- `CreatureCmd::Add<T>` **0x43237c** / add coroutine **0x432580** creates a
  side-2 creature through `CombatState::CreateCreature` **0x2e2098**, so the
  fixed summoned HP still consumes one Niche draw. Because the summon runs
  during side 2, the add coroutine does not prepare it for an action in the
  already-snapshotted phase; it acts next enemy phase, in slot order.
- `CreatureCmd::KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition` coroutine **0x43511c**
  runs the dying creature's `AfterDeath` before its secondary-enemy check.
  If the dead creature was the primary and every remaining living teammate
  has `OwnerIsSecondaryEnemy` (from `MinionPower`), it kills those teammates
  too. This is the existing GasBomb cascade generalized to Illusion minions:
  killing Parafright alone schedules revival, but killing TheObscura while
  Parafright lives kills the minion and ends combat.

### FogmogNormal and EyeWithTeeth (#150 correction)

- `FogmogNormal::GenerateMonsters` **0x27f9d6** creates only the fixed-78-HP
  A8+ / 74-below `Fogmog` in slot 1. `EyeWithTeeth` is only a possible/
  summoned monster. `Fogmog::GenerateMoveStateMachine` **0x260928** is:
  `ILLUSION -> SWIPE -> BRANCH`; BRANCH has
  `SWIPE_RANDOM` weight float32 **0.4** and `HEADBUTT` weight float32
  **0.6**, both CannotRepeat; `SWIPE_RANDOM -> HEADBUTT -> SWIPE`. Every
  branch is preceded by the distinct fixed `SWIPE`, so both weights are
  eligible and exactly one MonsterAi draw is consumed at each branch.
  `Enumerable.Sum<float>` rounds their float32 sum to exactly `1.0f`, so
  the simulator draws `NextFloat(1.0)` and selects random Swipe at
  `roll <= 0.4000000059604645`; it deliberately does not feed the two
  widened literals through Python's double-precision `sum`.
- `IllusionMove` **0x3a5208** adds `EyeWithTeeth` to slot `illusion`.
  `SwipeMove` **0x3a5364** attacks for 9 A9+ (8 below) and then applies
  Strength 1 to self. Both the fixed `SWIPE_MOVE` and the random
  `SWIPE_RANDOM_MOVE` call this same body. `HeadbuttMove` **0x3a5104**
  attacks for 16 A9+ / 15 below.
- `EyeWithTeeth` has fixed 6 HP (**0x25f64c**), a one-state self-looping
  `DISTRACT_MOVE` machine (**0x25f6a4**), and applies `IllusionPower` from
  `AfterAddedToRoom` **0x3a337c**. `DistractMove` **0x3a34bc** calls
  `AddToCombatAndPreview<Dazed>` with pile type 3 (Discard), count 3, and
  position 1 (Bottom): append exactly three Dazed and consume **zero Shuffle
  draws**. This corrects the older #150 note that described draw-pile/random
  insertion.

### Simulator and verification consequences

The engine derives `Monster.illusion` exactly from the two concrete species
(both unconditionally apply IllusionPower), adds shared fixed-HP slot-0 summon
handling, corpse revival, and the generalized secondary-enemy cascade. This
avoids a redundant memo-key field because `Monster.kind` already distinguishes
the behavior. TheObscura reuses the
uniform-CannotRepeat random-AI implementation; Fogmog uses a deterministic
loop plus a single weighted-branch helper. Eye's DISTRACT reuses the verified
`pile_inject(discard,bottom)` primitive. No new entry-state or cross-fight
state exists. Coverage matrix regeneration moves both encounters to
`modeled`; `FOGMOG_NORMAL` is removed from the refusal registry. No harness
was run: this isolated worktree has no local `versions/v0.111.0/solver/harness/venv`; the
positive model is based on complete current-build IL bodies, metadata, and
behavioral/counter pins rather than an assumed observation.

## Cruelty Vulnerable-multiplier primitive (Batch 129, 2026-07-25, #371)

The installed and archived sources were rechecked before implementation:
**v0.109.0 / c12f634d**, arm64 `sts2.dll`, SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.
Complete dumps covered the card, its nested OnPlay body, CrueltyPower, and
VulnerablePower. The fresh read corrected the CW8 summary: the branch at
CrueltyPower `IL_0012` enters the addition path when
`ValueProps.IsPoweredAttack` is true, not false.

- `Cruelty..ctor` **0x288488**: cost 1, Power, Rare, Self, max upgrade 1.
- `Cruelty.get_CanonicalVars` **0x288495**: CrueltyPower Amount 25.
- `Cruelty.<OnPlay>d__5.MoveNext` **0x3deda0**: after the PowerUp animation,
  await `Apply<CrueltyPower>(owner, current CrueltyPower value, owner,
  card, 0)`.
- `Cruelty.OnUpgrade` **0x288513**: CrueltyPower +25, producing 50.
- `CrueltyPower.get_Type/get_StackType` **0x24d16d/0x24d170**: both 1;
  reapplications add Amount and persist for combat.
- `CrueltyPower.ModifyVulnerableMultiplier` **0x24d194**: if the damage
  target is the power owner, return the incoming multiplier; if properties
  are not a powered attack, return it unchanged; otherwise return
  `multiplier + Decimal(Amount) / Decimal(100)`.
- `VulnerablePower.ModifyDamageMultiplicative` **0x256c94**: begin with
  Vulnerable's Decimal 1.5, let the direct player-attacker Paper Phrog
  replace that current value first, then obtain Cruelty from the dealer's
  Player or its PetOwner Player, apply Cruelty, and finally apply a target
  Debilitate listener when present.

The simulator stores Cruelty's mutable Amount in keyed state and maps only
the exact self-power template. At the one powered player/Osty attack seam,
Vulnerable's exact `Fraction(3, 2)` (or direct-player Paper Phrog
`Fraction(7, 4)`) receives `Fraction(cruelty, 100)` additively before the
existing single final damage conversion. Thus Cruelty 25 turns ordinary
Vulnerable into 1.75 and Paper Phrog into 2.0; it is not a standalone ×1.25
factor. Owned Osty attacks inherit Cruelty through PetOwner but not Paper
Phrog. Non-Vulnerable targets, unpowered damage, foreign/null dealers, and
damage targeting the Cruelty owner remain unchanged.

This batch admits only `CARD.CRUELTY`; every other refusal remains intact.

## Corruption owned-Skill late hooks (Batch 130, 2026-07-25, #370)

The installed and archived sources were rechecked before implementation:
**v0.109.0 / c12f634d**, arm64 `sts2.dll`, SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.
The issue's old OnPlay-body cite was stale; the current nested body is
`Corruption.<OnPlay>d__5.MoveNext` **0x3de1a0**.

- `Corruption..ctor` **0x288033**: cost 3, Power, Ancient, Self, maximum
  upgrade 1.
- `Corruption.get_CanonicalVars` **0x288040**: CorruptionPower Amount 1.
- `Corruption.<OnPlay>d__5.MoveNext` **0x3de1a0**: after the PowerUp
  animation, await `Apply<CorruptionPower>(owner, 1, owner, card, 0)`.
- `Corruption.OnUpgrade` **0x2880af**: `EnergyCost.UpgradeBy(-1)`, producing
  cost 2.
- `CorruptionPower.get_Type/get_StackType` **0x24cd57/0x24cd5a**: Type 1,
  StackType 2 Unique. The first application creates one persistent listener;
  reapplication neither duplicates nor reorders it.
- `CorruptionPower.TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate` **0x24cd6a**: require
  `card.Owner.Creature == power.Owner` and CardType 2 Skill; otherwise copy
  the incoming Decimal unchanged and return false. On success set the
  Decimal reference to zero and return true. There is no pile gate and no
  decrement hook, unlike FreeSkillPower.
- `CorruptionPower.ModifyCardPlayResultLocation` **0x24cd99**: the same
  owner + Skill gates, then mutate only `CardLocation.pileType` to 4
  (Exhaust), retaining the incoming position.
- `CorruptionPower.AfterModifyingCardPlayResultLocation` **0x24cdc7**:
  visual Flash only.

`CardEnergyCost.GetWithModifiers(-1)` **0x2c9ea4** still returns before all
hook walks for CostsX/negative-base cards. For fixed-cost Skills, Corruption
runs in Hook's Late walk after Tangled/Borrowed Time/Spiked Gauntlets and
writes an absolute zero. Co-active FreeSkill writes the same zero, but its
own BeforeCardPlayed consumer still decrements independently. Because
Corruption has no Hand/Play pile gate, All for One's live Discard cost
inspection also sees owned Skills at zero.

`Hook.ModifyCardPlayResultLocation` **0x2b0f90** threads the current
CardLocation through combat listeners in Creature power order and records
every listener that changed it. Thus a Rebound listener applied before
Corruption first changes Discard/Bottom to Draw/Top and is consumed by its
After hook; Corruption then produces Exhaust/Top. If Corruption runs first,
the later discard-gated Rebound does nothing and is not consumed.
Current-build `CardModel.<OnPlayWrapper>d__*.MoveNext` (`0x3e08bc`) captures
this ordered result before generating replay bodies and uses the
same path for manual play and AutoPlay. Replayed Skill bodies therefore
execute repeatedly but the exact physical card exhausts once. In contrast,
blocked/ShouldPlay-false AutoPlay calls
`CardModel::MoveToResultPileWithoutPlaying` **0x31b6e4**, which directly
removes only IsDupe, exhausts forced/keyword cards, or discards (including a
non-dupe Power);
it never invokes the global result-location hook, so Corruption does not
rewrite a blocked flip.

The simulator stores unique presence in keyed `State.corruption`, registers
its first application in the existing result-location listener order, and
maps only the exact raw CorruptionPower template. This batch admits only
`CARD.CORRUPTION`; every other refusal remains intact.

## Vicious power-amount listener (Batch 131, 2026-07-25, #393)

The installed and archived sources were rechecked before implementation:
**v0.109.0 / c12f634d**, arm64 `sts2.dll`, SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.

  upgrade 1.

- `Vicious.OnUpgrade` **0x29be5b**: Cards +1, producing 2.
- `Vicious.<OnPlay>d__5.MoveNext` **0x40f848**: after the PowerUp animation,
  await `Apply<ViciousPower>(owner, Cards.BaseValue, owner, card, false)`.
- `ViciousPower.get_Type/get_StackType` **0x2565eb/0x2565ee**: both 1;

combat-listener walk and serially awaits each listener.

The simulator stores Vicious's additive Amount in keyed `State.vicious`.
Player-side Vulnerable and successful post-Artifact monster-side Vulnerable
applications now pass through exact post-mutation dispatch seams. Existing
monster applications to the player carry `BreakerIdentity.MONSTER`, so they
cannot trigger Vicious. A positive owner-applied delta on either side draws
the current Vicious Amount through the established ordinary draw command
(`fromHandDraw=false`), retaining NoDraw, Fiddle, hand capacity, reshuffle,
drawn-card hook, and combat-ending behavior. Bag of Marbles runs before a
card Power can be active and needs no dispatch. The other #393 consumers
remain refused, so no co-active represented listener can observe or reorder

The complete invariant walk is
`invariant-walks/2026-07-25-233-batch131-vicious.md`.

## Batch 2 E1 — AfterBlockBroken dealer identity and Hand Drill (#345, 2026-07-17)

Every cite in this section was freshly dumped from the installed macOS-arm64
`sts2.dll`, **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**, SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.
The issue prose was used only as a work list; nested `MoveNext` bodies and
every modeled block-consuming source below were independently re-read.

### Event and relic bodies

`HandDrill::<AfterBlockBroken>d__6::MoveNext` **0x36f7f8** reads the event's
`breaker`. It continues exactly when the breaker equals
`Owner.Creature` (**IL_0020-0031**) or is non-null and
`breaker.PetOwner == Owner` (**IL_0033-004b**), then rejects a player target
(**IL_0052-005f**). The effect is
`Apply<VulnerablePower>(target, DynamicVars.Vulnerable.BaseValue,
applier=Owner.Creature)` (**IL_0064-0093**); Hand Drill's canonical amount is
**2**. Thus the exact solver distinction is a closed typed identity:
`PLAYER`, `PLAYER_PET`, `MONSTER`, or `NONE`. The first two trigger; the last
two do not. `damage_monster` only targets enemies, so the relic's
`target.IsPlayer` rejection is structural there; player damage is handled by
separate player-target paths and never dispatches Hand Drill.

`CreatureCmd::<Damage>d__12::MoveNext` **0x432a14** computes block through
`DamageBlockInternal` (**IL_02e0-02f8**), then sets `WasBlockBroken` to
`post-hit Block <= 0 && blockedDamage > 0` (**IL_04de-0500**). Therefore an
already-zero-block target does not emit, and props-6 Unblockable damage skips
block and cannot emit. The later result walk reads `WasBlockBroken` and calls
`Hook::AfterBlockBroken(combatState, choiceContext, receiver, dealer)`
(**IL_0b2f-0b53**) once per breaking result.

The emission precedes the kill batch: AfterBlockBroken begins at
**IL_0b2f**, while `CreatureCmd::Kill(killedCreatures, false)` is not called
until **IL_0ead-0eb4**. A lethal breaker therefore still emits. The target can
receive the debuff at that point: `PowerCmd::<Apply>d__1::MoveNext`
**0x438c50** gates on `Creature.CanReceivePowers` at **IL_0039-0044**;
`Creature::get_CanReceivePowers` **0x2c9115** delegates to
`Hook::ShouldAllowHitting`, and Illusion/Reattach reject only after their
`isReviving` bit has been set by the later death hook. Then normal death
cleanup removes Vulnerable. This order is modeled, not skipped: notably a
lethal break first lets Artifact intercept/decrement, after which the
illusion/reattach/stock cleanup runs. The pin covers a lethal blocked
Parafright with Artifact and verifies `artifact 1 -> 0`, no retained
Vulnerable, and pending revival.

`CreatureCmd::<LoseBlock>d__19::MoveNext` **0x435b2c** separately guards
combat-not-over, target alive, and amount > 0 (**IL_0019-004e**), snapshots
block, calls `LoseBlockInternal`, and emits only on `before > 0 && after <= 0`
(**IL_0053-0083**) with `breaker=remover` (**IL_0097-00b4**). The exhaustive
v0.109 call scan found only: SturdyClamp
`<AfterPreventingBlockClear>d__8` **0x37b554** (relic refused), Expose
`<OnPlay>d__8` **0x3e5cd4** (modeled by the Batch 72 exact whole body), and
BurrowedPower
`<AfterRemoved>d__6` **0x37fa28**. Burrowed removal is itself caused by the
Damage block-break event, so its block is already zero and its remover-null
`LoseBlock(999999999)` cannot emit a second event. Expose is the sole modeled
positive-block `LoseBlock` source; it shares only the already-audited Hand
Drill and Burrowed consumers, without exposing a generic block-strip step.

### Complete modeled `damage_monster` dealer audit

All blockable rows below pass the owning player's creature as the real
`CreatureCmd::Damage` dealer and are represented as `BreakerIdentity.PLAYER`.
The final column is the current-build body and direct call-site IL. Repeated
Inferno simulator sites are one engine hook: each is a different modeled way
for the player to take unblocked damage and reach that same hook.

| modeled source(s) | dealer result | current-build proof |

| all player card attacks, including Tesla Coil's opening attack | PLAYER | `AttackCommand::FromCard` **0x2dffcc IL_0048-0056** sets `Attacker=CardModel.Owner.Creature`; `<Execute>d__90::MoveNext` **0x43ac88 IL_0724-0743** passes `get_Attacker` as dealer |
| player Thorns | PLAYER | `ThornsPower::<BeforeDamageReceived>d__4::MoveNext` **0x392e48 IL_0065-0086** targets the incoming dealer and passes `PowerModel.Owner` |
| Flame Barrier / Reflect | PLAYER | `FlameBarrierPower::<AfterDamageReceived>d__4` **0x383928 IL_0052-0070** and `ReflectPower::<AfterDamageReceived>d__4` **0x38b94c IL_0065-0088** both target the incoming dealer and pass their power owner |
| Inferno retaliation | PLAYER | `InfernoPower::<AfterDamageReceived>d__8` **0x3865ec IL_00bf-00e1** damages all hittable enemies with `PowerModel.Owner`; its self-tick body **0x38679c IL_00e4-0102** targets/passes the same owner and is rejected by Hand Drill's player-target gate |
| Lightning passive/evoke, Tesla Coil passive, Dark and Glass orbs | PLAYER | `LightningOrb::<ApplyLightningDamage>d__15` **0x39b0ac IL_0112-0130**, `DarkOrb::<Evoke>d__11` **0x39a62c IL_0085-00a3**, `GlassOrb::<Evoke>d__11` **0x39add4 IL_0088-00a6**, and `<Passive>d__10` **0x39af38 IL_009a-00ae** all pass `OrbModel.Owner.Creature`; Tesla Coil `<OnPlay>d__5` **0x40b64c IL_012b-0142/01ad-01bf** invokes those Lightning passives without changing orb ownership |

| Fire Potion / Explosive Ampoule / Foul Potion / Potion-Shaped Rock | PLAYER | Fire d__8 **0x396da0 IL_0058-007d**, Ampoule d__8 **0x39699c IL_0119-0143**, Foul d__10 **0x3971bc IL_003b-0046/0092-00a1**, Rock d__8 **0x398c38 IL_0028-004c** all pass `PotionModel.Owner.Creature`; Foul's player result is rejected by target gate |

Two modeled enemy-damage callsites are intentionally negative and still pass
an explicit identity in the simulator. `PoisonPower::<AfterSideTurnStart>
d__9::MoveNext` **0x38a370 IL_005c-0075** passes **null** dealer and props 6,
so it is `NONE` and unblockable. `NecroMasteryPower::<AfterCurrentHpChanged>
d__4` **0x387eb8 IL_006f-00a2** passes the owning player but also props 6, so
it is `PLAYER` yet cannot consume block. GasBomb's modeled self-kill is really
`CreatureCmd::Kill`, not Damage; the simulator's internal HP-removal reuse is
unblockable with `NONE`. These negative paths preserve block and never fire
Hand Drill.

The pet arm is present in the game surface but not production-reachable in
current modeled content. `Osty::GenerateMoveStateMachine` **0x2664cc** is the
single no-op `NOTHING_MOVE`. `AttackCommand::FromOsty` **0x2e005c** would set
the pet as attacker, but every card that calls it remains refused, and no
modeled effect grants Thorns/Flame Barrier/Reflect to the pet. The typed
`PLAYER_PET` arm is nevertheless positively pinned against the Hand Drill
gate; `MONSTER` and `NONE` are negatively pinned. An AST guard requires an
explicit `dealer=` on every production `damage_monster` call, preventing a
future source from silently inheriting the test-only `NONE` default.

### Simulator consequence and pins

Hand Drill is now a known hand-modeled relic and its stale generated refusal
is removed. A single exact `block_broken` bit feeds both Hand Drill and the
pre-existing Tunneler Burrowed interrupt. The breaking hit keeps its original
block/HP arithmetic and is not retroactively Vulnerable-scaled; Hand Drill's
debuff is applied afterward through ArtifactPower. Pins cover player attack,
player pet, monster, none, already-zero block, unblockable damage, Artifact,
lethal illusion/revival ordering, and Hand Drill + Tunneler coexistence. No
fight/live pin is changed or weakened.

## Batch 3 E1 — Shiv tag, Accuracy, and Phantom Blades (#348, 2026-07-17)

Every cite in this section was freshly dumped from the installed macOS-arm64
`sts2.dll`, **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**, SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.
The issue prose was used as a work list, not as evidence; the card bodies,
power hooks, history order, generated-card entry path, and Retain mutation were
independently re-read.

### Cards and exact hook gates

`Accuracy::.ctor` **0x2835e3** is a cost-1 power with canonical Amount **4**
and upgrade **+2**. `Accuracy::<OnPlay>d__5::MoveNext` **0x3d1f1c** applies
AccuracyPower at that amount. `AccuracyPower::ModifyDamageAdditive`
**0x24b6d0** returns Amount exactly when dealer equals the power owner, the
damage is powered, card is non-null, and `card.Tags` contains CardTag **5**;
every failed gate returns zero.

`PhantomBlades::.ctor` **0x2937a6** is a cost-1 power with canonical Amount
**9** and upgrade **+3**. Current build correction: the nested play body is
`PhantomBlades::<OnPlay>d__7::MoveNext` **0x3fb14c** (not d__6); it applies
PhantomBladesPower. `PhantomBladesPower::ModifyDamageAdditive` **0x251a68**
requires powered damage, non-null CardTag-5 card, and dealer equal to owner,
then counts matching `CombatHistory.CardPlaysFinished`; it returns Amount only
when the count is zero. Predicate body **0x251aec** requires
`HappenedThisTurn`, CardTag 5, and the same player.

`PhantomBladesPower::AfterApplied` **0x2519d8** takes
`Owner.PlayerCombatState.AllCards`, filters CardTag 5 through its generated
predicate **0x389b12**, and applies keyword Retain (5) to each.
`AfterCardEnteredCombat` **0x251988** checks CardTag 5 first, then
`card.Owner == power.Owner.Player`, and applies Retain. `CardCmd::ApplyKeyword`
**0x2dbbbc** calls `CardModel.AddKeyword`; `CardModel::AddKeyword` **0x229966**
mutates that exact card's local keyword collection. This is instance state,
not a canonical tag or enchantment.

`Shiv::.ctor` **0x29706e** is cost 0, attack, SingleEnemy. Its canonical
damage is **4**, upgrade **+2**; `get_CanonicalTags` **0x297088** adds CardTag
5 and its canonical keyword body **0x2970aa** adds Exhaust (1).
`Shiv::<OnPlay>d__9::MoveNext` **0x404588** creates one powered
`AttackCommand.FromCard`: when `HasFanOfKnives` it uses all opponents;
otherwise it requires and uses the selected single target.
`Shiv::get_HasFanOfKnives` **0x2971cf** is true only for a mutable card with a
non-null owner whose creature has FanOfKnivesPower. CARD.SHIV is therefore a
closed intrinsic consumer that can be modeled safely. This #348-era host
boundary was superseded by W172: CARD.FAN_OF_KNIVES now has an exact
production mapping which applies the unique power before its first generated
Shiv and sets the low-level Fan flag through the audited card lifecycle.

### Damage and history order

`CardModel::get_Tags` **0x229108** caches the canonical tags used by both
power hooks. `Hook::ModifyDamageInternal` **0x2b2b98** walks every additive
listener and sums the results, then walks every multiplicative listener, then
applies caps. Accuracy and Phantom therefore add alongside Strength/Vigor
before Weak, Vulnerable, Shrink, Soar, Slow, or Pen Nib; there is one existing
final integer truncation.

`CardModel::<OnPlayWrapper>d__339::MoveNext` calls
`CombatHistory.CardPlayFinished` at **IL_0823** and only afterward calls
`Hook::AfterCardPlayed` at **IL_0849**, once per completed replay iteration.
`CombatHistory::CardPlayFinished` **0x2e3112** appends an entry carrying the
current round, side, and player-turn numbers. `CombatHistoryEntry::
HappenedThisTurn` **0x2e3464** requires a non-null combat state, the same
round/current side, and equal turn number for every player. In this solo
simulator that is exactly a per-player-turn reset. The counter advances after
OnPlay resolves and before AfterCardPlayed, including selection resume and
auto-play. A duplicated Shiv consequently receives Phantom on replay zero and
not on replay one; a pending unresolved play does not increment.

### Generated entry, full Hand, and pile identity

`Shiv::CreateInHand` nested body **0x404438** constructs fresh Shiv instances
and passes them to `CardPileCmd.AddGeneratedCardsToCombat` targeting Hand (2),
Bottom (1). The latter's body **0x42c464** records each generated card, invokes
`CardPileCmd.Add`, then fires AfterCardGenerated. `CardPileCmd::<Add>d__10::
MoveNext` **0x42aa00** selects the real destination: a full Hand redirects to
Discard, then `AddInternal` completes at **IL_07ed**; for a new combat card,
`Hook::AfterCardEnteredCombat` fires afterward at **IL_0824**. The dispatcher
body is **0x4158cc**. Thus Phantom marks the exact inserted instance even when
Hand overflow redirects it to Discard.

The simulator stores local Retain separately from the enchantment and carries
the whole instance tuple through draw, discard, reshuffle, selection, move,
exhaust, result pile, flush, and upgrade. Glam/Touch rewrites preserve local
keywords. The first local mutation dynamically enables and keys
`exact_piles`, because a retained plain generated Shiv beside an enchanted or
unretained identical Shiv makes live tie order load-bearing. This also avoids
attempting to canonical-sort a `None` enchantment against a tuple payload.

The admitted registry surface is intentionally narrow: Accuracy and Phantom
Blades load from the exact generated templates, SHIV is registered by hand at
levels 0/1, and its stale translator refusal is removed. The original #348
surface left FAN_OF_KNIVES refused; W172 supersedes that one host boundary
with an exact power-before-generation model. Infinite Blades, Sentry Mode,
Cunning Potion, and every other external generator in this historical
inventory retain their own boundaries. The #348 landing itself changed card
totals from modeled **197 to 200**, refused **303 to 302**, and untouched
**96 to 94**.

## Batch 4 E1 — RupturePower exact HP-loss-source pipeline (#350, 2026-07-17)

Verified live build: **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**, arm64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.
`Rupture` ctor **0x295f38** is a cost-1 power. `OnPlay` d__5
**0x40108c** applies `RupturePower` Amount 1, upgraded to 2. The power is
Type 1 / Intensity, so recasts add Amount and the permanent power survives
turn boundaries.

`RupturePower::BeforeCardPlayed` **0x252ec4** first requires the exact card's
owner creature to equal the power owner and `CombatManager.CurrentSide` to
equal the owner's side. It then performs
`playedCards.Add(exact CardModel, 0)`. `AfterDamageReceived` d__9
**0x38c624** requires the damaged target to be that owner, positive
`UnblockedDamage`, and the owner's current side. If the Damage command has a
non-null `cardSource` found under that exact dictionary key, it adds the
power's current Amount to the stored value. Otherwise it immediately calls
`Apply<StrengthPower>(owner, Amount)`. Consequently the increment is once per
qualifying `DamageResult`, not multiplied by HP lost.

`AfterCardPlayed` d__10 **0x38c4fc** owner-gates and calls
`playedCards.Remove(exact CardModel, out value)`. A failed removal returns;
successful removal unconditionally calls `Apply<StrengthPower>(value)` and
has no current-side gate. `PowerCmd::<Apply>d__2::MoveNext` **0x438e74**
early-outs while combat is ending and when Amount is zero at **IL_0039–005c**.
Positive `StrengthPower` is Type 1;
`ArtifactPower::TryModifyPowerAmountReceived` **0x24ba00** only blocks visible Type-2 debuffs,
so Artifact cannot consume or reduce either immediate or batched Rupture
Strength. Later powered card attacks read the resulting additive Strength
through `StrengthPower` **0x25488f/0x254898**.

`CreatureCmd::<Damage>d__12::MoveNext` **0x432a14** threads the same
`cardSource` to `AfterDamageReceived` at **IL_0d51–0d86**, once per surviving
damage result. Its `WasTargetKilled` branch precedes that hook, so a lethal
player result does not increment Rupture. The card wrapper still reaches its
finish cleanup: `CardModel::<OnPlayWrapper>d__339::MoveNext` **0x364ad0**
creates one `CardPlay` per replay iteration, dispatches `BeforeCardPlayed`
at **IL_0590–059b**, awaits OnPlay at **IL_063b–0640**, then dispatches
`CardPlayFinished` at **IL_0818–0823** and `AfterCardPlayed` at
**IL_0838–0849**. A selection suspension preserves that same play/key; a
Duplicator replay gets a fresh Add/Remove pair. Nested Havoc-style auto-play
temporarily has distinct outer and inner exact keys.

| player HP-loss producer | side / source observed in current IL | Rupture result |
|---|---|---|
| Bloodletting **0x3d668c**, BloodWall **0x3d6898**, Hemokinesis **0x3ee180**, Breakthrough **0x3d8580** | owner side; exact playing `CardModel` plus current `CardPlay` | accumulate under that exact play; one Strength application after finish |
| Beckon **0x3d5334**, Infection **0x3f027c**, Regret **0x3ffd30** turn-end hooks | owner side; card model plus null `cardPlay`, absent from active keys | immediate per result |
| monster Thorns d__4 **0x392e48** | owner side; null card source / play | immediate between attack hits, so it can strengthen a later hit |
| Galvanic d__10 **0x384800** and Foul Potion d__10 **0x3971bc** | owner side; null card source | immediate; same-play Galvanic can see a newly applied Rupture |
| Inferno d__7 **0x38679c**, Crimson Mantle d__9 **0x38190c**, Disintegration d__4 **0x382588** | owner side; power/owner source, not a playing card | immediate per surviving result |
| ordinary monster attacks | enemy side | rejected by `CurrentSide == owner.Side` even after positive HP loss |

The simulator represents Rupture Amount in keyed mutable state and carries a
six-integer per-play power latch through ordinary play, nested auto-play,
replay, and selection suspension. A registered playing source accumulates its
batch until the matching after-play cleanup; every direct player-HP mutation
site explicitly declares owner/side/source semantics. Fully blocked and zero
loss, wrong target, enemy-side damage, and lethal results add nothing. Zero,
lethal, and combat-ending plays still clear their local registration; a new
fight starts with no power or play-local batch. No unresolved ordering or RNG
ambiguity remains in this admitted surface.

## Colossus incoming-damage primitive (Batch 128, 2026-07-25, #396)

The installed build was rechecked before implementation:
**v0.109.0 / c12f634d**, arm64 `sts2.dll`, SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.
Complete dumps covered the card and power through every `SetResult`, plus
VulnerablePower, WeakPower, ShrinkPower, and SoarPower to prove the generic
damage-hook argument roles rather than infer them from the issue title.

- `Colossus..ctor` **0x287627**: cost 1, Skill, Uncommon, Self, max upgrade 1.
- `Colossus.get_CanonicalVars` **0x287657**: Block 4 and Colossus 1.
- `Colossus.<OnPlay>d__8.MoveNext` **0x3dc404**: Cast, await
  `GainBlock(Block, cardPlay, 0)`, then await
  `Apply<ColossusPower>(owner, 1, owner, card, 0)`.
- `Colossus.OnUpgrade` **0x2876db**: Block +3; power amount is unchanged.
- `ColossusPower.get_Type/get_StackType` **0x24c7b3/0x24c7b6**: both 1
  (positive Intensity; applications add to Amount).
- `ColossusPower.get_CanonicalVars` **0x24c7b9**: `DamageDecrease` is exact
  Decimal 0.5.
- `ColossusPower.ModifyDamageMultiplicative` **0x24c7f4**: target owner,
  powered attack, non-null Vulnerable dealer → 0.5; otherwise 1.
- `ColossusPower.<AfterSideTurnEnd>d__10.MoveNext` **0x380614**:
  `side == 2` → `PowerCmd::Decrement`; every other side is a no-op.

The simulator stores only the power Amount as keyed duration. The modifier is
at the one enemy powered-attack calculation seam, before owner Block,
Intangible, and Osty interposition. Its exact `Fraction(1, 2)` joins Weak,
player Vulnerable, and Shrink in the existing multiplicative chain, retaining
one final decimal-to-int conversion. This also means a Vulnerable dealer's
damage is reduced before a living Osty intercepts the unblocked remainder.
Player outgoing attacks, non-Vulnerable dealers, and unpowered/null-dealer
damage are unchanged. Enemy side-end decrements exactly one stack.

This batch admits only `CARD.COLOSSUS`. `CARD.CALCIFY` remains refused: its
outgoing owner/dealer additive modifier is a different half of #396 and is not
silently approximated by the new Colossus state.

Fresh installed macOS-arm64 v0.109.0 / `c12f634d` reads, `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`:

- **RAGE** — ctor `0x294c1a`: cost-0 Skill, `Power` 3 and upgrade `+2` ->
  5; `<OnPlay>d__6::MoveNext` `0x3fe244` applies `RagePower`.  Its Type and
  StackType are both 1 (`0x25231b` / `0x25231e`), so applications add.
  `<AfterCardPlayed>d__6::MoveNext` `0x38aae8` requires the played card's
  owner be the power owner and `Card.Type == 1`, then uses
  `CreatureCmd::GainBlock(Amount, prop 4)`.  `<AfterSideTurnEnd>d__7`
  `0x38abfc` removes the power only when `participants.Contains(owner)`: the
  player owner's side end, not the enemy side end.
- **SNEAKY** — ctor `0x297a93`: cost-2 Power with Sly keyword 6,
  `SneakyPower` 1 and upgrade `+1` -> 2; `<OnPlay>d__9::MoveNext`
  `0x405ce0` applies its power.  `SneakyPower` Type/StackType are both 1
  (`0x254103` / `0x254106`), and its owned-Attack `AfterCardPlayed` body is

  `AfterSideTurnEnd` override, therefore persists for the combat; only Rage

## Stars relic hooks (#427, 2026-07-17; v0.109.0 c12f634d)

This closes the five relic boundaries left by the Stars resource work.  All
five bodies were re-read from macOS arm64 `sts2.dll`, SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.

| relic | hook/body | exact modeled behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Divine Destiny | `AfterSideTurnStart`, `0x36c6b0` | owner participates and `TurnNumber <= 1` → `PlayerCmd.GainStars(7)` |
| Divine Right | `AfterRoomEntered`, `0x36c7bc` | `CombatRoom` → `GainStars(3)` before combat start |
| Lunar Pastry | `AfterSideTurnEnd`, `0x373540` | owner side end → `GainStars(1)` |
| Galactic Dust | `AfterStarsSpent`, `0x36ea24` | accumulate requested positive amount; for every crossed 10 grant raw prop-4 Block in one command; write `total % 10` after that awaited command |
| Mini Regent | `AfterStarsSpent`, `0x374038` | first positive event per owner turn sets `_usedThisTurn` before awaiting `Apply<StrengthPower>(1)` |

`CardModel.SpendStars` d__338 (`0x3661c4`) records `LastStarsSpent`, clamps
the resource via `LoseStars`, and emits `AfterStarsSpent` only for a positive
requested amount.  Consequently an overpay still advances Galactic Dust by
the requested amount.  `Hook::AfterStarsSpent` d__77 (`0x41aa70`) walks the
listener snapshot serially: Child of the Stars (a player power) precedes the
player relics.  Galactic Dust's block is not modified by Dexterity, but its
`GainBlock` still dispatches `AfterBlockGained`, including Juggernaut.  Its
post-await modulo and Mini Regent's pre-await latch commit even if that nested
event ends combat; `CreatureCmd.GainBlock` and `PowerCmd.Apply` (`0x438c50`)
themselves are ending-gated.

The simulator makes the three direct gains generated `stars` template steps;
their canonical amounts are exactly 7, 3, and 1, and relics have no card-like
upgrade dimension.  Galactic Dust's persistent `_starsSpent` remainder is a
memo-keyed `State.galactic_dust` field seeded from entry
`relic_counters[RELIC.GALACTIC_DUST]`; Mini Regent's memo-keyed sentinel is
`-1` absent / `0` fresh / `1` used.  Galactic's body uses `conv.r4`, float
division, and `Mathf.FloorToInt`; fixed supported Star payments and the
pinned multi-threshold fixtures are inside the contiguous float32 integer
domain, while an unbounded synthetic total beyond it is an explicit I5
refusal rather than a Python-integer rounding substitution.  Mini resets synchronously at
`BeforeSideTurnStart` (`0x243253`) and at combat end.  A `.run` can seed Dust
to zero only before its first owned combat; later action history does not
contain Stars spends, so the relay parser emits an explicit caveat and entry
refuses without a live-save props seed.

Ordering is intentionally narrow.  Divine Right fires before combat and
Divine Destiny's sole live fire is turn 1, before a card can establish Black
Hole, so their deterministic room/start neighbours commute.  Lunar Pastry and
Parrying Shield share `AfterSideTurnEnd`; when Lunar's Black Hole AoE or
Parry's target damage can remove an enemy, acquisition order is unrecorded
and the simulator refuses rather than choosing one.  The same I5 refusal is
used only when fresh Galactic Dust and Mini Regent share a threshold spend
whose Dust/Juggernaut chain can end combat.  Nonterminal paths commute; the
tests pin their exact target-stream behavior.  See invariant walk
`2026-07-17-86-stars-relics.md`.

## Anticipate temporary Dexterity (#172, 2026-07-17)

Current installed build: v0.109.0 / c12f634d; macOS arm64 sts2.dll SHA-256
06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82.

Anticipate ctor 0x283c7c is cost 0, CardType skill. Its CanonicalVars body
0x283c89 creates DexterityPower 2; OnUpgrade 0x283d07 calls
Dexterity.UpgradeValueBy(2), so the exact L0/L1 amounts are 2 and 4.
OnPlay wrapper 0x283cbc and full async body Anticipate/OnPlay d__5
0x3d3270 await Apply<AnticipatePower>(owner creature, DynamicVars.Dexterity
BaseValue, owner creature, this, false), after the cosmetic cast animation.
AnticipatePower ctor 0x24b976 is bare TemporaryDexterityPower; it has no
additional state or hook.

TemporaryDexterityPower is positive Type 1, StackType 1 (0x2554b0/0x2554bd).
BeforeApplied outer 0x2555f8, body d__20 0x391b04 immediately awaits
Apply<DexterityPower>(owner, +amount, applier, cardSource, true). On an
existing same power, AfterPowerAmountChanged outer 0x25565c, body d__21
0x39186c tests that it is this instance and applies exactly the changed
amount. Thus 2 then 4 is +6, while a Duplicator/Burst/Glam-generated
Anticipate L0 series reaches the same apply body once per CardPlay and grants
2 per iteration. The positive player-owned application is a buff, so it does
not enter the enemy Artifact/debuff interception path; no other modeled
Apply listener observes this wrapper. It is therefore exact to add the
translated amount directly to the existing State.temp_dexterity field.

AfterSideTurnEnd outer 0x2556cc, body d__22 0x39198c tests
participants.Contains(owner), removes the temporary wrapper, then awaits
Apply<DexterityPower>(owner, -Amount, owner, null, false). This is the
owner-side boundary, shared exactly with SpeedPotionPower (its bare subclass
ctor is 0x2542be). The simulator clears State.temp_dexterity at the existing
player-side-end site; permanent State.dexterity survives. Card block already
uses base + permanent Dexterity + temp_dexterity before Unmovable's x2 and
Frail's x3/4: Defend 5 with permanent 3, Speed 5, and Anticipate 2 is
(5 + 3 + 5 + 2) x 2 x 3/4 = 22.

The canonical raw snapshot keeps Anticipate's generated two power steps,
and the #423 composition removes only its reviewed explicit refusal. The
composed template maps AnticipatePower/self to the new temp_dexterity step.
No selection, draw, pile insertion, damage, healing, or RNG operation occurs:
the physical skill uses the ordinary discard-bottom result pile; all five RNG
stream keys are unchanged. Duplicator, Glam, and Burst already run their
non-power play count through the shared CardPlay loop, so no replay-specific
temporary state or ordering guess was introduced. POWER-card replay remains
the pre-existing explicit refusal, outside this skill's path. See invariant
walk 2026-07-17-87-anticipate-temp-dex.md.

## W88 shared DoomPower lifecycle (#177, 2026-07-17)

Current installed build: v0.109.0 / c12f634d; macOS arm64 sts2.dll SHA-256
06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82.

DoomPower is visible Type 2, StackType 1. `IsOwnerDoomed` 0x24dc12 is the
inclusive comparison `CurrentHp <= Amount`. `ShouldDoomTrigger` 0x24db54
rejects an over/ending combat, absent/dead/non-doomed owners, and every doomed
creature except the first in same-side list order. That first trigger
snapshots all living same-side creatures satisfying their own Doom threshold.
Enemy Doom fires at `BeforeSideTurnEnd` d__8 0x3827ac; player Doom fires at
`AfterSideTurnEnd` d__9 0x3826c0. `DoomKill` d__6 0x382898 walks the snapshot
in list order and calls `CreatureCmd::Kill(creature, false)` for each before
one `AfterDiedToDoom` batch. This is a direct kill, not Damage or HP loss.

The simulator stores Doom per creature, runs the player trigger after hand
flush but before enemy actions, and runs the enemy trigger after all monster
actions but before enemy-side duration/ritual handlers. Doom kills share the
existing post-death tail with Damage kills, preserving Infested spawn,
Illusion/Reattach, Axebot Stock respawn, Gremlin Horn, secondary-enemy
cascade, and fatal checks. Death clears Doom; the trigger itself consumes no
RNG.

Admitted current solo consumers:

| content | exact behavior |
|---|---|
| Scourge | cost-1 Skill; card-sourced Doom 13/16, then draw 1/2; Artifact and Lamp apply |
| Countdown | cost-1 Power 6/9; one CombatTargets enemy per owner side start; Artifact applies, Lamp does not |
| Neurosurge | cost-0 Power; energy 3/4, draw 2, install amount 3; each owner side start adds 3 Doom per stack to player |
| Reaper Form | cost-3 Power amount **1/1**; L1 adds Retain; own/own-pet powered positive integer TotalDamage applies that much Doom per stack |
| Potion of Doom | TargetType 2; canonical power-sourced Doom 33; Artifact applies, Lamp does not |

ReaperFormPower `AfterDamageGiven` d__6 0x38b1e8 uses
`DamageResult.TotalDamage`, whose getter 0x2c9d10 sums integer BlockedDamage
and integer UnblockedDamage. It dispatches before Damage's later Kill, so a
lethal hit still applies or Artifact-blocks Doom before death cleanup.
Countdown and Noxious Fumes share an application-order-dependent hook; when a
live enemy has Artifact, the simulator refuses before either listener mutates
it because State does not retain power application order.

Underworld is not a solo Reaper analogue: current body 0x3937d4 rejects the
owner and own pet and accepts multiplayer teammate/teammate-pet damage; its
side-2 removal is 0x393950. It was historically refused under #431 and is
modeled through Batch 169's narrow external teammate-damage boundary below.
Book Repair Knife, the sole current `AfterDiedToDoom` listener, is modeled by
W89 below. The canonical raw snapshot remains unchanged; the #177 reviewed
composition delta removes four solo card refusals and the potion refusal moves
out of `content_refusals.json`. Full invariant audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-17-88-doom-power.md`.

## W89 Book Repair Knife AfterDiedToDoom listener (#432, 2026-07-17)

Current installed build: v0.109.0 / c12f634d; macOS arm64 sts2.dll SHA-256
06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82.

`BookRepairKnife::get_CanonicalVars` 0x23d520 is `HealVar(3)`.
`AfterDiedToDoom` 0x23d534 counts the hook's original creature snapshot with
predicate 0x23d597:

`creature != Owner.Creature && creature.Powers.All(power =>
power.ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal())`.

At count zero it returns the completed task without flashing or healing. At a
positive count it flashes and calls `CreatureCmd::Heal` on the owner for
`3 * count` with the visual flag true. `Hook::AfterDiedToDoom` d__30 0x416c4c
runs listeners only after DoomPower's `DoomKill` has awaited every
`Kill(false)` in the original snapshot. Thus the predicate is post-batch and
does not ask whether a creature is currently dead. `PowerModel` defaults the
fatal predicate to true at 0x230460; the complete current-build override set
is `MinionPower` false at 0x250a5a and `ReattachPower`'s
`AreAllOtherSegmentsDead` result at 0x252694.

Consequences pinned in the simulator:

- GasBomb and Illusion creatures retain `MinionPower`, so they never count.
- Reattach segments count only when all other segments are dead after the
  complete batch. If two of three are doomed, neither counts; if all three are
  doomed, all three count.
- StockPower has no override. An Axebot in the snapshot therefore counts even
  after its inline Stock respawn; the predicate is not an actual-dead check.
- Secondary-enemy cascade deaths absent from the original Doom snapshot do
  not count. A cascade target present in the snapshot is still evaluated, and
  its MinionPower veto remains decisive.
- Player-side Doom supplies only the relic owner in solo play, so the explicit
  owner exclusion makes the listener a no-op; it cannot rescue the player.

The resulting heal is capped at player max HP by the existing Heal primitive.
It still fires after a fight-ending enemy kill even if the awaited Kill has
already entered `IsEnding`: `CreatureCmd::<Heal>d__20` 0x4347fc
IL_003c–005a skips during ending only when the heal target is *not* a player,
so Book's player-owner heal continues. Relic presence is immutable within a
fight and is stored as a key constant. The I3 alpha ceiling adds a broad
upper bound: 3 times every current monster, plus four possible Wrigglers from
a living Phrog and every not-yet-present slot up to the five-rat
CALL_FOR_BACKUP roster, times every remaining enemy side end. It overcounts
minions, dead creatures, and repeated Reattach deaths, so it remains sound
across every modeled spawn, Stock, and segment-revival cycle. The hook adds no
RNG, pile, selection, damage, or persistent cross-fight state. Full audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-17-89-book-repair-knife.md`.

## W90 Oblivion exact-card Doom latch (#389, 2026-07-17)

Current installed build: v0.109.0 / c12f634d; macOS arm64 sts2.dll SHA-256
06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82.

`OblivionPower` is visible Type 2 and Intensity. `BeforeCardPlayed`
0x2511cc requires a player Applier who owns the exact played CardModel, then
adds that exact card key with the power's current Amount. `AfterCardPlayed`
d__9 0x388904 removes the key; success applies the removed old amount as
DoomPower to the Oblivion owner with the player Applier and null card source.
`AfterSideTurnEnd` d__10 0x388a0c removes Oblivion at side 1 end.
`Oblivion.OnPlay` d__5 0x3f8da8 applies 3/4 Oblivion to its selected enemy.

The simulator represents the dictionary as a per-CardPlay tuple of
`(Monster.uid, old Amount)` registrations. Manual plays, every replay, and
every auto-play get a fresh frame; recursive auto-play retains the outer frame
while resolving its inner frame, and selection pending stores the hashable
outer tuple. uid is exact Creature identity: Axebot replacement bumps it,
while all deaths clear Oblivion. AfterCardPlayed requires the same uid still
live with the power present. Therefore a stale dead/replaced-owner latch
cannot fire, and duplicate target retargeting does not redirect ownership.

First cast applies only Oblivion: no power existed to register before OnPlay.
A recast with old A stacks 3/4 during OnPlay and then applies Doom A. The two
applications are separately Artifact-gated and ordered: with one Artifact,
the Oblivion reapply is blocked and old-A Doom lands; with two, both are
blocked. Card-sourced Oblivion is eligible for Unsettling Lamp; the later
power-sourced Doom has no card source, so Lamp is neutral.

AfterCardPlayed listener order follows `IterateHookListeners` 0x2dffd1:
player powers, all player relics, then enemy creatures in creature-list order.
Each encounter-native Slow/Vital/Galvanic power predates that creature's
player-applied Oblivion and runs first. This order is observable:
Kusarigama can kill an owner before its callback, and Galvanic can kill the
player before the same owner's or a later creature's callback. SmoggyPower is
enemy-applied but player-owned, so its current d__4 body 0x38ea5c (outer
0x253f00) runs in the player-power layer. Oblivion removes at the player side
end; callback-applied Doom remains for W88's later enemy-side-end trigger.

The card consumes no RNG under manual targeting and uses ordinary discard-
bottom routing. Auto-play and Kusarigama retain their pre-existing
CombatTargets draws. Persistent Amount and pending latch both join memo keys.
The canonical raw template is unchanged; reviewed composition removes only
the #389 refusal, moving card coverage from refused to modeled. Full audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-17-90-oblivion.md`.

## Mangle temporary negative enemy Strength (#334, 2026-07-17)

Current installed build: **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**; macOS arm64 `sts2.dll`
SHA-256 `06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.
All RVAs below were freshly re-dumped from that DLL.

`Mangle` ctor 0x290dbf is a cost-3 targeted Attack. Its canonical vars are
Damage 15 and StrengthLoss 10; `OnUpgrade` adds 5 to each. `OnPlay` async body
0x3f48c8 executes the Attack first, then `Apply<ManglePower>` to the selected
enemy with the owning player's creature and physical card as sources.

`ManglePower` ctor 0x250929 subclasses `TemporaryStrengthPower` and
`get_IsPositive` 0x250926 returns false. The base wrapper's
`<BeforeApplied>d__20::MoveNext` 0x392214 applies `sign * Amount` as an
internal `StrengthPower`, hence -10/-15. `StrengthPower::ModifyDamageAdditive`
0x254898 adds that signed amount only to powered attacks dealt by its owner.
The damage pipeline's final `Hook::ModifyDamage` 0x2b1214 IL_01b5-01c0 clamps
the fully modified result with `Math.Max(Decimal.Zero, result)`, so Strength
cannot make an attack heal or manufacture block.

The outer Mangle wrapper is visible Type 2. `ArtifactPower::
TryModifyPowerAmountReceived` 0x24ba00 zeros that outer application and its
AfterModifying hook 0x37e5c8 consumes one Artifact, so zero never reaches
`BeforeApplied`. If the wrapper passes, the internal negative Strength is
also amount-classified Type 2 by `PowerModel::GetTypeForAmount` 0x22fe14, but
Artifact was absent; this is one gate/consumption, not two. Every later stack
is a separate outer application and independently checks then-current
Artifact.

Unsettling Lamp's `BeforePowerAmountChanged` 0x2496b8 latches a card-sourced
Mangle only when Artifact is absent. Its multiplier 0x249764 doubles the
outer wrapper. `HasDoubledTemporaryPowerSource` 0x249828 compares an earlier
temporary wrapper's `InternallyAppliedPower` type with the current power:
the outer ManglePower is doubled because StrengthPower != ManglePower; the
subsequent internal StrengthPower is not doubled again because it matches.
Thus Lamp makes 10 -> one wrapper amount 20 plus one Strength delta -20,
never -40. An Artifact-blocked Mangle neither doubles nor consumes Lamp.

`TemporaryStrengthPower::<AfterSideTurnEnd>d__22::MoveNext` 0x39209c gates
on `participants.Contains(owner)`, removes the wrapper, then applies
`-sign * accumulated Amount` StrengthPower. Mangle therefore affects the
target enemy's action and reverts at the **target/power-owner enemy side
end**, after enemy-side Doom and all monster actions—not at the player
applier's side end. Same-target applications stack additively.

The simulator stores the signed internal temporary Strength delta on
`Monster.temp_strength`: Mangle contributes `-N`; the signed aggregate can
represent a future independently proven positive enemy wrapper. The same signed
delta is present in `Monster.strength` while active; owner-side expiry removes
it with `strength -= temp_strength`. The admitted Mangle wrapper and its
internal signed Strength delta share that lifetime, and both fields are
automatically copied and memo-keyed. Any future positive enemy wrapper must
be proven independently; Coordinate is AnyAlly and is not a consumer.

Death follows `Creature::RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath` 0x2c9a0c. Normal deaths,
Decimillipede fresh reattachment state, and Axebot's fresh replacement remove
both wrapper and internal delta (Axebot also bumps creature uid). Illusions
are the deliberate exception: `IllusionPower::ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath`
0x24faa2 preserves a candidate when it implements `ITemporaryPower` or its
fixed `get_Type` is not Type 2. ManglePower is Type2+ITemporary, while
StrengthPower's fixed `get_Type` 0x25488f is Type1 even when its negative
amount makes `GetTypeForAmount` return Type2. Both therefore survive illusion
death and `REVIVE_MOVE`, then expire normally at that enemy side end.

The raw translator snapshot remains byte-identical. Reviewed composition
removes only `CARD.MANGLE`'s #334 refusal; card coverage moves one refused row
to modeled. Exact tests cover card levels/command order, stacking, first and
later Artifact gates, Lamp, powered damage and zero-floor arithmetic,
owner-side expiry, normal/segment/Axebot/illusion death behavior, multi-enemy
independence, clone, and memo key. Full audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-17-91-mangle-temp-strength.md`.
