## W97 Scrolls of Biting / PaperCuts (#180, 2026-07-17)

Current installed build: **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**; macOS arm64 `sts2.dll`
SHA-256 `06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.
This section supersedes the stale EW2 refusal/cites above.

`ScrollOfBiting::GenerateMoveStateMachine` 0x268a28 is deterministic through
`CHOMP -> MORE_TEETH -> CHEW -> RAND`. CHOMP is 16 at A9+ / 14 below A9;
CHEW is 6 at A9+ / 5 below A9, twice; and MORE_TEETH move body d__30
0x3b1c30 applies `StrengthPower(2)` to its owner. The RAND after CHEW has
`CHOMP` then `CHEW` as CannotRepeat branches.

Since it is reached directly after `CHEW`, `CHOMP` is the only eligible
result, but `RandomBranchState` still consumes one `MonsterAi.NextFloat` draw.
The solver's recorded-run encounter loops use the
project-wide A9+ move values and retain both lower DLL tier values as explicit
content facts.

Weak `GenerateMonsters` 0x2808dc creates exactly three Scrolls; normal
`GenerateMonsters` 0x2807f4 creates exactly four. Each makes the Scrolls in
slot/Niche-HP order, takes exactly one `EncounterModel.Rng.NextInt(3)`, and
starts the first three at `k`, `(k+1)%3`, `(k+2)%3`; normal's fourth starts at
CHEW (index 2). These are not a selected/up-to-four roster. Initial HP is a
unique Niche draw per creature from 33--39 at A8+ and 30--37 below A8.

`PaperCutsPower::AfterDamageGiven` outer is 0x251864 and complete nested body
`d__4` is 0x389790. It requires the exact dealer to be the power owner, the
target to be the player, `IsPoweredAttack`, and positive `UnblockedDamage`;
then it invokes `CreatureCmd::LoseMaxHp(choiceContext, player, Amount, 0)`.
`ScrollOfBiting::AfterAddedToRoom` d__26 0x3b18e0 applies
`PaperCutsPower(2)`, so every qualifying player-result loses two Max HP. A
fully absorbed hit and a fully absorbed Osty-interposed result fail the
target/unblocked condition; a positive spill is the player result and fires
once.

`CreatureCmd::LoseMaxHp` outer 0x2ddf04 / nested `d__23` 0x435c84 first
computes raw `newMax = oldMax - amount`. When raw newMax is below current HP,
it awaits a nested `CreatureCmd::Damage(currentHp-newMax, props=6, null
dealer/source)` before `SetMaxHp(max(1,newMax))`; `SetMaxHp` is d__24
0x436204. Thus damage precedes cap storage and the cap floors at one even if
the nested result is lethal. Props 6 is unpowered and unblockable with null
dealer: it cannot invoke Flame Barrier, Reflect (zero blocked damage), The
Gambit, PaperCuts recursively, or Inferno; the enemy-side context rejects
Rupture. Centennial Puzzle is the surviving nested `AfterDamageReceived`
consumer. A nested Puzzle draw can itself end combat (for example via
Cacophony), and the original attack's later listener pass is then suppressed.

`State.max_hp` is mutable and auto-included in the dataclass-derived memo key;
clone keeps it local. The alpha bound already uses
`min(s.max_hp, s.hp + heal_potential(...))`, so Blood Potion percentage,
fixed-card healing, Regen, and all future healing cap at the lowered current
maximum. `solve()` is deliberately one-fight only: its objective remains
`(win, final_hp, potions_left, -turns)` and does not score a post-combat cap.
Subsequent fight entry HP/max-HP is independently read by `relay_parser` from
the recorded node snapshot, so this admission makes no unrecorded cross-fight
propagation claim. Full audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-17-97-papercuts.md`.

## Card-play result-location closure (#354, 2026-07-18)

Fresh v0.109.0 proof on base `6617dd9e218393589fb4688984399586c77edb9d`
established the single pipeline. Current-build
`CardModel::GetResultLocationForCardPlay` 0x7e018 returns Remove for
Power/IsDupe, Exhaust for forced/keyword Exhaust, otherwise Discard Bottom.
Current-build OnPlayWrapper 0x3e08bc calls that virtual once,
threads it through `Hook::ModifyCardPlayResultLocation` 0x2b0f90, invokes
After only for actual changers, then generates play count and bodies. One
final route is shared by the entire replay series and pending continuation.
Manual and `CardCmd::AutoPlay` converge here.

`CardPileCmd/<Add>d__10` 0x42aa00 maps position 1 to index -1 (append) and
position 2 to index 0 (top). The solver's shared resolver therefore prepends
Draw Top, appends Discard Bottom, uses the ordinary exhaust event for Exhaust,
and silently removes Powers. Owner death after OnPlay skips the epilogue
(`OnPlayWrapper` IL_08a7-08ec and 0993-0998); an enemy-ending play with a
living player still routes. Global listeners are suppressed when combat was
already ending before resolution, while a card virtual such as Shining Strike
still runs.

ReboundPower 0x2528a1 changes only an owner Discard input to Draw Top.
After 0x38b790 decrements only when Rebound was an actual changer; own-side
end 0x38b874 removes all stacks. Rebound's card 0x2952d7 attacks 9/12, then
applies one stack, so a fresh copy never redirects itself. An old stack may
redirect it, be removed, and the OnPlay application then appends a new
listener.

NostalgiaPower 0x25102c changes an owner Attack/Skill Discard only while the
count of all prior owner Attack/Skill `CardPlayStarted` entries this turn is
less than Amount. Predicate 0x2510e4 does not inspect PlayIndex or prior result
pile: every replay body, Shining Strike, and Exhaust result advances the
future window. Resolution is still once per action before current bodies, so
a duplicated first Attack at Amount 1 routes once and overshoots history from
0 to 2. Nostalgia is additive and persistent; its After only Flashes.

Creature.ApplyPowerInternal 0x2c986c appends new powers; stacking in
PowerCmd/<Apply>d__2 0x438e74 modifies the existing instance without moving
it; hook iterator 0x441190 preserves the list. Rebound and Nostalgia both
target Discard→DrawTop, so only the earlier listener changes it. The bounded
model keys their first-application order, Amounts, and all-body history. It
removes/reappends exactly with power lifecycle rather than adding a general
hook listener representation.

Shining Strike 0x297028 calls base and changes only natural Discard to Draw
Top; dupe/remove and Exhaust remain. Its OnPlay 0x404194 attacks 8/11 then
gains 2 Stars. Rebound/Nostalgia see its already-Draw result and do not
consume. Corruption (#370), Feral (#414), Make It So (#415), Particle Wall,
and multiplayer The Ball remain explicit negative space; their Exhaust/Hand,
late exact-instance, counter, or ownership semantics are not generalized.

exact card-id, step-kind, and source allowlist. They accept only integer

Current source remains **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**. The installed and archived
macOS arm64 `sts2.dll` files both have SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.

- **HittableEnemies**: `CombatState::get_HittableEnemies` RVA `0x2e23c9`
  materializes `Enemies.Where(IsHittable).ToList()`; predicate RVA `0x440ca2`
  calls `Creature.get_IsHittable`. A caller keeps an ordered concrete list,
  rather than a live filter. Every later `PowerCmd.Apply` independently
  re-enters the complete body at RVA `0x438e74`, including ending, recipient,
  modifier, Artifact, history, and after-hook gates.
- **Chill**: ctor `0x286f9f` is a cost-0 Self-target Uncommon Skill whose
  canonical keyword getter `0x286fac` adds Exhaust. Upgrade `0x287023` removes
  only Exhaust. OnPlay outer/body `0x286fd8` / `0x3db3d4` wait for animation,
  snapshot HittableEnemies once, ignore the concrete enemy values, and await
  one `OrbCmd.Channel<FrostOrb>` per original member. Each iteration therefore
  re-enters Channel RVA `0x436964`: a full-queue lethal evoke still completes
  the current enqueue/history/after hook (#449/#450), while a later separate
  call is entry-gated. A zero-member snapshot performs no call and therefore
  cannot trigger the zero-slot bootstrap.
- **Resonance**: ctor `0x2958ba` is a cost-1, star-cost-2 AllEnemies Uncommon
  Skill. Vars `0x2958ca` give owner Strength 1; upgrade `0x295947` changes it
  to 2 only. OnPlay outer/body `0x2958fc` / `0x400214` read the amount once,
  await owner `StrengthPower(+amount)` first, then snapshot HittableEnemies
  and serially apply `StrengthPower(-1)` to each member. SpendResources body
  `0x365ffc` pays energy then stars once per action; `SpendStars` `0x3661c4`
  records the amount and runs AfterStarsSpent, while every replay is a fresh
  CardPlay body using that one ResourceInfo payment.
- **Signed Strength**: `PowerModel::GetTypeForAmount` RVA `0x22fe14` returns
  Type2 for negative incoming Amount on an Amount-stacking AllowNegative
  power. Strength RVAs `0x25488f` / `0x254892` / `0x254895` establish its
  ordinary Type1, Amount stack type, and AllowNegative flag. Negative direct
  Strength therefore takes the normal visible Type2 Artifact/Lamp path;
  positive enemy Strength remains Type1. Artifact amount hook `0x24ba00` and
  decrement body `0x37e5c8` block/spend one application. Lamp latch
  `0x2496b8` skips Artifact carriers; multiplier `0x249764` doubles the first
  later visible Type2 application and the rest of that CardPlay, and
  AfterCardPlayed `0x2497c2` closes the trigger.

The engine admissions are deliberately bounded: Chill alone may use the
HittableEnemies-count Frost-channel step, and the serial all-enemy power step
accepts only Weak, Doom, or Resonance's exact Strength `-1`. Direct signed
Strength uses the shared type-sensitive Artifact/Lamp helper. Focused pins
cover fixed snapshots under target death, final-lethal channel completion,
full and zero-slot queues, exact target-stream movement, base/upgraded result
routing, owner-before-enemy order, signed stacking through zero, Artifact-first
Lamp order, replay/Lamp reset, payment once, AfterStarsSpent/Black Hole,

`invariant-walks/2026-07-18-108-chill-resonance.md`.

  `0x299d1f` adds one repeat, producing 3 x3/4.

`NextItem` exactly once, even for a one-member list. Duplicate filtering is
bypassed. Target selection precedes damage calculation and one powered damage
instance; then the loop rebuilds the live pool. A final kill therefore stops
later hits and draws. AfterAttack runs once around the outer command, so Vigor

RandomEnemy supplies no manual action target. AutoPlay body `0x428908` has an
up-front CombatTargets branch only for AnyEnemy target type 2, so these type-4
cards consume only their per-hit draws. Ricochet uses the existing
DiscardAndDraw/Sly body `0x4291a8`: discard first, complete the paired draw,
then AutoPlay the exact Sly instance without energy or an up-front roll.
Duplicator/Glam/One-Two Punch create a fresh random hit-series command per
generated body, while the physical card routes exactly once after the series.
Normal Discard and existing Rebound/Nostalgia Draw-top routing are unchanged.

The runtime admission is exact-card and exact-level-step bounded to these
three IDs. The generic `TargetingRandomOpponents` template refusal and the
unread Flak Cannon, Stardust, Sweeping Gaze, and Volley bodies remain refused.
Only these three IDs join the runtime CombatTargets-consumer set; the
cross-fight conservative set already contained them. Focused pins cover null
manual targets, one draw per hit with one opponent, duplicates, live-pool
recomputation, final-kill draw suppression, command-scoped Vigor/Pen Nib/
Skittish, per-hit Thorns, AutoPlay and Sly ordering, replay separation, exact

## W114 fixed generated-status source quartet and Debris (#138, 2026-07-18)

Current source remains **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**. Installed and archived
`sts2.dll` SHA-256 is
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.
Complete corrected pre-edit evidence is [#138 comment
5012859654](https://github.com/sansb/StsHistoryViewer/issues/138#issuecomment-5012859654).

Four zero-cost Defect cards apply an ordinary existing effect, then create
one fixed level-0 Status and add it at Bottom:

- **Boost Away**: Block 6/9, then Dazed to Discard; ctor `0x2859d5`, body
  `0x3d77e8`.
- **Collision Course**: targeted Damage 10/14, then Debris to Hand; ctor
  `0x28758b`, body `0x3dc1f0`.
- **Overclock**: Draw 2/3, then Burn to Discard; ctor `0x292f97`, body
  `0x3f9ed4`.
- **Turbo**: GainEnergy 2/3, then Void to Discard; ctor `0x29b3bb`, body
  `0x40dd28`.

**Debris** ctor `0x288fdd` is a cost-1 Status with Exhaust, max upgrade zero.
Its `OnPlay` `0x288ff5` returns `Task.CompletedTask` exactly. The scanner's
`OnPlay without async state machine` refusal is therefore a false positive
for an inert gameplay body; playing Debris pays one and follows the ordinary
Exhaust/AfterCardExhausted pipeline.

`CardPileCmd/<AddGeneratedCardsToCombat>d__6::MoveNext` `0x42c464` records
`CombatHistory.CardGenerated`, calls pile `Add`, then fires
`AfterCardGeneratedForCombat`. Hand Bottom uses `CardPileCmd/<Add>d__10`
`0x42aa00`: each card fits while Hand has fewer than ten cards, otherwise it
redirects to Discard Bottom. All fixed insertions are append operations and
consume no RNG.

A pre-edit scout claim required correction. The outer generated-card command
checks `IsInProgress`, which remains true while ending, but nested `Add d__10`
checks `IsEnding` at IL `0041-008a` and returns a failed combat-pile result.
Thus a fight-ending Collision body records/fires the unrepresented generation
events but inserts no Debris. In a replay series an earlier nonlethal body can
insert while a later killing body cannot.

The localized runtime seam is exact-source/card/destination allowlisted to
only these four level-0 Status additions and only Hand/Discard Bottom. It
preserves source-effect-before-insertion, existing full-Hand redirection, and
the ending skip. It does not expose arbitrary cards, pools, positions, random
generation, or generated-card listeners. Arsenal, Pillar of Creation, Rocket
Punch, Smokestack, Trash to Treasure, Begone, and Splash remain refused.

Focused pins cover both levels and order; no-RNG insertions; Debris cost,
Exhaust, Feel No Pain, and Dark Embrace; Hand fit and replay overflow; lethal
and mixed-replay insertion boundaries; duplicated Overclock draw-before-add
with a generated Burn reshuffle; later Burn/Void hooks; exact negative gates;
and raw/composed refusal and coverage boundaries. Card coverage advances
**284/312 -> 289/307**; all other categories are unchanged. Full walk:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-18-114-fixed-status-generation.md`.

## W116 negative TemporaryStrength AoE family (#138, 2026-07-18)

Current source remains **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**. Installed and archived
`sts2.dll` SHA-256 is
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.
Complete pre-edit evidence is [#138 comment
5012999217](https://github.com/sansb/StsHistoryViewer/issues/138#issuecomment-5012999217).

Three all-enemy cards apply concrete negative `TemporaryStrengthPower`
wrappers:

- **Crush Under**: cost 1, common Attack, Damage 7/8, then temporary Strength
  loss 1/2; ctor `0x288531`, body `0x3def24`.
- **Dying Star**: cost 1, Stars 3, rare Attack, Ethereal, Damage 9/11, then
  temporary Strength loss 9/11; ctor `0x28a596`, body `0x3e3ebc`.
- **Piercing Wail**: cost 1, common Skill, Exhaust, temporary Strength loss
  6/8; ctor `0x29391c`, body `0x3fb584`.

Crush Under and Dying Star store `HittableEnemies` before their one-hit
attack-all command, then apply their wrappers serially to that same stored
list. The exact solver step therefore captures `(Monster object, uid)` before
the attack, attacks those original objects, and applies only to surviving
members whose uid still matches. Phrog's four inline Wriggler spawns are new
objects and are excluded. Axebot respawn reuses the sim object but increments
its creation uid, so the replacement is also excluded. A fresh post-attack
`alive()` list would incorrectly debuff both replacement classes.

Piercing Wail snapshots once and serially awaits each original recipient.
Every per-recipient application retains combat-ending/liveness gates and the
existing visible Type-2 Lamp-then-Artifact path. The concrete wrapper creates
the corresponding signed Strength delta only after successful application;
Intensity stacks and owner-side turn end restores the accumulated amount.
Normal death and Segment replacement clear both pieces, while an Illusion
revival retains both until owner-side expiry.

The fused step is exact-card/value allowlisted to the four Crush/Dying level
shapes, and `power_all_serial` adds only the two Piercing Wail shapes. The raw
and composed `HittableEnemies` refusal rows remain unchanged; `STOMP` remains
refused for its separate dynamic-cost hooks and `HAZE` remains refused for its
Sly/Poison/VFX body. Focused pins cover identity, ordering, Artifact/Lamp,
lethal gates, modifiers, replay, resources, piles, lifecycle, streams, and
negative guards. Coverage advances **294/302 -> 297/299**, with all other
categories unchanged. Full walk:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-18-116-negative-temp-strength-aoe.md`.

top identity, when hand capacity makes a replay return nothing, and when a
draw listener ends combat before the later block command. Exact ID, level,
operand, and whole body gate the fused handler.

The centralized post-shuffle continuation runs after the complete
discard-to-draw sort/Fisher-Yates operation and before ordinary Draw,
Foregone Conclusion selection, or AutoPlayFromDrawPile flipping. Combat-start
shuffle and no-op ShuffleIfNecessary paths do not fire it. Biiig Hug records
one owner-generated L0 Soot, inserts it into Draw/Random with one additional
Shuffle draw, then reaches the currently inert generated-card hook. The
Abacus gains six raw relic block while preserving block-gained hooks and the
ordinary ending gate.

baseline Shuffle counter a hypothesis: its unrecorded shuffles determine

and [scout packet](https://github.com/sansb/StsHistoryViewer/issues/138#issuecomment-5016009184).

The five static listeners share the exact decimal modifier pipeline:

- **Paper Krane** `ModifyWeak` (`0x244fec`) replaces the Weak factor with
  `3/5` when powered damage is received by its owner.
- **Paper Phrog** `ModifyVulnerable` (`0x245044`) uses `7/4` when the direct
  player attacker owns the relic. An Osty attacker is a distinct dealer and
  receives ordinary Vulnerable `3/2`, not the Phrog factor.
- **Undying Sigil** `ModifyDamage` (`0x2495bc`) multiplies the owner's powered
  direct hit by `1/2` against another creature whose live HP is at or below
  its Doom amount. The predicate is re-read before every hit.
- **Vitruvian Minion** damage (`0x249d94`) and block (`0x249dd0`) multiply by
  `2` for the exact physical owner card with the Minion tag. It has no
  powered requirement; both powered and unpowered card-block commands route
  through the same tag predicate. Minion Strike and Minion Sacrifice are the
  currently modeled damage/block representatives; Minion Dive Bomb remains
  refused.
- **Instinct** `CanEnchant` (`0x281e43`) is Attack-only. Its current effect
  (`0x281e49`) multiplies powered damage from that exact enchanted physical
  card by `2`; forged non-Attack or non-unit payloads fail closed.

Arithmetic is now `Fraction` from the first card/creature base through every
modifier: base plus enchantment additive; Instinct; Strength, Vigor and relic
additives; Pen Nib, Weak, Vulnerable, Undying Sigil, Vitruvian Minion,
Shrink, Soar and Slow; one final decimal-to-integer truncation at block/HP
application. Powered block follows the analogous additive-then-multiplier
order. Frail no longer floors before a later multiplier, and Second Wind's
per-exhaust block commands use the common block funnel instead of duplicating
its former partial arithmetic.

The Batch 40 Rattle distinction remains structural: its physical card may
carry Instinct, and a qualifying Minion tag would remain visible, while the
Osty dealer excludes player-owner Weak/Phrog/Sigil gates. All single,
multi-hit, random, all-enemy, calculated, powered block, unpowered card block,
preview, and per-exhaust block routes reuse the centralized modifiers.

## W143 accelerated Batch 43: enchant-time keyword deltas (#138, 2026-07-19)

Current source remains **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**. Durable authority, exact
scope, the pre-edit negative-space audit, and current-build RVAs are in the
[Batch 43 GO](https://github.com/sansb/StsHistoryViewer/issues/138#issuecomment-5016257520).

Three enchantments mutate the exact physical card's keywords once, at enchant
time; they add no combat hook or mutable enchantment state:

- **Royally Approved** admits only Attack or Skill (`CanEnchant 0x281f2c`),
  then adds Innate and Retain (`OnEnchant 0x281f65`).
- **Souls Power** requires effective Exhaust (`CanEnchant 0x282119`), then
  removes Exhaust (`OnEnchant 0x282145`).
- **Steady** adds Retain without a type gate (`OnEnchant 0x282250`).

The simulator keeps canonical `Card` specs immutable. One physical-card
projection starts with canonical Exhaust/Innate/Retain plus combat-local
Retain, then applies exactly the enchantment's union or difference. Only the
three core lifecycle consumers and one existing selection predicate read it:
combat-start Innate partitioning and `innate_min_draw`, end-turn
`ShouldFlushFromHand`, the once-resolved play-result pile, and Sculpting
Strike's `without_effective_retain` Hand filter. Royally Approved moves its
exact copy into the
reversed opening Innate group and retains it if unplayed; Steady retains only
its exact copy; Souls Power sends its exact played copy to the ordinary result
pile instead of Exhaust. Both Retain enchantments are excluded from Sculpting
Strike selection, changing only that already-modeled action set.

`force_exhaust` remains higher precedence than the effective keyword, so
Havoc still exhausts a Souls Power card. Manual replay and auto-play continue
to resolve one result location for one physical card after every body replay.
Mixed plain/enchanted equal-ID copies keep the existing exact-pile live order
and identity. Amounts other than exact integer 1, malformed physical payloads,
Royally Approved on a non-Attack/Skill, Souls Power on a non-Exhaust card, and
every unrelated enchantment remain fail-closed.

The union/difference remains exact if a later upgrade cannot remove an added
Innate/Retain keyword or add the Exhaust keyword that Souls Power previously
removed. An exhaustive live-`CARDS` transition scan currently finds no such
upgrade. Entry with any of the three enchantments refuses if a future registry
change violates that invariant; the focused suite independently enumerates
and pins every transition.

Coverage keeps cards **366/230**, relics **192/108**, and potions **42/22**,
while enchantments advance **10/12 -> 13/9**. Full walk:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-19-143-b43-enchantment-keywords.md`.

## W144 accelerated Batch 44: player HP-loss pipeline (#138, 2026-07-19)

Current source remains **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**. The immutable corrected
authority packet, exact scope, pre-edit four-ID audit, and ordering correction
are in the [Batch 44 GO](https://github.com/sansb/StsHistoryViewer/issues/138#issuecomment-5016372911).
It supersedes the earlier owner-side-expiry and immediate-Osty-reactive
assumptions.

The player damage funnel now carries exact `Fraction` values through the four
ordered `ModifyHpLost` stages: `BeforeOsty`, `BeforeOstyLate`, `AfterOsty`,
and `AfterOstyLate`. A listener's after-callback is queued only when explicit
integer truncation changes across that listener; the fractional result still
continues even when no callback fires. **IntangiblePower** caps final damage
at 1 before block and player HP loss at 1 in `AfterOsty`; its additive player
stack decrements only after the enemy side ends. **BufferPower** zeros owner
HP loss in `AfterOstyLate` and decrements exactly once only on an integer
boundary change. Thus zero/full-block results and `0.5 -> 0` do not spend
Buffer, while `1.5 -> 0` does.

All seven player-result sites enter one commit primitive: monster Thorns
retaliation; Galvanic/Foul; card/power self loss; monster attacks; nested
`LoseMaxHp` damage; turn-end card damage/loss; and Disintegration. Monster
attacks additionally apply the pre-block Intangible cap. `LoseMaxHp` awaits
the full nested props-6 damage, then silently clamps max/current HP; combat
history records only positive nested loss, never the clamp.

DieForYou interposition preserves the two-pass split. The owner block and
pre-Osty passes run first; Osty receives its own after-Osty pass and loses
integer-truncated HP; a lethal fractional overkill becomes a fresh player
after-Osty pass. Player mutation/history precede the deferred pet
`AfterCurrentHpChanged`/NecroMastery dispatch, followed by dealer
`AfterDamageGiven` and player `AfterDamageReceived`. Buffer cannot protect
Osty but can cancel a player spill. A NecroMastery kill removes a Scroll of
Biting before PaperCuts can enter the later dealer hook.

Content admitted from current raw templates: **Apparition** (`ctor 0x283dba`)
costs 1 and applies Intangible 1; L0 has Ethereal+Exhaust and L1 removes only
Ethereal. **Buffer** (`ctor 0x28606f`) costs 2 and applies Buffer 1/2. **Ghost
in a Jar** (`OnUse d__10 0x394990`) applies Intangible 1 to the owner-player;
**Lucky Tonic** (`OnUse d__10 0x39523c`) applies Buffer 1 to the owner-player.
Both potion recipients are owner-fixed and remain exact with Osty present.
Wraith Form remains refused because its separate negative-Dexterity behavior
is outside this scope.

Coverage advances **cards 366/230 -> 368/228** and **potions 42/22 -> 44/20**;
relics remain **192/108** and enchantments **13/9**. Full invariant walk:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-19-144-b44-player-hp-loss.md`.

## W145 accelerated Batch 45: HP-loss relic pipeline (#138, 2026-07-19)

Current source remains **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**. Exact authority and the
complete current-build hook census are durable in the
[Batch 45 GO](https://github.com/sansb/StsHistoryViewer/issues/138#issuecomment-5016532013)
and [scout supplement](https://github.com/sansb/StsHistoryViewer/issues/138#issuecomment-5016533478).

Three relics now reuse the exact four-stage HP-loss evaluator from W144:

- **Beating Remnant** (`ModifyHpLostAfterOsty 0x23c7bc`) caps owner loss to
  `min(x, 20-D)`, where `D` is this owner turn's actual surviving
  UnblockedDamage. `AfterDamageReceived 0x23c81c` adds the post-modifier
  result and `BeforeSideTurnStart 0x23c870` resets `D=0` for its owner.
- **Tungsten Rod** (`ModifyHpLostAfterOsty 0x249280`) returns
  `max(0, x-1)` for owner-targeted results.
- **The Boot** (`ModifyHpLostAfterOstyLate 0x248830`) changes HP loss in
  `[1,5)` to 5 only for a powered result dealt by the owner-player or that
  player's Osty to another target. Its separate display threshold of 4 is
  not read by the modifier.

Player Intangible precedes Remnant/Rod; Buffer precedes Boot in the late
walk. Remnant/Rod do not protect Osty, while a lethal Osty overkill starts a
fresh player after-Osty pass and receives both. Boot sees monster Intangible
and block first, so it can raise their remaining positive sub-5 HP loss to 5.
Incoming owner/pet damage, unpowered results, non-owner dealers, zero and
sub-one fractions, and loss already at least 5 remain unchanged.

Relic acquisition order is not present in a .run. When Remnant and Rod are
co-owned, the evaluator runs both orders without mutation through the later
Buffer callback. It admits only if final integer HP loss and Buffer count
agree; otherwise it raises I5 before mutation. Thus the `c=1, x=2` case
refuses (including its preserve-vs-consume Buffer variant), while
`c=2, x=3` masked by Buffer and Intangible-normalized results admit.

All seven player-result routes advance Remnant only after a positive
nonlethal owner result. Fully blocked/zero, pet-targeted, and lethal player
results do not count. Exact Fraction arithmetic flows through every listener;
the final Decimal is clamped to `[0,999999999]` and truncated once by the
common commit boundary.

Coverage advances **relics 192/108 -> 195/105**. Cards remain **368/228**,
potions **44/20**, and enchantments **13/9**. Full invariant walk:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-19-145-b45-hp-loss-relics.md`.

  `0x36aee4`) snapshots HittableEnemies and deals unpowered blockable
  damage 3 to each after an owned card Exhaust.

  `0x36e1e8`) owner-gates each Exhaust, consumes one CombatTargets draw
  when the live pool is nonempty, and deals unpowered blockable damage 1.
- **Tingsha** (Damage 3, props 4; value `0x2489d5`, body `0x37bcd8`)

consumers. Empty pools consume zero draws and singleton/multi pools consume

  the player received a positive unblocked DamageResult this turn. It then
  executes one powered targeted AttackCommand for Damage 5 with one hit, or
  Repeat 2/3 when true. Retaliatory player damage during the command affects
  later bodies, not the current snapshot.
- **FTL** (ctor `0x28ca93`, vars `0x28caa8`, history getter `0x28cae0`
  / predicate `0x28cbac`, body `0x3e9720`) first awaits one powered
  targeted attack for Damage 5/6. Only after that attack returns
  (`IL_00d9`) does it recount prior owner CardPlayFinished entries
  (`IL_00da`) and Draw 1 when the count is below 3/4. The current FTL body
  is not finished yet, while a reentrant play completed during the attack is
  visible. A replay therefore may cross the threshold between bodies.

All eight level-specific bodies use one exact ID, level, physical-card, and
whole-body allowlist. Raw and composed translator refusals remain unchanged.
Manual bodies add no RNG: only the existing auto-play target roll and FTL's
ordinary Draw reshuffle can consume streams.

Coverage advances **cards 368/228 -> 372/224**. Relics remain **199/101**,
potions **44/20**, and enchantments **13/9**. Full invariant walk:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-19-147-b47-same-turn-history-cards.md`.

`CardModel.ResolveEnergyXValue` (`0x228e50`) requires CostsX, reads the
card's one `CapturedXValue`, and passes it through `Hook.ModifyXValue`
(`0x2b2174`). A full matching-method scan found only the inherited identity
implementation and `ChemicalX.ModifyXValue` (`0x23e426`). Chemical X returns
captured X + its canonical Increase 2 (`0x23e3b6`) only when relic and card
owners match. `BeforeCardPlayed` (`0x23e3d0`) only flashes for an owner
energy-X or star-X card; it has no combat-state effect. One shared simulator
resolver now serves every modeled X body: Whirlwind, Skewer, Eradicate,
Tempest, Multi-Cast, Heavenly Drill, Malaise, and Volley. Stardust is the sole
current star-X card and remains refused with its complete body unmodeled.

Manual `SpendEnergy` (`d__337`, `0x365ec0`) captures the amount actually paid
before history, energy loss, and `AfterEnergySpent`. Chemical X changes only
the later effective value: it cannot inflate `energy_spent_this_turn`, Orbit,
Ivory Tile, or any other actual-spend consumer. Generated manual replays reuse
the same capture and resolve the same +2 independently for each body.
`CardCmd.AutoPlay` (`d__0`, `0x428908`, IL `0409-043d`) instead captures live
owner energy when `!skipXCapture` and spends nothing. Draw-pile AutoPlay
(`d__21`, `0x42cb90`) and Sly DiscardAndDraw (`d__4`, `0x4291a8`) both pass
false. AnyEnemy auto-play chooses its one upfront target before capture;
RandomEnemy Volley has no upfront target and rolls only inside its hit loop.

- **Heavenly Drill:** ctor `0x28e273`, vars `0x28e2aa`, upgrade `0x28e323`,
  OnPlay body `0x3ed5f8`. It is a cost-0 X Rare AnyEnemy Attack for Damage
  8/10. It resolves X, doubles the hit count when effective X >= 4, and
  executes one powered FromCard command. X=0 retains the outer zero-hit
  BeforeAttack/AfterAttack lifecycle.
- **Malaise:** ctor `0x290d13`, target getter `0x290d20`, OnPlay body
  `0x3f4680`. It is a cost-0 X Rare AnyEnemy Exhaust Skill. Effective amount
  is X (+1 upgraded), then it serially awaits StrengthPower(-amount) and
  WeakPower(amount). `PowerCmd.Apply` body `0x438e74` rejects amount zero at
  IL `004a-005c` before `BeforePowerAmountChanged`, so L0/effective-X-zero
  consumes no Artifact and cannot latch Lamp. With positive amount, negative
  Strength is Type 2; Artifact is checked per application. Artifact 1 blocks
  Strength, then Weak latches/doubles under Lamp; Artifact 2 blocks both and
  leaves Lamp armed; Artifact 0 makes Strength latch and both applications
  double. Lamp finishes after each generated CardPlay, so a replay is
  undoubled after the first body consumes it.
- **Volley:** ctor `0x29bf6c`, vars `0x29bf7c`, upgrade `0x29bfe3`, OnPlay
  body `0x40fcb0`. It is a cost-0 X Uncommon RandomEnemy Attack for Damage
  10/14. One powered FromCard random-opponent command performs effective-X
  hits. Each executed hit rebuilds the live pool and consumes one
  CombatTargets draw, including singleton pools; duplicates are allowed.
  Zero hits draw none, and a terminal kill suppresses later hits/draws while
  preserving the outer command lifecycle.

Volley joins the current-fight `_TARGETS_CONSUMER_DECK_CARDS` gate. It was
already present in `solve_fight.TARGETS_CONSUMER_CARDS`; a prior deck holding
it therefore makes the later entering counter a hypothesis, while a current
fight that needs the stream refuses an unknown counter. Chemical X consumes
no stream and has no acquisition-order state because it is the sole override.
Raw/composed translator refusals and the card/relic censuses remain unchanged.

## Batch 57 AutoPlay family: Cascade, Dirge, Stardust (2026-07-19)

Current source remains **v0.109.0 / c12f634d** (macOS arm64 `sts2.dll`
SHA-256 `06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`).
The exact source packet and locked scope are durable in the
[Batch 57 GO](https://github.com/sansb/StsHistoryViewer/issues/138#issuecomment-5019097562).

`CardPileCmd.AutoPlayFromDrawPile` (`d__21`, `0x42cb90`) is a two-phase
command. It first gathers every Top selection into Play, running
`ShuffleIfNecessary` independently when required, and only then executes the
frozen list. Empty supply is a null/no-op selection. A terminal shuffle hook
prevents the next Play add; a terminal first body makes later gathered
`AutoPlay` entries no-op, so those cards remain in Play. Owner death instead
breaks the execution loop. This corrects the previous sequential simulator
shape, where a Rebound/Nostalgia DrawTop result could incorrectly become the
next selection.

Each supported batch is clone-simulated before the original's first pile or
RNG mutation. Selection bodies and generated replay modifiers remain
fail-closed, including when they appear later or beneath nested Havoc. The
shared synchronous primitive now covers Havoc, Distilled Chaos, Cascade, and
Sly. `AutoPlay` checks ending/owner death first, then keyword Unplayable and
`Hook.ShouldPlay`; Smoggy, Sloth, Enthralled, and no-target failures route
without playing. `MoveToResultPileWithoutPlaying` exhausts when forced or
when the effective card keywords contain Exhaust, else discards. Only its
IsDupe remove branch precedes both checks: a blocked non-dupe Power therefore
exhausts under Havoc and otherwise discards. Suspended dupe identity remains
in the B60 boundary.
Successful play resolves AnyEnemy targeting at execution time, captures live
Energy-X or Stars-X without spending, runs the ordinary play hooks/body, and
routes the physical result once. RandomEnemy bodies keep their own per-hit
rolls. `apply_action` buffers its optional event log alongside its cloned
successor, so a late refusal commits neither state/RNG/piles nor outer
spend/play/potion log entries.

- **Cascade:** ctor `0x286bcf`, body `0x3da7fc`. Canonical cost -1, Rare Self
  Energy-X Skill. It resolves X, adds one at upgrade level 1, then invokes
  `AutoPlayFromDrawPile(Top, forceExhaust=false)`. Manual play spends energy;
  AutoPlay captures live energy without spending it; Chemical X adds two to
  the effective count.
- **Dirge:** ctor/vars/body/upgrade `0x289b9b` / `0x289bb3` / `0x3e2228` /
  `0x289c4b`. Cost-0 Uncommon Exhaust Energy-X Skill. It serially summons
  Osty for 3/4 exactly X times, then creates X Souls (upgraded at level 1)
  and serially inserts them Draw/Random. Every insertion consumes one
  Shuffle draw; X=0 is a body no-op before the normal Exhaust result.
- **Stardust:** ctor/vars/body/upgrade `0x298d45` / `0x298d55` / `0x407f6c`
  / `0x298dbb`. Cost-0 Uncommon RandomEnemy Star-X Attack for 5/7. Manual
  play spends/captures the live Stars once; AutoPlay captures without
  spending. `ResolveStarXValue` shares Chemical X's +2 hook. One body-owned
  random-opponent command rolls once per executed hit; X=0 rolls none and a
  terminal hit stops the remainder.

Cascade and Stardust join the current-fight CombatTargets provenance gate.
Hand Trick joins both current/prior gates because it can mark a targeted
Skill transient-Sly and a later discard AutoPlays it with a null target;
Cascade, Dirge, and Havoc form the complete current modeled prior-fight card
set that can shift the run-lifetime Shuffle stream through draw-pile
AutoPlay or random insertion. The `.run` lacks exact prior play timing, so a
matching prior deck now surfaces an explicit counter hypothesis. Raw and
composed translator refusals remain as source provenance; hand registration
makes the three rows modeled. Coverage advances **cards 391/205 -> 394/202**;
relics remain **216/84**, potions **45/19**, encounters **43 modeled + 8
certified / 30 refused**, and enchantments **16/6**. Full walk:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-19-157-b57-autoplay-family.md`.

## Batch 60 resumable AutoPlay/phase prerequisite (2026-07-20)

The B57 synchronous boundary is replaced by a hashable continuation executor
without admitting content. Every combat card now has a deterministic immutable
uid, distinct even for payload-equal copies and preserved across all five
piles, active/direct bodies, upgrades, enchantments, keyword/slot-7 rewrites,
and clone. AutoBatch freezes gathered Play uids/cursor; CardPlay stores exact
uid, target identity, captured X/result route, replay index/latches and
remaining steps; Phase stores phase/subphase, frozen listener tokens/cursor
and later fresh subphases. LiveListener stores a registered work key and
iteration cursor while re-filtering live piles after each child CardPlay.
A blocking selection stores an exact uid-bearing pick; payload-equal siblings
remain separate hashable actions. Resume drains the same nested frames without
resnapshot or resampling. Forged/stale picks and unsupported Havoc/direct
AutoPlay bodies refuse before any caller state, RNG, allocator, or log change.

AutoPre runs after the complete existing SetupPlayerTurn pipeline as fresh
Early, Normal, and Late snapshots (`0x43eb40`, Hook `0x414a30`). AutoPost is a
single snapshot at the beginning of end-turn (`0x43d25c`, Hook `0x414894`),
before BeforeSideTurnEnd/DoTurnEnd/flush. An individual listener iterator
freezes order, then rechecks Contains before yield: moved cards remain eligible
in that pass, removed cards skip, and later subphases resnapshot. Direct
`CardCmd.AutoPlay` keeps a non-null source pile through OnPlay; only pile-null
cards enter Play. Draw-pile AutoPlay still gathers the whole frozen batch into
Play first. Fixed dead replay targets remain fail-closed under #496; missing
power/relic acquisition order remains #485; existing turn-start placement
remains #499. The phase registries are intentionally empty in this prerequisite,
so all #377 consumers and coverage totals remain unchanged. The
registered-but-uninvoked Stampede work shape re-filters current Hand attacks
and consumes exactly one Shuffle-stream `NextInt(0, count)` per nonempty
iteration, including singleton/post-terminal iterations, to implement native
`Rng.NextItem` before direct AutoPlay. Empty pools consume no draw. Full audit:
W161. Each complete LiveListener iteration clone-executes and atomically
commits its cursor, handler-local RNG, and nested CardPlay/pending result; a
late loud refusal leaves the caller state/key/RNG/log unchanged.

## Issue #493 Happy Flower exactness correction (2026-07-20)

Current source remains **v0.109.0 / c12f634d** (macOS arm64 `sts2.dll`
SHA-256 `06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`).
Installed and archived release metadata is byte-identical at SHA-256
`75ee66a07c047d2c5d48e785063c4f03231f1258a07f79f80406dbb5b3e95863`.

`HappyFlower.AfterSideTurnStart` (wrapper `0x240e68`,
`<AfterSideTurnStart>d__20::MoveNext` `0x36f930`) first requires the owner in
the participant set, advances persistent `TurnsSeen` modulo canonical
`Turns`, updates status, and only on wrap awaits `PlayerCmd.GainEnergy(1)`.
`PlayerCmd::<GainEnergy>d__3::MoveNext` `0x437b68` rejects an ending combat at
IL `0030–003c`, routes the amount through `Hook.ModifyEnergyGain` at
IL `0052–0067`, and mutates energy only when the final amount is positive.
`NoEnergyGainPower.ModifyEnergyGain` therefore zeros the grant without
rolling back the already-advanced counter.

The enclosing `CombatManager/<StartTurn>d__106::MoveNext` `0x43f6a4` invokes
`Hook.AfterSideTurnStart` at IL `0727`. `Hook.IterateCombatHookListeners`
(`0x41ccc0`) rejects an already-over/ending combat when enumeration starts.
Once started, `Hook/<AfterSideTurnStart>d__75::MoveNext` `0x41a6ac` awaits
every listener in the captured sequence without another ending check.
`CombatState.IterateHookListeners` `0x441190` builds the player sequence with
creature powers before relics, preserving the exact player-power/relic phase
boundary. Thus an effect in an earlier hook prevents Happy Flower from
running, while an earlier listener in the already-started side-start hook may
end combat without suppressing the persistent counter; only the nested energy
command becomes a no-op.

Relic acquisition order is absent from `.run`. The only current terminal
relic-order seam is Happy Flower versus Sai while Juggernaut can make Sai's
block lethal (Sai `0x246cdc`, body `0x3796bc`; Juggernaut body `0x38701c`).
Flower-first gains the energy before Sai ends combat; Sai-first still advances
Flower's captured counter but its GainEnergy returns. Both orders have the
same fight outcome, enemy HP, persistent counter, block, and RNG state; they
differ only in terminal energy and debug/visual output, neither of which can
feed another action or persist to the next combat. A deterministic two-order
pin records that accepted observable frontier. Any future energy hook with
RNG, persistent state, or terminal consequences requires a new

## Turn-start relic hooks — Brimstone, Fake Flower, Mr Struggles, Royal Poison

Batch 58 adds four current-build hand models. Fake Happy Flower owns a
separate cross-combat `TurnsSeen` counter: every captured player
`AfterSideTurnStart` listener advances it modulo 5 and a wrap attempts to gain
1 energy. It uses the same split lifecycle as Happy Flower—an earlier-hook
terminal result prevents counter mutation, while a terminal result from an
earlier listener in an already-captured side-start hook still permits the
counter mutation but suppresses nested GainEnergy.

Mr Struggles snapshots the current hittable-enemy sequence at
`AfterPlayerTurnStart` and deals each target blockable, unpowered damage equal
to the current owner TurnNumber. Death hooks and replacements run per target,
but PHROG spawns and Axebot replacement identities are not members of the
original bulk snapshot. Royal Poison runs on opening turn 1 only and sends 4
unblockable, unpowered damage directly to the owner with no dealer, card, or
source identity; it bypasses Osty redirect and uses the complete ordinary
owner HP-loss/history/listener pipeline. Brimstone runs later at
`AfterSideTurnStart`: owner Strength +2 resolves first, then the relic
snapshots living opponents and grants each +1 Strength.

Because same-hook relic acquisition order is absent from run data, the engine
refuses only compositions whose order can change a reachable terminal,
replacement, or RNG-consuming nested result. Legacy Inferno/Crimson Mantle
placement also requires narrow Mr/Fake/Brimstone refusals; the underlying
general phase issue is tracked in #499. Opening-only Royal compositions with
those powers remain unreachable while Royal is active and are admitted. Full
invariant walk:

The two Eye relics and Snecko Oil are modeled together because they are the

does not change combat state. Co-ownership applies the same stackable power
twice, producing one listener. Its Amount=2 is behaviorally unused, so each
eligible draw consumes exactly once while the real Eye's +2 draw applies once.

ConfusedPower.AfterCardDrawn (`0x24c9b0`, roll at `0x24ca1d`) checks owner
identity and canonical cost >= 0, then consumes one
`CombatEnergyCosts.NextInt(4)` and appends an absolute
`SetThisCombat(roll, reduceOnly=false)` row (`0x2ca07c`). Canonical X cost is
zero, so X consumes and stores a row even though the later X resolver ignores
all fixed-cost rows. Canonical-negative cards consume nothing. Confused is
installed before combat and therefore precedes card-play-created player powers
and every card-pile listener: the exact cost order is Confused, then Kingly,
then Slither. Slither's later Set wins. Captured listener walks finish for the
already-drawn card after a terminal earlier listener; a nested Gremlin Horn
draw consumes its own Confused roll before the suspended outer card listener.

Snecko Oil has Cards=7 (`get_CanonicalVars` 0x259368), TargetType 5 at
`0x259365`, and current OnUse wrapper/body `0x259394 / 0x3998a4`.
PotionModel.IsValidTarget `0x22f60c` accepts only an alive `IsPlayer`, so Osty
is never offered and the effect remains exact with a summoned ally. The solo
action encodes the sole player target as `None`; a forged non-None Oil target
fails before potion removal. Raw `.run`, replay, live-save, and MCR adapters
also require exactly one `players` entry before selecting a player, because
the combat State cannot represent a teammate's piles, powers, RNG ownership,
or potion recipient. The body
awaits one ordinary Draw(7), then re-reads the complete live Hand in pile order
(preexisting cards followed by actual drawn cards). For each card it requires

Each eligible card consumes `NextEnergyCost` at `0x2593e7` and appends
`SetThisTurnOrUntilPlayed(roll, false)` (`0x2ca036`). X and base-negative cards
consume nothing. A prior local row cannot make a base-nonnegative card
ineligible; Oil's later local Set wins that local sequence, while later global
Tangled still adds and a late Free power can override to zero. Expiration flag
6 clears at turn end (`0x2ca107`) or once after the complete physical
play/replay/result route (`0x2ca141`); upgrades clamp absolute Set rows through
`0x2ca17c`. If a drawn-card listener ends combat, Draw stops before moving its
next card, but Oil's already-running body still randomizes the resulting live
partial Hand.

Run-history accounting now treats real Eye and Oil as prior-fight draw sources;

## Batch 68 DoTurnEnd / ShouldFlush family (2026-07-21)

Current source remains v0.109.0 / c12f634d. `CombatManager/<DoTurnEnd>
d__133::MoveNext` `0x43c294` scans the initial Hand once into two disjoint
ordered snapshots. `HasTurnEndInHandEffect` wins classification; otherwise a
live effective Ethereal keyword enters the Ethereal-only snapshot. The latter
executes first through `CardCmd.Exhaust(..., causedByEthereal=true)`. Thus a
dual-property card never appears there: it later runs its turn-end body once.

`CardModel/<OnTurnEndInHandWrapper>d__329::MoveNext` `0x365900` moves the
exact captured card Hand -> Play/Bottom before awaiting its body. It then
re-reads the live effective Keywords and routes Ethereal to Exhaust with true
cause, otherwise to Discard/Bottom. The outer snapshot loops do not invent a
blanket ending check around child commands: their command-entry gates remain
authoritative, so a terminal turn-end body can leave its exact card in Play
until teardown. Cards drawn by nested damage/exhaust/death listeners were not
in either initial snapshot and join only the later live flush.

This ordering pins Dark Embrace's exact current body. `DarkEmbracePower/
<AfterCardExhausted>d__8` `0x381f4c` increments private `etherealCount` for a
true Ethereal cause and performs no immediate draw; an ordinary cause draws
Amount immediately. `AfterSideTurnEnd` `0x382068`, after flush and cleanup,
draws `Amount * etherealCount` and then resets the count. An Ethereal exhaust
can synchronously trigger Feel No Pain / Charon's Ashes, kill an enemy, and
let Gremlin Horn draw a card before the flush; that newly drawn card is live-
flushed before Dark Embrace's delayed draw enters the next hand.

`Hook.ShouldFlush` `0x2b26a8` short-circuits an AND over its concrete owner
listeners. `RingingTriangle.ShouldFlush` `0x246837` is false only while owner
TurnNumber <= 1; `RunicPyramid.ShouldFlush` `0x246cae` and
`WellLaidPlansPower.ShouldFlush` `0x256ee1` are pure false. RetainHandPower is
the existing amount-positive false listener. Any false result suppresses the
whole live-Hand move; only a true global result reaches each card's Retain
predicate. Acquisition order is immaterial because all concrete listeners
are pure predicates.

Well-Laid Plans is a 1->0 cost Uncommon Self Power (`0x29c16b`, body `0x4100fc`,
upgrade `0x29c178`) applying one unique WellLaidPlansPower (Type 1,
StackType 2). The relic constructors/rarity getters are
`0x246857/0x246827` and `0x246cbc/0x246cab`. None consumes Shuffle, Niche,
MonsterAi, CombatCardSelection, CombatTargets, or CombatEnergyCosts. Their
unrecorded prior-fight hand retention changes later cycle membership, so the
card and both relics join the conservative Shuffle-provenance inventory.

new Shiv already observes its dynamic AllEnemies target type. Re-casts keep

Fight Through is a cost-1 Defect Uncommon Self Skill (`.ctor 0x28bccf`,
canonical vars `0x28bcec`, upgrade `0x28bd4b`). Its OnPlay body d__7
`0x3e785c` first awaits powered card Block 13/17, then runs exactly two fresh
`CreateCard<Wound>(L0)` + `AddGeneratedCardToCombat(Discard, Bottom)`
commands. If the block's nested Juggernaut command ends combat, both later
CardGenerated events still enter history, while each nested pile add rejects
the ending combat. No Wound is inserted in that terminal case.

Up My Sleeve is a cost-2 Silent Uncommon Self Skill (`.ctor 0x29baaf`,
canonical vars `0x29babc`, upgrade `0x29bb33`). Its OnPlay body d__9
`0x40edf4` first serially awaits 3/4 fresh L0 Shiv creations. Only after the
loop it increments `_timesPlayedThisCombat` and calls
`EnergyCost.AddThisCombat(-1, false)` on this exact CardModel. The cost call
appends one Relative/Add row (kind 2), expiration ThisCombat (0),
reduceOnly=false; repeated bodies append repeated rows in order and the
ordinary resolver floors the final cost at zero. An exhaustive current-build
call scan finds no reader of the private counter beyond this card's own
getter/setter, so the ordered physical cost rows are its complete behavioral
state. Equal sibling copies remain unchanged and are exact-pile divergent at
combat entry.

W172 also closes Fan's exact play-count lifecycle for Duplicator and eligible
Echo Form, for manual and AutoPlay entry. GeneratePlayCount is captured once:
Duplicator is consumed once, Echo persists, both are additive, and the
first-in-series history counter advances once per action. Every CardPlay
iteration reapplies the unique Fan presence and then reruns the complete 4/5
Shiv loop; CardPlayFinished/AfterCardPlayed fire per completed iteration. The
Power result is resolved once before the series and removes the exact source
once after it. A living-owner enemy-terminal gate suppresses later iterations
but still performs that remove. GlobeHead Galvanic can instead kill the owner
after the first completed Fan iteration; owner death suppresses later bodies
and skips the result epilogue, leaving a manual source in Play or a direct

This is not a generic Power-replay opening. One exact source-combination
classifier preserves the older synthetic Glam-only proofs for Machine Learning

AutoPlay evaluates canonical/runtime Unplayable, Smoggy, Sloth, and Enthralled

Fight Through already uses the same
complete-body replay frame: each admitted Duplicator/Echo iteration gains 13/17

series. If the first Block's Juggernaut hit ends combat, its two CardGenerated
history events still occur, later replay bodies are suppressed, and the

## Batch 72 Expose and Hang exact bodies (2026-07-21)

Batch 72 admits exactly `CARD.EXPOSE` and `CARD.HANG`, both levels, while
preserving their raw and composed translator refusals as provenance. Expose

run in native order: Hand Drill first and target-owned Burrowed second. The
remaining body is exclusive: if Artifact remains, Expose removes the whole
ArtifactPower instance; otherwise it applies 2/3 Vulnerable. Hand Drill's
application is not card-sourced and cannot latch Unsettling Lamp; Expose's own
application is card-sourced and can.

Hang deals 10/13 powered card damage, then, only if the same captured target
creature survives, applies HangPower. Live amount `n` gives an application of
`max(2,n)`, adjusted before application so the nominal sum does not exceed
999,999,999. A zero adjusted amount is rejected before Lamp, Artifact, or
PowerCmd application. Lamp can double a positive application, after which the
stored amount is capped. Existing Hang on the exact target owner multiplies
only damage whose physical CardModel source is Hang. It composes with all
existing additive and multiplicative modifiers before the single final floor.

Hang is fixed Type 2 and is cleared by ordinary death, Illusion revival,
segment reattach, Axebot replacement, minion cascade, and fresh-creature
construction. Axebot's simulator object reuse is guarded by captured creature
uid, so the post-attack Hang application cannot land on the replacement.
Duplicator replays re-read Block and Hang live while routing the one physical
card once. Manual play uses its explicit target and consumes no stream;
targeted AutoPlay consumes exactly one CombatTargets draw.

## Batch 76 Uproar recursive Draw AutoPlay (2026-07-21)

Batch 76 admits exactly `CARD.UPROAR` at both levels while preserving its raw
and composed `call CardPile::get_Cards` translator refusal as provenance.
Defect Common pool enumeration `0x29d5b0`, constructor `0x29bc33`, canonical
vars `0x29bc40`, upgrade `0x29bca7`, wrapper `0x29bc54`, and nested
`<OnPlay>d__3::MoveNext` `0x40f2e0` establish cost 2, AnyEnemy Attack,
Damage 6/8, and exactly two hits. After the attack it freshly reads Draw,
materializes every Attack without effective keyword 4 (`Unplayable`),
`StableShuffle`s the complete pool, and takes its first card. Only when that
pool is empty does it freshly materialize and independently StableShuffle all
Draw Attacks, including Unplayable. A selected card enters
`CardCmd.AutoPlay(choiceContext, card, null, type=1, false, false)`.

Each StableShuffle is exact `.NET List.Sort()` plus complete Fisher-Yates on
the run-lifetime Shuffle stream: `n-1` draws, including candidates not taken;
empty and singleton pools consume zero. The Draw pile itself is not shuffled.
The selected physical UID remains in its native Draw position through the
body and is routed only when AutoPlay completes. An Unplayable fallback takes
AutoPlay's unplayed-result route. Enemy-targeted children consume one
CombatTargets draw; Self/AllEnemies children do not. A child that opens a
modeled card selection suspends on the existing nested CardPlay continuation
and resumes before outer Uproar routing.

Uproar has no ending gate after its attack. A final-lethal attack still
materializes and StableShuffles the applicable complete pool; child AutoPlay's
own entry gate then no-ops and leaves the selected source in Draw. The native
pool does not exclude cards currently being played. Exact selection can
therefore choose the same active Uproar UID or create A-to-B-to-A and longer
cycles. The model preserves active cards in the candidate pool, performs the
exact native selection, and only then refuses an already-active UID. Distinct
recursive Uproars remain admitted and are finite because every child adds a
new active physical UID.

Manual actions and direct AutoPlay clone-preflight the complete recursive
command before caller-visible mutation or buffered log publication. Thus an
active-UID cycle or later child refusal cannot leak outer two-hit damage,
Shuffle/CombatTargets movement, piles, allocator, frames, or logs. Calculated
play counts above one refuse at both entry routes before spend, latch, target,
activation, or body work; generic dead-target replay remains #496.

Uproar joins `PRIOR_FIGHT_SHUFFLE_CARDS`, `TARGETS_CONSUMER_CARDS`, and the
modeled current-fight target-consumer inventory. Its unrecorded play consumes
pool-size-dependent Shuffle and can remove a Draw card; a null-target child
can consume CombatTargets. No CombatCardSelection inventory changes. Coverage
advances cards **434/162 -> 435/161** (Common **97/3 -> 98/2**) and total
accepted/refused **784/279 -> 785/278**. Every other category is unchanged.
#268, #368, #393, #485, #496, and #499 remain open and untouched. Authority:

returned after a generated-entry listener makes combat ending. Payload-equal
pre-existing Shivs are never inferred as return values.

## Batch 81 Enlightenment and Byrd Swoop (2026-07-22)

Batch 81 admits exactly `CARD.ENLIGHTENMENT` and `CARD.BYRD_SWOOP` at both
levels while preserving their raw and composed translator refusals as
provenance. Both are Event-rarity cards with maximum upgrade level 1 and no
multiplayer constraint.

Enlightenment constructor `0x28aa08` is a cost-0 Self Skill and canonical
keyword getter `0x28aa15` returns Exhaust. Its synchronous `OnPlay` at
`0x28aa20` obtains the owner's Hand pile and directly enumerates its live
`Cards` collection in pile order. It rechecks the source card's `IsUpgraded`
on every iteration. Level 0 calls `CardEnergyCost::SetThisTurnOrUntilPlayed`

ThisTurnOrUntilPlayed=6, true)`. Level 1 calls `SetThisCombat` `0x2ca07c`

the entire level difference. The body consumes no RNG and returns

Both setters append when the requested amount is nonzero, so Enlightenment
stores a physical row even on negative- and X-cost cards. `GetWithModifiers`
`0x2c9ea4` returns before local-row traversal for a negative base or
`CostsX`, leaving those rows inert. `LocalCostModifier::Modify` `0x2cb074`
applies a reduce-only Set as `min(current, amount)` in append order. Level-0
expiration 6 is removed by either end-turn flag 2 or after-play flag 4;
level-1 expiration 0 lasts for combat. Existing upgrade handling clamps Set
rows only when a new base is lower.

Manual play, draw-pile flip AutoPlay, and Sly have moved the source to Play
before the body, so the source is absent from Hand. Direct AutoPlay preserves
a non-null source pile through every body: a Hand source is included and a
Draw, Discard, or Exhaust source is excluded. Every replay re-enters the
body and enumerates the then-live Hand; rows are neither deduplicated nor
captured at action entry. A direct Hand level-0 source receives its row, then
loses it in AfterCardPlayed cleanup after routing to Exhaust. The level-1 row
survives on the exhausted source. Source-Exhaust listeners occur after the
body, so cards they draw do not retroactively receive a row. The private
`enlightenment_exact` handler commits one ordered Hand rewrite through the
physical-card layer, preserving UID, enchantment, local/transient keywords,
mutable enchantment state, damage growth, temporary Star rows, and opaque
tails while automatically promoting exact pile identity when a mutation
creates distinguishable native-sort ties.

Bullet Time constructor `0x2861f3` is a Silent Rare Self Skill, cost 3, with

other card receives `CardModel.SetToFreeThisTurn` `0x229839`. After the loop,

for a negative canonical Energy cost; otherwise it appends `(Set=1, 0,

ThisTurn=true, UntilPlayed=true)` through `AddTemporaryStarCost` `0x2298cb`
and `TemporaryCardCost.ThisTurn` `0x2cb463`, including on negative Energy and

receives neither row. Existing Energy/Star rows, UIDs, enchantments, local
and transient keywords, mutable enchantment state, supported damage growth,
and opaque tails are preserved.

Manual play, draw-flip AutoPlay, and Sly move Bullet Time to Play before its
body, excluding the source. Direct AutoPlay keeps its source in the source
pile, so a Hand source participates while Draw, Discard, and Exhaust sources
do not. Result routing occurs after the replay series; a direct-Hand source's
turn-or-play rows therefore append on every body and clear once after the
series. Glam, Duplicator, Burst, and eligible Echo re-enter the body, reread
the then-live Hand, append duplicate rows, and add another NoDraw stack.
NoDraw blocks ordinary owner draws, permits `fromHandDraw`, and its whole
instance is removed at owner `AfterSideTurnEnd` (`ShouldDraw` `0x250f32`,
removal body `0x388524`).

Enlightenment and Bullet Time compose by native append order. Enlightenment
then Bullet leaves Set-1 reduce-only before absolute Set-0; Bullet then
Enlightenment leaves Set-0 before a min-with-1 row. Both resolve to zero.
Level-0 rows share expiration 6 and clear together. Level-1 Enlightenment's
expiration-0 row survives Bullet's cleanup. Bullet's Energy-X skip preserves
an existing inert Enlightenment row without appending a Star row.

Runic Capacitor constructor `0x246c48` establishes Shop rarity and RepeatVar
3 (`0x246c4b`). Its sole hook is `AfterSideTurnStart`; body `0x3795a4`
requires the owner participant and `TurnNumber <= 1`, then calls
`OrbCmd.AddSlots(owner, 3)`. The shared primitive `0x2de42c` no-ops while
ending and clamps capacity to 10. The hook runs immediately before the
existing Infused Core dispatch. It preserves the queue, base capacity, and
all RNG streams, and does not itself enter the CombatTargets inventory.

Runic Capacitor commutes with Infused Core only on the proven empty base-3
queue when Cracked Core is absent: capacity ends at 6 with three Lightning
orbs in either acquisition order. On a base-0 character, Infused-first
bootstraps one slot and its later channels auto-evoke, while Runic-first makes
three slots before the channels; that composition refuses. With all three
relics on base 3, Cracked Core first places one Lightning during
`BeforeSideTurnStart`; then Infused-before-Runic overflows and auto-evokes,
while Runic-before-Infused expands first. Because relic acquisition order is
absent from the run record, base-0 Runic+Infused (with or without Cracked) and
the base-3 three-way composition refuse immediately after State construction
and before initial random-AI, room, or turn mutation. Runic joins the existing
unknown-character orb-slot gate because Defect base capacity 3 versus other
characters' 0 changes its result.

## Batch 83 Expertise (2026-07-22)

Batch 83 admits exactly `CARD.EXPERTISE` at levels 0 and 1 while preserving
the raw and composed translator refusal `call IEnumerable`1::GetEnumerator`
as source provenance. Expertise remains absent from both template `cards`
maps and every refusal-ledger section; the private hand registration takes
precedence only at composition time.

Expertise constructor `0x28b0fd` is a Silent Uncommon Self Skill, cost 1,
with maximum upgrade level 1. Canonical vars `0x28b10a` create CardsVar 2;
upgrade `0x28b163` adds one, yielding 3. The OnPlay state-machine body
`0x3e5ba4` issues one ordinary owner `CardPileCmd.Draw` with
`fromHandDraw=false`, awaits its exact returned `IEnumerable<CardModel>`, and
then synchronously enumerates those returned identities in order. Each gets
`CardCmd.ApplySingleTurnRetain` `0x2dbc94`; that method calls
`CardModel.GiveSingleTurnRetain` `0x2299b0`, then performs presentation-only
table/visual lookup. There is no card selection, target, or body-owned RNG.

The returned-object boundary is load-bearing. `DrawInternal` moves one card,
runs the complete AfterCardDrawn listener chain, and returns the resulting
physical identity/payload. If a listener ends combat, the completed current
card remains in the returned prefix while the next draw iteration is
suppressed. Expertise's post-await Retain loop has no ending gate, so it
still marks every identity in that prefix. A terminal state before Draw,
NoDraw/Fiddle refusal, zero hand capacity, or empty source returns an empty
sequence and marks nothing. The private `expertise_exact` handler therefore
uses the ordered `draw_cards` return, never the Hand tail, and resolves every
returned UID/payload exactly in the live Hand before one atomic transient-
keyword commit. Equal siblings remain distinct; Confused and other draw-time
physical mutations are preserved.

`CardModel.get_ShouldRetainThisTurn` `0x22919e` returns canonical Retain OR
the one-turn flag. `CardModel.EndOfTurnCleanup` `0x22a034` clears that flag,
along with one-turn Sly and turn-scoped costs, after the flush. The simulator
represents the flag as transient `Retain`: it participates in the existing
per-card flush predicate, survives through that flush, and is cleared across
all five piles by the existing cleanup. Canonical and permanent combat-local
Retain remain separate and survive the transient cleanup.

Every replay re-enters the full body, issues another single Draw of 2/3, and
marks only that command's returned identities. Manual play and gathered
AutoPlay sources have moved to Play; direct sources retain their ordinary
source-pile behavior, but Expertise never scans a source pile. Draw and
reshuffle behavior, including reentrant Gremlin Horn and terminal prefixes,
stays owned by the established draw engine.

Because an unrecorded prior-fight Expertise play can keep its returned cards
through one flush, it can change later draw-cycle membership and reshuffle
boundaries. `solve_fight.PRIOR_FIGHT_SHUFFLE_CARDS` therefore includes
`EXPERTISE`; the predicted run-lifetime Shuffle counter is surfaced as a
hypothesis rather than silently treated as exact.

Admission freezes both complete 29-field Card surfaces, each complete body,
active physical source UID, and the private vocabulary before observable
manual/AutoPlay work. Metadata drift, private-vocabulary reuse, body suffix,
payload/level/name mismatch, active UID mismatch, or missing returned UID
refuses instead of guessing. Raw/composed templates, censuses, ledgers, and
generic translation remain byte-identical.

796**, and refused **268 -> 267**. Every other category is unchanged. #268,

minions; ReattachPower admits only the last living Segment; ordinary powers,

deals 20/25, does not Exhaust, and gains 20/25 gold. Keyed `State.gold`

## Batch 92 shared AttackContext result pair (2026-07-23)

Batch 92 admits exactly `CARD.ECHOING_SLASH` and `CARD.OMNISLICE` from the
current v0.109.0 / `c12f634d` build (macOS arm64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`).
Their raw/composed parser refusal `call
AttackCommand::CreateContextAsync` remains unchanged as IL provenance.

Echoing Slash is a Silent Rare, cost-1 AllEnemies Attack
(`SilentCardPool::GenerateAllCards` `0x29e95c` IL `0x0112`; ctor
`0x28a708`). Canonical Damage is 10 and upgrade `0x28a77f` adds 3.
`<OnPlay>d__3::MoveNext` `0x3e4334` creates one AttackContext and seeds
`attackCount = 1`. Every pending count reads a fresh HittableEnemies set,
deals one props-8 powered/blockable batch, adds its results, and increments
the remaining count by the number of `WasTargetKilled` results (predicate
`0x3e432a`). Thus every kill schedules another complete AoE wave, including
after Stock replacement, Reattach, or spawn, while Vigor/Pen Nib and
AfterAttack remain one shared command lifecycle.

Omnislice is a Colorless Uncommon, cost-0 AnyEnemy Attack
(`ColorlessCardPool::GenerateAllCards` `0x29d14c` IL `0x0151`; ctor
`0x292ba3`). Canonical Damage is 8 and upgrade `0x292c17` adds 3.
`<OnPlay>d__3::MoveNext` `0x3f9154` creates one AttackContext, deals the
selected target one props-8 powered/blockable batch, and adds the results.
From `FirstOrDefault` it obtains the result receiver's teammates, excludes
the exact original CardPlay target, filters live/hittable creatures
(`0x3f914a`), and freezes that peer list. A nonempty list takes
`TotalDamage + OverkillDamage` as one props-12 blockable/unpowered batch
before those results are added and the context closes. The secondary damage
does not receive Strength or Vulnerable scaling; block and damage caps still
apply through the ordinary unpowered path. A reused Axebot object is excluded
even after it receives a fresh uid.

The engine keeps the batches fused behind one private exact-card allowlist,
retaining Vigor until the single close and deferring Skittish/AfterAttack
until every batch completes. Echoing Slash's untargeted replays create fresh
contexts. Omnislice is added to the existing manual and AutoPlay calculated
multiplay refusal sets, preserving protected #496 rather than guessing how a
dead fixed target continues. Neither card directly consumes RNG or changes
card-cycle/prior-fight Shuffle state.

Coverage advances cards **451/145 -> 453/143**, rare **102/57 -> 103/56**,
uncommon **161/69 -> 162/68**, and aggregate accepted **809/1063 ->

## Batch 94 Undeath and Summon Forth (2026-07-23)

Batch 94 admits exactly `CARD.UNDEATH` and `CARD.SUMMON_FORTH` from the
current v0.109.0 / `c12f634d` build (macOS arm64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`).
Their raw/composed parser refusals remain unchanged as durable provenance:
Undeath `call CardModel::CreateClone`; Summon Forth
`call Player::get_PlayerCombatState`.

Undeath is a cost-0 Necrobinder Rare Self Skill. Constructor/canonical vars/
upgrade are `0x29b6ff`/`0x29b70f`/`0x29b76f`: powered Block is 7/9. The
canonical-vars constant 8 following the decimal 7 is the `BlockVar` property
mask, not the Block value. Nested `<OnPlay>d__5::MoveNext` `0x40e53c`
awaits the Block command, clones the exact live physical source, and inserts
that generated clone at Discard=3, Bottom=1.

Every replay therefore blocks and generates one fresh-UID clone before the
original routes once. Enchantment state, ordered local-cost rows, local and
turn-transient keywords, and the complete physical tail are copied from the
source at that exact command point. `Glam::AfterCardPlayed` `0x281c1b` marks
the source used between bodies, so the first clone carries fresh `GLAM` and
later replay clones carry `GLAM_USED`. If Block-triggered Juggernaut damage
ends combat, CardGenerated history still advances while the generated-card
Add rejects insertion.

Summon Forth is a cost-1 Regent Uncommon Self Skill with Forge 8/11.
Constructor/vars/upgrade are `0x2996d4`/`0x2996e1`/`0x299757`. Nested
`<OnPlay>d__5::MoveNext` `0x4095e0` freezes the owner's AllCards Sovereign
Blades accepted by predicate `0x4095c6`, calls plural `CardPileCmd.Add` to
Draw=2, Bottom=1, and only then calls Forge. The predicate excludes exactly
blades already in Draw.

The frozen move order is Hand, Discard, Exhaust, Play: that sequence appends
after the untouched existing Draw prefix with no capacity redirect, then
every blade is forged by 8/11. A non-active gathered Play blade can move and
the current source's active Play index is remapped by UID; an active
Sovereign Blade is outside the representable safe surface and refuses before
mutation. Replays re-read the live piles: when the first body generates a
missing blade in Hand, the second moves it to Draw/Bottom and forges it
again.

Neither body consumes RNG. Undeath joins the prior-fight Shuffle caveat
because every play adds a Discard clone; Summon Forth remains in the complete
Forge-source caveat. Coverage advances cards **455/141 -> 457/139**, Rare

Juggling is a cost-1 Ironclad Uncommon Self Power; L1 adds Innate
(`.ctor`/upgrade `0x28fa00`/`0x28fa5b`). OnPlay applies one additive
JugglingPower. `AfterApplied` `0x2503f0` seeds its private
`attacksPlayedThisTurn` from owner Attack `CardPlayStarted` history for the
current turn. PowerCmd's stack path modifies Amount and skips AfterApplied,
so stacking never reseeds.

`JugglingPower/<AfterCardPlayed>d__7::MoveNext` `0x387170` owner/type-gates
to Attack, increments the private counter, and compares it to **exactly 3**
at `IL_0073–0079`. At 3 it loops Amount times: `CreateClone` at `IL_009b`,

fire; `AfterSideTurnEnd` `0x25046f` is the only counter reset. This corrects

The player card-pile listener set is captured before player powers run.
Therefore a newly inserted Juggling clone cannot receive the triggering
event's Banshee Cry/Pinpoint/card-pile callback; preexisting exact UIDs still

`AdaptiveStrike/<OnPlay>d__5::MoveNext` `0x3d2288` awaits its powered target
attack, clones the exact active source at `IL_00de`, applies
`EnergyCost.SetThisCombat(0, false)` to only that clone at `IL_00ec`, and
adds it through `AddGeneratedCardToCombat` at `IL_00fa` with Discard=3,
Bottom=1. Generic multi-play remains refused under #496.

Both generated-card calls share the exact wrapper chain:
