## Batch 112 / W214 — Ruined Helmet first positive Strength (#576)

Verified live build: **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**, macOS arm64 `sts2.dll`
SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.
The archived DLL is byte-identical.

`RuinedHelmet` owns one private `_usedThisCombat` boolean.
`TryModifyPowerAmountReceived` **0x246bbc** first copies the incoming amount
to its out parameter. It returns false unless the power is
`StrengthPower`, the recipient is the relic owner's creature, the incoming
amount is positive, and `UsedThisCombat` is false. On success it multiplies
the out amount by exactly 2 and returns true.
`AfterModifyingPowerAmountReceived` **0x246c1e** flashes and sets the latch
true; `AfterCombatEnd` **0x246c32** resets it false.

`Hook.ModifyPowerAmountReceived` **0x2b1d90** walks all combat-hook
listeners in native listener order, retaining exactly the listeners that
return true. The complete current-build override census contains only
Ruined Helmet, `ArtifactPower`, and mock-only `MockRevivePower`.
Artifact modifies only visible Type-2 debuffs; positive Strength is Type 1,
so it is disjoint. Mock Revive returns true only for its reviving owner but
does not change the amount and inherits the no-op callback. The peer order
therefore cannot change a positive owner Strength result or Ruined's latch.
`Hook.AfterModifyingPowerAmountReceived` **0x2b0274**, nested `MoveNext`
**0x41892c**, invokes callbacks only for the retained modifier list after
the power command has accepted the application.

The centralized owner-Strength helper preserves the generic PowerCmd
boundaries: ending combat and zero amount are no-ops; negative amounts pass
through and do not consume Ruined; the first accepted positive amount is
doubled and consumes the keyed latch. Ownership is immutable. The used
latch is mutable and auto-keyed. A fresh fight starts false, which represents
the native `AfterCombatEnd` reset without carrying a combat state across
fights.

Positive temporary Strength needs a separate representation note.
`TemporaryStrengthPower/<BeforeApplied>d__20::MoveNext` **0x392214**
issues a nested `Apply<StrengthPower>(Sign * amount)` at IL_004b.
`AfterPowerAmountChanged` **0x391f7c** applies each later stack delta the
same way. At owner side end, nested `MoveNext` **0x39209c** applies only
`-Sign * wrapper.Amount` before removing the wrapper. Thus, when Ruined
doubles the first inner +N, expiry removes only N and leaves N permanent.
The solver keeps the original N in `temp_strength` and stores only the
doubled excess in permanent `strength`. This covers Flex Potion, Reptile
Trinket, and Setup Strike/Feeding Frenzy through the same helper.

### Exhaustive direct owner-Strength write census

The frozen pre-change engine had exactly fourteen syntactic Strength
mutation sites relevant to this audit:

| Site | Native shape | W214 disposition |
|---|---|---|
| Rupture immediate | positive owner Apply | routed |
| Demon Form turn tick | positive owner Apply | routed |
| Brimstone owner half | positive owner Apply | routed; enemy half remains excluded |
| Strength Potion | positive owner Apply | routed |
| Fysh Oil owner Strength | positive owner Apply | routed |
| Shared Fate owner half | negative owner Apply | routed, never consumes |
| Dominate live Vulnerable amount | positive owner Apply | routed |
| generic card `strength` step | positive owner Apply | routed |
| Friendship owner half | negative owner Apply | routed, never consumes |
| Mini Regent | positive owner Apply | routed |
| Rupture completed-card batch | positive owner Apply | routed |
| Rainbow Ring | positive owner Apply | routed |
| Shuriken | positive owner Apply | routed |
| generic relic-template `power_self` | positive owner Apply | routed |

Philosopher's Stone and every other enemy `strength` write, death resets,
negative enemy temporary-strength removal, Red Skull's pure damage modifier,
and the three owner
`temp_strength` wrapper-storage sites are not direct owner StrengthPower
state writes. The latter three are nevertheless routed through the helper
for their native nested inner Apply. An AST guard pins that direct permanent
and temporary owner writes now occur only inside the helper and the existing
owner-side temporary expiry.

### Complete first-positive order audit

- **AfterRoomEntered:** Vajra +1, elite Sling of Courage +2, and Sword of
  Jade +3 are separate acquisition-ordered applications. With Ruined, any
  active pair has distinct amounts and therefore a different final result
  depending on which is doubled. Those exact compositions refuse atomically
  before a public State. A same-amount pair would commute because either
  order adds the same one extra time.
- **Potion use:** the potion's complete OnUse body precedes
  `AfterPotionUsed`. Strength Potion/Fysh Oil permanent Strength or Flex
  Potion's temporary inner Strength therefore deterministically consumes
  Ruined before Reptile Trinket. An ordinary potion lets Reptile consume it.
- **Card play:** Stars-spend relic callbacks complete before OnPlay; OnPlay
  bodies complete before AfterCardPlayed. Direct/temporary card Strength
  therefore precedes Rupture's completed-card batch, then player relics.
  Brand's blocking selection resumes and finishes its Strength body before
  the captured AfterCardPlayed sequence. No unrecorded order crosses these
  phase boundaries.
- **AfterCardPlayed relic group:** Rainbow Ring and Shuriken can both be the
  first positive applications on one play, but each amount is exactly +1.
  Either acquisition order produces +3 total and one consumed latch.
  Rupture is in the earlier player-power group, so a positive batch has
  deterministic precedence. Letter Opener, Lost Wisp, and Kusarigama can
  make an earlier acquisition-ordered unpowered damage command terminal.
  If a death replaces an enemy, enumeration continues and the Strength
  application still succeeds; on a final kill the skipped latch is
  immediately reset by native AfterCombatEnd and no future action observes
  it. Strength cannot modify those unpowered damage commands.
- **Turn and damage hooks:** Demon Form is in the player-power group before
  Brimstone's relic group. A continuing fight with Brimstone has already
  applied its first +2 on turn 1, so it cannot first collide with a later
  Demon tick. Rupture immediate, Mini Regent's Stars-spend hook, and
  Sparkling Rouge's turn-3 template are the sole positive sources in their
  respective captured events. Captain's Wheel/Horn Cleat block can likewise
  reach terminal unpowered Juggernaut damage before Sparkling Rouge only in
  the no-future-action case; a replacement keeps enumeration live. Existing
  Mini Regent/Galactic Dust and Brimstone/Sai/core refusals already cover
  their nonterminal replacement/order surfaces.

No remaining first-positive surface depends on an unrecorded order. Ruined
adds no RNG draw, choice, pile move, HP/max-HP change, heal ceiling term,
parser field, or prior-fight stream/shuffle requirement.

and upgrade-then-Ghost produce exactly the same immutable card payload,

physical-card payload slot 3. It preserves canonical keywords, transient
keywords, UID, level, history/tail slots, and pile ordering, and it is
idempotent when Ethereal is already effective from any layer.

Existing centralized effective-keyword consumers then observe Ghost Seed
without special cases: Free Ethereal/Veilpiercer cost modification, the

`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`;
the archive is byte-identical.

Throwing Axe stores one private `_usedThisCombat` boolean. Its getter/setter
are **0x248941/0x248949**. `AfterRoomEntered` **0x248958** returns outside a
CombatRoom; in combat it resets UsedThisCombat false and sets cosmetic status
1. `AfterCombatEnd` **0x2489b5** resets the same bit and cosmetic status.
Neither lifecycle hook consumes RNG or changes combat state beyond the
private latch.

`ModifyCardPlayCount` **0x24897b** returns the incoming count unchanged when
the latch is used or the played card's owner is not the relic owner.
Otherwise it returns `incoming + 1`. `AfterModifyingCardPlayCount`
**0x24899a** sets the latch true, flashes, and clears cosmetic status.
`Hook.ModifyCardPlayCount` **0x2b0f24** records exactly the listeners whose
return value changed; `CardModel.<GeneratePlayCount>d__340.MoveNext`
**0x3647e0** first computes `1 + GetEnchantedReplayCount`, folds the hook,
then dispatches `AfterModifyingCardPlayCount` only to that recorded set.
The effect is therefore one extra generated play for the owner's first
successful card action of each combat, including AutoPlay, and not for a
blocked AutoPlay that never enters play-count generation.

The simulator stores the inverse native bit as one mutable keyed
`throwing_axe_available` boolean, initialized only when the relic is owned.
Both manual and AutoPlay generation add its one before constructing the
shared CardPlay frame and consume it only after the existing replay-body
preflights pass. The complete current-build relic census for
`ModifyCardPlayCount` contains Throwing Axe alone.

Glam runs before the hook; Duplicator, Burst, One-Two Punch, Echo Form, and
Throwing Axe each contribute a constant one. Their arithmetic is additive,
and their callbacks consume independent latches or power stacks, so listener
order cannot change the count or resulting state. Existing calculated
replay-body refusals remain authoritative. In particular, unsupported
dead-target replay bodies and unverified Power bodies refuse loudly before
the Axe latch is consumed. The already exact Fan of Knives Power body accepts
the Axe contribution through the existing replay frame.

There is no parser field, persistent counter, RNG draw, target choice, pile
operation, or prior-fight provenance registry. Coverage advances accepted
**844/1063 -> 845/1063**, relic modeled/refused **258/42 -> 259/41**, and
aggregate modeled/refused **836/219 -> 837/218**. Certified remains **8**.

## Batch 120 / W222 — Vambrace exact card-block lifecycle (#592)

Verified live build: **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**, macOS arm64 `sts2.dll`
SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.

Vambrace resets `TriggeringCard=null` and `BlockGainedThisCombat=false` in
`BeforeCombatStart` **0x24997e**. Its
`ModifyBlockMultiplicative` **0x24999c** returns **2** only when the block
properties include CardOrMonsterMove, the card source is non-null and owned
by the relic owner, the once-per-combat latch is unused, and either no source
has yet been captured or the source is reference-equal to the captured
CardModel. Every other path returns **1**.

`Hook.ModifyBlock` **0x2b0d28** folds additive modifiers before
multiplicative modifiers and truncates only after the complete decimal fold.
Vambrace therefore composes as one exact multiplicative factor with the
admitted Frail, Unmovable, and Vitruvian Minion factors; Fasten remains in
the earlier additive phase. Native NoBlock, Shadowmeld, and Pael's Legion
compositions remain outside admission. The generic final-zero path is still
pinned not to capture or consume Vambrace.

A direct `Hook.ModifyBlock` preview receives the same factor but does not by
itself represent a completed GainBlock command. The simulator's preview
helper therefore remains state-pure and does not capture
`vambrace_trigger_uid`.

`AfterModifyingBlockAmount` **0x249a02** records the exact card source only
when Vambrace changed the modifier result and the final modified amount is
positive. This callback occurs before `GainBlockInternal`, block history, and
`AfterBlockGained`; a nested Juggernaut hit can therefore end combat only
after the source identity is captured. Multiple positive block commands from
that same CardModel remain doubled. A different physical card cannot use the
factor while the first source is pending.

`AfterCardPlayed` **0x249a3c** consumes the latch only for an owner CardPlay
whose exact CardModel is the captured source. The simulator represents this
with mutable keyed `vambrace_available` and
`vambrace_trigger_uid` (`-1` means no source captured). Existing immutable
`PhysicalCard.uid` identity survives pile moves, manual play, direct and
gathered AutoPlay, nested continuations, upgrades, and generated replay
iterations.

Consumption happens after the first completed qualifying iteration, so a
replay's later iterations receive ordinary block. If an outer card has
already captured the relic, a nested different UID cannot use or consume it;
if the nested card produces the first positive block, that inner UID captures
and consumes it before the outer resumes. Powered and unpowered
card-sourced block use the same lifecycle. Flat power/relic block has a null
card source and remains untouched.

Pael's Legion shares the native block-modifier family but remains an
unsupported relic and therefore refuses at combat entry before mutation.
Its independent CardPlay latch is not approximated. The raw
`call Vambrace::set_TriggeringCard` template refusal remains checked in as
translator provenance while the reviewed hand-model layer admits Vambrace.

The relic adds no legal action, parser seed, persistent cross-combat
counter, pile move, or RNG draw. Coverage advances accepted
**847/1063 -> 848/1063**, relic modeled/refused **261/39 -> 262/38**, and
aggregate modeled/refused **839/216 -> 840/215**. Certified remains **8**.
Full invariant walk:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-24-222-batch120-vambrace.md`.

## Batch 124 / W226 — bounded exact Apotheosis

Verified live build: **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**, macOS arm64 `sts2.dll`
SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.

`Apotheosis..ctor` **0x283d1f** supplies Energy cost 2, Skill, Ancient
rarity, Self target, and max upgrade 1. `get_CanonicalKeywords` **0x283d2c**
returns Exhaust and Innate. `OnUpgrade` **0x283dac** calls
`CardEnergyCost.UpgradeBy(-1)`, yielding L1 cost 1 with no body or keyword
change.

Synchronous `OnPlay` **0x283d44** obtains the owner's
`PlayerCombatState.AllCards`, directly enumerates it, reference-excludes
only this exact Apotheosis CardModel, checks each remaining card's
`IsUpgradable`, and calls `CardCmd.Upgrade(card, style=1)` once.
`PlayerCombatState.get_AllPiles` **0x2c3d74** fixes the order
Hand/Draw/Discard/Exhaust/Play. `get_AllCards` **0x2c3dc8** is a SelectMany
over those live piles; its lambda **0x4222f6** returns `CardPile.Cards`.

The single-card upgrade wrapper **0x2db473** enters the enumerable body
**0x2db484**. That body first returns on `CombatManager.IsEnding`, rechecks
`IsUpgradable`, then runs `CardModel.UpgradeInternal` **0x22a57c** and
`FinalizeUpgradeInternal` **0x22a5c0**. Cost-decreasing upgrades retain
`CardEnergyCost.UpgradeBy` **0x2ca17c** semantics: base cost clamps at zero
and local Set rows above the new base are lowered before finalize
**0x2ca224**. No target, choice, RNG, pile move, card generation, or
cardinality change occurs.

The simulator represents this as the private step
`upgrade_all_combat_except_source_exact`. Every current live card is
preflighted in native pile order, the source is excluded strictly by
immutable UID, and all five replacement tuples commit together. Upgrade
rewrites preserve UID, enchantment/keyword/mutable payloads, ordered cost
rows, supported damage growth, and opaque tails. Central commit performs the
existing exact-sort-tie promotion. The whole helper clone-runs first because
direct AutoPlay may be invoked below listener-local callers that do not have
`apply_action`'s transaction boundary. Logs publish only after commit.

Native source exclusion creates one important bounded refusal. If
Apotheosis AutoPlays while another CardPlay is active, native code upgrades
that outer source. The simulator may already have frozen level-dependent
continuation data. Two reachable examples are Sly Apotheosis discarded by
L0 Hidden Daggers before its generated-Shiv suffix and by L0 Storm of Steel
after its Shiv level has been frozen. The model therefore requires
`active_cards == (apotheosis_uid,)` before mutation. Manual play, direct
AutoPlay, gathered draw flips, automatic phase listeners, and replays remain
admitted because they have exactly one active CardPlay.

`RazorTooth.AfterCardPlayed` **0x2463bc** runs only after a completed owned
Attack/Skill body and upgrades that exact source. Apotheosis consequently
leaves itself L0 during the first body, Razor Tooth can make it L1, and a
later generated replay re-reads the L1 spec while executing the unchanged
all-pile body. The final result route exhausts the same live UID. Ending
suppresses the shared Upgrade command, Razor Tooth, later replay bodies, and
result-pile mutation at their established native gates.

`start_combat` now treats the private body as an upgrade source and validates
every deck card's remaining ladder before monster or RNG work.
`solve_fight._can_upgrade_card_before_play` likewise recognizes it so I3's
healing and max-HP ceilings include reachable upgrades. Apotheosis changes
no represented RNG stream or card count and does not join either prior-fight
Shuffle or Forge caveat inventory.

**464/132 -> 465/131**, Ancient modeled/refused **14/4 -> 15/3**, and
aggregate modeled/refused **843/212 -> 844/211**. Certified remains **8**.

no-op.

The simulator represents the frozen object list as immutable physical UIDs,
not frozen payload tuples. This matters when an earlier exhaust mutates a
later captured Midnight's local-cost rows: the later command must exhaust
the same live object with its updated payload. Manual play has already moved
Fiend Fire to Play, so the ordinary snapshot excludes it. Direct Hand
AutoPlay deliberately keeps its non-null source pile; in that native shape
the snapshot includes Fiend Fire itself, and the wrapper's later Exhaust
result command re-exhausts the same source after removing it from its current
Exhaust location.

No direct RNG is consumed. Manual targeting is fixed before the body; direct
AutoPlay uses the established single CombatTargets draw before the snapshot.
Indirect exhaust listeners retain their existing stream accounting and
fail-closed acquisition-order guards. Because an unrecorded prior-fight play
can remove an arbitrary whole-Hand snapshot from the live draw cycle,
`FIEND_FIRE` joins the conservative prior-fight Shuffle caveat inventory.

SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.

`AllEnemies`, and max upgrade 1. `get_CanonicalVars` **0x298e38** creates one
powered Damage variable with base 12. `OnUpgrade` **0x298e9f** adds 3 Damage,
yielding 15 without changing cost, type, target, or keywords.

`Stomp.OnPlay` **0x298e4c** enters
`Stomp.<OnPlay>d__3.MoveNext` **0x408344**. After its presentation-only Cast
animation and one `HittableEnemies` walk used only to spawn spike VFX, it
creates `DamageCmd.Attack(Damage.BaseValue)`, associates the exact Stomp via
`FromCard`, calls `TargetingAllOpponents`, attaches the Ironclad heavy attack
animation/effects, and executes the one powered command. There is no player
target, random target roll, status rider, generated card, pile selection, or
post-attack mutation. The private `stomp_exact` step preserves that complete
body while keeping the translator's raw
`call ICombatState::get_HittableEnemies` refusal as provenance.

The cost behavior belongs to the physical Stomp CardModel.
`BeforeCardPlayed` **0x298f0a** checks that the played card's owner matches
Stomp's owner and that its type is Attack, then calls `ReduceCostBy(1)`.
`ReduceCostBy` **0x298f45** calls
`CardEnergyCost.AddThisTurn(-amount, reduceOnly=false)`: an ordered relative
local-cost row with expiration flag 2. Every live Stomp listener in
Hand/Draw/Discard/Exhaust/Play receives one row for every generated
CardPlay iteration. The currently played Stomp has already spent its
pre-hook resolved cost, but its active Play instance receives the same row
for later turns after result routing.

`AfterCardEnteredCombat` **0x298eb8** first requires the entered card to be
this exact Stomp and returns immediately for a clone. A non-clone filters
`CombatHistory.CardPlaysFinished` to Attack cards played by Stomp's owner
whose entries `HappenedThisTurn`, counts them, and calls `ReduceCostBy(count)`.
The predicate lambda is **0x298f55**. The simulator uses its existing
`attack_plays_finished_this_turn` projection and appends one `-count`
ThisTurn row. Clones retain the source CardModel's already-copied ordered
rows but do not backfill history a second time.

Rows compose in native append order with Confused/Slither absolute Sets,
Touch of Insanity, Tangled, Borrowed Time, and Free Attack. The resolved
Energy cost remains floored at zero. Existing turn-end cleanup removes only
the flag-2 Stomp rows; ThisCombat and UntilPlayed rows survive according to
their own flags. STOMP joins the exact physical-cost/divergent identity
allowlists so independently entered or cloned equal copies cannot collapse
after their cost histories diverge.

Generated replays and direct AutoPlay run `BeforeCardPlayed` per CardPlay
iteration, so each reduces every captured live Stomp once. AutoPlay spends
no Energy and consumes no CombatTargets draw because the card's static target
is AllEnemies. The powered attack-all command reuses the established Strength,
Weak, Vulnerable, Vigor, Pen Nib, damage-result, and attack-history pipeline.

STOMP changes no pile cardinality, draw-cycle membership, Forge state, or RNG
counter beyond an ordinary Attack's natural result route. It therefore joins

## Batch 132 / #612 — Thrash exhaust-Attack preview and growth

Verified live build: **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**, macOS arm64 `sts2.dll`
SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.

`Thrash..ctor` **0x29aaf8** supplies Energy cost 1, Attack, Ironclad Rare,
`AnyEnemy`, and max upgrade 1. `get_CanonicalVars` **0x29ab12** creates
Damage 8 and a hit count of 2; `OnUpgrade` **0x29abb8** adds 2 Damage.

`Thrash.<OnPlay>d__9.MoveNext` **0x40c644** first awaits the powered
FromCard attack against its captured target. It then snapshots every live
Exhaust card whose type is Attack and calls
`RunState.Rng.CombatCardSelection.NextItem`. Empty snapshots consume no RNG;
nonempty snapshots consume one draw.

The selected card's variable lookup order is `CalculatedDamage`, `Damage`,
then `OstyDamage`. Its value is calculated with target null and passed to
`Hook.ModifyDamage` with target null, properties 8, flags 14, and the selected
physical card as source. Thus selected-card enchantment and relic additives,
player Strength, Accuracy/Phantom, Strike Dummy, Weak, Shrink, Vitruvian
Minion, and Pen Nib's exact source-latch branch participate. Enemy-owned
Vulnerable, Soar, Slow, caps, and Undying Sigil do not. Vigor was already
consumed by the preceding Thrash attack.

The returned Decimal is added to Thrash's current `Damage.BaseValue` and its
retained `_extraDamage`. Weak/Shrink can make that value fractional, so the
physical payload stores an exact nonnegative `Fraction`; upgrade and explicit
lower-level reconstruction preserve it. On a Pen Nib tenth attack, Thrash is
the active latch and the selected card does not double. When BeforeCardPlayed
advances an unlatching counter to nine, the selected non-Play card's preview
does double.

The simulator preflights every candidate's admitted damage-var shape before
identity allocation and before the selection draw. It admits reviewed exact
CalculatedDamage sources, exact retained physical Damage cards, one ordinary
integer Damage step, and a fixed static OstyDamage set. Perfected Strike and
other unsupported Attack shapes fail closed without consuming selection RNG.

Finally, `CardCmd.Exhaust` **0x4295fc** removes the selected UID from its
current Exhaust position, appends it to Exhaust/Bottom, records history, and
dispatches exhaust hooks. Selection and growth precede that command; its
combat-ending gate means a lethal initial attack still selects and grows but
does not re-exhaust. Dark Embrace and other admitted exhaust listeners see the
already-reappended exact card.

## Batch 134 / #374 — Hellraiser early-draw Strike AutoPlay

Verified live build: **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**, macOS arm64 `sts2.dll`,
SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.
Current-build `CardTag` metadata is `None=0, Strike=1, Defend=2, Minion=3,
OstyAttack=4, Shiv=5`; the old CW8 word “Infernal” was interpretation rot.

`Hellraiser..ctor` **0x28e5fc** supplies Energy cost 2, Power, Rare, Self,
and max upgrade 1. `OnUpgrade` **0x28e69f** reduces cost by one.
`Hellraiser.<OnPlay>d__3.MoveNext` **0x3ee098** applies one
`HellraiserPower`; the power is unique (`get_Type` **0x24f5f6**,
`get_StackType` **0x24f5f9**), so reapplication neither adds a second
listener nor resets its private recursion data.

`Hook.<AfterCardDrawn>d__11.MoveNext` **0x415614** creates one
`IterateCombatHookListeners` enumerator and awaits every
`AfterCardDrawnEarly` callback, then creates a separate fresh enumerator for
ordinary `AfterCardDrawn`. A full-DLL override scan finds Hellraiser is the
only Early listener. Its body
`HellraiserPower.<AfterCardDrawnEarly>d__7.MoveNext` **0x385778** first
requires the drawn card owner to match the power owner and
`card.Tags.Contains(1)`—CardTag.Strike. It then awaits
`CardCmd.AutoPlay(choiceContext, card, null, true, false, false)` on that
exact CardModel.

The exact physical card remains in Hand through direct AutoPlay and routes
once afterward. Immutable UID captures it across nested bodies; the modeled
`Data.autoPlayingCards` projection is a keyed UID stack across the await.
Pommel Strike and Minion Strike can synchronously draw another Strike, which
re-enters the Early listener before the outer card routes. Each targeted
AutoPlay rolls the live `CombatTargets` stream once and replays reuse that
fixed target. Ending/no-target/playability/result routing remains the shared
exact AutoPlay behavior.

`CardPileCmd.<DrawInternal>d__19.MoveNext` **0x42cfc8** checks initial free
Hand capacity at IL_0162–0195, awaits the complete hook, then recomputes
`MaxCardsInHand - hand.Count` at IL_03b4–03fa before the next requested
iteration. A Hellraiser-routed Strike therefore frees a live slot; the old
simulator-wide one-time clamp was not exact for this listener. The fresh
ordinary listener snapshot happens only after Early AutoPlay completes, and
is empty if that AutoPlay ended combat. Otherwise Confused and exact
card-instance listeners receive the same captured object even after it moved
to Discard, so simulator rewrites resolve by UID in the current live pile.

The power's internal infinite-HP guard reads whether **all** currently
hittable enemies have `HpDisplay.IsInfinite` (LINQ `All`, including true for
an empty set). In that state entries 1–9 AutoPlay. At entry 10 and later,
AutoPlay is skipped, the message latch is set, and
`infiniteAutoPlaysThisTurn` still increments. Any admitted Strike against a
non-all-infinite pool calls `ResetInfiniteAutoPlayData` **0x24f74c** before
AutoPlay. `AfterSideTurnEnd` **0x24f6b7** resets the same counter/latch when
the participants contain the owner. `BeforeAttack` reads the active-card set
only for VFX and has no combat-state effect.

Sculpting Strike is the sole modeled Strike whose AutoPlay can open a
blocking card selection. Correctly suspending the awaited Draw requires a
general keyed Draw frame that preserves arbitrary caller suffixes and exact
returned-card consumers. Hellraiser plus Sculpting Strike therefore refuses
before combat; the listener clone-preflight also rejects any dynamically
reached selecting Strike without committing its counter, UID latch, target
RNG, piles, or log. This is a bounded explicit I5 seam tracked in **#616**,
not an approximate AutoPlay. Infernal Blade's frozen current-build pool does
not contain Sculpting Strike and needs no extra refusal.

Hellraiser joins the current-fight CombatTargets provenance gate and
`solve_fight.PRIOR_FIGHT_SHUFFLE_CARDS`: unrecorded power/trigger timing and
recursive Strike draws can change exact cycle membership and every later
reshuffle boundary. It consumes no Shuffle row directly.

## Batch 135 / #618 — Stoke exact exhaust and generation

Verified live build: **v0.109.0 / c12f634d**, macOS arm64 `sts2.dll`,
SHA-256
`06c78d946ca70658e85abb28f6dc2ee0a023a4467faf0708ff542180fe5f4c82`.

`Stoke..ctor` **0x298dd3** supplies Energy cost 1, Ironclad Rare Skill,
Self target, no keywords, and max upgrade 1. The upgrade changes no displayed
card field; it upgrades the generated cards instead.
`Stoke.<OnPlay>d__1.MoveNext` **0x408078** triggers the cast animation, reads
pile enum value **2 = Hand**, materializes `Hand.Cards.ToList()`, and preserves
that list's original count. It serially awaits
`CardCmd.Exhaust(choiceContext, capturedCard, false, false)` for each exact
captured CardModel in Hand order. The source is already in Play for a manual
play and is absent; a direct Hand AutoPlay leaves the source in Hand and
therefore captures it.

After the serial exhaust loop, Stoke reads the owner character's unlocked
card pool and calls
`CardFactory.GetForCombat(owner, pool, originalCount,
CombatCardGeneration)`. `GetForCombat` **0x2be85c** filters once, then calls
`Rng.NextItem` exactly once per result **with replacement**, creating a fresh
level-0 CardModel each time. For a fully unlocked solo Ironclad, the fixed
native `GenerateAllCards` order produces 78 candidates. The 12 exclusions
are Basic Bash/Defend/Strike; Ancient Break/Corruption; MultiplayerOnly
Blaze/Demonic Shield/Midnight/Outrage/Tank; and Feed/Not Yet, whose
`CanBeGeneratedInCombat` is false. Every one of the 78 candidates is modeled
at both levels; Stoke itself was the final refused member.

`CardCmd.Upgrade(generatedList, false)` **0x2db484** before insertion. A live
combat upgrades the complete fresh list. That command checks
`CombatManager.IsEnding` before enumeration, so a terminal exhaust hook still

advanced by the original count.

`CardPileCmd.<AddGeneratedCardsToCombat>d__6.MoveNext` **0x42c464** applies
one outer in-progress/empty gate, then processes the generated list in order:
record `CardGenerated`, await Add to Hand/Bottom, and await

the live Hand capacity for every card and redirects a full-Hand item to
Discard/Bottom. Represented `AfterCardEnteredCombat` listeners mutate the
same fresh UID. No admitted content has a live
`AfterCardGeneratedForCombat` listener; active consumers remain refused.

The simulator clone-preflights the whole exact body before real exhaust or
RNG mutation. It freezes physical UIDs and the original count, uses the
shared serial exhaust-hook pipeline, consumes one generation draw per
original card, upgrades before insertion, and appends every generated UID in
native order. Reentrant Dark Embrace draws never join the frozen set.
If an exhaust hook ends combat, later Exhaust commands no-op, all original
generation draws still occur, and the ending-gated Upgrade plus generated
insertion/history both do nothing.

Admission shares Infernal Blade's explicit Ironclad owner, fully-unlocked
epoch proof, and exact nonnegative entering `CombatCardGeneration` counter.
Because its possible leaves include selection and target consumers, exact
`CombatCardSelection` and `CombatTargets` counters are also required before a
specific generated card is known. Stoke joins
`solve_fight.PRIOR_FIGHT_SHUFFLE_CARDS`.

## Batch 137 / #621, corrected by #1957 R34 — The Bomb instances

The original Batch 137 singleton interpretation below was superseded after a
fresh current-build audit. Authoritative build: **v0.111.0 / 41cef1ea**,
macOS arm64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`9cb4f1ad8c9f284aa8fec3122ffd6d780bbf543d875c817abdd12ff63fbf12b4`.

`TheBombPower.get_Type` RVA **0xa9ed7** returns Buff,
`get_StackType` **0xa9eda** returns Counter, and `get_InstanceType`
**0xa9edd** returns **Instanced**. Consequently
`PowerCmd.FindExistingInstanceForStacking` RVA **0x1338d8** finds no prior
Bomb for a new application. Every cast and replay creates an independent
Amount-3 power. `TheBomb.<OnPlay>d__4.MoveNext` RVA **0x3c2968** awaits that
Apply and only then writes private BombDamage 40/50 on the returned new
instance. Recasts neither add turns to an older Bomb nor overwrite its damage.

Every live Bomb is therefore represented as `(uid, turns, damage)` with a
monotonic `next_the_bomb_uid`. The ordinary BeforeSideTurnEnd acquisition
order is typed: `("hailstorm",)` for the singleton Hailstorm listener and
`("the_bomb", uid)` for each Bomb. This permits the native order Bomb A,
Hailstorm, Bomb B without aliasing instances. Each Bomb has exactly one token;
duplicate/orphan tokens, duplicate UIDs, invalid turns/damage, missing order,
unknown tokens, or active legacy `the_bomb`/`the_bomb_damage` scalar snapshots
fail closed. Only the unambiguous old Hailstorm-only fixture may normalize an
empty order.

The ordinary pass is entered only while combat is live. Once its listener
snapshot starts, later bodies are still entered after a terminal prefix.
Amount above one uses the ending-gated `PowerCmd.ModifyAmount`; a terminal
earlier listener therefore suppresses that decrement. At Amount one, the Bomb
freezes the ordered HittableEnemies roster, issues ordinary property-4
blockable unpowered owner damage, then directly removes only that instance and
its token. That direct removal still runs after terminal or an empty snapshot
and publishes no AfterPowerAmountChanged event. Captured targets dead when
reached are no-ops; replacements and newly appended targets are excluded.

Strength, temporary Strength, Weak, Vigor, Double Damage, and powered-card
modifiers never affect BombDamage. Monster block and Intangible do. Shared
damage handling retains block break, damage history, reactions, death cleanup,
and terminal ordering. Multiplayer and reentrant listener compositions remain
explicit refusals until their complete continuation order is represented.

Python and Rust now use the same instanced authority. Rust stores the dynamic
rows and typed order in the cold copy-on-write sidecar that already backed
`fetch_finished_uids`; `HotState` remains 224 bytes and `FanoutState` remains
312 bytes. Bomb-bearing card plays and turns are whole-action transactions, so
late replay, listener, damage, or lifecycle refusal restores state and events.
The corrected full invariant walk is
`solver/invariant-walks/2026-09-02-issue1957-the-bomb-r34.md`; the old
`2026-07-26-01-batch137-the-bomb.md` is retained only as superseded history.

## Batch 138 / #624 — Purity ordered optional serial Exhaust

Verified live build: **v0.109.1 / c8c577f6**. The mandatory #625 impact gate,
merged in **#627**, proved Purity's complete managed type and CIL body
byte-identical to archived v0.109.0. The v0.109.1 `sts2.dll` SHA-256 is
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`.

`Purity..ctor` **0x294817** supplies Energy cost 0, Colorless Uncommon Skill,
Self target, Retain and Exhaust, with max upgrade 1. `CanonicalKeywords`
**0x294824** and `CanonicalVars` **0x294839** expose those keywords and Cards
3. `OnUpgrade` **0x294893** adds two only to Cards, producing 5.

`Purity.<OnPlay>d__5.MoveNext` **0x3fd608** awaits
`CardSelectCmd.FromHand` **0x430944** with MinSelect 0 and MaxSelect Cards.
The returned `IEnumerable<CardModel>` preserves the player's selection order.
The body enumerates it once and serially awaits
`CardCmd.Exhaust` **0x4295fc** for each exact returned object. An empty Hand
auto-returns the empty selection; a nonempty Hand opens a real modal that
permits empty through the level-specific maximum.

The simulator normalizes the replay-local live Hand to exact physical
identities and stores immutable UID+payload candidates in
`State.pending`. Legal actions enumerate every ordered 0..3/5 sequence,
including empty and physically distinct payload-equal siblings. The pending
candidate order, active CardPlay UID, card metadata/body, count, duplicate
status, selected UID/payload, and exact live Hand membership are all
fail-closed. The complete selection and serial hook suffix clone-preflight
before the real successor mutates or logs.

Each selected card leaves the live Hand immediately before its own shared
Exhaust pipeline. Dark Embrace, Feel No Pain, Charon's Ashes, Forgotten Soul,
Burning Sticks, Drum of Battle, and the rest of the established exact-card
listeners therefore observe native source removal and selection order. Every
Exhaust command independently checks combat ending: a terminal first hook
leaves later selected cards in Hand. The playing Purity then uses ordinary
result routing, so a terminal body leaves its exact source in Play.

Every manual replay and direct AutoPlay body creates a fresh live Hand
snapshot. A first replay's exhausted cards and reentrant hook effects are
therefore visible to the next replay rather than inherited from the earlier
modal. Direct Hand AutoPlay includes its still-resident source among the
native candidates. If selected, the body exhausts that exact source and its
ordinary result epilogue then locates it in Exhaust, removes it, and exhausts
it again: the pile retains one physical copy while listeners observe both
native Exhaust commands.

Purity consumes no RNG directly. Its unrecorded prior-fight play and selected
physical cards change cycle membership, so it joins the conservative
prior-fight Shuffle caveat inventory.

## Batch 139 / #629 — Bolas and Thrumming Hatchet exact prior-turn self-return

Verified live build: **v0.109.1 / c8c577f6**. The v0.109.1 `sts2.dll`
SHA-256 is
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`;
the mandatory #625/#627 impact gate proved no relevant managed delta from
archived v0.109.0.

`Bolas..ctor` **0x285715** and canonical vars **0x285722** supply Energy
cost 0, Colorless Rare Attack, AnyEnemy, and Damage 3. `OnUpgrade`
**0x2857db** adds 1. Its OnPlay body **0x3d7184** is an ordinary powered
single-target attack. `ThrummingHatchet..ctor` **0x29abd0** and canonical
vars **0x29abdd** supply Energy cost 1, Colorless Uncommon Attack, AnyEnemy,
and Damage 11. `OnUpgrade` **0x29ac93** adds 3. Its OnPlay body
**0x40ca6c** is the same ordinary powered single-target shape.

The two cards share the exact BeforeHandDraw contract. Their entries
**0x285790** / **0x29ac48** and state-machine bodies **0x3d7064** /
**0x40c94c** require a completed play of that same `CardModel` during the
immediately previous owner turn. If the card is already in Hand the hook is a
no-op; otherwise it awaits `CardPileCmd.Add` on that exact object at Hand
Bottom. This is physical pile movement, not generation: no new `CardModel`
is constructed and no generated-card stream advances. The original #228
route was therefore a false positive; the shared BeforeHandDraw dependency
was #268.

The simulator projects only the completed-play UIDs for these two card IDs
into immutable current-owner-turn and previous-owner-turn tuples. Beginning
an owner turn rolls current to previous and freezes the relevant physical
card listeners in native `AllPiles` order: Hand, Draw, Discard, Exhaust,
Play. Frozen listeners run after the established power/relic
BeforeHandDraw work and before hand draw. A card removed by an earlier
listener is skipped; a card already in Hand does nothing; and the combat
ending gate suppresses the nested Add. A full Hand redirects to Discard
Bottom, including remove-then-append reordering when the source was already
in Discard.

Successful movement dispatches the explicit `AfterCardChangedPiles`
boundary. The complete admitted listener census there—Lucky Fysh,
Darkstone Periapt, and Bing Bong—requires destination Deck, so all
Hand/Discard destinations in this batch are inert. Snapshot continuation is
preserved across Foregone Conclusion's pending selection. Clone and memo
keys include both history tuples and the frozen listener order; while any is
active, equal-payload legal play/exhaust choices retain physical UID so the
search cannot merge the card that owns prior-turn history with its sibling.

Neither body nor hook consumes RNG. Both IDs join
`PRIOR_FIGHT_SHUFFLE_CARDS`: an unrecorded play and next-turn return can
change subsequent flush and reshuffle membership/order.

## Neow blessing option generation (EVENT.NEOW) — #626, v0.109.1

IL read 2026-07-26 against the live v0.109.1 install (byte-identical in IL to
the archived v0.109.0; the 145 differing bytes are all build identity).
Modeled in `versions/v0.111.0/solver/neow.py`, certified against the real engine by
`versions/v0.111.0/solver/harness/probe_neow.py`.

### The stream is NOT player:Rewards

`EventModel.Rng` is a **dedicated per-event Rng**, built in
`EventModel/<BeginEvent>d__28::MoveNext` (RVA 0x366380):

```
Rng = new Rng(RunState.Rng.Seed
              + (IsShared ? 0 : RunState.GetPlayerSlotIndex(Owner))
              + StringHelper.GetDeterministicHashCode(Id.Entry))
```

- `StringHelper::GetDeterministicHashCode` (0x2b6ba8) = `XxHash64.HashToUInt64`
  over UTF-8, seed 0 — the same v0.109 hash `sts2_rng.py` already models.
- `EventModel::get_IsShared` (0x22c1b9) returns false; Neow does not override
  it, so the slot index is always added.
- `Rng::.ctor(ulong)` (0x61b81) seeds MegaRandom directly — **counter 0**.
- `ModelId.Entry` for `EVENT.NEOW` is the literal `"NEOW"` (verified against
  the engine: the probe reads it back off the model).

So the offered blessings are fully determined by the run seed + slot alone,
independent of anything consumed earlier in the run.

### Option pools

`Neow::get_CurseOptions` (0x276250) — 10, in array order: CursedPearl,
DowsingRod, HeftyTablet, LargeCapsule, LeafyPoultice, NeowsBones,
NeowsSacrifice, PrecariousShears, SilkenTress, SilverCrucible.

`Neow::get_PositiveOptions` (0x2760bc) — 14, in array order: ArcaneScroll,
BoomingConch, FishingRod, GoldenPearl, Kaleidoscope, LeadPaperweight,
LostCoffer, MassiveScroll, NeowsTorment, NewLeaf, PhialHolster,
PreciseScissors, ScrollBoxes, WingedBoots.

Six singleton getters (0x2761e4–0x27623e) supply the coin-flip pairs:
LavaRock/SmallCapsule, NutritiousOyster/StoneHumidifier, NeowsTalisman/
Pomander. `get_AllPossibleOptions` (0x276044) is the union — display/census
only; generation never calls it.

Array order is load-bearing: `UnstableShuffle` permutes this exact list.

### Neow::GenerateInitialOptions (0x2766e0)

```
if (Owner.RunState.Modifiers.Count > 0) -> modifier path (IL_0248), no RNG
curses = CurseOptions.ToList();  curses.RemoveAll(!IsAllowedAtNeow)   // b__35_0
curse = Rng.NextItem(curses)                                          // 1 draw
positives = PositiveOptions.ToList()
  curse is CursedPearl      -> remove GoldenPearl                     // b__35_1
  curse is HeftyTablet      -> remove ArcaneScroll                    // b__35_2
  curse is LeafyPoultice    -> remove NewLeaf                         // b__35_3
  curse is PrecariousShears -> remove PreciseScissors                 // b__35_4
  curse is NeowsSacrifice   -> remove PhialHolster AND LostCoffer     // b__35_5, b__35_6
if (curse is NOT LargeCapsule)                                        // IL_0184
    positives.Add(NextBool() ? LavaRock : SmallCapsule)               // 1 draw
positives.Add(NextBool() ? NutritiousOyster : StoneHumidifier)        // 1 draw
positives.Add(NextBool() ? NeowsTalisman   : Pomander)                // 1 draw
positives.RemoveAll(!IsAllowedAtNeow)                                 // b__35_7
return positives.UnstableShuffle(Rng).Take(2) + [curse]               // len-1 draws
```

Two details that are easy to get wrong:

- **b__35_6 is inside the NeowsSacrifice branch** (`brfalse.s` at IL_0136
  targets IL_0184, past both RemoveAlls), so LostCoffer is struck only by
  NeowsSacrifice — not unconditionally.
- **A LargeCapsule curse skips the Lava Rock / Small Capsule flip entirely**,
  costing one fewer draw *and* one fewer pool entry. Both shift every
  subsequent draw.

`Rng::NextBool` (0x61c13) is `_random.Next(2) == 0` — true on **zero**.
`Rng::NextItem` (0x61f80) is one `NextInt(0, count)`.
`ListExtensions::UnstableShuffle` (0x2bf170) is a full backward Fisher-Yates
over the whole list (`n-1` draws) *before* `Take(2)` — the discarded tail
still costs draws.

### IsAllowedAtNeow gates

`RelicModel::IsAllowed` (0x2309e4) is `return true`; `IsAllowedAtNeow`
(0x2309e7) forwards to it. Only five pool members deviate:

| relic | gate |
|---|---|
| SilverCrucible (0x24794d), WingedBoots (0x24a372) | `Players.Count == 1` |
| MassiveScroll (0x242b2e) | `Players.Count > 1` |
| Kaleidoscope (0x241858) | base && `UnlockState.CharacterCardPools.Count == AllCharacters.Count` |
| ScrollBoxes (0x246e96) | `CanGenerateBundles(player)` && base |

`UnlockState::get_Characters` (0x114b0) starts from the five
`ModelDb::get_AllCharacters` (0x22d276) entries and removes any whose
`Silent1/Regent1/Necrobinder1/Defect1` epoch is not revealed;
`UnlockState::IsEpochRevealed` (0x118cf) is plain set membership on the
save's `unlocked_epochs`, so Kaleidoscope is decidable from a save.

`ScrollBoxes::CanGenerateBundles` (0x246ef0) needs the character's
epoch-filtered, multiplayer-constrained card pool to hold **>= 4 rarity-2 and
>= 2 rarity-3** cards. That pool is not in the save and reconstructing it
needs the full per-character card table (#138 census), so per I5
`versions/v0.111.0/solver/neow.py` **refuses** unless the caller states the verdict.

### Certification

`versions/v0.111.0/solver/harness/probe_neow.py` drives the real `GenerateInitialOptions` in
sts2.dll v0.109.1. Fixture: `versions/v0.111.0/solver/testdata/neow_options_v109.json`, 52
seeds, all 10 curses represented. `versions/v0.111.0/solver/neow.py` reproduces **all 52
option triples and all 52 draw counts exactly**.

Live-game corroboration: capture `2026-07-26/084144.724_save_6ccd86c1.save`
(seed `LPTMBBTY7FQY`) predicts NewLeaf / Kaleidoscope / **LargeCapsule**; the
follow-up save `085337.192_save_8b453cf1.save` from the same seed, taken
after Neow, shows the player holding `RELIC.LARGE_CAPSULE`. Engine, solver,
and live game agree.

For that account the engine reports `ScrollBoxes.IsAllowedAtNeow = True` and
`Kaleidoscope.IsAllowedAtNeow = True`.

## Batch 140 / #646 — Seeker Strike exact Draw shortlist

IL read 2026-07-26 against v0.109.1/c8c577f6
(`sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`).
The mandatory #625/#627 impact gate found the managed body byte-identical to
archived v0.109.0/c12f634d.

`SeekerStrike` constructor/tags/vars/upgrade are
`0x29675c/0x296769/0x296778/0x2967f3`; its generated `OnPlay` body is
`<OnPlay>d__5::MoveNext` at `0x402980`. It is a Colorless Uncommon
AnyEnemy Strike Attack costing 1. L0/L1 Damage is 9/12; `Cards` remains 3.

The body order is exact:

1. await one ordinary powered attack against the captured CardPlay target;
2. copy the complete live Draw pile with `ToList`;
3. `StableShuffle` that copy with `RunRngSet.CombatCardSelection`;
4. `Take(Cards)` from the shuffled copy;
5. call `CardSelectCmd.FromCombatPile` for exactly one Draw card whose
   **object identity** occurs in that shortlist;
6. await `CardPileCmd.Add` of the returned exact object to Hand/Bottom.

`StableShuffle` first sorts the copy by `CardModel.CompareTo` (ID then
upgrade through the repository's exact .NET 9 port), then runs a complete
backward Fisher-Yates. A Draw pile of size `n` therefore consumes
`max(0,n-1)` CombatCardSelection draws even though only three shuffled
objects are retained. The shortlist decides membership only:
`FromCombatPile` enumerates the still-live Draw pile, so player options keep
live Draw order restricted to those exact physical UIDs rather than shuffled
order. Empty and singleton candidate sets auto-resolve; larger sets suspend
the CardPlay through the standard exact-selection frame.

The selected object moves to Hand Bottom. A full Hand redirects it to
Discard Bottom through the established `CardPileCmd.Add` rule. If the attack
kills the final enemy, native code still completes `ToList`, full
`StableShuffle`, and `Take`; `FromCombatPile` then returns empty at its
ending gate and the later Add moves nothing. A replay performs the whole
attack/shuffle/select body again against the then-live Draw pile. If an
earlier replay kills its fixed target while another enemy survives, the
generic loud #496 boundary remains in force.

Direct AutoPlay uses the same resumable CardPlay frame and exactly-once
result routing. Hellraiser + Seeker Strike remains refused under #616:
Hellraiser's early draw hook awaits an AutoPlay which can itself block on
this selection, requiring the still-unimplemented general resumable Draw
caller/return frame.

Seeker Strike already belongs to `CARDSEL_CONSUMER_CARDS` and now joins
`PRIOR_FIGHT_SHUFFLE_CARDS`. A current fight requires an exact entering
CombatCardSelection counter. Prior-fight deck presence makes that counter
unknown and also makes later draw-cycle membership/Shuffle boundaries
unreconstructible because `.run` records neither the play nor chosen object.

Coverage advances accepted **868/1063 -> 869/1063**, card modeled/refused
**481/115 -> 482/114**, Uncommon modeled/refused
**176/54 -> 177/53**, and aggregate modeled/refused
**860/195 -> 861/194**. Certified remains **8**.
Full invariant walk:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-26-05-batch140-seeker-strike.md`.

## Batch 141 / #659 — Catastrophe live Draw AutoPlay loop

IL read 2026-07-26 against v0.109.1/c8c577f6
(`sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`).
The mandatory #625/#627 impact gate found every managed body byte-identical
to archived v0.109.0/c12f634d.

`Catastrophe` constructor/vars/upgrade are
`0x286c2b/0x286c38/0x286c93`; the async wrapper is `0x286c48` and
`<OnPlay>d__3::MoveNext` is `0x3da908`. It is a Colorless Uncommon Self
Skill costing 2 with no keywords. `Cards` starts at 2 and upgrade adds one.
Predicate `<OnPlay>b__3_0` (`0x3da8f6`) is exactly
`!card.Keywords.Contains(Unplayable)`.

Every loop iteration performs this exact sequence:

1. freshly resolve the owner's live Draw pile;
2. copy only cards whose current effective keywords exclude Unplayable;
3. `StableShuffle` the entire copy on `RunRngSet.Shuffle`;
4. take `FirstOrDefault`;
5. only when that result is null, freshly resolve Draw again, copy every
   card including Unplayable, independently `StableShuffle` that complete
   fallback on the same advancing stream, and take `FirstOrDefault`;
6. if non-null, await `CardCmd.AutoPlay` with null target and default flags;
7. increment the cursor and re-read this exact source's live
   `DynamicVars.Cards.IntValue` for the continuation test.

Both StableShuffles use the established exact .NET 9
`CardModel.CompareTo` sort followed by complete backward Fisher-Yates.
A nonempty preferred pool of size `n` consumes `n-1` Shuffle draws. An empty
preferred pool performs a real zero-draw shuffle before the fresh fallback;
fallback size `m` then consumes `m-1`. Empty Draw still executes both
zero-draw shuffles and completes one iteration. Neither copy reorders Draw.

The repeat bound is deliberately **not frozen at body entry**. An AutoPlayed
Apotheosis can upgrade the resolving physical L0 Catastrophe between awaited
iterations, changing the next live bound read from 2 to 3. The simulator's
resumable frame is bounded by the current-build maximum of three but consults
the exact active source level before its optional third slot. W226's former
blanket nested-Apotheosis refusal is relaxed only for the structurally exact
three-frame stack: outer Catastrophe CardPlay, its keyed live-loop frame, and
inner Apotheosis CardPlay. Every other or malformed nested stack still
refuses before mutation.

The selected exact physical UID remains in its live Draw source throughout
direct AutoPlay, then follows ordinary exactly-once result routing.
Enemy-targeted children roll one CombatTargets draw through the existing
null-target AutoPlay path; other child bodies retain their already-audited
stream and pending-selection behavior. A child selection suspends above the
live-loop frame. On resume the child completes first, then the next iteration
freshly re-reads Draw; no selected/frozen batch is carried across the await.
Manual play, repeated bodies, and direct AutoPlay all use this same keyed
continuation.

Catastrophe has no outer combat-ending gate. A child that makes combat ending
finishes the already-entered command according to normal command gates; every
remaining outer iteration still copies, sorts, and shuffles live Draw. A
non-null pick still calls AutoPlay, whose own leading IsOverOrEnding gate
then no-ops and leaves that card in Draw.

Direct AutoPlay can leave an active Catastrophe physically in Draw. While
combat is live, native selection can therefore pick that same UID or form a
longer A→B→A cycle. The model preserves the exact pool/sort/shuffle/pick
first, then refuses the active UID rather than pretending the unbounded
recursive chain terminates. After combat is ending, the same pick reaches
AutoPlay's leading ending gate and harmlessly no-ops instead.

Catastrophe joins current/prior CombatTargets consumer inventories and
`PRIOR_FIGHT_SHUFFLE_CARDS`. A current fight requires an exact entering
CombatTargets counter because an ordinary AnyEnemy child now rolls. In a
prior fight, omitted play timing, variable live pool sizes, child effects,
and the Apotheosis extension make later Shuffle positions and draw-cycle
membership unreconstructible.

Coverage advances accepted **869/1063 -> 870/1063**, card modeled/refused
**482/114 -> 483/113**, Uncommon modeled/refused
**177/53 -> 178/52**, and aggregate modeled/refused
**861/194 -> 862/193**. Certified remains **8**.
Full invariant walk:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-26-07-batch141-catastrophe.md`.

## Batch 142 / #661 — Beat Down frozen Discard AutoPlay batch

IL read 2026-07-27 against v0.109.1/c8c577f6
(`sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`).
The #625/#627 impact gate found every managed body byte-identical to archived
v0.109.0/c12f634d.

`BeatDown` constructor/vars/async wrapper/upgrade are
`0x284acf/0x284adc/0x284aec/0x284b37`; filter lambda
`<OnPlay>b__3_0` is `0x3d4dea`, and `<OnPlay>d__3::MoveNext` is
`0x3d4e08`. It is a cost-3 Colorless Rare RandomEnemy Skill with no
keywords. `Cards` is 3 and upgrade adds one.

Before the first await, the body performs this exact sequence:

1. resolve the owner's live Discard pile;
2. filter exactly `Type == Attack && !Keywords.Contains(Unplayable)`;
3. materialize that complete physical-card list;
4. `StableShuffle` it on `RunRngSet.Shuffle`;
5. read the source's current `Cards.IntValue` once and freeze `Take(3/4)`.

`StableShuffle` (`0x2bf130`) copies and sorts the full list, then calls
`UnstableShuffle` (`0x2bf170`), a complete backward Fisher-Yates. A filtered
pool of size `n` consumes `max(n-1, 0)` Shuffle draws even when only its
first three or four entries execute. `CardModel.CompareTo` (`0x22a884`)
delegates ID ordering through `AbstractModel.CompareTo` (`0x22631a`) and
`ModelId.CompareTo` (`0x22dc8c`): category and entry use
`StringComparison.Ordinal`, then current upgrade level is compared. Full
ties retain the repository's exact .NET 9 introsort behavior.

The enumerator freezes object references and order, not every later field of
each object. Before each child the simulator locates that UID in every live
pile and uses its current payload, so an earlier child upgrade or move is
visible. If an earlier transform removed the captured object entirely, the
immutable `(uid, frozen payload)` continuation recreates the still-held
native object reference with no guessed replacement. The frame cursor,
entries, flags, and source are immutable and keyed; a blocking child
CardPlay stays above it and completes before the next frozen entry.

For each captured object, native code first checks
`CombatManager.IsOverOrEnding` (`MoveNext` IL_00b6-00c0). Ending therefore
does not suppress the initial full Shuffle, but a child that ends combat
suppresses every remaining child, including its target read. Otherwise the
body re-reads that child's live `TargetType`. Exactly `AnyEnemy` consumes
one `CombatTargets.NextItem` over the then-live hittable enemies and passes
that explicit target to `CardCmd.AutoPlay`; every other target type passes
null.

`CardCmd.AutoPlay` wrapper/body are `0x2db204/0x428908`. Its AnyEnemy branch
rolls only when the supplied target is null (IL_023c-0305), so Beat Down's
explicit target prevents a duplicate draw. The entire AutoPlay and nested
`OnPlayWrapper` are awaited serially, preserving selections, replays,
result routing, and nested Catastrophe/Uproar/Beat Down LIFO order.

Issue #496 remains explicitly out of scope. Before committing a frozen
iteration, the simulator projects every additive AutoPlay play-count source.
An AnyEnemy child with calculated count greater than one refuses
transactionally because generic fixed-dead-target replay retention is not
yet modeled. Active-UID recursion likewise refuses instead of approximating
an unbounded native cycle.

No approximate leaf fallback is admitted. `start_combat` rejects every
unmodeled deck card before pile/RNG setup, while the two broad admitted
random card pools (Infernal Blade's Attacks and Stoke's solo Ironclad pool)
validate every reachable level against `CARDS`. All other admitted generation
uses fixed modeled identities.

Beat Down joins current/prior CombatTargets inventories and
`PRIOR_FIGHT_SHUFFLE_CARDS`. A current fight requires an exact entering
CombatTargets counter. A prior unrecorded Beat Down play makes later Shuffle
positions and cycle membership hypotheses because `.run` omits its pool,
order, target choices, and nested child effects.

**483/113 -> 484/112**, Rare **113/46 -> 114/45**, and aggregate

`Rend` constructor/canonical-vars/upgrade are
`0x2957ad/0x2957bc/0x295873`; `ShouldCountPower` is `0x2958a1`,
the multiplier lambda is `0x4000c2`, and `<OnPlay>d__5::MoveNext` is
`0x4000f8`. Contrary to #623's stale "Uncommon" description, the current
constructor and coverage census both identify a cost-2 **Colorless Rare**
AnyEnemy Attack with no keywords. Damage is `15 + 5*n`; upgrade adds three
to both variables, yielding `18 + 8*n`.

At command construction time the body re-reads the selected target's live
`Powers` collection and counts actual instances satisfying both:

1. `GetTypeForCurrentAmount() == 2`;
2. the object does not implement `ITemporaryPower`.

The checked `target_power_census.json` records every represented
enemy-owned or player-applied-to-enemy power family, its current-build RVAs,
amount/sign/removal rules, stack/instance type, temporary status, and exact
simulator projection. The 12 counted singleton predicates are:

- aggregate `StrengthPower` iff `strength < 0`;
- Weak, Vulnerable, Hang, Poison, Doom, Oblivion, Shrink, and Conqueror iff
  the corresponding modeled amount is positive;
- Shriek iff the Terror Eel's `shriek` instance remains;
- Slow for every live Bygone Effigy, including when its separate private
  `slow` cards-played counter is zero;
- Imbalanced for every live Bowlbug Rock.

Amount is never cardinality: Weak 1 and Weak 999 are each one
`PowerModel` instance. `OblivionPower` is native InstancePerApplier, but the
admitted solo surface has exactly one player applier and therefore one
instance; the focused structural pin fails if another admitted writer
appears.

All six represented negative temporary-Strength wrappers—Mangle, Dark
Shackles, Enfeebling Touch, Crush Under, Dying Star, and Piercing
Wail—derive `TemporaryStrengthPower` and implement `ITemporaryPower`, so
their outer instances never count. Their internally applied ordinary
StrengthPower is the shared aggregate singleton above and counts only while
its total amount is negative. Artifact, Burrowed, Galvanic, Hardened Shell,
Hard to Kill, Illusion, Infested, Intangible, Minion, Paper Cuts, Personal
Hive, Plating, Reattach, Ritual, Skittish, Slumber, Soar, Stock, Territorial,
Thorns, Vigor, and Vital Spark are current Type 1 and do not count.

The central projection fails closed on a new encounter/spawn kind, invalid
amount/boolean state, non-live target, or invalid native discriminator. Its
literal kind inventory is pinned to every current encounter builder plus
every registered mid-fight loop kind. All projection inputs are already
`Monster.key()` fields or immutable kind identity, so clone/memo identity
remains exact.

Rend uses the ordinary powered card-damage path after calculating its live
base. Strength, Weak, Vulnerable, block, relics, and attack-result listeners
therefore retain their established order. A duplicated play re-runs the
projection: an Envenom-applied PoisonPower after the first hit increases the
second body's count. A fixed target that dies/replaces before another replay
still refuses transactionally at the generic #496 boundary.

Rend consumes no RNG itself. Manual AnyEnemy choice is explicit; null-target
AutoPlay targeting remains attributed to the established outer auto-player
consumer. No new prior-fight stream inventory entry is required.

Coverage advances accepted **871/1063 -> 872/1063**, cards
**484/112 -> 485/111**, Rare **114/45 -> 115/44**, and aggregate
modeled/refused **863/192 -> 864/191**. Certified remains **8**.

`invariant-walks/2026-07-27-02-batch143-rend.md`.

## Batch 144 / #666 — Jackpot, Calamity, and Discovery generation

IL read 2026-07-27 against v0.109.1/c8c577f6
(`sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`).

### Jackpot

`Jackpot` constructor/vars/filter/body/upgrade are
`0x28f8c7/0x28f8d4/0x3f1300/0x3f132c/0x28f94f`. It is a cost-3 Colorless
Rare AnyEnemy Attack. The body first performs one ordinary powered attack
for 25, then calls `GetForCombat` for three cards from the owner's unlocked
pool filtered to non-null `EnergyCost`, canonical integer zero, and
`CostsX == false`. Upgrade adds five Damage and upgrades every fresh
generated card once.

In current solo fully-unlocked Ironclad native order, the exact predicate
projection is:

`ANGER, BATTLE_TRANCE, BLOODLETTING, BRAND, BULLY, OFFERING, PACTS_END,
PRIMAL_FORCE, RAGE, SPITE`.

`GetForCombat` samples with replacement, so Jackpot consumes exactly three
CombatCardGeneration `NextInt(10)` draws. Duplicate identities are legal.
The attack completes before any generation draw, even when it ends combat.
The complete three-card list is created before serial generated insertion;
Jackpot+ cards are L1, but neither level applies a free-cost modifier.

### Calamity

`Calamity` constructor/body/upgrade are
`0x28680c/0x3d9e10/0x286867`. It is a Colorless Rare Self Power costing
3/2 and applies one additive `CalamityPower`.

`CalamityPower` type/stack metadata are `0x24c36b/0x24c36e`.
`BeforeCardPlayed` `0x24c378` owner- and Attack-gates, then stores the
power's current Amount against that exact `CardModel`.
`AfterCardPlayed` wrapper/body `0x24c3d8/0x37fea0` removes that exact key but
uses the `Remove` out value only as discarded storage. When membership was
present, IL_00b2 freshly reads the power's live `Amount` and passes that to
`GetForCombat` on the same 33-card fully-unlocked Ironclad Attack pool frozen
for Infernal Blade. Sampling is with replacement; every result is a fresh
L0 card with no free-cost modifier.

The exact-card mark is frozen independently for every repeated Attack body,
while the generation count is the current AfterCardPlayed Amount. Calamity
generation is dispatched on the player-power AfterCardPlayed layer. When
Calamity and Juggling would both generate on one Attack, or another
same-event player-power command can end combat before generated insertion,
the simulator refuses before mutation because power acquisition order is
not recorded and changes observable hand order/history. Nonterminal,
disjoint listeners retain the established exact layer order.

### Discovery

`Discovery` constructor/keywords/body/upgrade are
`0x289c62/0x289c6f/0x3e24cc/0x289cc3`; `MockSelectedCard` is
`0x289ccc`. It is a cost-1 Colorless Uncommon Self Skill. L0 has Exhaust;
upgrade removes Exhaust and changes nothing else.

The body calls `GetDistinctForCombat` for three cards from the complete
78-card fully-unlocked solo Ironclad pool frozen for Stoke. Native
`UnstableShuffle` performs a full 78-card shuffle, consuming exactly 77
CombatCardGeneration draws, then exposes the first three distinct fresh L0
cards through `FromChooseACardScreen`. Only the selected option receives
`SetToFreeThisTurn`; only that option emits generated history and enters
Hand/Bottom (or Discard/Bottom when Hand is full).

The v0.111.0 / 41cef1ea correction was re-read against `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`9cb4f1ad8c9f284aa8fec3122ffd6d780bbf543d875c817abdd12ff63fbf12b4`.
Discovery's `MoveNext` at **0x399254** passes `canSkip=true` at
**IL_0096–0097**. Its result-null branch at **IL_0102–0103** jumps to
**IL_016f**, bypassing free-cost mutation, card creation, generated history,
listener dispatch, and pile insertion. The full 78-card shuffle has already
consumed all 77 Generation draws before the screen appears. The nullable
fourth action still resumes the ordinary play wrapper, including Exhaust or
Discard routing and serial replay bodies.

The blocking choice is represented by an identity-keyed pending
`CardPlayFrame`. Replays create one screen at a time: the first choice and
play epilogue complete before the next body consumes its independent
77-draw shuffle. Forged, stale, malformed, or wrong-source options refuse
atomically. The private `_mockSelectedCard` branch has no caller in the
installed assembly; it remains an external test seam and is not silently
used by normal combat.

### Shared insertion, provenance, and coverage

`CardPileCmd.AddGeneratedCardsToCombat` body `0x42c464` emits
`History.CardGenerated` before each individual Add, but only after the
command's leading InProgress gate. Jackpot uses one list command: if it
entered live and an earlier generated-entry listener ends combat, later list
history can still advance while later individual Adds no-op. Calamity awaits
one singular command per card and therefore repeats the leading gate;
Discovery also uses one singular command. If combat is already ending before
any of these commands begins, generation RNG may already have advanced but
history and insertion remain zero. Fresh physical UIDs, listener rewrites,
strike accounting, clone keys, and full-Hand redirects all use the shared
exact generated-entry path.

All three cards require a known fully-unlocked solo Ironclad pool and a
known CombatCardGeneration counter. Calamity and Discovery additionally
require exact CombatCardSelection and CombatTargets entry counters because
their reachable generated leaves span the full 33/78-card pools. Jackpot's
ten-card leaf pool does not consume either stream. All three remain in the
prior-fight generated-source inventory because `.run` omits generation
results, play timing, and generated child effects.

Coverage advances accepted **872/1063 -> 875/1063**, cards
**485/111 -> 488/108**, Rare **115/44 -> 117/42**, Uncommon
**178/52 -> 179/51**, and aggregate modeled/refused
**864/191 -> 867/188**. Certified remains **8**.
