`invariant-walks/2026-07-27-03-batch144-generation.md`.

## Batch 144 tools / #667 — Splash character-pool census

Read and probed 2026-07-27 against v0.109.1/c8c577f6
(`sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`).
The local headless-engine oracle `harness/probe_card_pools.py` booted
`ModelDb` and recorded the checked `card_pool_census.json`; ordinary tests
never load the game DLL.

`UnlockState.CharacterCardPools` **0x115d4** projects the unlocked
characters' card pools in character order. The fully unlocked order is
Ironclad, Silent, Regent, Necrobinder, Defect. Their raw
`GenerateAllCards` arrays are respectively **90/91/91/91/91** entries at
**0x29dc04/0x29e95c/0x29e544/0x29e0cc/0x29d5b0**. Per-row unlock epochs are
attested by replaying each pool's `FilterThroughEpochs`
(**0x29df3c/0x29ec9c/0x29e884/0x29e40c/0x29d8f0**) at each cumulative
character epoch. `CardPoolModel.GetUnlockedCards` **0x22aa00** retains list
order while applying those epochs and the run's
`CardMultiplayerConstraint`.

`Splash.<OnPlay>d__2::MoveNext` **0x407284** materializes
`CharacterCardPools`. Only when `Count > 1` does it remove the owner's
`CardPool`; this is a load-bearing edge, not an unconditional removal. It
then `SelectMany`s each remaining pool's `GetUnlockedCards` result, filters
`CardType.Attack` in lambda **0x407276**, and calls
`CardFactory.GetDistinctForCombat(..., 3, CombatCardGeneration)`.
`FilterForPlayerCount` **0x2be490** removes MultiplayerOnly cards for a
single-player run. `FilterForCombat` **0x2be8be** then requires
`CanBeGeneratedInCombat` and rejects Basic, Ancient, and Event rarities
before `Distinct`.

For a fully unlocked solo Ironclad, owner removal leaves a complete ordered
pool of **112** eligible Attacks: Silent 23, Regent 29, Necrobinder 32,
Defect 28. `GetDistinctForCombat` therefore performs one complete
Fisher-Yates and consumes exactly **111 CombatCardGeneration draws** before
taking three options. At the #667 base, 103 leaves are modeled and nine are
refused: Strangle (#383), Debilitate (#333), Misery (#670), Sic Em (#672),
The Scythe (#673), Flak Cannon (#668), Go for the Eyes (#669), Rocket Punch
(#336/#368), and Scrape (#671). The Hunt is explicitly absent because its
`CanBeGeneratedInCombat` override **0x29a7b9** returns false.

The oracle also found exactly two pre-existing type disagreements with
`cards_census.json`: live The Scythe is Attack while that constructor scan
says Skill, and live Genetic Algorithm is Skill while the scan says Attack.
Both are pinned and routed to the separate census-parser correction #674;
the #667 artifact is not changed to agree with known-bad older output.

With only one unlocked character pool, Splash skips `Remove(owner)` and
retains Ironclad. The same filters then produce the exact 33-card Infernal
Blade Attack pool and consume **32** draws, rather than producing an empty
option list. Both orderings, every pool row, exclusions, routes, build hash,
and the generator itself are SHA-attested by `test_card_pool_census.py`.

This track changes no solver mechanic or admission contract and does not
model Splash, so it uses no invariant-walk file. It supplies the checked
artifact and durable blocker graph required by the later serialized Splash
implementation.

## Batch 145 tools / #678 — Alchemize potion pool, RNG, and belt census

Read and probed 2026-07-27 against v0.109.1/c8c577f6
(`sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`).
The local headless-engine oracle
`harness/probe_potion_generation.py` records the checked
`potion_pool_census.json`; ordinary tests consume only that JSON and never
load the game DLL.

`Alchemize.<OnPlay>d__5::MoveNext` **0x3d2a48** gets the owner's
`RunRngSet.CombatPotionGeneration`, calls
`PotionFactory.CreateRandomPotionInCombat(player, rng, null)`, makes the
result mutable, and awaits `PotionCmd.TryToProcure(..., slotIndex: -1)`.
Constructor/upgrade **0x2839cc/0x283a27** establish cost 1/0; both levels
Exhaust. The body does not pre-check belt capacity, so a full belt still
consumes generation RNG before procurement fails.

`PotionFactory.GetPotionOptions` **0x2bef46** concatenates the owner's
`PotionPool.GetUnlockedPotions` result followed by
`SharedPotionPool.GetUnlockedPotions`. `CreateRandomPotionInCombat`
**0x2bee68** then filters live
`PotionModel.CanBeGeneratedInCombat` through lambda **0x42020b**.
`CreateRandomPotions` **0x2beeb8** materializes that order, consumes
`Rng.NextFloat(1)` (**0x61d5f**) for rarity, and selects from the matching
stable-order partition with `Rng.NextItem` (**0x61f80**). The float32
comparisons are Rare `<= 0.10000000149011612`, Uncommon
`<= 0.3499999940395355`, otherwise Common. `NextItem` consumes one
`NextInt(0,n)` for every nonempty partition, so each Alchemize body advances
the named stream exactly twice. Removal in `CreateRandomPotions` prevents
duplicates only within one multi-result call; separate Alchemize plays can
repeat a potion.

The checked fully unlocked solo-Ironclad order is three Ironclad potions
followed by 45 Shared potions. Only Fairy in a Bottle, Fruit Juice, and
Regen Potion return `CanBeGeneratedInCombat=false`, leaving **45 reachable
options**, not the scout's initial 39. Their exact partitions are Common 16,
Uncommon 15, and Rare 14. The live sweep also corrected the initial refused
leaf count from nine to **eleven**: it additionally reaches Mazaleth's Gift
(#256) and Powdered Demise (#681). The remaining routes are Attack,
Colorless, Orobic Acid, Power, and Skill potions (#228), Bottled Potential
(#231), Gigantification (#252), Soldiers' Stew (#677), and Entropic Brew
(#680). Every reachable refusal must carry one of these durable routes or
the probe aborts.

`PotionCmd.<TryToProcure>d__1::MoveNext` **0x438850** invokes
`Hook.ShouldProcurePotion` **0x2b2918** before calling
`Player.AddPotionInternal` **0x2c35fc**. A negative slot requests
`List.IndexOf(null)`, i.e. the first empty slot. The live A0 probe began at
`[null, Strength Potion, null]`, inserted Weak Potion at slot 0, inserted
Speed Potion at slot 2, then returned `TooFull` without mutation on a fourth
potion. Capacity is not universal: entry evidence must preserve the actual
`max_potion_slot_count`.

Successful insertion alone appends a `ModelChoiceHistoryEntry(id, true)` when
the current map-history entry exists and then runs
`Hook.AfterPotionProcured` **0x41952c**. The current override inventory is
exactly Sozu's pre-insert veto **0x247daf** and Belt Buckle's post-success
hook **0x23ca7c**; the latter removes its empty-belt Dexterity after the first
successful insert. Full-belt and Sozu paths do not run success history or the
post hook, but the already-completed two RNG draws remain spent.

The implementation blocker is representational, not a missing list.
Save-backed entries already carry exact `max_potion_slot_count`, each held
potion's `slot_index`, and the `combat_potion_generation` counter. The
solver adapters currently collapse slots into dense `State.potions` and
constant `State.inert_potions`; `.run` history records IDs used/discarded but
cannot reconstruct the resulting holes. #679 therefore owns a keyed
fixed-length slot tuple (including null and modeled/inert identity), the
named stream, save/MCR slot propagation, Belt Buckle/Sozu behavior, and the
I3 potion-bank re-audit. A run-history-only Alchemize entry must refuse
unless exact slot topology is separately proven.

This #678 track changes no solver mechanic or admission contract and does
not model Alchemize, so it intentionally has no invariant-walk file. Its
deliverable is a build/SHA-attested oracle artifact, DLL-free agreement
tests, corrected blocker graph, and the fail-closed #679 implementation
contract.

## Batch 145 / #677 — Hidden Gem and Soldier's Stew BaseReplayCount

IL read 2026-07-27 against v0.109.1/c8c577f6
(`sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`).

### Shared physical replay state

`CardModel.BaseReplayCount` getter/setter are `0x228e81/0x228e89`.
`GetEnchantedReplayCount` `0x228ea8` first reads that base value and then
passes it through the card's enchantment, when present. `GeneratePlayCount`
wrapper/body `0x22a434/0x3647e0` starts at
`GetEnchantedReplayCount + 1`, folds the ordinary
`ModifyCardPlayCount` listeners, and creates that many serial `CardPlay`
bodies. Energy/Star spend and final result-pile routing remain outside the
body loop; body hooks and `CardPlayFinished` occur once per generated play.

The simulator stores nonnegative `BaseReplayCount` as the optional sixth
member of the existing keyed slot-7 `PHYSICAL_CARD_STATE`. It is additive,
physical-UID-specific, and survives pile moves, upgrades, local Energy and
Star-cost rows, damage growth, enchantments, cloning, memo keys, and opaque
tail payloads. Every play-count consumer—including manual play, direct
AutoPlay, preview, replay guards, and Drum of Battle—reads base plus the
existing Glam/Spiral enchantment contribution.

Base replay applies to every card type. For Powers, it is the native generic
`GeneratePlayCount` source and therefore serially repeats every registered
Power body; it composes with Duplicator, Echo Form, and Throwing Axe.
Enchantment replay keeps its older source-specific allowlists because those
enchantments have separate mutable lifecycle rules. A forged Power carrying
both base and fresh enchantment replay refuses atomically; neither admitted
source can create that combination.

The exhaustive closure sweep exposed #683: `CARD.DEMON_FORM` was already
template-admitted as `("demon_form", 3/4)` but lacked its application
dispatch. Current-build ctor/vars/body/upgrade are
`0x28986d/0x28989c/0x3e1ab8/0x2898fb`.
`<OnPlay>d__5::MoveNext` reads
`DynamicVars["StrengthPower"].BaseValue` and applies additive
`DemonFormPower` to the owner. The new minimal dispatch adds that amount to
the already-keyed `demon_form` field; the established turn-start listener
continues to convert it into Strength.

### Hidden Gem

Hidden Gem ctor/vars/body/predicates/upgrade are
`0x28e93b/0x28e94b/0x3ee9a8/0x3ee93c/0x3ee984/0x28e9bb`.
It is a cost-1 Colorless Rare Self Skill and grants base replay 2/3.

The body copies the live Draw pile after its animation. Empty Draw returns
before selection RNG. The first predicate rejects effective Unplayable,
native card types 5 and 6, and
`GetEnchantedReplayCount >= 1`. In this build the checked census maps types
5/6 to **Curse/Quest**, not Status/Curse as #677 originally said. Status is
type 4 and is the intentional fallback shape. The second predicate keeps
types 1..3 (Attack/Skill/Power); that preferred subset is used when nonempty,
otherwise all eligible Status cards remain.

`CombatCardSelection.NextItem` consumes exactly one draw for every nonempty
final pool, including a singleton, in live Draw order. The chosen exact
physical UID receives the additive base grant and the pile becomes
identity-sensitive. Fresh Glam, Spiral, and any existing positive base
replay are ineligible; spent Glam contributes zero and can be selected
without losing its enchantment payload.

### Soldier's Stew

Soldier's Stew TargetType/OnUse/predicate are
`0x259429/0x259440/0x399a9a`. TargetType 5 accepts the selected player in
the solo model. OnUse snapshots `PlayerCombatState.AllCards`, whose native
order is Hand, Draw, Discard, Exhaust, Play; `Where(...).ToList()` freezes
the exact identities before mutation. The predicate reads canonical
`CardModel.Tags.Contains(CardTag.Strike)`, then each matching physical card
increments `BaseReplayCount` once. No RNG stream is read.

Hand registrations now derive canonical `Tags.Strike` from their existing
checked `strike_tag` projection, preventing the damage-hook and potion views
from diverging. Duplicate payloads remain separate physical UIDs. Existing
base replay is incremented, enchantment state is preserved, and a no-match
use returns before identity promotion. Potion-belt removal retains slot
order; Belt Buckle and other established post-use hooks run only after the
complete synchronous body.

### Provenance and coverage

Hidden Gem joins the current/prior CombatCardSelection and prior draw-cycle
inventories. Soldier's Stew joins the modeled potion set and prior
draw-cycle inventory: `.run` records a prior use but not which exact
in-fight Strike instances later replayed or how those bodies changed cycle
timing.

Coverage advances accepted **875/1063 -> 877/1063**, cards
**488/108 -> 489/107**, Rare **117/42 -> 118/41**, potions
**49/15 -> 50/14**, and aggregate modeled/refused
**867/188 -> 869/186**. Certified remains **8**.

`invariant-walks/2026-07-27-04-batch145-hidden-gem-stew.md`.

## Batch 147 / #413 — Entropy exact turn-start Transform

IL re-read 2026-07-27 against v0.109.1/c8c577f6
(`sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`).
The installed and archived ARM64 DLLs matched this digest.

Entropy ctor/upgrade **0x28ab69/0x28abe3** establish a cost-1 Colorless Rare
Self Power, Cards 1; the upgrade adds only Innate. OnPlay wrapper/body
**0x28ab98/0x3e5064** applies one additive `EntropyPower` to the owner.
`EntropyPower` Type/StackType **0x24e163/0x24e166** are both Intensity, so
reapplications add to one listener amount without moving it in power order.

`EntropyPower.<AfterPlayerTurnStart>d__6::MoveNext` **0x383418** first
owner-gates, constructs `CardSelectorPrefs(TransformSelectionPrompt, Amount)`,
and awaits `CardSelectCmd.FromHand(..., this)`. Current
`FromHand` **0x430944** returns empty before enumeration when combat is ending,
uses the live Hand in pile order with no filter, and auto-returns the complete
Hand when `RequireManualConfirmation == false` and `count <= MinSelect`.
Here MinSelect == MaxSelect == Amount. A larger Hand exposes a blocking,
ordered, exactly-Amount selection. The resulting list is materialized once,
then each exact object is serially passed to
`CardCmd.TransformToRandom(card, CombatCardSelection, style=1)`.

The simulator freezes `(physical UID, payload, Hand order)` after the ordinary
turn-start draw and every earlier admitted player-power listener. A blocking
selection joins the memo key with full pile identity. Resolution transforms
the chosen ordered UIDs, then resumes at the later
AfterPlayerTurnStart relic listeners; it never repeats hand draw, Loop,
Rolling Boulder, or SummonNextTurn and never skips the Late, Side, orb, or
AutoPre suffix. Loop, Rolling Boulder, SummonNextTurn, Inferno, Crimson
Mantle, Tools of the Trade, and Tyranny share this hook in first-application
order and can win/lose before Transform's ending gate. R39 replaces the old
split-family guard with one lossless eight-token order in both canonical state
and the compact engine. Hibernate remains outside that native order behind its
symmetric coexistence wall.

`TransformToRandom` wrapper/body **0x2db65c/0x42a5dc** creates one
`CardTransformation`, calls `CardCmd.Transform(..., rng, style=1)`, and
returns the first replacement. `CardTransformation.GetReplacement`
**0x2caecc** delegates to
`CardFactory.CreateRandomCardForTransform` **0x2be95c**. The factory obtains
`GetDefaultTransformationOptions` **0x2be8ec**, consumes exactly one
`CombatCardSelection.NextItem` for every nonempty pool, and creates a fresh
canonical L0 object in the original scope. No upgrade, enchantment, keyword,
local cost, replay, growth, or opaque physical payload survives. Current
`CardModel.get_IsTransformable` **0x229290** is
`IsRemovable || Pile.Type != Deck`; every live Hand card is therefore
transformable, including Eternal cards.

`GetFilteredTransformationOptions` **0x2be9bc** keeps
Common/Uncommon/Rare unless the original rarity is Token or Status, applies
`CanBeGeneratedInCombat` in combat, excludes the original ModelId, applies
the solo player-count filter, and preserves pool order. Basic and ordinary
Ironclad originals use the 78-entry Ironclad pool already shared with Stoke.
Colorless, Quest, Ancient, Curse, and Event originals use the exact
50-entry Colorless pool. Status originals use the exact 10-entry Status pool;
Token originals use the exact 10-entry Token pool. These lists require
explicit fully-unlocked solo-Ironclad provenance. R39 closes the complete
owner-aware replacement graph to a fixed point before choice or RNG. That
includes Ironclad -> Primal Force -> Giant Rock -> Token -> Soul and Colorless
-> Splash -> the matching owner Attack/generator recursion. Rolling Boulder is
an admitted replacement because its first application now appends to the same
authoritative order.

`CardCmd.Transform` wrapper/body **0x2db7b4/0x4299d8** captures the original
pile/index, obtains the replacement, removes the old object, then inserts the
fresh object at that exact index. It records `CardGenerated`, dispatches
`AfterCardEnteredCombat`, `AfterCardChangedPiles`, add-finished and transform
callbacks, then `AfterCardGeneratedForCombat`, and removes the old object from
combat state. The simulator allocates a fresh immutable UID, updates
Supermassive's generated history and Perfected Strike's live Strike count,
applies Phantom Blades to a generated Shiv, and runs the established generic
entry-state helper. The admitted changed-pile listeners require Deck and are
inert for a replacement whose live pile is Hand. The replacement is then
dispatched through the admitted `AfterCardGeneratedForCombat` power walk before
the detached original's combat-state row is removed. A generated callback that
ends combat publishes that completed singular transform and suppresses every
later selected card and Sel draw.

R39 re-read this contract against v0.111.0 / current arm64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`9cb4f1ad8c9f284aa8fec3122ffd6d780bbf543d875c817abdd12ff63fbf12b4`.
The transform-callback census contains exactly
`SovereignBlade.AfterTransformedFrom` at RVA **0xec060**; its only effect is

## Batch 149 / #333 — outgoing multiplier and enemy-debuff seam

IL re-read 2026-07-27 against v0.109.1/c8c577f6
(`sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`).

Debilitate ctor/vars/upgrade are **0x288ee3/0x288f2a/0x288fab**.
Its nested OnPlay body **0x3e0674** awaits the Attack first, then applies
DebilitatePower to the same CardPlay target. L0/L1 are cost 1, damage 10/12,
and duration 2/3. DebilitatePower Type/StackType
**0x24d641/0x24d644** are Debuff/Intensity. Its vulnerable listener
**0x24d682** owner/target/powered-gates and maps the current multiplier
`x -> x + (x - 1)`. Its weak listener **0x24d6aa** owner/dealer/powered-gates
and maps `x -> x - (1 - x)`. Both are presence-gated; Amount is duration, not
multiplier magnitude. The side-end body **0x382194** decrements at the
monster owner's enemy-side end.

Knockdown ctor/vars/upgrade are **0x28fd4b/0x28fd5b/0x28fddb**.
Its nested OnPlay body **0x3f1d34** likewise awaits the Attack, then applies
KnockdownPower. L0/L1 cost 3, deal 10/14, and apply multiplier 2/3.
KnockdownPower Type/StackType/InstanceType
**0x2504d9/0x2504dc/0x2504df** are Debuff/Intensity/1. PowerCmd's
FindExisting switch **0x2dedf0** creates no existing match for InstanceType
1, so every successful application is a distinct listener. Its multiplier
body **0x250548** requires the powered target to be the owner, returns one
when dealer equals that listener's Applier, and otherwise returns Amount.
Every instance removes itself at its owner's side end through
**0x3872f8**.

Knockdown is `MultiplayerOnly` at getter **0x28fd58**. The exact represented
route has one player owner and that player's Osty: card applications store
only the owning player as Applier, while damage distinguishes player from
Osty dealer. Thus the owner is exempt from its own Knockdown and Osty is not.
Arbitrary teammate-applier identities are outside the represented state and
fail closed; admission does not claim a general multiplayer simulation.

Tracking ctor/upgrade are **0x29b0cf/0x29b147** and its nested OnPlay body is
**0x40d3f4**. It is a Self Rare Power, cost 2/1, applying 50
TrackingPower. Type/StackType **0x2561b3/0x2561b6** are
Intensity/Intensity. Its multiplicative listener **0x2561dc** requires
powered damage, a non-null source card, dealer equal to the owner or one of
the owner's pets, and WeakPower on the target; it returns
`1 + Amount / 100`. Reapplications add to the one persistent listener.

Current VulnerablePower **0x256c94** walks Paper Phrog, dealer/PetOwner
Cruelty, then target Debilitate. Current WeakPower **0x256e00** walks Paper
Krane, then dealer Debilitate. Hook.ModifyDamageInternal **0x2b2b98** runs
the additive walk, then the multiplicative walk, then caps, without an
intermediate integer conversion. The solver therefore carries all three
new factors as exact Fractions through the existing one-final-truncation
damage pipeline. Unpowered damage bypasses all three.

Both enemy powers use the established card-sourced Unsettling Lamp then
Artifact application seam. Lamp doubles one successful application;
Artifact blocks the entire visible Type-2 application and spends one stack
without latching Lamp. A separately awaited application is skipped after
lethal combat end, target death/removal, or Axebot uid replacement.
Creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath **0x2c9a0c**, default
ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath, and Illusion's override **0x24faa2** remove
these non-temporary Type-2 powers on death. Debilitate is one scalar
singleton; Knockdown is a tuple of exact `(amount, player-applier)` listener
instances. Both project into Rend's live Type-2 instance count and clone/memo
identity.

Manual and direct AutoPlay use the established exact AnyEnemy target route.
Generated play counts rerun each complete body serially: Debilitate stacks
duration, Knockdown creates distinct listeners, and Tracking stacks
intensity. None of the three consumes a new RNG stream, mutates a card pile
beyond ordinary result routing, generates content, or adds a prior-fight
stream/cycle caveat.

IL re-read 2026-07-27 against v0.109.1/c8c577f6

AnyEnemy Attack. L0 attacks for 7 then draws 4; L1 attacks for 10 then draws
5. The returned card sequence is filtered by resolved Energy cost zero or
`CardEnergyCost.CostsX`, then passed as one ordered plural Discard command.

`CardPileCmd::<DrawInternal>d__19::MoveNext` **0x42cfc8** appends the exact
`CardModel` reference to its result list at IL **0279-0285** before it awaits
the Hand insertion, history, `Hook.AfterCardDrawn`, and `InvokeDrawn`.
Returned order is therefore draw order, and a completed iteration retains its
card in the returned prefix even if a later hook moves or mutates that object.
A hook that makes combat ending only suppresses later draw iterations.

Scrape's LINQ `Where` is deferred. `CardCmd::<DiscardAndDraw>d__4::MoveNext`
**0x4291a8** first checks `IsOverOrEnding`, then eagerly materializes the
enumerable with `ToList` at IL **003a-0046**. Consequently every predicate
runs exactly once, in returned order, only after the complete awaited Draw
and all draw hooks, but before the first discard or discard hook. An ending
attack or draw tail evaluates no predicate and performs no discard.

`CardEnergyCost.GetWithModifiers(-1)` is **0x2c9ea4** and `CostsX` is
**0x2c9e39**. FreeAttack, FreeSkill, FreePower, and Veilpiercer late hooks
(**0x24e9bc/0x24eb74/0x24ea98/0x256510**) write zero only while the queried
card is in Hand or Play. Corruption has no pile gate. The solver therefore
freezes only returned physical UIDs, re-locates each UID across all five live
piles after the complete Draw, and evaluates its then-live payload: ordinary
cost resolution in Hand/Play, the same calculation without consumable Free*
listeners elsewhere, and an independent X-cost admission.

The plural Discard snapshots that filtered identity order. Each still-live
UID moves from its current pile to Discard/Bottom, records discard history,
and completes the serialized `AfterCardDiscarded` walk before the next UID.
Only after the whole batch completes do collected Sly identities AutoPlay in
the same order. Later Sly children are re-located by UID immediately before
play, so an earlier child may move or upgrade the native referenced object.
A selecting child stores the remaining UID tail in the existing immutable
AutoBatch continuation beneath that child and above the outer Scrape
CardPlay. Terminal discard hooks suppress the undiscarded suffix and the
complete Sly tail.

Each replay repeats attack, fresh Draw, live filter, and discard/Sly batch;
the physical Scrape source follows ordinary result routing exactly once after
the complete replay series. Direct AutoPlay uses the same body. Scrape adds
no intrinsic random choice: existing Shuffle, CombatEnergyCosts,
CombatTargets, and nested-card routes own any draws. It joins
`PRIOR_FIGHT_SHUFFLE_CARDS` because an unrecorded play changes draw-cycle
timing and membership, but adds no independent Targets-consumer entry.

## Batch 157 / #673 — The Scythe local and master-deck growth

IL re-read 2026-07-27 against v0.109.1/c8c577f6
(`sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`).

The Scythe ctor/canonical vars/upgrade/nested OnPlay are
**0x29a857/0x29a8bd/0x29a947/0x40c004**. It is a cost-2 Necrobinder Rare
AnyEnemy Attack with Exhaust. Both levels begin at CurrentDamage 13. L0
increases by 4 after each body; L1 increases by 5.

The attack reads the active physical object's live CurrentDamage and awaits
the complete attack command. The tail then re-reads that same object's live
level/Increase, increments its combat-local IncreasedDamage, recomputes
CurrentDamage as `13 + IncreasedDamage`, and performs the same increment once
on its non-null master-deck `DeckVersion`. Upgrade and downgrade rebuild the
canonical level fields while preserving accumulated growth. Final-enemy
lethal does not suppress the mutation tail; player death follows the existing
awaited-tail cancellation boundary.

Combat-local growth uses the existing keyed physical-card payload. Original
deck copies additionally carry a stable deck-row token into the keyed
`State.scythe_deck_growth` projection. Duplicate deck copies therefore remain
distinct and only the played copy's master row changes. Native
`MutableClone()` copies the local CurrentDamage/IncreasedDamage pair but has a
null DeckVersion, so generated and cloned copies grow locally without
changing an original deck row. The public `the_scythe_deck_props` projection
emits the native two-int save shape.

Every replay observes the prior body's growth. Duplicator therefore deals 13
then 17 at L0 and leaves local/master growth at 8. Native replay continues
against the captured Creature even when the first body killed it and another
enemy keeps combat live; the second attack is a no-op but its unconditional
growth tail still runs. This is a The-Scythe-only exception to the general
#496 dead-fixed-target refusal. Final-enemy lethal suppresses later generated
CardPlay bodies through ordinary combat termination while retaining the
first body's tail. Direct AutoPlay uses the existing single CombatTargets
draw and the same body/result routing.

Live coaching preserves the native
`props.ints = [CurrentDamage, IncreasedDamage]` fields. Entry requires exactly
those two nonnegative integer fields and
`CurrentDamage == 13 + IncreasedDamage`; missing, malformed, or explicitly
ambiguous state refuses. Historical `.run` rows are post-fight endpoints.
Zero growth proves zero at every earlier eligible entry, while a positive
valid endpoint proves only the first eligible fight after acquisition entered
at zero. Later fights are marked ambiguous instead of backfilling growth.
Removal snapshots use the same rule.

The body consumes no RNG and adds no prior-fight Shuffle,
CombatCardSelection, or independent CombatTargets inventory entry. Existing
Thrash live-Damage preview admits The Scythe's physical growth.

IL re-read 2026-07-27 against v0.109.1/c8c577f6
(`sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`).

Misery's ctor/canonical vars/upgrade/nested OnPlay are
**0x291b86/0x291b93/0x291bfb/0x3f6518**. It is a cost-0 Necrobinder Rare
AnyEnemy Attack for 7. The upgrade raises damage to 9 and adds Exhaust.

Before attacking, the body snapshots the selected target's Powers in native
acquisition order, retaining only powers whose current
`PowerModel.TypeForCurrentAmount` is Type 2. The predicate and cloning
lambdas are **0x3f64ca/0x3f64d5**; concrete copies use
`ClonePreservingMutability` **0x226367** and preserve Amount. The temporary
power adjustment lambda **0x3f64f5** cancels an `ITemporaryPower` wrapper's
matching internal contribution in the saved rows. The solver therefore
admits only the 12 concrete families whose identity, Amount, applier, and
listener state are exact: Weak, Vulnerable, Hang, Poison, Doom, Oblivion,
Strangle, finite Shrink, Conqueror, Debilitate, Sic Em, and each distinct
Knockdown instance. Negative Strength, temporary Strength aggregates,
Shriek, Slow, Imbalanced, infinite Shrink, and malformed/inconsistent order
refuse before mutation.

Shrink copying is bounded to a fresh recipient instance. The existing active
recipient Shrink path remains refused because own-hook versus generic
duration-tick order is not verified. The frozen source amount, card-given
amount after Lamp, and resulting recipient amount must each remain strictly
below the represented `999999999` infinite-duration sentinel. Clone preflight
makes active stacking and Lamp/sentinel refusals atomic before the real
attack.

`Monster.misery_debuff_order` records this concrete acquisition order.
Scalar singleton powers contribute one token while every InstanceType-1
Knockdown contributes a repeated token. Stacking preserves position, whole
removal deletes the token, and fresh reapplication appends. Oblivion and
Strangle's filtered order must exactly match
`after_card_played_power_order`. Historical/synthetic states with zero or
one active admitted power normalize uniquely; multiple live powers without
an order refuse.

After the powered attack completes, `CombatState.HittableEnemies`
**0x2e23c9** is materialized. The original target Creature identity is
excluded; a Stock replacement with a fresh uid is a distinct creature and
is eligible. For each frozen recipient in roster order, each frozen source
power is then applied in source acquisition order. Every separately awaited
Apply/Modify rechecks combat ending, recipient liveness, and the exact frozen
uid, so death or replacement during an earlier application suppresses later
copies. `PowerCmd.FindExistingInstanceForStacking` **0x2dedf0** and the
Apply/Modify bodies **0x438e74/0x4395f4** retain the ordinary applier,
Unsettling Lamp, Artifact, Vicious, Snecko Skull, listener-order, and
InstanceType semantics.

The snapshot precedes attack listeners: powers added, changed, or removed by
the hit do not change frozen rows. A lethal selected target still supplies
its saved rows when another enemy survives; final-enemy lethal has no
post-hit roster. Copying Oblivion/Strangle preserves their later hook order
and lethal suppression. Direct AutoPlay consumes only the existing one
CombatTargets selection; Misery itself and all clone applications consume no
additional stream.

Misery is the one attested safe exception to Batch 43's general
keyword-upgrade monotonicity rule. L0 cannot carry Souls Power because
`CanEnchant` requires the card's current Exhaust keyword. Royally Approved
and Steady add only Innate/Retain, which commute with L1's later native
Exhaust; `CardCmd.Upgrade` preserves the physical enchantment payload, and
result routing therefore sees and honors L1 Exhaust. L1 has no further
upgrade. The exception compares both complete immutable Misery Card surfaces,
so a forged added-Exhaust transition remains refused by the general guard.

Coverage advances cards **501/95 -> 502/94**, Rare
**124/35 -> 125/34**, aggregate modeled/refused
**881/174 -> 882/173**, and accepted **889/1063 -> 890/1063**; certified
remains 8. Splash-family coverage is now complete at **112 modeled of 112**.
Full invariant walk:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-27-15-batch158-misery.md`.

## Batch 159 / #676 — Splash exact recorded-unlock generation

IL and token evidence were re-read 2026-07-28 against
v0.109.1/c8c577f6 (`sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`).
Splash's ctor, nested OnPlay state machine, and `MockGeneratedCard` setter are
**0x29858f/0x407284/0x2985e7**. A whole-assembly token scan found no caller of
the setter: canonical gameplay cards retain the constructor's null
`_mockGeneratedCard`, so the private non-null test branch is not admitted as
a combat-state dimension.

The canonical branch materializes `UnlockState.CharacterCardPools`. It
removes the owner's pool only when the list has more than one entry,
concatenates the remaining pools' `GetUnlockedCards` rows in native character
and card order, filters Attack at **0x407276**, then calls
`CardFactory.GetDistinctForCombat(..., 3, CombatCardGeneration)`. The checked
`card_pool_census.json` supplies that complete order, every per-card unlock
epoch, player-count constraint, type, rarity, and
`CanBeGeneratedInCombat` result. Loading that checked JSON in the engine is
the same repository-artifact dependency already used for
`card_templates.json`, `cards_census.json`, and rarity metadata; no game DLL
is loaded at runtime. The census schema, build, character order, endpoint
projections, and every reachable L0/L1 solver leaf are validated before RNG
construction or state mutation.

Live saves and decoded MCR saves carry the cumulative
`UnlockState.unlocked_epochs`; their adapters normalize and pass the entire
set. Character pools are present when their `CHARACTER1_EPOCH` is unlocked,
Ironclad is always the owner pool, and each row is retained only when its own
epoch is unlocked and it is a solo-eligible Common/Uncommon/Rare Attack that
can be generated in combat. Distinct preserves the first native row. Three
exact projections are pinned:

- all character epochs: **112 cards / 111 draws**;
- Ironclad-only one-pool edge: **33 cards / 32 draws**;
- Sean's current recorded profile (Defect epochs 1–2, missing 3–7):
  **109 cards / 108 draws**, exactly the 112-card order without Barrage,
  Flak Cannon, and Helix Drill; the compact `CARD.`-prefixed list hashes to
  `028da2b981b4e77741b36d32b3e9a48d884841e2ace7535c0fe61cf8743667c1`.

The raw `.run` format carries no unlock state. It refuses Splash even when
the legacy fully-unlocked pool assertion is supplied; an assertion is not
substituted for recorded provenance. Missing/malformed epochs, non-Ironclad
ownership, a missing generation counter, census drift, or any unmodeled L0
or L1 leaf refuses before `RunRngSet` construction.

`GetDistinctForCombat` materializes the derived pool and performs a complete
Fisher-Yates on `CombatCardGeneration`, consuming pool-size minus one draws,
then exposes the first three distinct fresh L0 cards as a blocking ordered
choice. Splash+ upgrades all three choices before the screen. The v0.111.0 /
41cef1ea body passes `canSkip=true`; the shared choice screen `MoveNext` at
**0x3e58c0** forwards that flag to `ShowScreen` at **IL_0223–0229** and maps a
negative synced result index to null at **IL_03af–03c5**. A chosen card becomes
physical, receives a fresh UID, is marked free this turn, and is added with
generated-card hooks to Hand Bottom or, when the hand is full, Discard Bottom.
Skip occurs only after the complete pool shuffle has been consumed and emits
no UID, free-cost mutation, generated history, listener dispatch, or pile
insertion. Either result resumes the exact suspended `CardPlayFrame`; the
source routes normally to Discard, and duplicator/replay bodies suspend and
resolve serially with a fresh complete shuffle. Terminal combat suppresses
later generated insertion exactly.

Splash is added to both generated-leaf card-selection/target provenance gates
and the prior-fight Shuffle ambiguity inventory. The latter is required
because an unrecorded generated choice and its later play/flush timing can
change pile membership and reshuffle boundaries. Retrospective MCR action
replay still does not decode blocking card-choice screens; that separate
adapter limitation is tracked by #708 and does not block live entry or solver
planning.

Coverage advances cards **502/94 -> 503/93**, Uncommon
**184/46 -> 185/45**, aggregate modeled/refused
**882/173 -> 883/172**, and accepted **890/1063 -> 891/1063**; certified
remains 8.
Full invariant walk:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-28-01-batch159-splash.md`.

## Batch 160 / #679 — Alchemize exact potion generation and procurement

IL and the checked #678 headless-engine census were re-read 2026-07-28
against v0.109.1/c8c577f6 (`sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`).
Alchemize's ctor/upgrade/nested OnPlay are
**0x2839cc/0x283a27/0x3d2a48**. It is a cost-1 Colorless Rare Self Skill
with Exhaust; L1 changes only cost to 0.

The body calls `CombatPotionGeneration -> CreateRandomPotionInCombat ->
ToMutable -> TryToProcure(-1)`. The checked current-build fully unlocked solo
Ironclad pool contains exactly 45 reachable identities, partitioned in native
stable order as Common 16, Uncommon 15, and Rare 14. Each body consumes one
rarity `NextFloat(1)` and one partition `NextItem`. The float32 thresholds
are inclusive at 0.1 for Rare and 0.35 for Uncommon. All 45 leaves and both
draws are pinned.

`TryToProcure(-1)` fills the first null slot of the fixed-size belt. A full
belt and Sozu's pre-insert veto leave the belt unchanged but occur after both
generation draws. An already-ending combat suppresses the body before RNG.
Successful procurement alone reaches `AfterPotionProcured`; Belt Buckle then
removes its empty-belt Dexterity and clears its latch, so using the final
potion can apply the Dexterity again.

`State.potion_slots` is the single authoritative belt representation for an
Alchemize-admitted fight: an ordered fixed-length tuple containing nulls and
potion identities. `potions` and `inert_potions` remain compatibility views
and are validated against it before keys and actions. Legal potion actions
carry the exact slot index, so equal-ID duplicates remain distinct. A
generated modeled leaf becomes usable immediately; a generated unmodeled
leaf is keyed inert state with the conditional-optimum caveat from #634.
Strict mode preflights and refuses an unmodeled result before the real stream
or belt changes. Because reporting currently occurs from the root state,
non-strict live coaching warns up front whenever an Alchemize remains, naming
all ten reachable unmodeled leaves even if the entering belt is fully modeled.
The warning disappears after the source is gone when no inert potion was
actually generated.

Entry requires explicit solo Ironclad ownership, the fully unlocked potion
epochs, exact positive capacity and slot rows, and a nonnegative recorded
CombatPotionGeneration counter. Live saves preserve `max_potion_slot_count`
and slot indices. Schema-19 and legacy counter shapes are both decoded. MCR
replay uses its header build and resolves potion use against the current
State slot, including a potion generated after entry. Raw `.run` records
lack these facts and refuse. Mixed-payload exact piles also refuse because
generated Gambler's Brew/Ashwater selection cannot yet represent ordered
physical picks.

Because a remaining Alchemize can add healing or bank value,
`final_hp_ceiling` returns no finite I3 bound until every copy has left the
remaining card zones. Afterwards the ordinary bound prices the actual
current modeled belt.

Coverage advances cards **503/93 -> 504/92**, Rare
**125/34 -> 126/33**, aggregate modeled/refused
**883/172 -> 884/171**, and accepted **891/1063 -> 892/1063**; certified
remains 8. Solo Colorless advances from 50 modeled / 3 refused to
51 modeled / 2 refused, leaving Stratagem and Jack of All Trades.
Full invariant walk:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-28-02-batch160-alchemize.md`.

## Batch 161 / #616 — resumable Draw frame (caller/return contract)

`CardPileCmd.Draw` is now suspendable. `DrawInternal` (d__19 `0x42cfc8`)
awaits, per iteration: `ShuffleIfNecessary` (d__22 `0x42e608`), the hand
`Add`, and `Hook.AfterCardDrawn` (d__11 `0x415614` — the complete Early
enumerator, disposed, then a FRESH ordinary enumerator, with
`PlayerChoiceContext` push/await/pop per listener). Its result list gets the
drawn card BEFORE the awaited hand Add, and free hand capacity is recomputed
live after every awaited hook (`IL_03b4-03fa`). Hellraiser
(`<AfterCardDrawnEarly>d__7` `0x385778`) keeps the exact CardModel in
`Data.autoPlayingCards` across its awaited `CardCmd.AutoPlay` and removes it
only after the await returns.

The solver models a suspension of that await chain as a `DrawFrame`
continuation (`_FRAME_DRAW`): requested-count cursor, completed-iteration
count, the exact ordered result so far (`("uid", uid)` entries for
physically identified cards, `("payload", card)` for pre-normalization
legacy draws — the in-flight card included, matching the native result.Add
order), `from_hand_draw`, the suspension stage, the in-flight uid, and a
registered caller continuation. The frame is inserted BENEATH the parked
child CardPlay chain at the stack depth captured before the Early hook, so
the LIFO unwind resumes the interrupted iteration after the selecting
Strike's own frame completes. The resume performs the deferred latch
drift-check/pop, relocates the drawn uid (loud if vanished), runs the fresh
ordinary listener pass exactly once iff not over/dead, recomputes capacity
live, and continues the remaining iterations; completion materializes the
ordered result (uid entries resolve to the live located card, exactly the
native live-reference semantics) and dispatches the caller continuation
exactly once. Hand capacity is never frozen in the frame.

Caller/return audit (every `draw_cards` site):

- `_run_steps` body steps whose draw ends the step — `draw`,
  `drum_of_battle_exact`, `exhaust_draw` (step and select-op forms),
  Impatience, FTL, Compile Driver, fetch, draw_space, Spoils of Battle —
  pass `caller="none"`: the universal post-step pending check parks the
  body tail as a nested continuation and the CardPlay frame resumes it.
- Reified suffix callers: `turn_start`
  (`_after_turn_start_hand_draw`, the extracted AfterPlayerTurnStart
  cascade), `escape_plan`, `pillage` (loop re-entry keyed on the exact
  returned instance), `expertise`, `scrape`, `brightest_flame`, `big_bang`,
  `restlessness` (separately awaited one-card Draws), `potion_epilogue`
  (Swift/Cure All/Glowwater), `clarity_potion`, `snecko_oil`, and
  `sly_after_draw` (re-arms the established "Sly discard" AutoBatch frame;
  payload-frozen Sly entries must resolve to exactly one physical instance
  after the mid-draw normalization or refuse), plus `gremlin_horn_death`.
- Unconverted sites (draw inside player_attack/damage/exhaust hook chains or
  the turn-start suffix itself): Centennial Puzzle,
  Pendulum, Game Piece, Vicious, Dark Embrace, the SWIFT enchantment, and
  the legacy in-play selection resume (guarded loudly). `caller=None`
  suspensions raise; the `start_combat` gate refuses Hellraiser + a
  selecting Strike alongside any statically detectable unconverted source,
  so the blanket Hellraiser+{Sculpting,Seeker} refusal is now this narrow
  combination gate. Seeker Strike's attack-suspension refusal (a nested
  choice during `player_attack`, before the shortlist) is unchanged.

Direct AutoPlay keeps the selecting Strike in Hand through its own body, so
the Strike is itself an eligible candidate of its own FromHand selection —
the suspended choice can legally target the in-flight card.

No card/potion/encounter status changes; coverage remains 892/1063. This
primitive unblocks #401 (Stratagem, the AfterShuffle seam — the frame's
stage vocabulary reserves "after_shuffle") and transitively #686 (Jack of
All Trades). Full invariant walk:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-28-03-batch161-draw-frame.md`.

## Batch 162 / #401 — Stratagem exact AfterShuffle selection

`CARD.STRATAGEM` is admitted for both levels (ctor `0x299221`: cost 1 Power,
Self; OnUpgrade `0x29927b`: EnergyCost -1 → Stratagem+ costs 0). OnPlay d__1
`0x408bf8` applies one `StratagemPower` stack (Type 1 / StackType 1
Intensity: reapplication adds to the one listener's Amount).

`StratagemPower.<AfterShuffle>d__4` `0x38feb0`: owner gate → Flash →
`CardSelectCmd.FromCombatPile(choiceContext, Draw pile, player, prompt,
CardSelectorPrefs(Amount))` — the prefs ctor chain (`0x2e41f0` →
`0x2e4214`) pins **MinSelect == MaxSelect == Amount** with no manual
confirmation — then one awaited `CardPileCmd.Add(card, Hand, Bottom)` per
selected card. FromCombatPile re-enumerates the live pile, so candidates
keep true pile order, the count clamps to the pile (the established
auto-take rule), and a full Hand routes an Add to Discard
(`<Add>d__10` isFullHandAdd).

Hook order: `IterateCombatHookListeners` walks player creature powers
before relics, so Stratagem fires before the Batch 38 AfterShuffle relics;
`_after_player_shuffle` is split accordingly and a suspended selection
defers the relic tail (`_after_player_shuffle_relics`) to the resume.

Suspension: a real choice (live Draw pile > Amount) is resumable only
beneath a Draw command — the #616 DrawFrame's reserved **"after_shuffle"**
stage: the reshuffle is fully committed, `pending =
("stratagem_select", sel)`, and the resume applies the exact physical
picks, runs the relic tail, then re-enters the interrupted iteration
through DrawInternal's post-ShuffleIfNecessary candidate/capacity gates
(`IL_022e-0274` — Stratagem's Adds can drain the reshuffled pile or fill
the Hand before the pop, both modeled as loop exits). At every other
shuffle site (selection-path ShuffleIfNecessary, Reboot's explicit
Shuffle) a real choice fails loudly; the auto-take path completes
synchronously everywhere. No RNG is consumed by the selection itself, and
the resume never repeats the reshuffle sort/Fisher-Yates.

Entropy's Colorless transform pool leaf `STRATAGEM` is now a modeled
selection target (the Batch 147 machinery admits it generically).

Coverage advances cards **504/92 → 505/91**, Uncommon **185/45 → 186/44**,
aggregate modeled/refused **884/171 → 885/170**, and accepted
**892/1063 → 893/1063**; certified remains 8. Solo Colorless advances from
51 modeled / 2 refused to 52 modeled / 1 refused, leaving only Jack of All
Trades (#686). Full invariant walk:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-28-04-batch162-stratagem.md`.

## Batch 165 / #717 — Gremlin Horn resumable post-Draw death suffix

Current-build evidence was read directly from the installed ARM64
`sts2.dll`: **v0.109.1 / c8c577f6**, SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`.
`GremlinHorn.AfterDeath` (outer `0x240cd8`) starts nested
`<AfterDeath>d__6::MoveNext` (`0x36f66c`). The nested body rejects a target
on the owner's side (`IL_0024-0041`), flashes, awaits
`PlayerCmd.GainEnergy(EnergyVar.BaseValue)` (`IL_0046-00b7`), then awaits
`CardPileCmd.Draw(choiceContext, CardsVar.BaseValue, owner, false)`
(`IL_00bc-012b`) and returns immediately after `GetResult` (`IL_0130-0131`).
There is no in-progress or ending gate in this body.

The suffix after that awaited Draw belongs to the enclosing death chain.
`Hook/<AfterDeath>d__28::MoveNext` (`0x416a84`) awaits listeners serially and
advances its enumerator only after each result (`IL_00ae-012e`).
`CreatureCmd/<KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition>d__15::MoveNext` (`0x43511c`)
awaits `Hook.AfterDeath` at `IL_03c7-041f`, then snapshots teammates/removes
powers and, for the last primary enemy with only secondary teammates, awaits
the frozen teammate `Kill` cascade at `IL_05b7-0671`. The outer
`CreatureCmd/<Kill>d__14::MoveNext` (`0x434e14`) performs its later
combat-ending handling only after every `KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition`
await in its frozen input list (`IL_008c-0125`, then `IL_012b+`).

The solver now registers `gremlin_horn_death` in
`_DRAW_CALLER_HANDLERS`. A primary death stores `("death",)`; a suspended
secondary cascade stores `("cascade", frozen_monster_indices, next_cursor)`.
Both payloads are immutable/keyable. The handler first completes the Horn
listener's deferred observable suffix, then runs the later physical-card
AfterDeath listener, resumes the exact frozen cascade cursor, and reaches
the terminal boundary only after every nested Horn Draw has unwound. A Horn
Draw that triggers another lethal Hellraiser AutoPlay therefore parks an
inner death DrawFrame above the outer one: the inner Horn/listener suffix
finishes before the outer Draw returns, matching the nested await chain.
Malformed suffix payloads and frozen-index drift refuse loudly.

The Hellraiser + selecting-Strike entry gate is narrowed by exactly
`RELIC.GREMLIN_HORN`. Centennial Puzzle, Pendulum, Game Piece, Vicious,
Dark Embrace, and Swift remain pinned refusals because their caller suffixes
are still unconverted. Effect pins cover deferred-listener order, nested
death-frame unwind, secondary cascade Draw order, and the final terminal
boundary. No content status, coverage total, or RNG consumer changes. Full
invariant walk:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-28-06-batch165-gremlin-horn.md`.

## Batch 165 / #718–#720 — current-build translator-refused card scouts

The Silent, Defect, and Regent content tracks re-read twelve complete card
bodies, including every nested async `<OnPlay>d__N::MoveNext`, against the
installed **v0.109.1 / c8c577f6** ARM64 assembly (SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`).
**0 modeled, 12 retained as I5 refusals.** Each complete behavior needs
engine/state work outside the class-shard-only tracks. The raw translator
reasons remain byte-stable provenance; the Batch 165 tests add the semantic
absence pins, targeting/callset evidence, pool/build anchors, and exact routes.
No mechanic changed in these tracks, so walks 07–09 remain deliberately unused.

### Silent (#718)

- **BLADE_SYMPHONY** — AllAllies + MultiplayerOnly
  (ctor/getter `0x28510a/0x285124`). `<OnPlay>d__7::MoveNext`
  `0x3d608c` enumerates alive teammates and creates two L0 Shivs in each
  teammate Hand. Local-player-only generation is inexact; routed to the
  multiplayer player/pile boundary **#431**.
- **KNIFE_TRAP** — `<OnPlay>d__6::MoveNext` `0x3f1b74` freezes every
  Shiv-tag card in Exhaust, upgrades the exact frozen instances iff the
  source is upgraded, then serially direct-AutoPlays them at the original
  target. Routed to high-complexity nested-play/physical-card issue **#725**
  (blocked by target-lifecycle **#496**); it remains unassigned pending Sean's
  required high-tier review.
- **SHADOW_STEP** — `<OnPlay>d__3::MoveNext` `0x403a9c` plural-discards
  the live Hand and applies ShadowStepPower. Its turn-start body `0x38d810`
  later applies DoubleDamagePower and removes itself; the multiplier
  `0x24ddfc` covers owner/pet powered attacks and decrements at side end
  (`0x382e0c`). Routed to **#726**.
- **THE_HUNT** — `<OnPlay>d__9::MoveNext` `0x40bd44` snapshots the
  fatal predicate, attacks for 10/15, and on captured `WasTargetKilled`
  inserts a CardReward into `CombatRoom.ExtraRewards` before applying its
  marker power. Routed to high-complexity run/reward-state issue **#727**,
  distinct from advisory #523; it remains unassigned pending Sean's required
  high-tier review.

### Defect (#719)

- **COMPACT** — `<OnPlay>d__7::MoveNext` `0x3dc9b8` gains Block 6/7,
  snapshots every transformable Status in Discard, creates one fresh Fuel per
  exact source (upgraded iff Compact is upgraded), then performs the ordered
  bulk transform. Routed to fixed-result Discard transform issue **#721**.
- **GENETIC_ALGORITHM** — `<OnPlay>d__16::MoveNext` `0x3ea3ac` gains the
  exact combat copy's mutable CurrentBlock, then increments both that copy and
  its exact master-deck `DeckVersion` by 3/4. `BuffFromPlay` `0x28d16b`
  and `UpdateBlock` `0x28d181` make this persistent per-instance state, not
  a static block card. Routed to **#722**.
- **HIBERNATE** — Self + MultiplayerOnly
  (`0x28e753/0x28e760`). Its body `0x3ee334` applies a duration keyed to
  the exact played card, then serially channels two/three Frost orbs;
  HibernatePower decrements at owner turn start (`0x385d60`). The original
  **#431** routing was retired by Batch 278 / **#1172** after the current-build
  body, duration, multiplayer gate, and turn-start boundary were modeled.
- **ONE_FOR_ALL** — AllAllies + MultiplayerOnly

## Batch 167 / #496 — exact fixed-target replay lifecycle

Current-build behavior was re-read from the installed **v0.109.1 / c8c577f6**
ARM64 assembly, SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`.
`CardModel/<OnPlayWrapper>d__339::MoveNext` `0x364ad0` builds every generated
`CardPlay` with the wrapper's original `target` (`IL_0525-0544`). Its loop
checks combat ending (`IL_0422-042c`) but never replaces a dead target.
`AttackCommand.Targeting` `0x2e010f` stores that Creature unchanged;
`GetPossibleTargets` `0x2dfdc4` returns the singleton; and nested
`AttackCommand/<Execute>d__90::MoveNext` `0x43ac88` filters it through
`IsAlive` (`IL_0166-0196`) and exits on an empty live-combat list
(`IL_019b-01b3`).

The simulator now resolves every generated body against its captured
`(slot, uid)` even after ordinary death. The exact dead Monster object reaches
the card body, where each modeled Attack/Power/result command applies its own
native no-op gate; unconditional body tails still run while another enemy
keeps combat live. A missing object or same-slot/fresh-uid replacement remains
a loud transactional refusal. Result lists remain replay-local, and the one
physical card still resolves one precomputed result route.

Manual, direct AutoPlay, Glam, Duplicator, Burst, One-Two Punch, Echo Form,
and physical BaseReplayCount all share this frame path. Current AutoPlay IL
(`CardCmd/<AutoPlay>d__0::MoveNext` `0x428908`) consumes one CombatTargets
choice at `IL_0343-0372` and passes it once to OnPlayWrapper at
`IL_060b-062a`; replays consume no further target draws. Beat Down's frozen
batch continues to freeze `(card_uid, payload)`, cursor, and terminal policy,
but no longer rejects a targeted child solely because that child has multiple
generated plays. The child is preselected once and every replay retains that
same target identity.

The existing terminal rules are unchanged: a final-enemy kill makes the
wrapper skip later generated bodies, and the result-pile command keeps its own
ending gate. Non-targeted whole-pile/self-body refusals (Reboot, Storm of
Steel, Particle Wall, and Primal Force) remain separate and loud. Knife Trap
and all #725 behavior are intentionally outside Batch 167.

and aggregate accepted remains **894/1063** (certified 8). No capture or

## Batch 168 / #725 — Knife Trap frozen Exhaust-Shiv batch

Current-build behavior was re-read from the installed **v0.109.1 / c8c577f6**
ARM64 assembly, SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`.
`KnifeTrap::.ctor` `0x28fc74` establishes cost 2, Rare Skill, AnyEnemy, and
one upgrade rung. `KnifeTrap/<OnPlay>d__6::MoveNext` `0x3f1b74` null-guards
the original target (`IL_001d-0032`), materializes the Exhaust pile's
Shiv-tagged cards to an ordered list (`IL_0032-006c`), then serially processes
those exact references. Before each AutoPlay it re-reads the source upgrade
state and, for Knife Trap+, calls `CardCmd.Upgrade(card, false)`
(`IL_0091-009c`). It awaits each `CardCmd.AutoPlay` completely before
advancing (`IL_00a1-0124`), always passing the original `CardPlay.Target`.

The simulator extends its immutable physical-card batch frame with an optional
fixed target and per-entry upgrade flag. Knife Trap snapshots ordered
`(card_uid, payload)` entries after identity normalization. At each cursor it
prefers the exact live UID wherever awaited work relocated or mutated it,
falls back to the frozen payload only when that UID is absent, validates the
card still has the canonical Shiv tag, performs at most one current-rung
upgrade while preserving UID/enchantment/local physical state, and starts one
fully resumable AutoPlay child. A missing or same-slot replacement of the
original target refuses transactionally; ordinary death does not replace the
object, so later children receive that exact dead target and do not roll or
retarget to a peer.

Native re-reads the in-Play Knife Trap source's `IsUpgraded` state per
iteration; the simulator currently freezes `source[1] > 0` in the batch frame.
That flag is extensionally exact only while no admitted path can upgrade the
in-Play source mid-batch, as is true for the current closed child action graph.
Any future arbitrary-card AutoPlay admission must convert this to a live source
re-read at every cursor or refuse the reachable interaction loudly. Admitting
such a route while retaining the frozen flag would be an I5 violation.

`CardCmd/<AutoPlay>d__0::MoveNext` `0x428908` was re-read with both target
branches. A supplied target bypasses CombatTargets selection and is forwarded
to OnPlayWrapper without an alive check. This remains true when Fan of Knives
makes a Shiv's effective targeting AllEnemies: the supplied target object is
still passed, and the Shiv body owns its dynamic all-enemy effect. Consequently

batch's existing terminal cursor gate suppresses every later child before its
upgrade. With another enemy alive, later Shivs still complete against the
dead original target and never damage the peer.

Burst and other generated Knife Trap bodies take fresh Exhaust snapshots.
Each child still owns the existing single physical result route, so captured
Shivs leave and return to Exhaust through ordinary AutoPlay lifecycle. Knife
Trap resolves once to Discard while combat remains live; the existing terminal
result-pile gate otherwise leaves it in Play. Raw and composed translator

## Batch 169 / #431 — explicit teammate damage boundary and Underworld

Current-build behavior was re-read from the installed **v0.109.1 / c8c577f6**
ARM64 assembly, SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`.
The installed binary and archived current-build binary are identical.

`Underworld::.ctor` **0x29b787** is a cost-2 uncommon Self Skill with one
upgrade rung. `get_MultiplayerConstraint` **0x29b794** returns
MultiplayerOnly. `Underworld/<OnPlay>d__7::MoveNext` **0x40e6b4** triggers
the owner's PowerUp animation and applies `UnderworldPower(owner, 1, owner)`.
`OnUpgrade` **0x29b80b** removes Exhaust and changes no amount or cost.

`UnderworldPower` is Type 1 / StackType Intensity
(**0x256357/0x25635a**). Its
`<AfterDamageGiven>d__6::MoveNext` **0x3937d4** performs the complete ordered
gate:

1. dealer is non-null;
2. dealer side equals owner side;
3. dealer is not the owner;
4. dealer's `PetOwner` is not the owner's `Player`;
5. props are `IsPoweredAttack`;
6. `DamageResult.TotalDamage > 0`.

It then applies `DoomPower` to the event target for
`TotalDamage * UnderworldPower.Amount`, with the Underworld owner as applier.
Thus a teammate player and a teammate-owned pet qualify, while the owner and
owner's pet do not. `Hook/<AfterDamageGiven>d__24::MoveNext` **0x4165f4**
serially awaits the `CombatState.IterateHookListeners` snapshot, and
`CreatureCmd::Damage` reaches that walk after its DamageResult is fixed but
before its later Kill. The modeled listener stays in first-application power
order and stacks the one existing amount without moving it.

The simulator does not predict a teammate turn. Instead, a public blocking
event boundary accepts one externally observed teammate Damage command at a
time. Its payload is the exact pre-pipeline command amount, powered bit,
teammate-versus-teammate-pet relation, and exact target `(slot, uid)`.
Resolution goes through the existing damage command projection, including
caps, block, HP-loss modifiers, DamageResult construction, ordered listeners,
and death work. While the event is pending it is the only legal transition.
The initializer refuses dead/replaced targets, nonpositive or inexact amounts,
foreign dealer relations, non-boolean powered flags, combat-ending states, and
every overlap with a card selection, enemy choice, active card, continuation,
or residual Play-pile card. Enumeration and direct resolution use that same
validator, so a forged valid payload cannot clear its marker, deal damage, or
publish a log while another blocking event or non-quiescent pile state remains.
Multiple observed teammate commands must be supplied and resolved serially.

This boundary deliberately carries no teammate hand, draw/discard/exhaust
piles, action choice, card target selection, potion, relic, orb queue, or
generated-card ownership. The ordinary `.run`/fight adapter still admits
exactly one player and refuses Underworld in a solo deck; a default solo State
does not enumerate or execute the card. Consequently Ignition and Imitation
Learning remain refused under #734, and Soulbound remains refused under #736.

`UnderworldPower/<AfterSideTurnEnd>d__7::MoveNext` **0x393950** checks
`side == 2` and removes the whole stacked power. Enemy Doom is a
`BeforeSideTurnEnd` listener (**0x3827ac**), so its complete kill batch
precedes Underworld's removal. The simulator performs the same boundary after
the enemy Doom pass and removes both amount and listener-order entry. A combat
ending during Doom keeps the existing terminal suppression of later
AfterSideTurnEnd work.

Coverage advances cards to **508 modeled / 88 refused** and aggregate accepted
to **896/1063**; relics, potions, encounters, enchantments, and certified
encounters are unchanged. No capture or `fight_states` pin was weakened.
Focused pins cover both card levels, solo refusal, exact teammate and
teammate-pet reachability, block/cap-derived TotalDamage, Artifact, serial
event ordering, malformed/overlapping boundary refusal, keyed pending state,
and enemy-Doom-before-expiry order. Full invariant audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-28-09-batch169-underworld.md`.

## Batch 171 / #736 — Soulbound ownership and generated-Soul recursion

Current-build behavior was re-read from the installed **v0.109.1 / c8c577f6**
ARM64 assembly, SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`.

`Soulbound::.ctor` **0x297d26** and multiplayer getter **0x297d33** establish
a cost-1 Uncommon AnyAlly MultiplayerOnly Power. Its nested OnPlay body
**0x4061f0** preserves the selected `CardPlay.Target` through both player
PowerUp animations, then applies `SoulboundPower(1)` to that selected
Creature. The card owner's Creature is the applier. `OnUpgrade` **0x297d97**
adds Innate and changes no amount, cost, or target rule.

`SoulboundPower` is Type 1 / StackType Intensity
(**0x2541d5/0x2541d8**). Its
`<AfterCardGeneratedForCombat>d__10::MoveNext` **0x38ee48** exits when the
creator is null; a nonnull creator must satisfy
`creator.Creature == power.Applier`. It then requires the generated CardModel
to be `Soul` and requires the power's private `IsAddingSoul` latch to be
false. A qualifying callback sets that per-power latch, creates the power's
live Amount of fresh L0 Souls for `power.Owner.Player`, and awaits
`AddGeneratedCardsToCombat(Draw, owner.Player, Random)` before previewing the
results and clearing the latch. Thus card ownership is not a trigger gate:
a locally created Soul can trigger a power owned by a selected teammate
because the applier remains the local player. The newly created teammate
Souls name that teammate as creator, so they fail the local-applier identity
gate naturally. A self-owned power instead sees its own generated Souls and
depends on `IsAddingSoul` to stop recursion. This differs deliberately from
the separately byte-verified ArsenalPower gate: Arsenal accepts a null
creator and rejects only a known foreign creator.

The global hook remains the serial
`Hook/<AfterCardGeneratedForCombat>d__14::MoveNext` **0x415ba4** over
`Hook.IterateCombatHookListeners` **0x41ccc0**.
`CombatState/<IterateHookListeners>d__69::MoveNext` **0x441190** snapshots
each allied Creature in `_allies` order, adding its powers before its relics,
potions, orbs, and combat-pile cards. Combat setup does not prove local
first: `CombatRoom/<EnterInternal>d__40::MoveNext` **0x302308** and
`EventCombatSynchronizer.InitializeForEvent` **0x21a044** enumerate
`runState.IPlayerCollection.Players`; `CombatState.AddPlayer` **0x2e207d**
delegates to `AddCreature`, whose **0x2e2520** body appends to `_allies`.
Because the projection does not carry the local player's run-state slot, a
local-recipient Soulbound cannot coexist with a teammate-recipient
Soulbound. Applying the second side or dispatching a forged coexistence
refuses before mutation.

Within admitted states, local Arsenal/Soulbound application order and the
ordered teammate Soulbound projection remain exact. Arsenal can coexist
with teammate Soulbound because their state effects commute across the
unknown creature order: Arsenal changes only Strength for the original
local-created card and consumes no pile/RNG state, while teammate
Soulbound-created Souls use the teammate as creator and fail Arsenal's
foreign-creator gate. Rocket Punch changes only local-owned generated Status
cards, while Soul is a Skill, so it likewise cannot rewrite the
teammate-owned nested Souls. Every nested generated Soul still starts a fresh
listener snapshot and observes the executing power with its latch true.

`CardPileCmd/<AddGeneratedCardsToCombat>d__6::MoveNext` **0x42c464** retains
the established per-card order: CardGenerated history, awaited pile Add, then
the awaited global generated-card hook. Soulbound passes pile enum 1 = Draw
and position enum 3 = Random, not Hand/Bottom. Every generated Soul therefore
consumes one shared Shuffle draw and is inserted into the selected power
owner's Draw pile. The bounded teammate projection adds exactly that Draw
tuple and that player's creator-scoped CardGenerated count. Explicit empty
teammate entered/generated-hook assertions exclude unrepresented teammate
relic, card, or power effects; no teammate hand, action, resource, choice, or
turn prediction is added.

Manual AnyAlly targeting inherits Batch 170's exact self/live-player
enumeration and whole-context live-pet refusal. Null-target AutoPlay still
uses **0x4283f0** and consumes one CombatTargets draw over live non-owner
teammate players only. Power applications stack by selected owner without
moving the existing listener. Raw and composed translator refusals remain as
parser provenance; the reviewed hand model is authoritative for execution
and coverage.

Coverage advances cards from **510 modeled / 86 refused** to **511 modeled /
85 refused** and aggregate accepted from **898/1063** to **899/1063**.
Relics, potions, encounters, enchantments, and certified encounters are
unchanged. Focused tests pin both card levels, manual and AutoPlay AnyAlly
identity, owner/applier stacking, null/foreign creators, the absence of a
generated-card-owner gate, Draw/Random recipient routing and Shuffle count,
per-power latch behavior, local/teammate Soulbound coexistence refusal,
Arsenal's distinct null-creator rule, Arsenal+teammate commutation, local

visibility. Full invariant audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-28-11-batch171-soulbound.md`.

command's private result lists and checks captured `DamageResult.WasTargetKilled`.
Both conditions must be true. The existing fatal predicate projection remains
exact: Minion/illusion veto, Segment Reattach's other-live-Segment gate, and
Stock's inherited true result are all read before damage.

On a qualifying result, `CardCreationOptions.ForRoom(owner,
combatRoom.RoomType)` is constructed and passed to `new CardReward(options,
3, owner, null)`, then `CombatRoom.AddExtraReward(owner, reward)` **0x5be25**.
`ForRoom` **0x4bf5c** uses the owner's Character card pool, creation source
Encounter, and Regular/Elite/Boss encounter rarity odds. `CardReward::.ctor`
**0x5fa5c** stores those options and OptionCount 3; it creates no cards and
consumes no RNG. `CardReward.Populate` **0x5fb90** later calls
`CardFactory.CreateForReward` during room-end reward-set generation. The combat
model therefore stores the exact deferred serializable descriptor, never
guessed card identities or a combat-time reward-stream advance.

The room-end consumer is explicit: `RewardsSet.WithRewardsFromRoom` **0x609f8**
appends the local player's ordered `CombatRoom.ExtraRewards`, and
`<GenerateWithoutOffering>d__32::MoveNext` **0x305034** calls `Populate` on
each reward before reward hooks and final index sorting.

`CombatRoom.ToSerializable` **0x5bd0c** writes each player-keyed ordered reward
list through `Reward.ToSerializable`; `CardReward.ToSerializable` **0x5fe58**
writes source, rarity odds, card-pool IDs, and option count. `FromSerializable`
**0x5bb10** resolves the player key and reconstructs the list in order. The
simulator's ordered local The Hunt reward tuple mirrors precisely that
persistent subset and participates automatically in State.key().

Reward insertion precedes the separately awaited
`PowerCmd.Apply<TheHuntPower>` at body IL `0x01a3-0x0254`.
`TheHuntPower` Type/StackType **0x255ebc/0x255ebf** are buff/intensity and it
has no hook body. The generic Apply command is combat-ending gated: a final
lethal retains the reward but does not add the marker; a revived or nonfinal
fatal retains the reward and then increments the marker. Fixed-target replays
reuse the original target object: a dead unreplaced target yields no second
DamageResult/reward, while a qualifying fresh/revived target may reward again.
Every reward appends, and every admitted marker application stacks, preserving
native order and count.

The solver's declared terminal objective remains combat-local HP, retained
potions, and turns. Deferred card identities do not yet exist and cannot be
assigned an exact HP value. Instead, the complete descriptor list is retained
in terminal State, memoized, returned in solve stats, and narrated. This makes
the post-combat result observable without expanding the advisory reward-screen
work in #523 or inventing a card-value heuristic.

Coverage advances cards from **511 modeled / 85 refused** to **512 modeled /
84 refused** and aggregate accepted from **899/1063** to **900/1063**.
Relics, potions, encounters, enchantments, and certified encounters are
unchanged. Full invariant audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-28-12-batch172-the-hunt.md`.

## 2026-07-28 — Batch 173: Centennial Puzzle continuation graph (#738 / #729)

Current-build evidence is **v0.109.1 / c8c577f6**, ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`.

`CentennialPuzzle.AfterDamageReceived` outer **0x23e25c** and nested
`<AfterDamageReceived>d__10::MoveNext` **0x36ac54** owner/unblocked/unused-gate,
disarm once, then issue three separately awaited singular Draw commands
(`IL_0076-0116`). `Hook/<AfterDamageReceived>d__26::MoveNext` **0x416798**
serially awaits the ordinary listener enumerator (`IL_0045-0119`) before
creating and awaiting the Late enumerator (`IL_013f-023c`).
`CreatureCmd/<Damage>d__12::MoveNext` **0x432a14** awaits that complete hook
(`IL_0d51-0ddf`), then advances the frozen target cursor
(`IL_0e79-0e84`) and later awaits the killed-creature batch
(`IL_0ead-0f0d`). `AttackCommand/<Execute>d__90::MoveNext` **0x43ac88**
retains the current hit target/result across the same nested await before its
later hit, history, and AfterAttack work.

The solver now mirrors that call graph with validated immutable LIFO frames.
Centennial's frame records each returned one-card prefix. Damage suffix and
LoseMaxHp frames retain the remaining ordinary/Late listeners, frozen Inferno
target cursor, and later SetMaxHp. Player attacks retain original and current
target identities, remaining hits, frozen pre-Thorns damage, exact result
snapshots, command Vigor, and source signature. Monster attacks retain the
completed hit facts and remaining-hit cursor; move and enemy-phase frames
retain the exact move suffix and not-yet-acted enemy UID snapshot.

Turn-end frames retain the one initial OnTurnEndInHand physical-UID snapshot.
Native `CombatManager/<DoTurnEnd>d__133::MoveNext` **0x43c294** checks
IsOverOrEnding at `IL_009f`, then builds `<turnEndCards>5__2` exactly once at
`IL_00ac-00f8`: it iterates the pile into a fresh list containing precisely
the cards whose `HasTurnEndInHandEffect` is true before any per-card await.
A Puzzle-drawn turn-end card therefore cannot join that phase's snapshot; it
is live-flushed but not reprocessed.
Side-switch, AfterCardPlayed, and turn-start frames cover Disintegration,
Galvanic, Royal Poison, Inferno, and Crimson Mantle suffixes. Child
Draw/CardPlay/death work stays above the awaiting outer frame, so a selecting
Puzzle AutoPlay may kill, trigger a Gremlin Horn Draw, and expose another
selection; that inner chain completes before the outer Draw or Damage cursor
advances.

Already-committed HP loss, block, Rupture, combat history, draw prefixes, and
RNG draws are never replayed. A suspended card attack rewinds only to its
await site and consumes one exact keyed completed-command record, while the
current hit's modifier result remains frozen. Terminal gates remain on their
native child commands, killed results skip their later damage-received walk,
and random-target attacks check ending before consuming CombatTargets.

The registered caller performs three distinct `draw_cards(..., 1)` calls and
the `start_combat` gate is narrowed by exactly `RELIC.CENTENNIAL_PUZZLE`.
Pendulum and Game Piece remain refused. Coverage regeneration is a no-op:
cards remain **512 modeled / 84 refused**, relics **265 / 35**, and aggregate
accepted **900/1063**. Full invariant audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-28-13-batch173-centennial-puzzle.md`.

## 2026-07-28 — Batch 175: card-generation potions (#228 / #138)

Current-build evidence is **v0.109.1 / c8c577f6**, ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`.
The four choice bodies are `AttackPotion/<OnUse>d__6::MoveNext`
**0x3951a0** (Attack predicate **0x395192**),
`ColorlessPotion/<OnUse>d__6::MoveNext` **0x395b70**,
`PowerPotion/<OnUse>d__6::MoveNext` **0x398f44** (Power predicate
**0x398f36**), and `SkillPotion/<OnUse>d__6::MoveNext` **0x3996a8**
(Skill predicate **0x39969a**).

Each resolves the owner's pool and UnlockState, then calls
`CardFactory.GetDistinctForCombat(3, CombatCardGeneration)`. This is a full
unstable shuffle, not three draws: the exact fully unlocked solo-Ironclad
pools and counter advances are Attack **33/32**, Skill **27/26**, and Power
**18/17**; the Colorless pool is **50/49**. The bodies then await
`FromChooseACardScreen(..., canSkip=true)`. Native skip returns null after the
potion and full shuffle have been consumed, creates no card or generated
history, and still completes the normal post-potion wrapper. A choice applies
`SetToFreeThisTurn` and awaits singular
`AddGeneratedCardToCombat(Hand, owner, Bottom)`.

`CosmicConcoction/<OnUse>d__8::MoveNext` **0x395d20**, with canonical
Cards=3 at **0x257bd8**, performs one 50-card Colorless shuffle (49 draws),
then loops per card: `CardCmd.Upgrade` at **IL_0098**, followed by the
separately awaited singular generated add at **IL_00a7**, before advancing to
the next card. It never makes the cards free.
`OrobicAcid/<OnUse>d__6::MoveNext` **0x39843c**, with Attack/Skill/Power
predicates **0x39841a/0x398425/0x398430**, performs three consecutive full
shuffles on the same stream in that order (**32+26+17=75** draws), takes one
fresh L0 card from each, frees all three, then passes the list to one
`AddGeneratedCardsToCombat` call.

Full-Hand handling is evaluated per add, redirecting each overflow card to
Discard bottom. The singular/list terminal distinction is preserved: a
listener ending combat after Cosmic's first awaited add prevents the loop
from upgrading or adding/history-recording either later card. Orobic's list
wrapper passes its leading gate once, so the same listener still permits later
generated-history records while their individual pile insertions no-op.

`PotionModel.OnUseWrapper` **0x3670b4** removes the potion before its body and
defers EndCardOrPotionEffect, execution-finished history, and AfterPotionUsed
until a choice or skip resolves. Entry requires an explicit Ironclad owner,
an explicitly fully unlocked card pool, and exact
CombatCardGeneration/CombatCardSelection/CombatTargets provenance. Alchemize's
checked pool can reach exactly Attack, Colorless, Orobic, Power, and Skill
Potion, but not Cosmic Concoction, so it receives the same conservative
reachable-leaf gates. Because native `ColorlessCardPool::FilterThroughEpochs`
**0x29d3a0** independently removes the rows for each unrevealed Colorless
epoch, direct Colorless Potion, direct Cosmic Concoction, and Alchemize's
reachable Colorless Potion additionally require the recorded normalized tuple
to contain `COLORLESS1_EPOCH` through `COLORLESS5_EPOCH`. That exact tuple is
kept as Splash provenance if the Colorless shuffle yields Splash. The
Ironclad fully-unlocked flag alone is insufficient; missing or partial
Colorless rows refuse. Attack, Orobic, Power, and Skill Potion remain admitted
without this additional Colorless gate.

Coverage advances potions from **50 modeled / 14 refused** to **56 modeled /
8 refused** and aggregate accepted from **900/1063** to **906/1063**. Cards,
relics, encounters, enchantments, and certified encounters are unchanged.
Full invariant audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-28-14-batch175-generation-potions.md`.

## 2026-07-28 — Batch 177: finite relic lifetimes (#754 / #138)

Current-build evidence is **v0.109.1 / c8c577f6**, ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256

Pumpkin Candle, and Tea of Discourtesy.

Bone Tea's constructor **0x23d308** seeds `CombatsLeft=1`; its direct
