walks the captured Hand in order through one-level `CardCmd.Upgrade` calls,
then decrements. Ember Tea's constructor **0x23f23f** seeds 5; its
`AfterRoomEntered` root **0x23f1f4** and nested body **0x36cec8** require an
unused counter and CombatRoom, await owner Strength 2, then decrement. Fake
Venerable Tea Set's constructor **0x23faeb** seeds false;
`AfterRoomEntered` **0x23fa83** charges it at a rest site, while the
`AfterEnergyReset` root **0x23faa0** and nested body **0x36de78** await owner
energy gain 1 and then clear the charge.

Pumpkin Candle's constructor **0x246112** seeds zero. `AfterObtained`
**0x246087** calls `Rekindle` **0x2460fc** for +5; the KINDLE option
**0x2c1568** is the only other caller. `AfterCombatEnd` **0x2460c7**
decrements with a zero floor, and `ModifyMaxEnergy` **0x246094** adds one
while positive. Tea of Discourtesy's constructor **0x24876b** seeds
`CombatsLeft=1`; its `BeforeCombatStart` root **0x248728** and nested body
**0x37bad4** await
`AddToCombatAndPreview<Dazed>(owner, Draw, 2, owner, Random)`, then decrement.
The generic list wrapper **0x42c8a4**, singular generated wrapper
**0x42c464**, and pile-add body **0x42aa00** establish, for each fresh
owner-created Dazed in series: CardGenerated history, one
`Shuffle.NextInt(live draw size + 1)` insertion, then
AfterCardGeneratedForCombat. The second insertion sees the first; both occur
after combat-start shuffle and before SetupPlayerTurn's bottom/Innate rewrite
and opening draw.

The exact serialized properties are `CombatsLeft` (Bone, Ember,
Discourtesy), `GainEnergyInNextCombat` (Fake Tea), and `KindleCount`
(Pumpkin). JSON typed property rows and decoded MCR flat properties retain
those names. The live adapter canonicalizes decoded MCR's unprefixed
card/relic/potion/enchantment IDs and `upgrade_level` rows to the prefixed
entry form also produced from JSON's `current_upgrade_level`. Scoped
SavedProperties require the complete exact group/name/type/cardinality:
unknown groups, duplicates, cross-type/wrong-group rows, and extra fields
omit the required counter/charge so combat entry refuses. Inherited false
`IsWax` / `IsMelted` defaults may remain omitted and are never invented; a
present true flag is outside the admitted active-relic boundary. Entry accepts
only exact integers in 0..1, 0..5, 0..1, and nonnegative respectively, plus
an exact bool; missing, misnamed, wrong-type, or out-of-range state refuses
instead of using constructor defaults.
Finished-run reconstruction replays every owned combat room, including event
combats, plus ordered rest/KINDLE events. Same-node event acquisition retains
both grant/fight orders and emits a counter only after the candidates
converge.

room-entry Strength seam, including Ruined Helmet's distinct-amount order
refusal. Fake Tea uses the ordinary no-energy-gain modifier and clears after

while charged; its post-combat decrement is reconstructed at the next
independently grounded fight entry. Active Bone refuses unrecorded
same-AfterPlayerTurnStart relic order except Bellows, whose clipped sequential
upgrades commute. Active Discourtesy refuses Snecko Eye or Fake Snecko Eye
because unrecorded BeforeCombatStart relic order determines whether the new
Dazed receive Confused costs; a used-up counter is inert. Discourtesy alone
joins the prior-fight draw-cycle caveat inventory because `.run` omits the
later play/exhaust timing of its two generated Status cards.

## 2026-07-28 — Batch 178: survive-lethal / death retention (#215)

Current-build evidence is **v0.109.1 / c8c577f6**, ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`.
This batch converts exactly Fairy in a Bottle, Lizard Tail, and the Waterfall
Giant boss. Test Subject remains refused behind #216.

`CreatureCmd.Damage` root **0x2ddb04**, nested body **0x432a14**, collects
lethal results and routes them through `Kill(false)`. The core
`KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition` body **0x43511c** runs `BeforeDeath`, then
`Hook.ShouldDie` **0x2b24f0**. That hook completes the entire ordinary
`ShouldDie` pass before starting `ShouldDieLate`; the first false listener is
the sole preventer. The prevented branch broadcasts
`AfterDeath(wasRemovalPrevented=true, deathAnimLength=0)` through root
**0x2afac8** / body **0x416a84**, then dispatches only that still-present
preventer through `AfterPreventingDeath` root **0x2b07a8** / body
**0x419a24**. The actual-death branch freezes the removal veto through
`ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath` **0x2b2498**, broadcasts
`AfterDeath(false)` before removal/power pruning, and consults combat-end veto
`ShouldStopCombatFromEnding` **0x2b29c8**.

Fairy in a Bottle is passive (`get_Usage` **0x2580de** = 3).
`ShouldDie` **0x25812b** rejects death only for its owner. Its selected
preventer body **0x396bd8** calls `PotionModel.OnUseWrapper`; the wrapper body
**0x3670b4** calls `RemoveBeforeUse` **0x22f587** before the effect. `OnUse`
body **0x396ca8** then heals `max(MaxHp * 0.3, 1)`. The simulator removes the
first exact occupied Fairy slot before healing; dense legacy belts remove the
first matching entry. Passive Fairy is never offered as a manual action, and
a forged manual use refuses before mutation.

Lizard Tail's `ShouldDieLate` **0x24276c** returns false only for the unused
owner relic. Its selected preventer body **0x3725b0** sets saved
`WasUsed=true` through setter **0x24274e** before healing
`max(1, MaxHp * 50 / 100)`. Because Fairy's ordinary pass completes first,
one lethal consumes Fairy alone; a later lethal may consume Tail. The
`WasUsed` bool is keyed and reconstructed from exact JSON/MCR SavedProperties
for live saves. Finished `.run` files can prove false only before the first
owned combat; later owned fights omit the seed and refuse rather than infer
whether it fired.

Waterfall Giant HP is **250** at A8+ / 240 below (**0x27093f**). Its
deterministic machine **0x270af4** is PRESSURIZE → STOMP → RAM → SIPHON →
PRESSURE_GUN → PRESSURE_UP → STOMP. The current A9+ values are Stomp 16, Ram
11, Pressure Up 14, Pressure Gun 23 increasing by 5; Siphon heals 15 at A8+.
PRESSURIZE applies `SteamEruptionPower` 20 at A9+; Stomp, Ram, Siphon,
Pressure Gun, and Pressure Up each add exactly 3 after their primary effect
(bodies **0x3bf34c**, **0x3befc4**, **0x3bf154**, **0x3beb1c**,
**0x3becc0**). Mutable pressure, gun damage, buildup index, saved eruption
damage, and phase flag are all memo-keyed. Siphon healing is included in the
exact move transition; Fairy/Tail remaining heals are included in the I3
ceiling and Fairy's banked-potion objective value without double counting.

Steam Eruption is actual death retention, not a `ShouldDie` veto.
`SteamEruptionPower` returns true from combat-end veto **0x254547**, false for
owner removal at **0x25454a**, and false for death pruning at **0x254558**.
Its `AfterDeath(false)` body **0x38f7b0** calls Giant transition body
**0x3bf55c**, which sets `IsAboutToBlow`, sets current/max HP to 999,999,999,
and forces ABOUT_TO_BLOW. That no-attack move body **0x3be7c0** snapshots and
removes the Steam amount, then sets buildup to 7. EXPLODE body **0x3be990**
attacks for the snapshot and calls `Kill(self,false)`; with Steam removed,
the second death is removable and terminal.

Test Subject is deliberately not generalized from this seam.
`AdaptablePower.AfterDeath(false)` body **0x37df88** retains an unhittable
dead owner and calls `TriggerDeadState` **0x3b7910**. Respawn body
**0x3b70fc** advances combat-local `Respawns`, toggles `DoRevive` before HP
restoration, enters 200/212 and 300/313 HP forms, and applies/removes
PainfulStabs, Nemesis, and Adaptable in form-specific order. Retained-dead
scheduling, three-form continuation, and staged power state remain refused
under #216.

Coverage advances exactly one encounter, one relic, and one potion:
encounters **44 modeled / 29 refused**, relics **277 / 23**, potions
**57 / 7**, and aggregate accepted **920/1063**. Full invariant audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-28-21-batch178-survive-lethal.md`.

(**0x36b544**). The second successor is
`PHASE3_LACERATE_MOVE` (**11×3**, **0x36b65c**) → `BIG_POUNCE_MOVE`
(**45**, **0x36b140**) → `BURNING_GROWL_MOVE` (five Burns to discard-bottom,

## 2026-07-31 — Batch 185: Meat on the Bone victory projection (#759)

Current-build evidence is **v0.109.1 / c8c577f6**, ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`.
The installed and archived DLLs are byte-identical.

`MeatOnTheBone::get_CanonicalVars` **0x242d0a** supplies
`HpThreshold=50` and `Heal=12`. `WillHealOnCombatFinished` **0x242dd4**
converts `Decimal(MaxHp * 50 / 100)` to `int` and compares
`CurrentHp <= threshold`, so the positive-HP threshold is inclusive and odd
maximum HP truncates down. `BeforeCombatStart` **0x242d3a** and
`AfterCurrentHpChanged` **0x242d50** only maintain the display status; the
latter requires the exact owner and an in-progress combat.

The mechanical writer is `AfterCombatVictoryEarly` root/body
**0x242d90/0x373bfc**. It returns when the owner is dead, re-reads the
threshold predicate, clears the status, and awaits `Heal(12, true)`, whose
ordinary command caps at maximum HP. Global `Hook.AfterCombatVictory`
root/body **0x2af800/0x4160f0** completes the Early listener pass before its
ordinary victory-listener pass. `CombatManager.EndCombatInternal` root/body
**0x2e1758/0x43c720** performs combat-end cleanup and `AfterCombatEnd` before
calling that victory hook. Meat on the Bone is the only current-build relic
overriding `AfterCombatVictoryEarly`.

The solver therefore keeps ownership as an immutable fight-entry constant
but does not fire the heal in the combat state machine. At a true living-owner
victory, terminal evaluation projects exactly one inclusive-threshold,
maximum-HP-capped heal. Losses, nonterminal states, and forced endings with a
living enemy retain live HP. The projected value is used consistently by
exact search, rollout terminal scoring, returned score, and `stats.final_hp`;
the underlying terminal `State` remains unchanged.

Chosen Cheese is the exact excluded composition. Its `AfterCombatEnd`
root/body **0x23e4e4/0x36b2f4** awaits `GainMaxHp(1)`, raising both current
and maximum HP before the victory hook. Thus 40/80 becomes 41/81 and no
longer satisfies Meat's floor-40 threshold, while 39/80 becomes 40/81 and
still heals. Applying Meat to the pre-Cheese pair can reverse rankings, so
co-ownership is rejected at fight entry and again at the I3/objective
boundaries. The tracked Cheese provenance is immutable; malformed provenance
also refuses.

I3's final-HP ceiling reserves 12 HP whenever the relic is owned. This
deliberately over-bounds lines that ultimately win above the threshold, which
can only weaken pruning. The exact terminal projection matters for ordering:
at 41/80 HP against a six-HP target, Strike wins at 41 and receives no heal,
while Hemokinesis first pays two HP, wins at 39, and projects to 51; exact
search must choose the latter when Chosen Cheese is absent. Duplicate
ownership, non-boolean ownership provenance, and the Cheese composition fail
closed.

Full invariant audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-31-28-batch185-meat-on-the-bone.md`.
## 2026-07-31 — Batch 185 proof-first relic closure (#773, #774, #775)

All three relics remain **REFUSED**, with their routing narrowed from generic
template failures to exact engine work. Current-build evidence is
**v0.109.1 / c8c577f6**, ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`.
The installed and archived DLLs are byte-identical. Each root type and every
transitively nested compiler-generated type were freshly re-dumped.

### Brilliant Scarf — retained refusal, engine route #773

`BrilliantScarf::get_CanonicalVars` **0x23d95a** supplies `CardsVar(5)`.
The relic owns mutable `_cardsPlayedThisTurn`; its setter
**0x23d96f** asserts mutability, stores the value, and updates display only.
Owner `BeforeSideTurnStart` **0x23d9f5** resets it to zero, and
`AfterCombatEnd` **0x23da77** clears it again.

`AfterCardPlayed` **0x23da1c** returns outside combat, for every
`CardPlay.IsAutoPlay`, and when `card.Owner` is not the relic owner. Every
remaining completed CardPlay increments the counter once. Replay iterations
therefore count, while direct/draw/Sly AutoPlay iterations do not. This is not
the existing `owner_card_plays_finished_this_turn` projection, which records
every completed owner play including AutoPlay, nor Velvet Choker's likewise
AutoPlay-inclusive private count.

`ShouldModifyCost` **0x23da88** requires all of: combat in progress; exact
owner-creature identity; counter equal to `CardsVar.BaseValue - 1`, hence
exactly four; and the physical card currently in pile type 2 (Hand) or 5
(Play). A null pile and Draw/Discard/Exhaust cards do not qualify.
`TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate` **0x23d9bd** and `TryModifyStarCost`
**0x23d9d9** first copy the incoming Decimal to the out parameter, then set it
to zero and return true only under that shared predicate.

The Energy hook is the absolute-zero Late phase after every Early modifier in
`Hook::ModifyEnergyCostInCombat` **0x2b13e8**. `CardEnergyCost::
GetWithModifiers` **0x2c9ea4** returns before all hooks for X and
negative-base Energy costs, runs local rows before the hook walk, and clamps
after it. Thus Scarf overrides Tangled/Borrowed Time/Spiked Gauntlets and
local positive costs, and commutes with the existing absolute-zero Late
powers; it does not free Energy-X or negative-base cards. Fixed Star costs use
`CardModel::GetStarCostWithModifiers` **0x229f40** and
`Hook::ModifyStarCost` **0x2b200c**; Star-X returns the live Stars pool before
that hook, and a negative fixed Star cost returns unchanged.

Exact admission therefore needs a new keyed manual-play-only turn counter,
both live cost readers, the completed-play increment/reset sites, physical
pile/owner validation, clone/key coverage, and same-hook composition pins.
The content registry and generated relic-template vocabulary can express none
of those stateful reads/writes. Adding membership alone would silently ignore
the relic, so the proof-first content lane stops without a walk or coverage
change.

### Delicate Frond — retained refusal, engine route #774

`BeforeCombatStart` root/body **0x23e994/0x36beb8** flashes, then enters a
live loop. Each iteration calls
`Owner.RunState.Rng.CombatPotionGeneration`, creates one random potion with
`PotionFactory::CreateRandomPotionOutOfCombat` **0x2bee30**, converts it to a
mutable object, and awaits `PotionCmd::TryToProcure(potion, owner, -1)`. It
loops only when that result succeeded **and** the owner's
`HasOpenPotionSlots` remains true; otherwise it returns.

The generator delegates to `CreateRandomPotionsOutOfCombat` **0x2bee40** and
`CreateRandomPotions` **0x2beeb8**. It materializes the owner's unlocked
character pool followed by the unlocked shared pool
(`GetPotionOptions` **0x2bef46**) with **no**
`CanBeGeneratedInCombat` filter. Each generated potion consumes exactly two
CombatPotionGeneration draws: one `NextFloat(1)` rarity roll (Rare at
`<= 0.10000000149`, Uncommon at `<= 0.34999999404`, otherwise Common), then
one `NextItem` from that materialized rarity partition. Because every loop
iteration is a fresh count-one factory call, successive slots may receive
the same potion.

`Player::get_HasOpenPotionSlots` **0x2c2789** is exactly
`_potionSlots.Any(slot == null)`; occupied modeled and inert potions are both
non-null. `PotionCmd/<TryToProcure>d__1::MoveNext` **0x438850** first runs
`Hook::ShouldProcurePotion` **0x2b2918** (Sozu is the sole current veto), then
calls `Player::AddPotionInternal` **0x2c35fc**. Slot `-1` selects the first
null slot and fails when none exists. A success records history and serially
awaits `Hook::AfterPotionProcured`; Belt Buckle is the sole current
post-success listener and removes its applied Dexterity when the belt becomes
nonempty.

Consequently a non-Sozu entry with `n > 0` exact null slots generates and
procures exactly `n` potions and consumes `2n` draws. A full belt still
generates one potion and consumes two draws before procurement fails. Sozu
likewise consumes two draws before its first procurement is vetoed. Exact
capacity, sparse slot order, inert identities, unlocked out-of-combat pool,
stream counter, procurement result, and Belt Buckle latch all matter.

The solver already carries exact fixed-length potion slots and
CombatPotionGeneration state, but its only generation dispatcher is the
single in-combat Alchemize path over the 45-item combat-eligible pool. Relic
templates cannot generate a potion, loop on a live procurement result,
advance that stream, mutate the slot tuple/mirrors, or await
AfterPotionProcured. This requires a shared pre-action engine dispatcher and
atomic admission, so no walk or coverage change is claimed here.

### Petrified Toad — retained refusal, engine route #775

`BeforeCombatStartLate` root/body **0x2455a0/0x377314** has no guard or RNG.
It flashes, awaits exactly one
`PotionCmd::TryToProcure<PotionShapedRock>(owner)`, discards the
`PotionProcureResult`, and returns. The generic wrapper body
**0x438774** creates one mutable canonical potion and delegates to the same
`TryToProcure(..., -1)` body above. `PotionShapedRock` is the already-modeled
enemy-targeted, blockable, unpowered 15-damage potion; its body is
**0x398c38**.

`Hook/<BeforeCombatStart>d__18::MoveNext` **0x41b674** completes the entire
ordinary `BeforeCombatStart` listener walk before it takes a fresh listener
snapshot for every `BeforeCombatStartLate` callback. Petrified Toad is the
only current relic overriding the Late method. Therefore Delicate Frond, if
co-owned, completes its early generation/procurement loop before Toad tries
the fixed rock. Sozu can veto the attempt; a full belt makes it fail; a
success fills the first null slot and then runs Belt Buckle's exact
AfterPotionProcured removal. The attempt itself consumes no RNG.

The lower-level fixed potion, slot tuple, Sozu gate, and Belt Buckle
procurement response are present, but the simulator has no Late
combat-start relic fire point or content-template step that invokes
procurement. Treating it as an ordinary BeforeCombatStart template would
erase its proven phase order, especially against Delicate Frond. It remains
refused until a small shared engine registration/dispatch change wires that
exact phase; no walk or coverage delta is taken.

The reviewed refusal ledger now names #773–#775 directly so clean template
regeneration cannot return these items to a blind content scout. Relic
coverage receives no delta from these three proof tracks. With Meat on the
Bone integrated above, Batch 185 closes at **292 modeled / 7 refused /
299 eligible**, and aggregate accepted coverage is **935/1062**.

## Batch 186 — Ambergris and Pael's Eye extra-player-turn sequencer

Current-build authority is v0.109.1/c8c577f6, ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`.

`CombatManager/<SwitchFromPlayerToEnemySide>d__138::MoveNext` **0x44059c**
locks the combat, clears `_playersTakingExtraTurn`, and snapshots every player
for whom `Hook.ShouldTakeExtraTurn` **0x2b2a20** returns true. It then awaits
`SwitchSides` **0x2e1ba0**. With a nonempty snapshot, SwitchSides keeps the
current side as Player, increments only the snapshotted players'
`PlayerCombatState.TurnNumber`, does not increment
`CombatState.RoundNumber`, and still runs the creature side-switch/turn-ended
callbacks. The caller next serially awaits every listener through
`Hook/<AfterTakingExtraTurn>d__79::MoveNext` **0x41ad50**, then enters the
ordinary full `StartTurn`/`SetupPlayerTurn` path. The simulator consequently
keys owner `turn` and `round_number` separately and branches only after the
complete player-side end graph; an extra turn skips the enemy phase but not
the next owner turn's block/energy/draw/hook setup.

`Ambergris/<OnUse>d__9::MoveNext` **0x394db8** first heals the selected target
by `floor(MaxHp * 50 / 100)`, then, only while combat remains in progress,
applies `AmbergrisPower(1)`. The power is invisible and additive.
`ShouldTakeExtraTurn` **0x24b900** requires positive Amount and the queried
player to equal its owner. Its nested
`<AfterTakingExtraTurn>d__7::MoveNext` **0x37e3e8** decrements exactly one
stack for the owner. Each unspent potion therefore enters both the I3 healing
ceiling and potion-bank objective at 50% Max HP; drinking stacks one extra
turn after the heal. AnyAlly selection remains solo-only and fails before
belt removal when a real pet/player choice exists.

`PaelsEye.ShouldTakeExtraTurn` **0x2443ae** requires all of: unused this
combat, no qualifying owner manual `CardPlayFinished` in the current history
window, owner participation in the preceding player side, and queried-player
owner identity. `AnyCardsPlayedThisTurn` **0x244468** ignores AutoPlay and
has the exact Whispering Earring exception on owner TurnNumber 1.
`BeforeCardPlayed` **0x2442e4** excludes AutoPlay and non-owner cards.
`AfterSideTurnStart` **0x244344** refreshes the owner-participation latch
while unused. `AfterTakingExtraTurn` **0x244427** marks the relic used for
every owner extra turn, even when another listener (Ambergris) supplied it.

The Pael early side-end wrapper is **0x2443d4** and its nested body is
**0x375820**. Under the same qualification predicate it freezes the live Hand
with `ToList`, then serially awaits `CardCmd.Exhaust(card, false, false)` for
each captured physical card. Player powers complete first; Pael's relic
listener precedes ordinary relic turn-end listeners and `DoTurnEnd`. A keyed
`PaelsEyeEndFrame` preserves the remaining frozen UIDs and the earlier
Orichalcum latches across nested Dark Embrace/Joss/Hellraiser pauses. Newly
drawn cards are absent from Pael's frozen list but remain live for the later
ordinary turn-end snapshots/flush.

The two extra-turn listeners compose without an order ambiguity. If either
qualifies, the shared player snapshot contains the owner once. The complete
AfterTaking listener walk then decrements one Ambergris stack (when present)
and marks Pael used (when owned); the writes commute. Multiple Ambergris
stacks can therefore grant consecutive extra owner turns, one stack per
completed player side. Pael grants at most one per combat. Real multiplayer
extra-turn snapshots remain fail-closed because teammate turn advancement is
not represented.

## Batch 187 — Delicate Frond and Petrified Toad entry procurement

Current-build authority is v0.109.1/c8c577f6, ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`.
The installed and archived DLLs are byte-identical.

Delicate Frond's `BeforeCombatStart` root/body **0x23e994/0x36beb8**
flashes, then executes a live do-while loop. Each attempt obtains
`Owner.RunState.Rng.CombatPotionGeneration`, calls
`PotionFactory::CreateRandomPotionOutOfCombat` **0x2bee30**, converts the
result to a mutable potion, and awaits
`PotionCmd::TryToProcure(potion, owner, -1)`. It repeats only after a
successful procurement when `Player::get_HasOpenPotionSlots` **0x2c2789**
still finds a null slot.

`CreateRandomPotionOutOfCombat` delegates through
`CreateRandomPotionsOutOfCombat` **0x2bee40** to
`CreateRandomPotions` **0x2beeb8**. `GetPotionOptions` **0x2bef46**
materializes the unlocked character pool followed by the unlocked shared
pool, without the in-combat `CanBeGeneratedInCombat` filter. The attested
fully unlocked solo Ironclad census is therefore 48 stable identities:
16 Common, 16 Uncommon, and 16 Rare. Relative to Alchemize's 45-item pool,
the exact additional leaves are Fairy in a Bottle, Fruit Juice, and Regen
Potion. Every attempt consumes a `NextFloat(1)` rarity draw and one
`NextItem` draw from the selected stable partition. The rarity thresholds
are Rare at `<= float32(0.1)`, Uncommon at `<= float32(0.35)`, otherwise
Common. Fresh count-one factory calls allow duplicates between slots.

`PotionCmd/<TryToProcure>d__1::MoveNext` **0x438850** first asks
`Hook::ShouldProcurePotion` **0x2b2918**; Sozu is the sole current veto. It
then inserts through `Player::AddPotionInternal` **0x2c35fc**, where `-1`
means the first null slot, and serially awaits `Hook::AfterPotionProcured`
on success. Belt Buckle's listener **0x41952c** removes its applied two
Dexterity after the first successful insertion. Thus `n` open slots consume
exactly `2n` draws and fill in slot order; a full belt or Sozu still consumes
two draws before the first failed procurement.

Petrified Toad's `BeforeCombatStartLate` root/body
**0x2455a0/0x377314** has no predicate or RNG. It flashes, awaits exactly one
generic `TryToProcure<PotionShapedRock>(owner)`, discards the result, and
returns. The generic fixed wrapper **0x438774** creates the canonical potion
and enters the same `TryToProcure(..., -1)` body. Potion Shaped Rock's
already-modeled enemy-targeted, blockable, unpowered 15-damage body is
**0x398c38**.

`Hook/<BeforeCombatStart>d__18::MoveNext` **0x41b674** completes the full
ordinary listener walk before taking the distinct Late listener snapshot.
The simulator consequently completes Frond and every admitted ordinary
entry peer before attempting Toad. If Frond filled the belt, Toad fails
without RNG; if a null remains because Frond was absent, Toad fills the first
one unless Sozu vetoes. The ordinary peers other than Belt Buckle mutate
disjoint block, power, pet, or card state. Belt Buckle commutes in final
state with Frond's placement within the ordinary pass: success removes an
earlier latch, while failure leaves the empty-belt application intact.

Admission requires exact positive slot capacity and sparse slot topology.
Frond additionally requires the current-build stream counter, explicit
fully unlocked solo Ironclad pool provenance, and non-mixed card piles
because reachable Gambler's Brew and Ashwater actions require physical
selection. Real multiplayer owners fail closed. A clone preflight makes
strict rejection of an unmodeled generated leaf atomic. No new keyed field
is needed: the existing potion slot tuple, dense modeled/inert mirrors,
Belt Buckle latch, Sozu flag, and `potion_generation` state cover every
mutation. The v0.109 stream reconstruction now explicitly preserves the
64-bit build-specific seed for CombatPotionGeneration and every reachable
downstream named stream (CombatCardSelection, CombatTargets,
CombatEnergyCosts, CombatCardGeneration, and MonsterAi), rather than passing
those already-derived seeds through the legacy 32-bit-default constructor.

## Batch 188 — Blessed Antler and Toasty Mittens BeforeHandDraw relics

Current-build authority is v0.109.1/c8c577f6, ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`.
The installed and archived DLLs are byte-identical.

Blessed Antler's canonical getter **0x23cf55** supplies Energy 1 and Cards 3.
`ModifyMaxEnergy` **0x23cf98** owner-gates and adds the Energy variable. Its
`BeforeHandDraw` wrapper is **0x23cfc0** and the sole nested async body
`<BeforeHandDraw>d__7::MoveNext` is **0x369360**. The body owner-gates,
requires owner TurnNumber 1, flashes, constructs one list containing three
separately created owner L0 Dazed CardModels, and awaits exactly one
`CardPileCmd.AddGeneratedCardsToCombat` at IL **0x009d** with Draw (pile 1)
and Random (position 3). It previews the returned results and performs only a
cosmetic wait afterward.

Pile 1 is the already-pinned `PileType.Draw` enum value (the same
Draw/Random pair used by Soulbound), not Hand. Each successful nested Add
consumes one owner Shuffle `NextInt(0, live Draw count + 1)` and inserts the
fresh physical card at that index. Draw insertion has no Hand-cap check and
no overflow destination. The list wrapper performs its in-progress/empty
gate once:
after a generated-card listener ends combat, later pre-created entries still
record CardGenerated and run their failed nested Adds without another Shuffle
draw or pile insertion. All three object identities are allocated before the
list begins, preserving creation order across recursively generated cards.
The existing Arsenal, Soulbound, Regalite, and Rocket Punch listener pipeline
runs after each successful insertion. A `BeforeHandDrawRelicFrame` plus the
existing `GeneratedCardRelicFrame` returns from a suspended Regalite block to
the exact remaining list index.

Toasty Mittens' canonical getter **0x248afb** supplies Strength 1. The async
wrapper is **0x248b40**; its sole nested body
`<BeforeHandDraw>d__6::MoveNext` is **0x37be78**, and predicate lambda
`<>c::<BeforeHandDraw>b__6_0` is **0x37be66**. After the exact owner gate it
awaits `CardPileCmd.ShuffleIfNecessary` at IL **0x005b**. On turn 1 it chooses
the first live Draw card whose effective keyword set lacks enum value 3 in
the nested predicate. Enum value 3 is the already-pinned `Innate` value
(SetupPlayerTurn and Arsenal's `AddKeyword(3)` independently anchor it); if
none exists it falls back to the first Draw card. The native predicate reads
the CardModel's live `get_Keywords` collection, mirrored by
`card_effective_keywords`: canonical Innate, local/transient keyword grants,
and Royally Approved's enchant-time Innate addition all participate, while
Ethereal is irrelevant. On
later turns it takes the first Draw card directly. Empty Draw returns without
another command. A selected exact CardModel is awaited through
`CardCmd.Exhaust(card, false, false)` at IL **0x011b**, then the body awaits
owner `StrengthPower(1)` at IL **0x01a6**. Thus the move/history and complete
AfterCardExhausted power/relic/card-listener walk precede Strength; an ending
combat suppresses the final PowerCmd.

The simulator reuses StableShuffle, Perfect Fit's pre-commit reorder, and the
complete power-before-relic AfterShuffle dispatch. A blocking Stratagem
selection parks on the Mittens frame and resumes the relic tail before the
live Draw choice. The exact selected UID is removed from Draw before Exhaust.
Dark Embrace and Joss Paper can each park their own Draw frame above the
Mittens frame; only after those awaited listener chains unwind does Mittens
apply Strength and continue the remaining BeforeHandDraw card listeners and
ordinary turn-start hand draw.

Player powers are a fixed earlier listener group and physical combat-pile
listeners are a fixed later group. Relic acquisition order is not present in
the run/MCR entry, so Antler or Mittens co-ownership with any other modeled
BeforeHandDraw relic (including each other) refuses before entry mutation:
their random insertion, shuffle/exhaust, generated hooks, counters, and
terminal gates do not generally commute. Ownership flags are local-player
constants; represented teammates are unchanged. Prior-fight ownership of
either relic now surfaces a Shuffle-counter caveat because Antler consumes
three immediate random-position draws and changes cycle membership, while
Mittens can reshuffle and exhaust one Draw card every owner turn.

Coverage advances relics from **295 modeled / 4 refused** to
**297 modeled / 2 refused** and aggregate accepted from **939/1062** to
**941/1062**. Full invariant audit:

Current-build authority is v0.109.1/c8c577f6, ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256

`BrilliantScarf::get_CanonicalVars` **0x23d95a** supplies `CardsVar(5)`.
The mutable private counter getter/setter are **0x23d967/0x23d96f**.
`BeforeSideTurnStart` **0x23d9f5** resets the counter whenever the owner
participates. `AfterCardPlayed` **0x23da1c** first requires combat in
progress, rejects `CardPlay.IsAutoPlay`, and owner-gates the played card,
then increments exactly once. Each ordinary replay iteration is a separate
non-AutoPlay completed CardPlay and therefore counts. `AfterCombatEnd`
**0x23da77** clears the value again; terminal combat state has no later cost
observation.

The already-keyed `manual_card_plays_finished_this_turn` history projection
introduced by Batch 186 is exactly that observable counter during live
combat: it advances at CardPlayFinished for owner non-AutoPlay iterations and
resets at every owner side switch, including extra turns. It deliberately
does not use `owner_card_plays_finished_this_turn`, Velvet Choker, or Sloth,
all of which include AutoPlay or count at a different seam. Scarf ownership
is an immutable per-fight constant; the shared manual count remains mutable
and auto-keyed.

`ShouldModifyCost` **0x23da88** requires combat in progress, exact owner
creature identity, counter exactly `CardsVar.BaseValue - Decimal.One` (four),
and the queried physical CardModel currently in pile type 2 or 5. The pinned
pile enum cross-checks are Hand=2 and Play=5. Null, Draw, Discard, and Exhaust
do not qualify. Solver production reads carry immutable `PhysicalCard` UIDs;
an identity-less or missing-pile cost query at the firing boundary raises
instead of selecting an equal-payload duplicate. Manual SpendResources
retains an explicit exact-Hand transit provenance between the solver's Hand
removal and Play insertion.

`TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate` **0x23d9bd** copies its incoming Decimal,
calls the shared predicate, and on success replaces the out value with zero.
`CardEnergyCost::GetWithModifiers` **0x2c9ea4** returns before every hook for
Energy-X and negative base costs, applies ordered local rows, then
`Hook::ModifyEnergyCostInCombat` **0x2b13e8** walks every Early listener
before every Late listener and finally clamps nonnegative. Scarf therefore
overrides Tangled, Borrowed Time, Spiked Gauntlets, and positive local rows.
Its absolute zero commutes with Corruption and the Free-power Late family;
Energy-X and negative-base cards bypass it.

`TryModifyStarCost` **0x23d9d9** has the same copy/predicate/absolute-zero
shape. `CardModel::GetStarCostWithModifiers` **0x229f40** returns the live
Stars pool immediately for Star-X. Fixed combat-pile costs instead pass the
last ordered temporary Star row into `Hook::ModifyStarCost` **0x2b200c**,
which returns negative inputs before its listener walk. Scarf thus zeros any
nonnegative fixed Star cost after temporary rows, while Star-X and the native
no-Star-cost negative sentinel bypass it.

Relic acquisition order is absent from `.run` entry. Scarf's counter write
commutes with ordinary completed-play effects except Mummified Hand: on a
fourth manual Power, whether Scarf increments before Mummified constructs its
cost-sensitive four candidate pools can change the selected pool and RNG
result. That pair is refused atomically. The existing Iron Club/Tuning Fork
same-hook peer gate likewise refuses their unrecorded acquisition-order
composition with Scarf. Duplicate forged Scarf ownership and malformed
counter/identity provenance also fail closed.

Coverage advances relics from **297 modeled / 2 refused** to
**298 modeled / 1 refused** and aggregate accepted from **941/1062** to
**942/1062**. Full invariant audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-31-32-batch189-brilliant-scarf.md`.

## Batch 190 — Fur Coat exact marked-fight HP command

Current-build authority is v0.109.1/c8c577f6, ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`.

Fur Coat's canonical Combats variable is 7 at **0x240142**. `AfterObtained`
**0x240159** stores the current act index and invokes `AddMarkedRooms`
**0x240198**. That map writer returns when the current act differs from the
stored act. If the stored coordinate projection is absent or invalid, it
enumerates Monster/Elite map points that do not already contain the Fur Coat
quest, creates `Rng(owner, relicId, 0)`, unstable-shuffles the eligible
points, takes seven, writes parallel `FurCoatCoordCols` and
`FurCoatCoordRows` arrays, sets `FurCoatCoordsSet`, and adds the quest. A
valid saved projection re-adds the quest at every stored coordinate; a
missing coordinate is an exception, not a fallback. `GetMarkedCoords`
**0x240464** returns null unless the latch is true and otherwise reconstructs
the parallel arrays index-for-index. `ModifyGeneratedMapLate` **0x24018d**
is the only later map-writing hook.

`BeforeCombatStart` **0x2403d4**, nested body **0x36e85c**, performs exact
current-coordinate membership. On a match it marks the completed-history
player-stat bit, snapshots `HittableEnemies`, and serially awaits
`CreatureCmd.SetCurrentHp(1)` for every member. The generic command's nested
body is **0x435eb0**: current HP becomes `min(amount, max HP)`, it dispatches
AfterCurrentHpChanged only when the supplied amount differs from the old
value, and only then performs its ordinary death check. The admitted enemy
AfterCurrentHpChanged overrides are cosmetic hurt/display hooks for this
positive assignment, so the simulator preserves the exact HP/max-HP
projection without inventing a gameplay listener.

`AfterCreatureAddedToCombat` **0x240418**, nested body **0x36e734**, first
requires side enum 2 (Enemy), repeats the exact coordinate membership, and
awaits the same SetCurrentHp command. It has no combat-ending predicate. The
complete currently modeled enemy-addition census is Wriggler creation,
Axebot stock respawn (a new Creature UID on the singular model), Obscura
illusion creation, Living Fog Gas Bomb creation, and Two-Tailed Rat backup.
Each dispatches Fur Coat exactly once after insertion. Owner/Osty summons are
not Enemy-side additions. Segmented and Illusion revival/reattachment paths
reuse an existing Creature and never redispatch. A later enemy addition is
therefore set to 1 HP even after combat has begun ending; Philosopher's
Stone's nested PowerCmd remains independently suppressed by its own ending
gate. The two effects commute on every admitted live state.

Completed `.run` history is the authoritative historical boundary: each
fight reads only its own `is_affected_by_fur_coat` player-stat bool. The
endpoint relic props are never backfilled across earlier fights. Live JSON
saves and decoded MCR snapshots instead validate the complete saved-property
shape (`FurCoatActIndex`, both coordinate arrays, and `FurCoatCoordsSet`),
allow only inherited false `IsWax`/`IsMelted` defaults, validate seven
parallel integer coordinates when complete, and derive membership from the
exact current visited coordinate. Missing, partial, mixed-type, duplicate,
or malformed provenance remains unknown and an owned Fur Coat refuses before
combat mutation. Multiplayer is rejected at the existing single-player
adapter boundary.

The exact marked-fight bool is preserved by clone and deliberately remains
in memo identity. Fur Coat consumes no combat RNG and changes no piles,
choices, resources, ownership, or cross-combat counter. Its map-selection RNG
is already resolved into the saved coordinate provenance before the solver's
combat window.

Coverage advances relics from **298 modeled / 1 refused** to

The global `Hook/<AfterSideTurnEnd>d__81::MoveNext` **0x41a2c0** walks the

Scalar state does not retain relative application order among player powers.
Every nonterminal peer commutes except two exact frontiers. Lethal player
Doom before Ritual suppresses the ending-gated Strength command, while
Ritual-first changes keyed Strength before Doom kills. Dark Embrace's
Ethereal draw under Hellraiser can replay attacks whose damage changes if
Ritual fired first. Both co-occurrences refuse before the side-end flush;
NoDraw removal, Hellraiser's counter reset, retained-hand/shrink ticks, and
temporary-power expiry commute and remain admitted. Joss/Hellraiser is not
ambiguous because all player powers, including Ritual, precede the relic.

The only new persistent state is nonnegative integer `player_ritual`; it is
automatically cloned and memo-keyed. Malformed bool, negative, fractional,
string, or null values refuse before potion removal or direct turn-end phase
mutation. Exact potion slots remove only the selected copy, the body finishes
before Belt Buckle/Reptile Trinket, and all six combat RNG streams remain
unchanged except RNG independently consumed by later peers such as Parrying
Shield.

The checked Alchemize pool remains RNG-identical but its reachable Mazaleth's
Gift leaf changes from refused to modeled; the remaining generated refusal
caveat is four. Coverage advances potions from **59 modeled / 5 refused** to
**60 modeled / 4 refused** and aggregate accepted from **944/1062** to
**945/1062**. Full invariant audit:

Current-build authority is v0.109.1/c8c577f6, ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`.
The installed and archived DLLs are byte-identical. All RVAs below were
freshly re-dumped from that installed DLL; they supersede the stale v0.108
addresses and unresolved ordering claim in the historical P3 refusal.

`GigantificationPotion.get_Rarity/get_Usage/get_TargetType` are
**0x2587bf/0x2587c2/0x2587c5** (Rare, Active, enum value 5).
`PotionModel.IsValidTarget` **0x22f60c** first rejects dead creatures and its
value-5 branch returns `target.IsPlayer`; `AssertValidForTargetedPotion`
**0x22f759** enforces the pick. Osty is never offered. The supported local
player is represented by target `None`; a forged non-`None` value refuses
before belt mutation because it can denote another player outside the solo
quotient.

`get_CanonicalVars` **0x2587c8** constructs
`PowerVar<GigantificationPower>(1)`. `OnUse` is **0x2587dc** and its complete
nested body `<OnUse>d__8::MoveNext` is **0x397a2c**. It validates the selected
player and awaits exactly
`PowerCmd.Apply<GigantificationPower>(target, 1, owner.Creature, null, false)`.
There is no second gameplay command and no RNG.

`GigantificationPower.get_Type/get_StackType` are
**0x24ee63/0x24ee66** (Buff/Intensity). `InitInternalData` **0x24ee69** creates
the private `Data` object whose constructor is **0x384c2e** and whose sole
gameplay member is `commandToModify`. `BeforeAttack` **0x24ee70** requires an
AttackCommand whose `ModelSource` is an Attack `CardModel`, whose card owner
creature equals the power owner, and whose damage props are powered. It writes
the exact AttackCommand only while `commandToModify` is null. It does not
require the command attacker itself to equal the owner: `AttackCommand.FromCard`
**0x2dffcc** preserves the player-owned CardModel source, so a FromOsty attack
from that physical card is eligible.

`ModifyDamageMultiplicative` **0x24eef0** repeats the player-owned card and
powered gates. While a command is bound, another CardModel source returns one;
the bound source returns Decimal three. Thus all hits and all targets inside
the same AttackCommand receive x3, independent of the power Amount. `AfterAttack`
is **0x24ef5c** and its complete nested body
`<AfterAttack>d__8::MoveNext` is **0x384c38**. Only exact object identity with
`commandToModify` qualifies; it clears the member, then awaits one
`PowerCmd.Decrement`. Intensity stacks therefore provide one future command
each, never a `3 * Amount` multiplier.

The complete `AttackCommand/<Execute>d__90::MoveNext` body is **0x43ac88**.
Its combat-ending and dead-attacker gates precede `Hook.BeforeAttack`; the
BeforeAttack walk precedes hit-count modification. Each hit refreshes its
possible-target set, random targeting is per hit, and every target result is
calculated/damaged before the next target/hit. A live command with zero hits
or no possible result still reaches the one `Hook.AfterAttack` call; a command
rejected before BeforeAttack does not bind. `Hook/<BeforeAttack>d__2::MoveNext`
**0x41ae98** and `Hook/<AfterAttack>d__3::MoveNext` **0x414744** each serially
await the full listener snapshot once per command.

`Hook.ModifyDamage` **0x2b1214** delegates to
`ModifyDamageInternal` **0x2b2b98**. That body completes every
`ModifyDamageAdditive` listener first, then every
`ModifyDamageMultiplicative` listener, applies caps, and performs the shared
final integer conversion. Gigantification consequently multiplies the exact
post-additive value by three and composes with Pen Nib, Weak, Vulnerable, and
the existing exact Fraction factors without an intermediate floor.

The simulator keys the additive nonnegative Amount and the one active
`commandToModify` latch. `PlayerAttackFrame` freezes whether a suspended
command owns that latch. This is necessary, not decorative: Centennial
Puzzle can park an outer command while Hellraiser plays a nested Attack. The
nested command observes the occupied latch and remains ordinary; after it
closes, the outer frozen result resumes once, clears the latch, and decrements
one current stack. Separate replay bodies construct separate AttackCommands,
so one stack affects only the first replay. Zero-hit/no-live-result commands
consume; direct or unpowered damage and pre-entry terminal gates do not.

Current-build authority is v0.111.0, ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`9cb4f1ad8c9f284aa8fec3122ffd6d780bbf543d875c817abdd12ff63fbf12b4`.
These fresh reads supersede the stale `0x395e64` P6 refusal cite and the
earlier v0.109.1 listener RVAs below.

`PowderedDemise::.ctor` is **0x25903f**.
`get_Rarity/get_Usage/get_TargetType` are
**0x258fcb/0x258fce/0x258fd1** (Uncommon, Active, one enemy).
`PotionModel.IsValidTarget` **0x22f60c** requires an alive creature on the
opposing side for target enum value 2. `get_CanonicalVars` **0x258fd4**
constructs Decimal dynamic var `Demise = 9`. `OnUse` is **0x258fec** and the
complete `<OnUse>d__9::MoveNext` body is **0x398e28**: it first calls
`AssertValidForTargetedPotion`, then awaits exactly
`PowerCmd.Apply<DemisePower>(target, Demise.BaseValue, owner.Creature,
null card, false)` at IL_0056. The body consumes no RNG and has no suffix.

`DemisePower::.ctor` is **0x24d7e3**;
`get_Type/get_StackType` are **0x24d788/0x24d78b** (Debuff/Intensity).
Generic `PowerCmd/<Apply>d__2::MoveNext` **0x438e74** rejects ending, zero,
dead/nonreceiving, or out-of-combat applications, modifies an existing
singleton in place, and sends every fresh visible Type-2 application through
the target's Artifact listener before acquisition. Thus repeated potions add
9 without moving the listener, one Artifact stack consumes one whole
application, and the null potion card source cannot latch Unsettling Lamp.
Misery's card-sourced clone is separately Lamp- and Artifact-processed and
joins the exact debuff acquisition-order projection.

`AfterSideTurnEnd` is **0x24d790** and its complete
`<AfterSideTurnEnd>d__4::MoveNext` body is **0x338c88**. It returns unless the
participants contain the owner, flashes, then awaits one
`CreatureCmd.Damage(choiceContext, owner, Amount, props 6, null dealer,
null card)`. It never decrements or removes itself. Props 6 is unpowered and
unblockable: Block, Strength, Weak/Vulnerable, and card-source modifiers are
skipped, but the normal Damage/HP-loss pipeline remains live. HardToKill and
Intangible cap it; positive HP loss wakes Slumber, can cross Shriek's stun
threshold, fires normal damage/death hooks, and can end combat. Because it
does not consume Block it cannot break Burrowed or dispatch AfterBlockBroken.

Global `Hook/<AfterSideTurnEnd>d__81::MoveNext` **0x3d11c0** awaits the
listener snapshot from `CombatState/<IterateHookListeners>d__69::MoveNext`
**0x3f9720**. That iterator walks allied creatures, then enemy creatures in
slot/list order; within each creature it walks powers in first-application
order before the model tail. The simulator therefore freezes `(object, uid)`
for the enemy hook walk. A Phrog death may append Wrigglers and Axebot stock
may replace the Creature identity, but neither the spawn nor replacement can
join the already-started walk. Each Demise Damage fully resolves before the
next owner; terminal combat stops all later damage commands.

The two noncommuting represented same-owner peers are Intangible and Ritual.
A new Demise applied while Intangible exists is later in the listener list:
Intangible decrements first, then Demise observes the new duration. A later
FYSH Fade creates Intangible after an existing Demise, so Demise damages first
and the current tick remains capped. Keyed `demise_after_intangible` records
that relation. Ritual's side-end callback (**0x342a94**) can be skipped when a
lethal earlier Demise removes its owner, so `demise_before_ritual` separately
records whether Demise preceded the first Ritual acquisition. Stacking any
singleton preserves its listener position; removal, death, or creature
replacement clears the corresponding relation. Doom runs in
BeforeSideTurnEnd and can remove Demise before this hook snapshot. Other
represented duration, Territorial, Slumber, Shriek, and Burrowed effects
commute or route through the shared Damage pipeline. Active Waterfall Giant
SteamEruption plus Demise remains narrowly refused: lethal Damage revives the
same owner while a frozen later-power suffix can still exist, and that
listener identity graph is not represented. Direct turn-end entry also
preflights the six ordinary Waterfall pressure-building intents, so a
zero-pressure Demise owner that would acquire SteamEruption this enemy action
refuses before phase mutation.

`Monster.demise` is a nonnegative persistent Amount and is auto-cloned/keyed.
It joins the protected target-power census as one Type-2 singleton for Rend,
the Misery snapshot/order registry (validating both source and existing
recipient before a clone can stack), every ordinary death/cascade/replacement
cleanup, targeted-potion legal actions, exact belt slots, and the pet-safe
enemy-target whitelist. Malformed Amount/order state and the Waterfall
surface refuse before direct turn-end mutation. Coverage advances potions
from **61 modeled / 3 refused** to **62 modeled / 2 refused**, and aggregate
accepted from **946/1062** to **947/1062**. Full invariant audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-31-37-batch194-powdered-demise.md`.

## Batch 195 — Entropic Brew exact out-of-combat generation loop

Current-build authority is v0.109.1/c8c577f6, ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`.
The installed and archived DLLs are byte-identical. These fresh reads
supersede the stale `0x3937dc` refusal cite.

`EntropicBrew::get_Rarity/get_Usage/get_TargetType` are
**0x257f97/0x257f9a/0x257f9d** (Rare, AnyTime usage 2, target enum 5). `OnUse` is
**0x257fa0**, the constructor is **0x257fe3**, and the complete
`<OnUse>d__6::MoveNext` body is **0x396728**. The body first calls
`AssertValidForTargetedPotion`, reads the selected target's `Player`, then
enters a do-while loop. Each iteration passes that player's
`RunState.Rng.CombatPotionGeneration` to
`PotionFactory.CreateRandomPotionOutOfCombat`, converts the result to its
mutable form, and awaits `PotionCmd.TryToProcure(potion, targetPlayer, -1)`.
It repeats only when procurement succeeded and the same target player still
has an open potion slot. The first attempt is unconditional. A truly full
target belt or Sozu fails only after generation consumed its draws; combat
ending does not veto generation or procurement into an open slot.

`PotionFactory::CreateRandomPotionOutOfCombat` is **0x2bee30**;
`CreateRandomPotionsOutOfCombat/CreateRandomPotions/GetPotionOptions` are
**0x2bee40/0x2beeb8/0x2bef46**. For a fully unlocked solo Ironclad the stable
unfiltered pool is the three-character rows followed by the 45 shared rows,
partitioned 16 Common / 16 Uncommon / 16 Rare. Unlike Alchemize's in-combat
filter, it retains Fairy in a Bottle, Fruit Juice, and Regen Potion. Every
attempt calls `NextFloat(1)` once, maps the native float32 result to Rare at
`<= 0.1`, Uncommon at `<= 0.35`, otherwise Common, then calls `NextItem` once
on that stable partition. Each factory call requests one item, so its local
without-replacement list is rebuilt between attempts and duplicate potion
identities are legal. Successful procurement always fills the first null
slot; consuming Entropic Brew removes its exact source slot before this body,
so even an initially full source belt normally has one live opening.

`PotionCmd::TryToProcure` is **0x438850** and
`Player::AddPotionInternal` is **0x2c35fc**. Neither has a combat-ending gate.
Procurement calls
`Hook.ShouldProcurePotion` before slot mutation (Sozu is the sole current
veto), uses the first null slot for index `-1`, and raises
`Hook.AfterPotionProcured` only after success. Belt Buckle therefore removes
its empty-belt Dexterity after the first successful insertion, while a Sozu
failure leaves the consumed source slot empty and the later
`AfterPotionUsed` hook can apply Belt Buckle. The complete
`PotionModel.OnUseWrapper` nested body is **0x3670b4**: source removal precedes
the potion body, and `AfterPotionUsed` is the post-body listener boundary.

The simulator reuses Batch 187's exact generation/procurement primitive and
ordered `potion_slots` representation. It requires the represented local
player, exact positive belt capacity, explicit Ironclad owner, fully unlocked
potion and card pools, the complete Colorless unlock epochs, and exact
nonnegative CombatPotionGeneration plus every reachable generated-potion
consumer counter. Real multiplayer players, forged non-self targets,
malformed slot mirrors, and strict-mode unmodeled leaves refuse before
published mutation. Batch R52D subsequently proved Bottled Potential's fresh
Draw `ToHashSet` enumeration and removed the old mixed-payload/inert caveat;
see the corrected Bottled authority below. Because Entropic Brew can add
arbitrary healing and bankable potion identities, `final_hp_ceiling` returns
no finite bound while one remains held. Coverage advances potions from **62
modeled / 2 refused** to **63 modeled / 1 refused**, and aggregate accepted
from **947/1062** to **948/1062**. Full invariant audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-31-38-batch195-entropic-brew.md`.

**0xd3eaf/0xd3eb7**); zero stolen leaves the flag false. Gold proportion is

**0xbe9f8/0xbea04** (11–15 at A8+, 10–14 below); its machine **0xbea48**

without a turn-1 draw. Every later intent traverses RAND, whose
`GetNextState/GetStateWeight` are **0x225734/0x2257f0**: one MonsterAi
`NextFloat(sum)` and a uniform choice between the two moves not just logged.

Lash **0x260c64** = 4, and LashRepeat **0x260c6f** = 2 (below A9: 9/12/3).

Frail 1 if its suffix remains admissible), Latch **0x3a5744** (one attack),
and Lash **0x3a5630** (one `AttackCommand` with hit count 2).

`SuckPower::get_Type/get_StackType` **0x25498b/0x25498e** are Type 1 /
Intensity. Its wrapper is **0x2549b4** and complete `AfterAttack` body is
**0x39027c**. It requires command attacker identity equal to the owner,
opposing target side, and powered attack properties. It copies the command's
per-hit result groups. Within each group it finds pet results and removes the
paired result whose receiver is that pet's owner; the group counts once iff
any remaining result has `UnblockedDamage > 0`. A positive count flashes and
awaits `Apply<StrengthPower>(owner, Amount * count, owner, null, false)`.
Thus a solo Latch/Tackle grants +3 only after positive player HP loss, while
Lash grants 0/+3/+6 after the entire two-hit command. Existing Strength does
affect both frozen Lash hits; Strength earned from the first result does not,
because the application is after the command. With Osty, the pet's actual HP
loss controls the paired group and player spill is not double-counted.

`AttackCommand` complete body **0x43ac88** checks attacker death before each
hit, records all completed result groups, writes attack history, then invokes
`Hook.AfterAttack`; the global listener body **0x414744** awaits listeners in
snapshot order. The simulator carries an exact qualifying-group accumulator
through the existing Paper Cuts and Centennial Puzzle frames, then applies
Suck once at command completion. Thorns may prevent a hit or kill the owner;
Reflect/Flame Barrier may kill it after a qualifying result; player death may
make combat terminal. In all three cases `PowerCmd.Apply` **0x438c50** rejects
the later Strength because combat is ending or the owner cannot receive
powers. Ordinary death removes Suck. The Amount is a keyed/cloned Type-1
non-debuff row: Rend validates it but does not count it. Malformed Amounts,
missing live Fossil Suck(3), and Suck on another kind refuse before attack
mutation.

## Batch 199 — Exoskeleton weak hybrid random/deterministic AI (#209)

Current-build authority is v0.109.1/c8c577f6, ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`;
the installed and archived DLLs are byte-identical. These fresh reads
supersede the stale C186 RVAs (the machine shape and values were right, but
every cited address predates the current build).

`ExoskeletonsWeak::GenerateMonsters` **0x27f640** creates exactly three
`Exoskeleton` models in named `first`, `second`, `third` creation/slot order.
There is no Encounter-stream roster draw. `get_MinInitialHp/get_MaxInitialHp`
**0x25f23f/0x25f24b** are A8+ 25–29 (24–28 below), so construction consumes
three Niche unique-HP draws over one shared uniqueness set. `AfterAddedToRoom`
**0x25f284**, complete nested body **0x3a2e98**, awaits base and applies one
`HardToKillPower(9)` to each owner. The existing damage cap is per complete
Damage command before block and does not make Rend count the Type-1 power.

`GenerateMoveStateMachine` **0x25f2c8** creates `SKITTER_MOVE`,
`MANDIBLES_MOVE`, `ENRAGE_MOVE`, `RAND`, and `INIT_MOVE`. RAND adds only
SKITTER then MANDIBLES, each with literal repeat type 2 = CannotRepeat and
float32 weight 1.0. Follow-ups are SKITTER -> RAND, MANDIBLES -> ENRAGE, and
ENRAGE -> RAND. The INIT lambdas **0x25f5f0/0x25f607/0x25f61e/0x25f635**
map slots first/second/third/fourth to SKITTER/MANDIBLES/ENRAGE/RAND.
Accordingly the modeled weak encounter starts on three concrete MoveStates
and consumes zero setup MonsterAi draws.

`MonsterMoveStateMachine::FindNextMoveState` **0x225304** retains the last
`ShouldAppearInLogs` state reached while traversing branch nodes and appends
it after reaching a MoveState. The direct MANDIBLES -> ENRAGE edge therefore
logs ENRAGE despite consuming no draw. `RandomBranchState::GetNextState` /
`GetStateWeight` **0x225734/0x2257f0** always calls one
`MonsterAi.NextFloat(sum)` per RAND traversal. Thus the exact cycle is:

- after SKITTER, RAND consumes one draw; CannotRepeat zeroes SKITTER, so the
  result is forced MANDIBLES but the draw is not optimized away;
- after MANDIBLES, the direct edge logs ENRAGE and consumes no draw;
- after ENRAGE, RAND consumes one genuine draw with both branches live.

Prepare-for-next-turn processes living creatures in slot order, so the first
weak turn interleaves draw / no draw / draw for its SKITTER, MANDIBLES, and
ENRAGE starters on the one shared MonsterAi stream. If an earlier actor ends
combat, neither the remaining actor suffix nor any prepare draws occur. The
simulator keys and clones the concrete next move and trailing three logged
moves, validates the complete Exoskeleton state before move or stream
mutation, and refuses missing HardToKill(9), unknown moves, empty logs, or a
log whose last entry does not equal the current intent.

Complete move bodies are SKITTER **0x3a323c** (`DamageCmd.Attack(1)` with hit
count **4** at A9+, 3 below; getter RVAs **0x25f257/0x25f25a**), MANDIBLES
**0x3a3138** (one attack for **9** at A9+, 8 below; getter **0x25f265**), and
ENRAGE **0x3a2fd8** (apply `StrengthPower(2)` to itself). The encounter census
cross-check remains exact: three move states, one random node, no card effects
or summons, and only HardToKillPower plus StrengthPower applications.

`ENCOUNTER.EXOSKELETONS_NORMAL` remains **REFUSED**, not scheduled or
partially registered. Its roster body **0x27f570** creates a fourth slot whose
INIT arm enters RAND immediately over an empty log, consuming a fight-start

## Batch 200 — Snapping Jaxfruit / exact two-phase Flyconid AI (#193)

Current-build authority is v0.109.1/c8c577f6, ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`2cb39e2eee651743829abcc0df4dd9cd7e65f46287c7ca264481115c9602382f`;
the installed and archived DLLs are byte-identical. These reads supersede the
stale W8 addresses and retire its broad “fight-start ordering unknown” claim.

`SnappingJaxfruitNormal::get_AllPossibleMonsters` **0x28107a** names
SnappingJaxfruit and Flyconid. `GenerateMonsters` **0x281097** creates exactly
two mutable models, Jaxfruit first at array/slot 0 and Flyconid second at
array/slot 1, with null named slots and no Encounter-stream call. Creature
construction uses the ordinary unique-HP path **0x2c924c** in that order.
Snapping Jaxfruit's min/max getters **0x26a48e/0x26a49a** yield A8+ 34–36
(31–33 below), and Flyconid's **0x2606bb/0x2606c7** yield A8+ 51–53 (47–49
below), so generation consumes exactly two Niche draws over disjoint ranges.

Snapping Jaxfruit's machine **0x26a50c** contains one self-looping
`ENERGY_ORB_MOVE`, used as the initial concrete MoveState. Its complete body
**0x3b43b4** performs one powered attack for `EnergyDamage` **0x26a4a6** = 4
at A9+ (3 below), awaits it, then applies `StrengthPower(2)` to itself if the
owner and combat remain live. Its `AfterAddedToRoom` wrapper/body
**0x26a4b4/0x3b42e0** only await base and start a cosmetic audio loop; no
combat power or listener is omitted.

Flyconid's machine **0x2606ec** contains three concrete states plus separate
`INITIAL` and `RAND` RandomBranchStates. `INITIAL` AddBranch order is
`FRAIL_SPORES_MOVE`, `SMASH_MOVE`, both weight 1 with CannotRepeat metadata;
the machine constructor receives `INITIAL`. Steady `RAND` AddBranch order is:

- `VULNERABLE_SPORES_MOVE`: cooldown 3, CannotRepeat, weight 1;
- `FRAIL_SPORES_MOVE`: cooldown 2, CannotRepeat, weight 1;
- `SMASH_MOVE`: cooldown 0, CannotRepeat, weight 1.

Every concrete move follows steady `RAND`. `RandomBranchState::GetNextState`
and `GetStateWeight` **0x225734/0x2257f0** calculate weights from the native
StateLog, call exactly one `MonsterAi.NextFloat(sum)`, and subtract branches
in AddBranch order until `roll <= 0`. Consequently even an all-zero table
(the reachable trailing `VULNERABLE,FRAIL,SMASH` case) consumes
`NextFloat(0)` and selects the first Vulnerable branch; it must not be treated
as an impossible state or optimized away.

The fight-start order is now complete. `StartCombatInternal` **0x43f270**
iterates `CombatState.Creatures` in creation order and awaits
`AfterCreatureAdded` for each before global `Hook.BeforeCombatStart` and
`StartTurn`. `AfterCreatureAdded` **0x43bf6c** awaits the creature's
`AfterAddedToRoom`, then calls `MonsterModel.RollMove` when it is an enemy on
the current side. `RollMove` **0x22e948** uses `RunRngSet.MonsterAi`.
`MonsterMoveStateMachine` ctor/RollMove/FindNextMoveState
**0x225214/0x2252b0/0x225304** uses a concrete initial MoveState without a
transition, but traverses a branch initial state and appends the reached
concrete move to StateLog. Thus Jaxfruit consumes no setup draw; Flyconid,
second, consumes exactly one INITIAL draw and logs Frail or Smash. Both happen
before the global before-combat hook and turn start. Later
`Creature::PrepareForNextTurn` **0x2c96bc** calls RollMove in living slot order,
so each completed Flyconid move consumes one steady draw. A terminal earlier
attack suppresses the composite suffix, remaining actors, and prepare draws.

Complete Flyconid bodies are Vulnerable Spores **0x3a4f34**, which applies
enemy-origin `VulnerablePower(2)` to the player with no attack; Frail Spores
**0x3a4c38**, which attacks once for `SporeDamage` **0x2606e0** = 9 at A9+
(8 below) then applies enemy-origin `FrailPower(2)` if still live; and Smash
**0x3a4e30**, which attacks once for `SmashDamage` **0x2606d3** = 12 at A9+
(11 below). Census agreement is exact: Flyconid is 3 move states / 2 random
nodes with Frail and Vulnerable only; Jaxfruit is 1 / 0 with Strength only;

add no enemy-target debuff count for Rend.

## Batch 201 / #169 — Fabricator and Minion bots (2026-07-31)

Current-build source: installed/archive-equivalent STS2 v0.110.1
`db5d3552`, `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`5a8fb7eb62510a86fd03653b9210cd8f67b511b632331a1f174042de39c92bd9`.
This read supersedes the stale W2 Fabricator refusal and its old RVAs.

### Roster, slots, HP, and initial intent

`FabricatorNormal.get_Slots` 0xd6fcf names, in order, `bot1`, `bot2`,
`fabricator`, `bot3`, `bot4`; `GenerateMonsters` 0xd70d4 creates exactly one
Fabricator in the middle named slot (slot 2, uid 0). Fabricator HP is fixed
155 at A8+ (150 below; getters 0xb712f/0xb7141), but side-2
`CreateCreature` still performs the one Niche unique-HP draw.

`GenerateMoveStateMachine` 0xb7168 contains three concrete moves and a
conditional initial/follow node. `get_CanFabricate` 0xb72d4 is exactly
`GetTeammatesOf(self).Count(IsAlive) < 4` (the count includes self). When
true, RAND contains `FABRICATE_MOVE` then `FABRICATING_STRIKE_MOVE`, weight
1 each, both `CannotRepeat`; traversing it consumes one MonsterAi
`NextFloat` (`RandomBranchState.GetNextState` 0x7cb98), even when one branch
is forced. When false it follows and logs
`DISINTEGRATE_MOVE` without a draw. Every concrete move returns to that
conditional. The initial one-creature roster therefore consumes one
fight-start MonsterAi draw and logs its chosen concrete move.

Move bodies are exact at A9+: `FABRICATE_MOVE` (outer/body
0xb7310/0x357da8) awaits a defensive spawn and then an aggressive spawn;
`FABRICATING_STRIKE_MOVE` (0xb7354/0x357f50) attacks 21 (18 below A9;
getter 0xb7149), then awaits one aggressive spawn; `DISINTEGRATE_MOVE`
(0xb7398/0x357ca4) attacks 13 (11 below; getter 0xb7156).

### SpawnBot and listener order

The static constructor 0xb75a8 fixes aggressive options to Zapbot/Stabbot
and defensive options to Guardbot/Noisebot. `SpawnBot` outer/body
0xb7464/0x358180 filters the
selected pool against the single shared `_lastSpawned`, calls MonsterAi
`NextItem` over the remaining materialized pool (a singleton still spends
one `NextInt`), writes `_lastSpawned`, converts the model mutable, then awaits
`CreatureCmd.Add(model, side 2, Encounter.GetNextSlot(state))`
(`GetNextSlot` 0x83038). Each child
therefore spends one Niche unique-HP draw and receives the first never-used
named slot and the next creation uid. Dead enemies remain in `Enemies`, so
their slots never free. `GetNextSlot` is `FirstOrDefault`: after all five
named slots have been occupied it returns the empty string, but
`CombatState.CreateCreature` 0x13a8e0 has no empty-slot rejection and still
runs unique HP, AttachCreature, and Add. The simulator projects that name as
slot index -1 (`Slots.IndexOf("")`); multiple such children retain stable
creation order before named slots. `CanFabricate` remains the only live-count
gate, so sufficiently many dead retained bots can make this path reachable.

`CreatureCmd.Add` outer/body 0x135b14/0x3e69ac inserts the creature, runs the child's
`AfterAddedToRoom` and initial deterministic RollMove, and then the global
`AfterCreatureAdded` walk. In the represented listener census,
Philosopher's Stone 0x9cbec applies Strength 1, then Fur Coat outer/body
0x978b4/0x322e44 sets current HP to 1 on a marked node. Only after that awaited Add
returns does `SpawnBot` apply MinionPower. Mid-phase children are absent from
the frozen enemy actor snapshot and first act on the next enemy phase.

### Bot machines and powers

All four bot machines are single-state self-loops:

- Zapbot HP 19..24 A8+ (18..23 below; 0xc8dfb/0xc8e07), `ZAP_MOVE`
  machine 0xc8e68 / outer/body 0xc8ebc/0x3741cc attacks 15 (14 below;
  0xc8e13). `AfterAddedToRoom` outer/body 0xc8e24/0x37406c applies
  HighVoltagePower 2. That power is Type 1 / Amount stacking
  (0xa70bb/0xa70be); at its owner's side end, outer/body
  0xa70e4/0x33a414 applies Strength equal to Amount, hence +2 every surviving bot
  turn.
- Stabbot HP 19..24 A8+ (18..23 below; 0xc316e/0xc317a), `STAB_MOVE`
  machine 0xc31dc / outer/body 0xc3238/0x36a77c attacks 12 (11 below;
  0xc3186), then
  applies Frail 1 to the player.
- Guardbot HP 17..21 A8+ (16..20 below; 0xb97a9/0xb97b5), `GUARD_MOVE`
  machine 0xb9808 / outer/body 0xb9858/0x35bd20 snapshots living same-side creatures,
  including itself and Fabricator, then serially grants each Block 15.
- Noisebot HP 19..24 A8+ (18..23 below; 0xbdc38/0xbdc44), `NOISE_MOVE`
  machine 0xbdc98 / outer/body 0xbdce8/0x362684. Per player target it creates two fresh
  Dazed and serially adds the first to Discard/Bottom, then the second to
  Draw/Random. Solo therefore spends exactly one Shuffle draw, for the
  draw-pile insertion only.

### Minion terminal semantics and Rend census

MinionPower is fixed Type 1 / Instance stacking (0xa813f/0xa8142), marks
its owner secondary (0xa8148), is retained after owner death (0xa814b),
and vetoes Fatal for that owner's death (0xa814e). A bot death while the
primary Fabricator lives is ordinary and leaves its corpse/slot in the enemy
tuple. When the final primary dies, `KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition`
cascades every frozen living secondary in slot order. Its outer/body
0x136070/0x3e964c retains the dying Creature object across the awaited
`AfterDeath` hook, then materializes living teammates, removes the creature,
and queries its unchanged `IsPrimaryEnemy` before entering the cascade only
when that value is true and `All` survivors are secondary.
It then awaits `CreatureCmd.Kill(list, false)`; that command's outer/body
0x136024/0x3e9344 materializes and serially invokes the full per-creature
kill path before terminal evaluation. The projection therefore includes
each child's exact Gremlin Horn/death-listener work before crossing the
terminal boundary. The simulator reifies that immutable projected identity
through a suspended Gremlin Horn Draw, so a nested bot death cannot steal the
outer Fabricator's pending cascade. `Monster.secondary` is auto-keyed/cloned and generalizes the
existing GasBomb/illusion secondary predicate. `target_power_census.json`
records MinionPower and HighVoltagePower as Type-1 non-debuff exclusions;
neither increases Rend damage.

## Batch 203 / #796 — v0.110.1 relic remodel cluster (2026-07-31)

Current-build source is the installed/archive-equivalent STS2 v0.110.1
`db5d3552`; both DLLs have SHA-256
`5a8fb7eb62510a86fd03653b9210cd8f67b511b632331a1f174042de39c92bd9`.
The release metadata SHA-256 is
`cd3abf5bea78ff74db5f09f592b0ea7524be7aeb602225989204a0f8a5a16e47`.
The historical v0.109.1 reads in Batches 51, 109, 184, 188, and 190 remain
the evidence for that older build; the reads below supersede their runtime
values and hook placement for v0.110.1 only.

### Exact variable and hook reads

- **Beautiful Bracelet.** `get_CanonicalVars` **0x93d42** returns
  `CardsVar(4)` and named `Swift=2`. `AfterObtained` **0x93d88**, body
  **0x31c9f0**, selects exactly four deck cards and enchants each with Swift
  amount 2. It has no combat hook; fight-entry deck payloads already contain
  the acquisition result.
- **Fiddle.** `get_CanonicalVars` **0x97072** returns `CardsVar(2)`.
  `ModifyHandDraw` **0x9707f** owner-gates and adds 2. `ShouldDraw`
  **0x970a7** retains the exact old predicate: permit the hand draw, a draw
  for another player, or a draw outside the owner's active side; refuse only
  an ordinary owner draw on the owner's side. `AfterPreventingDraw`
  **0x970d9** is cosmetic. Fiddle is no longer a Late modifier.
- **Fur Coat.** `get_CanonicalVars` **0x975de** returns named `Combats=8`.
  `AfterObtained` **0x975f5** and `ModifyGeneratedMapLate` **0x97629** retain
  the exact marked-room mechanism. `BeforeCombatStart` **0x97870**, body
  **0x322f6c**, freezes the current hittable enemies and serially sets HP to
  1 on a marked coordinate. `AfterCreatureAddedToCombat` **0x978b4**, body
  **0x322e44**, applies the same HP command to later opposing additions.
  Replay still consumes the exact history-derived mark bit; it does not
  reconstruct eight map choices from combat state.
- **Pendulum.** `get_CanonicalVars` **0x9c636** remains `Cards=1, Turns=3`.
  `BeforeHandDraw` **0x9c69c** owner-gates, advances
  `(TurnsSeen + 1) % 3`, and flashes on zero. `ModifyHandDraw` **0x9c71e**
  adds one exactly when that completed counter is zero. The former
  `AfterPlayerTurnStart` standalone Draw no longer exists, removing its
  #616 Draw caller and its Bellows/damage acquisition-order refusal edges.
- **Regalite.** `get_CanonicalVars` **0x9db1e** returns flat `BlockVar(6,
  props=4)`. `AfterCardGeneratedForCombat` **0x9db48**, body **0x32d54c**,
  accepts null or owner Creator, returns when `_usedThisTurn` is already
  true, writes that latch before awaiting the block, and therefore grants at
  most once per owner turn. `BeforeSideTurnStart` **0x9db93** resets the
  latch when the owner participates; `AfterCombatEnd` also clears it.
- **Seal of Gold.** `get_CanonicalVars` **0x9e856** returns `Energy=1,
  Gold=3`. `AfterSideTurnStart` **0x9e884**, body **0x32e4fc**, checks live
  gold at 3, awaits GainEnergy(1), then loses 3 gold. The established ending
  boundary and gain-before-loss order are unchanged.
- **Signet Ring.** `get_CanonicalVars` **0x9ec16** returns `GoldVar(888)`.
  `AfterObtained` **0x9ec28**, body **0x32ec98**, awaits GainGold(888). It
  has no combat hook; live fight-entry gold already reflects acquisition.
- **Toasty Mittens.** `get_CanonicalVars` **0xa003b** remains Strength 1.
  `AfterPlayerTurnStart` **0xa0080**, body **0x330420**, owner-gates, opens
  `CardSelectCmd.FromHand` with exact min/max 1, exhausts the selected live
  Hand identity with command flags `(false,false)`, awaits the complete
  exhaust-listener chain, and only then applies Strength 1. The old
  BeforeHandDraw shuffle/Draw-card heuristic is not present in v0.110.1.

### Ordering, continuation, and guard contract

The concrete v0.110.1 `ModifyHandDraw` census is Bag of Preparation, Big
Mushroom, Booming Conch, ClarityPower, DemesnePower, DrawCardsNextTurnPower,
Fiddle, MachineLearningPower, MindRotPower, Pael's Blood, Pendulum,
Pocketwatch, Pollinous Core, Ring of the Drake, Ring of the Snake, Snecko Eye,
Tools of the Trade Power, and TyrannyPower. Player powers run first; Mind
Rot's max-zero clamp is therefore complete before the ordinary relic group.
Every represented relic contribution is additive, so Fiddle and Pendulum
commute with their ordinary peers. Pendulum advances once after the power
portion of BeforeHandDraw, before any Toolbox pause, and its later modifier
reads that stored value.

The other ordinary v0.110.1 relics at Toasty Mittens' hook are Bellows, Bone
Tea, Choices Paradox, Emotion Chip, Festive Popper, Gambling Chip, Mercury
Hourglass, Mr Struggles, Royal Poison, and Vexing Puzzlebox. Each can observe
or mutate Hand, RNG, damage, or terminal state around Toasty's blocking
choice and awaited Exhaust. Relic acquisition order is absent from the run,
so every Toasty/co-peer pair refuses before combat mutation. Solo Toasty
freezes exact Hand UID/payload/order in its pending state. Its dedicated
continuation preserves the selected UID across Dark Embrace, Joss Paper,
Hellraiser, and nested death/draw work, then applies Strength only after the
Exhaust command completes. Pending state, continuation, and Regalite's latch
are key-visible and clone-exact.
