## #808 — Same-hook relic dispatch order is the saved inventory list (2026-08-01)

Current-build source: installed/archive-equivalent STS2 v0.110.1
`db5d3552`, `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`5a8fb7eb62510a86fd03653b9210cd8f67b511b632331a1f174042de39c92bd9`.
All RVAs below are `dump_il.py`/`dump_method.py` MethodDef RVAs from that
DLL.

### Dispatch order

`Hook::AfterCardPlayed` **0x10705c** starts
`Hook/<AfterCardPlayed>d__16::MoveNext` **0x3ca4d0**, which takes one
`ICombatState::IterateHookListeners` snapshot, then awaits each model's
`AfterCardPlayed` strictly in snapshot sequence (PushModel → await →
InvokeExecutionFinished → PopModel per element).
`CombatState::IterateHookListeners` **0x13ac75** defers to
`CombatState/<IterateHookListeners>d__69::MoveNext` **0x3f6700** (the
v0.110.1 body of the iterator previously read as 0x441190): per creature
(`_allies` first, then `_enemies`), it appends the creature's Powers
(AddRange), then — players only — walks `Player::get_Relics` by ascending
index `0..Count-1` (IL `00c7–0103`), skipping `RelicModel::get_IsMelted`,
then PotionSlots, Orbs, and the card piles, before global Modifiers and
BadgeModels. **Same-hook relics therefore fire in `Player._relics` list
order, first to last.**

### The list is acquisition-ordered and the save records the list itself

`Player::get_Relics` **0x11a0f8** returns the `_relics` field directly.
`Player::AddRelicInternal` **0x11ac94** appends (`_relics.Add`) when its
index argument is −1 and only `Insert`s at an explicit caller index. Its two
callers are `RelicCmd/<Obtain>d__1::MoveNext` **0x3ee564** (forwards the
`RelicCmd.Obtain` index parameter; ordinary pickups append) and
`Player::PopulateRelics` **0x11b3c0** (always −1, preserving input order;
reached from `Player::LoadInventory` **0x11a748** on save load).
`Player::ToSerializable` **0x11a804** projects `get_Relics` through an
order-preserving `Select` into `SerializablePlayer.Relics`, serialized as an
ordered list (`WriteList`/`ReadList<SerializableRelic>`). So
`players[N].relics` in a schema>=19 save equals the live `_relics` list =
the same-hook dispatch order, even across an explicit-index insert.
Empirical confirmation: all 66 saves of the 2026-07-31 live run (seed
`TQM88QFMHSQR`) show strictly append-only relic lists matching pickup order.

### Solver consequences

`tools/live_coach.py build_entry` sets
`relics_entering_dispatch_ordered: true` for schema>=19 saves (`rng.rngs`
present); `.run`/MCR reconstruction has no such provenance and never sets
it. `start_combat` admits Iron Club/Tuning Fork with same-AfterCardPlayed
peers only when that flag vouches for the entry list and every peer
precedes both counters in it — exactly the order the sim's fixed
`_after_card_played_counter_relics` suffix implements (peer bodies first,
counters last). A recorded order that places any peer after the first
counter still refuses (the fixed suffix cannot represent it), as do
duplicate involved relics (ambiguous index), malformed flags, and all
orderless entries. The Iron-then-Fork order inside the suffix remains
observable only on a simultaneous threshold, which keeps its runtime
refusal regardless of recorded order. No other acquisition-order guard
(Batch 37/188 pair refusals, BeforeHandDraw/BeforeSideTurnEnd families) is
relaxed by this read. Tests: `test_relic_dispatch_order.py`. Full walk:
`invariant-walks/2026-08-01-01-relic-dispatch-order.md`.

## Merchant shop inventory generation (2026-07-31, v0.110.1 db5d3552)

How shop stock is drawn from the pre-shuffled relic grab bags, IL-read
against the archived v0.110.1 `sts2.dll` (sha 5a8fb7eb…, byte-identical
to the live install) and validated live on seed TQM88QFMHSQR.

**Entry.** `MerchantRoom::EnterInternal` **0x5d5c4** (async body
`<EnterInternal>d__13::MoveNext` **0x30ecd4**) calls
`MerchantInventory::CreateForNormalMerchant` **0x11fb80** once per
player, before asset preload, with NO earlier RNG consumption; the
inventories persist on the room (`get_Inventories` 0x5d538). Stock is
therefore fixed at room entry and predictable from a save captured at
shop-node arrival.

**Population order** (`CreateForNormalMerchant` 0x11fb80):
character cards → colorless cards → relics → potions → card removal.

- `PopulateCharacterCardEntries` **0x11fc14**: sale index =
  `Shops.NextInt(5)` FIRST, then 5 entries with
  `_coloredCardTypes = [Attack, Attack, Skill, Skill, Power]`
  (`.cctor` **0x11fe5c**, blob 9380B9AE… = int32 {1,1,2,2,3}). Each
  entry (`MerchantCardEntry::Populate` **0x11f194** → typed
  `CardFactory::CreateForMerchant` **0x115f84**): rarity =
  `CardRarityOdds.RollWithoutChangingFutureOdds` **0x65cb0** — one
  **Rewards** `NextFloat(1.0)` (the odds `_rng` is bound to Rewards:
  `PlayerOddsSet::.ctor` **0x65f41** / `FromSerializable` **0x65f94**)
  against `GetBaseOdds` source 4 = Shop (`ShopCommonOdds` .585/.54
  **0x65c0d**, `ShopRareOdds` .045/.09 **0x65c1f**, second constant =
  2-player value); `GetNextAllowedRarity` **0x1167e0** consumes no RNG;
  card pick = **Shops** `NextItem` (excludes Starter rarity and cards
  already stocked); `RollForUpgrade` **0x116832→0x116848** draws one
  **Rewards** `NextFloat(1.0)` UNCONDITIONALLY (before the
  IsUpgradable check — always exactly 1 draw); price
  (`MerchantCardEntry::CalcCost` **0x11f310**) = base ×
  **Shops** `NextFloat(0.95, 1.05)`, halved for the sale slot.
- `PopulateColorlessCardEntries` **0x11fcb8**:
  `_colorlessCardRarities = [Uncommon(3), Rare(4)]` (.cctor), via the
  rarity-fixed `CreateForMerchant` **0x116110** — NO odds roll; per
  entry: Shops NextItem + one Rewards upgrade roll + Shops price.
- `PopulateRelicEntries` **0x11fd2c**: rarities =
  `[RollRarity(player), RollRarity(player), Shop(5)]`.
  `RelicFactory::RollRarity` **0x116b41→0x116b54** draws the player
  **Rewards** stream (NOT Shops): `NextFloat(1.0)` `< 0.5` →
  Common(2), `< 0.83` → Uncommon(3), else Rare(4) (float32 compares).
  Each slot: `MerchantRelicEntry::.ctor` **0x120084** → `FillSlot`
  **0x1200a8** (blacklist null at initial stock; predicate =
  `!blacklist.Contains(r) && r.IsAllowedInShops`, closure 0x3d82dd) →
  `RelicFactory::PullNextRelicFromBack` **0x116afc** →
  `RelicGrabBag::PullFromBack` **0x4eb5c**: scan the rarity's deque
  from the LAST index down, take the first predicate match
  (`RemoveAt`). **Shops are the game's only back-pullers** — every
  other consumer (RelicReward, RelicTrader, events, Wongo) goes
  through `PullNextRelicFromFront`/`PullFromFront` **0x4eb0c** (head
  scan), so shop stock burns the bag TAIL while reward order keeps the
  head. Price (`MerchantRelicEntry::CalcCost` **0x1200e5**) =
  round(MerchantCost × **Shops** `NextFloat(0.85, 1.15)`).
- `PopulatePotionEntries` **0x11fd88**: 3 potions via
  `PotionFactory.CreateRandomPotionsOutOfCombat(player, 3, Shops,
  null)`; potion price (`CalcCost` **0x11ff48**) = rarity base 50/75/
  100 (`GetCost` **0x11ff24**) × **Shops** `NextFloat(0.95, 1.05)`.

**Deque selection** (`GetAvailableDeque` **0x4ecfc**), per pull:

1. `RemoveDisallowedRelicsFromDeques` **0x4edac** REMOVES (mutation,
   persists in the bag) every relic with `IsAllowed(runState)` false
   from all deques. v0.110.1 relic overrides of `IsAllowed` (base
   **0x87e48** true): the 17-relic egg family (AmethystAubergine,
   BookOfFiveRings, BowlerHat, DragonFruit, FrozenEgg, Girya,
   JuzuBracelet, LastingCandy, LuckyFysh, MealTicket, MoltenEgg,
   OldCoin, Planisphere, Shovel, ToxicEgg, WhiteBeastStatue,
   WhiteStar) forwards to `IsBeforeAct3TreasureChest` **0x87e5c** =
   `TotalFloor < (players > 1 ? 38 : 41)`; `MassiveScroll` **0x99fca**
   = MP-only; `SilverCrucible` **0x9ee8d** / `WingedBoots` **0xa18b2**
   = SP-only. (Kaleidoscope 0x98cf4 / ScrollBoxes 0x9e3d6 override
   only `IsAllowedAtNeow` — irrelevant to shops.)
2. Empty deque + `_refreshAllowed` → `RefreshRarity` **0x4f030**
   rebuilds from `_originalRelics`; the PLAYER bag is built with the
   parameterless ctor (**0x4e878**, at `Player::CreateForNewRun`
   **0x11a548**) so `_refreshAllowed` is false and this path never
   runs for shops (also `_originalRelics` is not serialized —
   `LoadFromSerializable` **0x4ef2c** leaves it null).
3. If the deque has no relic passing the SHOP predicate
   (`DequeHasAnyRelics` **0x4ed98**), downgrade rarity via the switch:
   Common→Uncommon→Rare→stop, Shop→Common (so an exhausted Shop pool
   falls back to Common→Uncommon→Rare). Full exhaustion → null →
   `RelicFactory.FallbackRelic` = Circlet **0x1169ff**.
4. Every successful pull ALSO calls
   `SharedRelicGrabBag.Remove(relic)` **0x4ebc0** (id-match RemoveAll
   across the shared bag's deques).

`get_IsAllowedInShops` (base **0x87c9a** true; the predicate SKIPS
these without removing them): AmethystAubergine **0x934ba**, BowlerHat
**0x94c7e**, LuckyFysh **0x99e9a**, OldCoin **0x9b20e**, TheCourier
**0x9fe12**.

**Stream accounting per shop generation.** Player **Rewards**: 12
draws for cards (5 character × [odds roll + upgrade roll] + 2
colorless × [upgrade roll]) then the two relic rarity rolls = draws 13
and 14 relative to entry state. Player **Shops**: 1 sale index + 5 ×
(card NextItem + price) + 2 × (colorless NextItem + price) = 15 draws
before the 3 relic price rolls (16–18), then potion generation +
prices. The Rewards/shops split means relic IDENTITY depends only on
Rewards draws 13/14 plus bag order; Shops affects prices/cards/potions
only. No relic implements the merchant hooks in v0.110.1
(`ModifyMerchantCardPool` is implemented by the CharacterCards game
mode only; `ModifyMerchantCardRarity` / `ModifyMerchantCardCreationResults`
/ `ModifyCardRewardUpgradeOdds` have no non-engine implementers), so
these draw counts are stable.

**Restock after purchase**: relics `RestockAfterPurchase` **0x12019c**
= fresh `RollRarity` (one more Rewards draw) + `FillSlot` with the
currently-stocked relics as blacklist; cards **0x11f3d8** re-Populate
(sale flag cleared). Card removal entry (`CalcCost` **0x11f42a**):
cost = BaseCost + PriceIncrease × CardShopRemovalsUsed, where BaseCost
**0x11f403** = 75 (100 at Ascension 6+) and PriceIncrease **0x11f40f**
= 25 (50 at A6+) via `AscensionHelper::GetValueIfAscension`; no RNG.

**Live validation** (seed TQM88QFMHSQR, 2026-07-31, first shop,
capture `versions/v0.111.0/solver/testdata/TQM88QFMHSQR_shop_entry.save`): entry save
had rewards counter 13; replaying its recorded xoshiro state gives
draws 13/14 = 0.780438 / 0.713137 → Uncommon, Uncommon; tail pulls
took uncommon[31] Orichalcum then uncommon[30] Parrying Shield, and
the Shop slot took shop[25] Bread — all three matching the observed
in-game stock exactly. Predictor: `versions/v0.111.0/solver/tools/shop_stock.py`
(`predict_shop_relics`), pinned by `versions/v0.111.0/solver/test_shop_stock.py`.

## 2026-07-31 — Batch 204: v0.110.1 reward boundary (#798 / #794 / #138)

This is a current-build audit, not a reward-identity predictor. The installed
and archived v0.110.1/db5d3552 DLLs are byte-identical at SHA-256
`5a8fb7eb62510a86fd03653b9210cd8f67b511b632331a1f174042de39c92bd9`;
their release metadata is byte-identical at SHA-256
`cd3abf5bea78ff74db5f09f592b0ea7524be7aeb602225989204a0f8a5a16e47`.
Batch 172's v0.109.1/c8c577f6 evidence remains historical and unchanged;
the runtime surface below is current-build only.

### Rarity and reward-generation reads

`CardRarityOdds.Roll` **0x65c4c** and
`RollWithoutChangingFutureOdds` **0x65ca1/0x65cb0** retain the stateful
Encounter rarity path. The latter consumes exactly one Rewards
`NextFloat(1.0)`, tests Rare against `GetBaseOdds(type, Rare) + currentValue`,
then tests Uncommon against that completed Rare threshold plus
`GetBaseOdds(type, Uncommon)`. `RollWithBaseOdds` **0x65d4c** is the actual
v0.110.1 semantic delta: after one Rewards `NextFloat(1.0)`, it tests Rare
against `rareBase`, then Uncommon against `rareBase + uncommonBase`, then
returns Common. The v0.109.1 body at **0x649f8** incorrectly compared the
second branch with `uncommonBase` alone. `GetBaseOdds` is **0x65d8c**.

`CardFactory.RollForRarity` **0x11676c** uses the stateful `Roll` only for
Encounter source with Regular/Elite/Boss encounter odds; every other source
uses the corrected `RollWithBaseOdds`. It then calls
`GetNextAllowedRarity` **0x1167e0** to wrap upward until the filtered pool
contains an allowed rarity. `CardFactory.CreateForReward`
**0x1161cc/0x116528** iterates options in order. For each option it first
rolls rarity, then chooses one card from the rarity-filtered pool with
Rewards `NextItem`, then executes `RollForUpgrade` **0x116832/0x116848**,
whose first action is one Rewards `NextFloat(1.0)`. Thus the exact
per-option reward-stream order is rarity draw, identity draw, upgrade draw.

`CardReward.Populate` **0x60ee4** is the caller of `CreateForReward`; this is
post-combat reward-set work. `RewardsSet.WithRewardsFromRoom` **0x61d4c** and
`GenerateWithoutOffering` **0x61e08** / body **0x310c1c** transfer and later
populate the room rewards. No combat solver or live-coach route predicts the
resulting identities.

### The Hunt descriptor and mock-pool boundary

Current `TheHunt` ctor/vars/body are **0xf217c/0xf218c/0x3c052c**. On a
qualifying fatal, body IL **0x01a3-0x01d2** creates
`CardCreationOptions.ForRoom(owner, roomType)`, constructs `CardReward` with
option count 3, and calls `CombatRoom.AddExtraReward` **0x5d179**. The
ordinary `CardReward` ctor **0x60db0** stores options/count and consumes no
RNG. The simulator therefore continues to append only
`(player_key, owner_pool, Encounter, room_odds, 3)` before the separately
awaited The Hunt marker. All eight run streams remain unchanged at this
combat boundary. Reward identities remain deliberately absent.

`DeprivedCardPool.get_IsMock` **0xf53d6** returns true.
`GenerateAllCards` **0xf53f8** grows from 12 to 13 entries and appends at
index 12 a canonical Common `MockTurnEndInHandRecorderCard`. This is test
infrastructure: the production descriptor allowlist remains exactly the five
owner pools Ironclad, Silent, Defect, Necrobinder, and Regent. Deprived is
not admitted as an owner pool, so the new mock card cannot enter The Hunt or
another production reward descriptor.

Pael's Wing's `TryModifyCardRewardAlternatives` and Prismatic Gem's
`ModifyCardRewardCreationOptions` remain reward-only/post-combat boundaries;
Batch 204 does not reinterpret them as combat hooks. With the descriptor
surface and all callers re-read, #798 leaves the atomic current-build pending
tuple. v0.110.1 remains globally fail-closed under #794 while #795 and #797
remain. Full audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-07-31-47-batch204-v01101-rewards.md`.

## 2026-08-01 — Batch 207: Hunter Killer and signed player stats (#181 / #222)

Current-build source is installed/archive-equivalent v0.110.1/db5d3552
ARM64 `sts2.dll`; protected build hashes are centralized in
`attestations.json`. RVAs below are current `dump_il.py`/`dump_method.py`
MethodDef RVAs.

### Signed Strength and Dexterity boundary

`StrengthPower` type/stack/negative metadata is
**0xac043/0xac046/0xac049** and its additive damage modifier is **0xac04c**.
`DexterityPower` type/stack/negative metadata is
**0xa4eaf/0xa4eb2/0xa4eb5** and its additive Block modifier is **0xa4ecc**.
Both powers therefore admit exact negative integer aggregates. The complete
damage fold still clamps only at the end of `Hook::ModifyDamage`
**0x108c04**, IL `01b5-01c0`; the complete Block fold does the same in
`Hook::ModifyBlock` **0x108718**, IL `0100-010b`. Positive Strength receipts
continue through received-power modifiers, including Ruined Helmet, while
Dexterity is an ordinary signed additive.

The represented player surface has no Artifact source: every current player
Artifact creation route remains refused, so this batch does not invent an
Artifact field or suppression rule. The shared signed primitive is also
caller-bounded. Lagavulin Matriarch's Soul Siphon nested body **0x35ef64**,
Lost's Smog nested body **0x36dcbc**, and Forgotten's Miasma nested body
**0x36d118** were re-read, but their encounters remain refused under their
independent #221/#198 boundaries. This primitive does not admit any prefix of
those encounters.

### Hunter Killer roster, machine, and RNG

`HunterKillerNormal::GenerateMonsters` **0xd74e3** creates exactly one
default-slot Hunter Killer. Its fixed A8+ HP is 126 (below A8: 121), with HP
getters **0xb9b69/0xb9b75**. Encounter construction consumes exactly one
Niche draw for fixed HP and no Encounter draw.

`HunterKiller::GenerateMoveStateMachine` **0xb9ba4** begins with the concrete
`TENDERIZING_GOOP_MOVE`, then enters RAND with `BITE_MOVE` followed by
`PUNCTURE_MOVE` in `AddBranch` order. Both random branches carry literal
`CannotRepeat` value 2 and equal default weight. The concrete opener consumes
no MonsterAi draw. Each later intent roll consumes exactly one MonsterAi
float even when the previous move leaves only the alternating branch eligible.

The exact move bodies are:

- Tenderizing Goop wrapper/nested **0xb9c90/0x35c510** applies one
  `TenderPower` to the player with the exact Hunter Killer as applier.
- Bite wrapper/nested **0xb9cdc/0x35c40c** attacks once for 19 at A9+
  (17 below A9).
- Puncture wrapper/nested **0xb9d20/0x35c670** attacks three times for 8 at
  A9+ (7 below A9).

### Tender continuation and event semantics

`TenderPower` is type 2 with stack type 1 at **0xad3d3/0xad3d6**. Its private
card counter getter/setter is **0xad41e/0xad426**. `AfterCardPlayed` wrapper
**0xad43c**, nested **0x34688c**, owner-gates the CardPlay, increments the
private counter, then awaits Strength -1 and Dexterity -1 on that player in
that order, with the exact Hunter Killer owner as source/applier. Each
CardPlay counts independently: replay copies are separate events, and a
generated card counts when it is played rather than when generated. Teammate
CardPlays do not pass the owner gate. If an already-captured hook observes
combat ending, the counter increment survives while both nested `PowerCmd`
applications no-op at their ordinary ending guard. Tender's acquisition order
relative to ordinary player powers is not serialized. Before mutation, the
simulator enumerates every plausible sequence of applicable Panache, Black
Hole, Storm, and Afterimage/Rage/Sneaky Block listeners on isolated clones,
including their nested Juggernaut hits and cumulative damage. If any peer
sequence can end combat, it refuses: Tender-first and terminal-peer-first
differ on whether the two signed commands survive. Sequences that remain
nonterminal commute with Tender.

`AfterSideTurnEnd` wrapper **0xad490**, nested **0x346a30**, gates on the
participants containing the Tender owner. At the player's side end it applies
Strength +counter, then Dexterity +counter, and resets the counter only after
both commands complete. The power remains. Both restoration applications use
`TenderPower.Applier`, the exact Hunter Killer, rather than the player.
Player-power callbacks precede the relic group; positive Strength restore
consequently traverses Ruined Helmet's received-power hook. Tender
amount/counter and the exact Hunter Killer owner identity are validated before
mutation and both integers participate in the memo key.

Hunter Killer Normal moves from refused to modeled. Encounter coverage is now

## Batch 208 — Lagavulin Matriarch and keyed forced follow-up (#221, 2026-08-01; v0.110.1 db5d3552)

The installed/archive-equivalent current build moves
`LAGAVULIN_MATRIARCH_BOSS` from refused to modeled. Its generator
`0xd7832` creates one default-slot Matriarch and consumes one Niche draw for
fixed A8+ HP 233 (222 below A8; getter `0xbb48a`). There is no Encounter or
MonsterAi draw. `AfterAddedToRoom` nested `0x35e818` enters `Sleep` nested
`0x35ed28`, applying Plating 12 and then Asleep 3.

The machine `0xbb6c4` keeps `SLEEP_MOVE` current while Asleep exists, then
enters the deterministic cycle Slash → Disembowel → Slash2 → Soul Siphon →
Slash. The current nested move bodies are Slash `0x35ec0c` (21 once),
Disembowel `0x35e940` (10 twice), Slash2 `0x35ea6c` (14 once then Block 14),
and Soul Siphon `0x35ef64` (player Strength -2, player Dexterity -2, owner
Strength +2, serially). The signed player-stat primitive is the Batch 207
implementation; no new approximation or player Artifact state is introduced.

Asleep's damage hook nested `0x332c54` requires the exact owner and positive
`UnblockedDamage`. A fully blocked hit does nothing. The first qualifying
DamageResult removes Plating, marks the owner awake, installs a forced
`WAKE_UP_MOVE` with `SLASH_MOVE` follow-up, then removes Asleep. Later hits in
the same multi-hit/replay see no Asleep and cannot retrigger. A lethal hit
still removes both powers, but `Creature.StunInternal` rejects the dead owner,
so no forced state survives death. The same Damage boundary applies to an
externally supplied teammate or teammate-pet command without predicting an
action or target.

The forced-state seam follows `Creature.StunInternal` `0x1211c4`,
`MonsterModel.SetMoveImmediate` `0x85dd4`, and
`MonsterMoveStateMachine.ForceCurrentState`/`FindNextMoveState`
`0x7c753/0x7c768`. Dynamic bodies are keyed by `(owner kind, move id)` and
their ordinary follow-up state must resolve uniquely in the registered
machine. While the dynamic state has not performed,
`MustPerformOnceBeforeTransitioning` rejects an ordinary non-forced
transition. The sole admitted caller/body here is Matriarch
`WAKE_UP_MOVE`, whose body is cosmetic; it spends exactly one enemy action,
then installs Slash. Unknown callers, bodies, follow-ups, malformed composite
state, and missing or duplicated owner identity refuse before any Damage/wake
mutation. Shape validation precedes dead/spawn intent early returns, so
Asleep cannot coexist with a continuation and `WAKE_UP_MOVE` cannot exist
without its follow-up. This does not admit Beast or Queen: both retain their
whole-encounter #220 card-affliction refusals.

Natural wake uses Asleep `BeforeSideTurnEndVeryEarly` nested `0x333054` and
`AfterSideTurnEnd` nested `0x332ef4`. Three enemy Sleep actions occur. On the
third side end, VeryEarly removes the remaining Plating power before Doom;
the Block already gained at that side start remains. AfterSideTurnEnd then
decrements/removes Asleep and calls WakeUp directly, so the next intent is
Slash with no forced no-op. This listener runs before a later-acquired Demise
listener; an amount-1 Demise on that final side end therefore cannot re-stun
the naturally awakened owner. Poison and all other positive unblocked Damage
use the same synchronous damage-wake boundary.

`Monster.asleep` and `Monster.forced_follow_up` are ordinary dataclass fields,
so key/clone/equality retain the complete continuation state. Rend validates
Asleep and Plating as exact nonnegative Type-1 power state but counts neither.
Lagavulin's admission changes encounter coverage to 8 certified, 52 modeled,
and 21 refused; aggregate accepted content becomes 956. The complete invariant
walk is `invariant-walks/2026-08-01-05-batch208-lagavulin-matriarch.md`.

## Batch 210 / R41 — Queen Boss fixed roster and ordered Amalgam-death graph (#866, #1967; v0.111.0 9cb4f1ad)

`QueenBoss::GenerateMonsters` **0xd4a1c** creates Torch Head Amalgam first
in slot 0, then Queen in slot 1. Both use fixed A8+ HP: Amalgam 211 and
Queen 419. Construction consumes two Niche draws and no Encounter draw.
Amalgam carries `MinionPower`; it is the sole secondary enemy, while Queen is
primary. The simulator validates that exact two-object slot/uid/HP/secondary
shape before any Queen action, either roster member's damage, or an enemy
Doom batch.

Torch Head Amalgam's machine **0xc2c98** is Strong Tackle 32 → Tackle 22 →
Soul Beam 8x3 → Tackle 16 → Tackle 16 → Soul Beam. The final Tackle points
back to Soul Beam, producing the stable Beam/Tackle/Tackle suffix. Current
nested bodies are AfterAdded/Minion **0x371e7c**, Soul Beam **0x371fbc**,
Strong Tackle **0x37217c**, Tackle **0x372280**, and Weak Tackle
**0x372384**.

Queen's machine **0xbc37c** starts Puppet Strings → You're Mine → Burn
Bright. Puppet Strings nested **0x3678b0** applies Chains of Binding 3; the
Batch-209 exact card-affliction layer therefore Bounds the first three
qualifying player-side draws and enforces the one-Bound-play latch. You're
Mine nested **0x367a10** serially applies Frail 99, Weak 99, and Vulnerable
99. Burn Bright nested **0x3672b0** snapshots living teammates excluding
Queen, applies Strength 1 to the one live Amalgam, then grants Queen Block
20; while the Amalgam remains alive it self-loops. The two conditional
branches use ordered `!HasAmalgamDied` / `HasAmalgamDied` predicates
**0xbc84b/0xbc856** and **0xbc85e/0xbc869**.

After the Amalgam-death latch, the branch enters Off With Your Head 4x5 →
Execution 18 → Enrage Strength 2 → Off With Your Head. Their nested bodies
are **0x3677a0**, **0x367698**, and **0x367538**. Queen's `AfterDeath`
**0xbc734** tests the dying creature's Torch Head Amalgam type; the fixed
roster makes that a unique UID. If Burn Bright
is currently pending, it calls `SetMoveImmediate(ENRAGE_MOVE, false)`;
otherwise it leaves the current intent in place and the next native branch
observes the latch.

The death listener is deliberately part of the resumable death suffix.
`Hook/<AfterDeath>d__28::MoveNext` **0x3cb260** and
`CombatState/<IterateHookListeners>::MoveNext` **0x3f9720** place the
Queen model after player relic and card-pile listeners. Thus a Gremlin Horn
draw, including a selecting Hellraiser suspension, completes first;
Melancholy's exact physical-card update follows; only then does Queen latch
the Amalgam death and possibly retarget Burn Bright. The DrawFrame carries
the immutable Queen-roster dying kind without changing the historical
two-field payload for non-Queen deaths. A reentrant Horn draw can kill Queen
before this listener resumes, in which case the dead owner does not latch or
retarget. A keyed internal death-await bit spans the synchronous AutoPlay
preflight and the parked DrawFrame, and is cleared immediately before the
Queen listener; no ordinary dead-Amalgam state may set it.

The outer monster `AttackCommand` also awaits that nested Thorns death path.
Its already-modified damage is frozen in a keyed `MonsterAttackFrame` before
the Horn selection is exposed; player Block/HP and the remaining-hit cursor
do not advance until the child Draw resumes. Both initial and resumed Queen
roster attacks revalidate the exact ordered collection `[Amalgam, Queen]`
before any player HP, Block, intent, or continuation mutation.

Killing Queen while Amalgam lives snapshots Queen as primary, runs all death
listeners, then invokes the established secondary-enemy cascade on the
Amalgam before the terminal boundary. Killing Amalgam alone leaves Queen
alive and combat open. Malformed roster cardinality, identity, slot/uid,
fixed max HP, secondary flag, move index, dynamic move state, latch/HP
relation, and impossible pre-/post-death machine phases refuse before the
relevant mutation. `ENCOUNTER.QUEEN_BOSS` moves from refused to modeled; no
other refusal changes. Full audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-08-01-14-batch210-queen.md`.

SKITTER then MANDIBLES at equal weight with `CannotRepeat`. INIT lambdas
**0xb6f28/0xb6f3f/0xb6f56/0xb6f6d** map slots 0..3 respectively to SKITTER,
MANDIBLES, ENRAGE, and RAND. Current complete move bodies are ENRAGE
**0x357638**, MANDIBLES **0x357798**, and SKITTER **0x35789c**; damage/hit
getters **0xb6b8f/0xb6b92/0xb6b9d** retain 1x4 SKITTER and 9 MANDIBLES at
the represented ascension, while ENRAGE applies Strength 2.

**0x139adc/0x3f02f8** reach `MonsterModel.RollMove` **0x85dac** after the
creature add body. `MonsterMoveStateMachine` construction/RollMove
**0x7c678/0x7c714** traverses the slot-four INIT arm into RAND. Current
`RandomBranchState::GetNextState/GetStateWeight` **0x7cb98/0x7cc54** consumes
one `MonsterAi.NextFloat` and selects SKITTER or MANDIBLES. Slots 0..2 already
hold concrete logged MoveStates and consume no setup draw. Thus exactly the
fourth instance consumes one setup MonsterAi draw, after its exact empty
`next_move`/StateLog precondition; the weak three-instance roster still
consumes zero setup draws.

draw), slot 1 MANDIBLES follows ENRAGE (zero draws), slot 2 ENRAGE traverses

## Batch 222 / #268 — Hello World and Sentry Mode BeforeHandDraw generation

Current-build source is installed v0.110.1/db5d3552 (`sts2.dll` SHA-256
`5a8fb7eb62510a86fd03653b9210cd8f67b511b632331a1f174042de39c92bd9`).
`CombatState.IterateHookListeners` nested `MoveNext` **0x3f6700** builds the
ordinary hook listener list eagerly, but rechecks that the concrete listener
is still contained immediately before yielding it. Therefore a later power
removed by an earlier listener is skipped, while a power added after the
snapshot cannot join that invocation. The late hook is a separate fresh
snapshot. `CombatManager.SetupPlayerTurn` nested `MoveNext` **0x3f3cf0**
captures each power's turn-start amount through `Creature.BeforeTurnStart`,
then runs regular `BeforeHandDraw`, then a separately enumerated
`BeforeHandDrawLate`, then hand-draw modification and the actual draw. The
simulator preserves this split: it freezes only the regular power listeners
here, retains its existing closed late/relic/card families, and records power
application order so equal stacks cannot erase acquisition order.

Hello World's ctor/outer/body are **0xa6ce4**, **0xa6e08**, and nested
`<BeforeHandDraw>d__4.MoveNext` **0x339b7c**. It is a cost-1 Defect Common
Power; L1 adds Innate without changing Amount. The body owner-gates and uses
the `AmountOnTurnStart` snapshot, not a later live stack count. It obtains the
fully unlocked solo-Defect Common pool through
`CardFactory.GetDistinctForCombat` **0x116290** and its combat filter
**0x11634a** / predicate **0x3d48da**, then performs the complete
`UnstableShuffle` **0x116bfc** with CombatCardGeneration and takes the first
`min(AmountOnTurnStart, 20)` entries. The exact ordered v0.110.1 pool is:
Ball Lightning, Barrage, Beam Cell, Boost Away, Charge Battery, Claw, Cold
Snap, Compile Driver, Coolheaded, Focused Strike, Go for the Eyes, Gunk Up,
Hologram, Hotfix, Leap, Lightning Rod, Momentum Strike, Sweeping Beam, Turbo,
and Uproar. A single plural Hand add then processes that list in order. Thus
the full 20-card shuffle consumes 19 generation draws even when the amount is
smaller. Each generated card records history and runs the generated-card
listener walk; if combat ends during one card's listener suffix, later list
members still record generated history, while their pile insertion is
suppressed by the nested add's terminal gate.

Sentry Mode's ctor/outer/body are **0xaaa4c**, **0xaaba8**, and nested
`<BeforeHandDraw>d__6.MoveNext` **0x34195c**. It is a Defect Power costing 2,
or 1 at L1, and applies Amount 1. After the owner gate its loop condition
rereads the live power Amount after every awaited insertion. Each iteration
constructs one fresh L0 Sweeping Gaze and awaits one *singular*
`AddGeneratedCardToCombat` to Hand Bottom before evaluating the next loop
condition. It consumes no RNG. Current v0.110.1 singular
`AddGeneratedCardToCombat` outer/nested **0x133f74/0x3e064c** delegates to
plural `AddGeneratedCardsToCombat` outer/nested **0x133fd0/0x3e0730**. The
plural body gates on `IsInProgress`, which remains true while combat is
ending. Thus a terminal first listener does not stop later Sentry iterations:
all still record `CardGenerated`, while nested pile
`CardPileCmd/<Add>d__10::MoveNext` **0x3df3cc** rejects the later insertions
because combat is ending. A stack gained during an awaited generated-card
suffix extends the loop; a removed or decremented stack shortens it.

Both power bodies use the existing exact generated-card listener
continuation and return contract. A dedicated BeforeHandDraw power frame
freezes listener order and its cursor before invoking a body, carries Hello's
already-shuffled list cursor or Sentry's completed-iteration cursor, and
resumes only after all nested Regalite/Juggernaut/Gremlin Horn/Hellraiser
work returns. Foregone Conclusion may pause an earlier listener and then
resume at the later frozen power exactly once. Its FromCombatPile UI retains
the two payload-distinct sub-multisets for four equal Strikes plus Bash (SS and
SB); each value choice is canonically rebound to exact physical UIDs before
the awaited move, so the enclosing continuation does not multiply identical
UI choices or weaken identity. Before the real hook mutates power order, UID
allocation, CombatCardGeneration, pile order, or generated history, a clone
executes the complete reachable hook/continuation surface; unsupported
listener combinations or pool/provenance drift therefore refuse atomically.

Hello World is admitted only for an explicit Defect owner, an explicit fully
unlocked card-pool projection, an exact CombatCardGeneration counter, and the
exact 20-card pool. Because that pool contains CombatTargets consumers, the
existing missing-CombatTargets counter gate retains precedence over those
additional Hello-specific provenance checks. Sentry Mode needs no generation
provenance beyond its fixed Sweeping Gaze payload. Call of the Void remains
refused at outer/body
**0xa39f4/0x3346b4** because its independently shuffled fully unlocked
solo-Necrobinder pool still has nine direct refused leaves. Creative AI
remains refused at **0xa4598/0x335d2c** because its independently selected
19-card Defect Power pool still has four refused leaves. Spectrum Shift
remains refused at **0xaba18/0x343524** because the Colorless generator has a
transitive Regent owner-pool boundary. No generic random-card generation or
new pool approximation is admitted. Full audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-08-03-05-batch222-before-hand-draw-generation.md`.

The card and power bodies were re-read from that assembly rather than the

Pillar of Creation's ctor/canonical-vars/OnPlay/upgrade methods are

Power whose `BlockVar` has props 4 and base 2; L1 adds one, so the applied

flashes, reads the live power Amount, and awaits one props-4 GainBlock with a
null CardModel. Therefore it fires for every qualifying generated card, not
only the first generated card this turn. The 2/3 current amount and every-card
behavior supersede the historical 5/7 first-card read at the older
`0x389b3c` body.

Pillar's props-4 Block is flat and unpowered: Dexterity, Frail, Unmovable,
card enchantments, and card-block history do not modify it. Positive Block
still reaches `AfterBlockGained`, so Juggernaut consumes one CombatTargets
draw and deals its ordinary props-4 hit. The generated callback reads its
live stacked Amount at callback time. Reapplying the Type-1/Intensity power
adds the new amount to the existing instance without moving its original
listener position.

Smokestack's ctor/canonical-vars/OnPlay/upgrade methods are **0xef26f**,
**0xef27c**, **0xef290** with nested `<OnPlay>d__5::MoveNext`
**0x3b9f64**, and **0xef2db**. It is a cost-1 Power; after a
presentation-only PowerUp animation it applies `SmokestackPower` 5/7. The
power's Type/StackType are both 1 at **0xab855/0xab858**. Its callback
outer/body are **0xab85c** and
`<AfterCardGeneratedForCombat>d__4::MoveNext` **0x343194**. It first
requires generated `CardModel.Type == 4`, which is **Status** in this build,
not Curse. It then applies the same null-or-owner Creator predicate as
Pillar, without a generated-card-owner predicate. After Flash, it freezes
the current power Amount and current ordered `HittableEnemies`, then awaits
one `CreatureCmd.Damage` command over that set. Props 4 makes each result
blockable and unpowered: neither Strength nor Vulnerable modifies it, while
ordinary block, damage caps, damage hooks, and death work remain live. One
callback uses one frozen amount across the whole AoE even if nested work could
change the power later.

Global `Hook.AfterCardGeneratedForCombat` outer/nested are
**0x106fbc/0x3ca380**; `Hook.IterateCombatHookListeners` outer/nested are
**0x106b3e/0x3d149c**. The iterator performs its combat-ending check when
enumeration begins. A hook begun after combat starts ending yields nothing.
If an earlier yielded listener ends combat, later snapshotted listeners are
still invoked, but Pillar's GainBlock and each Smokestack Damage command own
their terminal entry gates. The simulator preserves that distinction rather
than returning from the power loop merely because an earlier callback set
`over`.

Player creature powers precede relics, physical cards, and enemy creatures.
The simulator extends the existing `local_generated_power_order` with
`pillar_of_creation` and `smokestack` tokens alongside Arsenal and local
Soulbound. First application appends one token; reapplication stacks without
moving it. Soulbound recursion re-enters the same ordered power snapshot with
its per-instance latch set. After all player powers, Regalite runs; Rocket
Punch follows in frozen AllCards order; Aeonglass follows as the frozen enemy
listener. Generated-card owner remains relevant only to listeners such as
Rocket Punch, never to Pillar or Smokestack.

Every real generated writer retains its pre-history admission call.
CardGenerated history and pile insertion/entry hooks therefore finish before
the callback. `CardCmd.Transform` continues to record CardGenerated history
without dispatching `AfterCardGeneratedForCombat`. A generated-power command
can enter a blocking selection only through enemy death and Gremlin Horn
Draw. That Draw has two represented blocking branches: Hellraiser's Early
AutoPlay of a selecting Strike, or an empty Draw pile reshuffling a larger-
than-Amount Discard under live Stratagem. Batch 223 does not add a generic
power-listener or AoE continuation: before any generated history, UID, pile,
or RNG mutation, a narrow guard counts qualifying Pillar and
Status/Smokestack callbacks, includes owner-recipient Soulbound's bounded
nested Souls, and refuses when their props-4 damage can reach either branch.
It also counts cards a writer will add to Discard before the callback and the
direct or primary-to-secondary-cascade deaths that can drain existing Draw
cards. The ordinary Horn draw audit adds Cacophony, the sole modeled non-hand
AfterCardDrawn listener with immediate damage: if its live countdown can fire
within that Horn prefix, the guard includes every recipient its props-4 hit,
optionally followed by the remaining generated-power budget, can kill. This
also covers the callback's pre-reset reentrant Cacophony chain. Speedster is
hand-draw-only; Automation, Corrosive Wave, and represented physical draw
hooks cannot kill synchronously. Generated Hand/Draw additions are not
misclassified as reshuffle candidates. No Horn, no lethal budget, a Cacophony
countdown outside the prefix, insufficient combined damage, a Draw too deep
to empty, a prevented/full-hand Draw, and Stratagem's one-to-one auto-take
remain synchronous boundaries. Existing suspendable Regalite
callers keep their dedicated `GeneratedCardRelicFrame`; the guard also covers
the case where earlier generated-power damage makes Regalite's later
Juggernaut hit lethal.

At this historical Batch-223 boundary Trash to Treasure was still refused.
Its current callback outer/body are **0xada1c/0x347a0c** and the missing
CombatOrbGeneration/channel continuation was tracked by **#732**. Batch 227
below closes that dependency; the historical four-leaf Creative AI count is

## Batch 225 / #723 — fixed-target selected-card transforms

Current-build source is installed/archive-identical v0.110.1/db5d3552,
ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`5a8fb7eb62510a86fd03653b9210cd8f67b511b632331a1f174042de39c92bd9`.
All methods below were re-read from that assembly.

Charge's ctor/outer/nested bodies are **0xde6fe**, **0xde72c**, and
`<OnPlay>d__5::MoveNext` **0x38f43c**. It selects exactly two live Draw-pile
cards (`IL_002c-00c0`), materializes the selection with `ToList`, and awaits
one `TransformTo<MinionDiveBomb>` for each selected object in list order
(`IL_015d-01ca`). After each transform returns, upgraded Charge reads the
still-live source's `IsUpgraded`, checks the non-null replacement, and awaits
`CardCmd.Upgrade` (`IL_01d0-01ee`). Charge is cost 1 at both levels.

Guards' ctor/outer/nested bodies are **0xe5334**, **0xe535c**, and
`<OnPlay>d__5::MoveNext` **0x3a0314**. After its presentation-only animation,
it selects 0..999999999 live Hand cards (`IL_00a9-012e`) and materializes
their order with `ToList`. For each object, it creates a fresh L0
`MinionSacrifice` (`IL_0159-0165`), upgrades that replacement first iff the
live Guards source is upgraded (`IL_016c-0177`), then awaits singular
`Transform` (`IL_017c-01de`). Guards costs 2 and Exhausts at both levels.

Seance's ctor/outer/upgrade/nested bodies are **0xede5b**, **0xede8c**,
**0xeded7**, and `<OnPlay>d__7::MoveNext` **0x3b67f4**. It selects exactly one
live Draw-pile card (`IL_002c-00c0`), materializes the selection with `ToList`,
then serially awaits `TransformTo<Soul>` (`IL_015a-01c7`). It is Ethereal and
upgrades only its cost, 1 to 0.

The singular transform core is `CardCmd.Transform` outer overloads
**0x133260/0x1332ac/0x133364** and nested
`<Transform>d__13::MoveNext` **0x3de300**. Each command owns an independent
ending gate (`IL_002d-003e`), freezes the original pile/index, removes the
original from its pile, and inserts the fresh replacement at that same index.
It records `CombatHistory.CardGenerated` at `IL_03f6-0417`, awaits
`AfterCardEnteredCombat` at `IL_041c-0480`, awaits `AfterCardChangedPiles` at
`IL_0485-04fb`, calls `InvokeCardAddFinished` at `IL_0500-0506`, runs
`AfterTransformedFrom`/`AfterTransformedTo` at `IL_050b-051c`, and records the
result at `IL_0521-052d`. The successful combat-pile result path at
`IL_0963-0985` then reads the state/card/owner and calls
`Hook.AfterCardGeneratedForCombat` at **`IL_09a6`**, awaits it through
`IL_09fe`, and only then removes the detached original from `CombatState` at
`IL_0a03-0a22`. `CardCmd.Upgrade` **0x133034** has its own ending gate, which
is why Charge+'s post-transform upgrade remains a distinct command after the
whole Transform return path.

Batch 225 reifies the materialized ordered selection as one immutable
`FixedTransformFrame`. It validates every selected physical UID and complete
payload before the first mutation, then resolves each UID at its live combat
pile for that singular iteration. Each replacement gets a fresh UID, keeps
the original's current pile/index, and records one generated-history entry.
After the inert entry/pile-change/transformation callbacks, the frame freezes
the result UID in `after_generated` and dispatches the full generated-card
listener graph. Arsenal and Regalite see Charge's L0 Dive Bomb before its
separate Upgrade; Soulbound sees Seance's Soul; every listener sees each
already-upgraded Guards result. A Regalite death chain can park the existing
generated-relic/Draw/Hellraiser frames above the transform and returns through
the registered `fixed_transform` contract. Resumption removes the original
from state, then runs Charge's independently ending-gated Upgrade before the
next selected UID. Terminal commands advance without new writes.

Immutable review rejected candidate
`f2084a0ec35750bc639e6886cec626ed438439ea` / tree
`b3da09a1f7e34629727b389a4ebb4da4c6e4c1b1`: it stopped its read before the
late successful-result suffix, falsely documented Transform as hook-free, and
pinned that false negative in a listener test. The repair re-read the complete
`0x3de300` body through `IL_0a22`, reified the missing hook/resume/removal
suffix, and replaces the false negative with listener, suspension, terminal,
ordering, clone, and malformed-frame regressions.

Second immutable re-review rejected repaired candidate
`00712ec481254413d063597528b40d8893af03e1` / tree
`c99a5ae592fe7c981f16d4341bc3d5ff769e29bf`. Its private Dive Bomb admission
trusted only the caller's `return_to="fixed_transform"` string, its parked
transform frame validated only the sign of `result_uid`, and its Regalite
frame did not bind that UID to an underlying transform. A forged direct hook,
stale terminal result, or mismatched nested return could therefore cross the
private boundary. Also, the whole-selection preflight covered generated powers
and Regalite but not every later hook admission; an unsupported teammate
generated-card listener could refuse only after the first replacement write.
The second repair requires the exact live top `FixedTransformFrame`, its
`after_generated` stage, matching result UID, expected caller-specific card,
and located physical pile entry. A fixed-transform Regalite frame now carries
that UID and validates the immediately underlying transform before popping.
Whole-batch preflight now validates multiplayer listener absence, Soulbound/
power order, power/relic suspension, result types, and the complete physical
Rocket Punch suffix on a clone before any replacement UID, history, pile, or
log mutation.

Third immutable re-review rejected candidate
`04d652c0d521287659edd8f08a2011d0aa42f07c` / tree
`02944969e5005bb1ceda9c386578d4026428beee`. Although it located the parked
result, it did not structurally prove that its fresh UID differed from the
source and every selected original, nor prove that the current selected

## Batch 228 / R49 — exact Outbreak and Poison identity lifecycle (#2044)

Current authority is v0.111.0; installed macOS arm64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256 is
`9cb4f1ad8c9f284aa8fec3122ffd6d780bbf543d875c817abdd12ff63fbf12b4`.
Outbreak constructor/canonical/OnPlay/upgrade are
**0xe6df1/0xe6e20/0xe6e34/0xe6e7f** and the nested OnPlay body is
**0x3b07fc**. It captures the living roster, serially applies Poison 9 (12 at
L1), then captures a fresh roster and triggers each then-live Poison. Rust
executes both serial waves synchronously under one clone rehearsal; it does
not persist Python's solver-only Outbreak continuation frames.

Poison type/stack/TriggerCount/side-turn/Trigger/constructor are
**0xa5d53/0xa5d56/0xa5d60/0xa5e5c/0xa5ea8/0xa5eeb**; the side-turn and Trigger
bodies are **0x340c58/0x340d30**. Trigger freezes
`min(initial amount, 1 + living-opponent Accelerant)`, then repeats
unpowered-unblockable damage and a live-owner decrement. The application wave
has the player applier and therefore may run Sleight of Flesh exactly once per
successful application. Every Trigger decrement and ordinary side-turn
decrement has a null applier: the full recorded power-amount listener order is
authenticated, but Vicious, Shroud, and Sleight are not invoked. Sleight's
type/stack/canonical/AfterPowerAmountChanged/body/constructor are
**0xa7ba6/0xa7ba9/0xa7bac/0xa7bb4/0x344dc4/0xa7c18**.

Stable Poison is an identity-bearing power: each positive amount owns one
unique nonnegative UID below the checked cursor and exactly one Poison token
in Misery order; zero/absent Poison owns neither. Corpse-attached Poison,
duplicate/future UIDs, wrong wire types, malformed listener order, and
multiplayer Outbreak roots refuse at boundary/admission and again before any
public mutation. Waterfall's detached old trigger remains command-local while
the revived owner has no inherited Poison identity; Phrog and Axebot
replacement are captured only by the fresh second snapshot.

Outbreak supports direct play, replay, Havoc/Cascade and Mayhem AutoPlay, and
local-Sly discard AutoPlay beneath exact synchronous parent grammars. Pending
or forged parents and any child-created suspension refuse atomically. The
full audit is `solver/invariant-walks/2026-09-04-issue2044-outbreak-r49.md`.

Current-build source is installed/archive-identical v0.110.1/db5d3552,

`5a8fb7eb62510a86fd03653b9210cd8f67b511b632331a1f174042de39c92bd9`.

Consuming Shadow's constructor/canonical vars/OnPlay outer/body/upgrade are
**0xdf557**, **0xdf595**, **0xdf5b8/0x391d80**, and **0xdf603**. It is a
cost-2 Rare Self Power. The body initializes `i=0`, serially awaits one
`Channel<DarkOrb>` per iteration, increments `i`, and re-reads the live
Repeat dynamic var at **IL_0127-013d**; Repeat is 2/3. Only after that loop
does it await `Apply<ConsumingShadowPower>` with amount 1 at
**IL_0142-01ca**. The power getters **0xa40eb/0xa40ee** are both literal 1,
so applications add to the existing instance without moving its listener.

`ConsumingShadowPower.AfterSideTurnEnd` outer/body are
**0xa40f4/0x335150**. The callback first requires its owner in participants,
then reads the owner's orb queue and returns immediately when its initial
Count is zero (**IL_0027-0060**). Otherwise it initializes `i=0`, serially
awaits `OrbCmd.EvokeLast(owner.Player, true)` (**IL_0071-00d8**), awaits only
a cosmetic 0.25-second wait, increments `i`, and re-reads the live power
Amount at the back-edge (**IL_014c-0158**). The initial nonempty test is not
repeated: later iterations still call the empty-safe command after the queue
has drained.

`EvokeLast` outer/body **0x136a5c/0x3eb3d4** returns on an empty queue,
captures the exact current `Last`, and awaits `Evoke(player, captured,
dequeue=true)`. `Evoke` outer/body **0x136ab0/0x3eb19c** checks ending and
queue emptiness, removes that exact captured instance before its effect,
awaits the orb effect, then—while the owner remains in combat—awaits global
`AfterOrbEvoked` before final internal removal. Global `AfterOrbEvoked`
outer/body are **0x107d60/0x3cd54c**. Thunder's sole represented consumer,
outer/body **0xad7e4/0x347518**, accepts only Lightning, filters the effect's
already-selected targets to living creatures, then serially deals live
Amount as props-4 unpowered damage; it consumes no new target RNG.

The shared state-owned random-orb lifecycle is extended only with two
authenticated sources. The card source fixes the selected channel kind to
Dark and reuses the already-reviewed exact Channel stages (oldest auto-evoke,
orb effect, Thunder, enqueue/history, Metronome). The side-end source has a
distinct EvokeLast entry and post-hook stage: it removes the last orb before
the effect, parks beneath death/Gremlin-Horn/Draw continuations, completes
Thunder exactly once, and advances the live-Amount cursor without enqueue or
Metronome. A dedicated side-end return frame preserves the later player
relic/card/enemy suffix. The genuine turn-end dispatcher additionally issues
an independent, monotonic, state-owned side-end epoch before even the native
initial-empty gate. Its state is `issued`, then either `completed` at the
empty gate or `running` before the EvokeLast child is created. Only the child
loop can increment the epoch's state-owned completed-iteration receipt, and
its exact lifecycle-free terminal frame can publish `running -> completed`
only when receipt count, child cursor, and live Amount agree. The return
consumes only `completed`. Thus dropping a genuine child cannot
skip the power body, while terminal, Thunder, and nested Draw returns still
complete and consume exactly once. The return frame carries only that epoch's
identity; a matching return plus random-orb frame/auth payload cannot forge
dispatcher provenance. Every child resume also joins its cursor to the
state-owned completed-iteration receipt before any stage or orb mutation, so
a stale recreated cursor cannot repeat an evoke and fail only afterward.
Every frame field must equal its state-owned lifecycle
record; source, caller, cursor, orb kind/value, target identities, and
effect/hook completion cannot be asserted by frames alone.

Player powers in the ordinary side-end group are visited in first-application
order by `CombatState.IterateHookListeners` outer/body
**0x13ac75/0x3f6700**; global AfterSideTurnEnd is
**0x10866c/0x3cea9c**. The solver does not yet retain a general order for

precede the relic/potion/orb/card and enemy groups.

## Batch 230 / R46 — Whistle: exact Queen/Amalgam player Stun (#2033)

Current-build source is installed v0.111.0, ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`9cb4f1ad8c9f284aa8fec3122ffd6d780bbf543d875c817abdd12ff63fbf12b4`.

**Whistle** (ctor `0xf027f` = cost 2, AnyEnemy Attack; keyword Exhaust;
granted by the combat-inert Tanx's Whistle quest relic — census hooks `[]`)
has CanonicalVars Damage 33 (`0xf029d`) and OnUpgrade `UpgradeValueBy(11)`
(`0xf030f`) -> 44. OnPlay outer `0xf02bc` and nested
`<OnPlay>d__7::MoveNext` `0x3c72f4`: one
awaited FromCard `AttackCommand` on `cardPlay.Target`, then
`CreatureCmd.Stun(target, null)`. The template pipeline refuses the card on
that Stun call; R46 ports the exact post-attack step and authenticates the
generated L0/L1 rows at the public boundary and across all five piles.

**Player-stun semantics.** The current command chain is
`CreatureCmd.Stun` `0x132ae0` -> nested command body `0x3ed060` -> overload
`0x132b2c`; the null delegate `<>c::<Stun>b__26_0` `0x3e8f83` is the exact
`CompletedTask` no-op. The visual wrapper factory is `0x3e8fc8` and its
executable MoveNext is `0x461f58`; `Creature.StunInternal` is `0x11d7cc`.
Players cannot be stunned; dead/no-combat targets no-op. With a null/empty
`nextMoveId` the
follow-up is `MoveStateMachine.StateLog.Last().Id`. The log invariants are
authenticated at `ConditionalBranchState.get_ShouldAppearInLogs` `0x78d8f`,
`RandomBranchState.get_ShouldAppearInLogs` `0x79110`, and the base
`MonsterState` implementation `0x78f8e`, so the last logged state IS
the telegraphed move. The dynamic `STUNNED` `MoveState` carries the caller
intent, `FollowUpStateId`, and `MustPerformOnceBeforeTransitioning`; its
one setter caller is StunInternal itself, and `get_CanTransitionAway`
(`0x78ff3`) is false only for an unperformed such state, so
`SetMoveImmediate` (`0x825f0`, force=false) makes a second stun before the
first performs a silent no-op. No RNG stream is consumed. The simulator
models this as the registered forced one-shot `("none", ())` under
`(kind, "STUNNED")`, follow-up = the current telegraph; QUEEN and
TORCH_HEAD_AMALGAM are the verified target kinds, all others refuse (I5).
Queen's exact machine is `0xbc37c`, AfterDeath is `0xbc734`, and the
Amalgam machine is `0xc2c98`. Queen loops 3..5 are admitted only after the
Amalgam-death latch; the retained Burn route stays distinct from every other
parked row.

**Queen composition.** `Queen::AfterDeath` (`0xbc734`) retargets via
reference equality `NextMove == BurnBrightForMeState` before
`SetMoveImmediate(EnragedState, false)`. A stunned Queen's NextMove is the
dynamic STUNNED state: the predicate fails (and force=false would be
blocked anyway), `HasAmalgamDied` still latches, and the parked Burn Bright
later performs against an empty living-teammate snapshot
(`<BurnBrightForMeMove>d__43` `0x3672b0`): the strength foreach never runs
and the trailing unconditional `CreatureCmd.GainBlock(20)` still lands,
after which the `HasAmalgamDied` branch (`0xbc85e/0xbc869`) advances to Off
With Your Head. `Monster.queen_burn_bright_retained` latches exactly that
shape; the roster validator admits a dynamic move only as the verified
STUNNED one-shot whose follow-up equals the telegraph at `loop_pos`.

**AfterCardExhausted order** (same batch): the historical Dark Embrace +
Feel No Pain co-active refusal keyed on unrecorded player-power application
order. `State.after_card_exhausted_power_order` now records first
application (`PowerCmd` stacks an existing instance without moving it —
the restack retains position), and `Hook.AfterCardExhausted` (`0x415a14`)
dispatches the two powers in that order: FNP-first completes its awaited
GainBlock (with its block-gain listeners) before Dark Embrace's Draw
enters. Direct fixtures that set both Amounts without the recorded order
keep the refusal, as does an FNP-first walk suspended by Toasty Mittens.
The hook serially AWAITS each listener, and FNP's GainBlock nests the
only AfterBlockGained listener (Juggernaut d__4 `0x384218`), whose hit
can kill and suspend through death listeners (Gremlin Horn draw →
Hellraiser selection) — a resume the synchronous walk cannot await (PR
#954 immutable-review P1). The unsupported selecting capability requires live
Feel No Pain, a lethal Juggernaut hit, and Gremlin Horn reaching either a
Hellraiser autoplay selector or an empty-Draw reshuffle whose Stratagem pool
exceeds its Amount, independent of Dark Embrace; it refuses at the exhaust
producer boundary. Gremlin Horn without either blocking selector completes
through its registered Draw/death suffix and remains admitted. The preflight
reuses the generated-power damage capability walk (including lethal-recipient,
Horn-draw, Cacophony-cascade, and Stratagem-threshold accounting) and precedes
selection RNG, source-pile removal, history, Exhaust insertion, frames, and listener/relic
mutation; `_card_exhausted` repeats it for direct callers. With Juggernaut
absent the AfterBlockGained walk is a mutation-free no-op and the synchronous
serial order is exact.

Producer preflight is evaluated against an exact non-mutating projection of
the post-source-removal Hand, Draw, or Discard pile. This is observable: a

## Batch 231 / #952 — Creative AI recursive serial Power generation

Current-build source is installed/archive-identical v0.110.1/db5d3552,
ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`5a8fb7eb62510a86fd03653b9210cd8f67b511b632331a1f174042de39c92bd9`.

Creative AI's constructor is **0xdfbb7**: it is a Rare Self Power costing 3,
then 2 when upgraded, and applies one additive `CreativeAiPower`. The power's
`BeforeHandDraw` outer method is **0xa4598** and its nested
`<BeforeHandDraw>d__4::MoveNext` body is **0x335d2c**. After the owner gate,
the body initializes its loop cursor and, while the cursor is below the
freshly re-read live Amount, independently requests one random eligible
Defect Power, awaits one singular generated-card add to Hand, increments the
cursor, and repeats. Each random request full-shuffles the complete pool; the
shuffle is not shared across stacks.

The exact fully-unlocked solo-Defect current-build projection, in native pool
order, is 19 cards: Buffer, Bulk Up, Capacitor, Consuming Shadow, Coolant,
Creative AI, Defragment, Echo Form, Feral, Hailstorm, Iteration, Loop, Machine
Learning, Smokestack, Spinner, Storm, Subroutine, Thunder, and Trash to
Treasure. Ancient Biased Cognition and multiplayer-only One for All are not
eligible. The projection is re-derived from `card_pool_census.json`, requires
both L0 and L1 modeled, and is guarded by explicit Defect-owner,
fully-unlocked-pool, CombatCardGeneration, and CombatTargets provenance.

Creative AI extends the Batch 222 `BeforeHandDrawPowerFrame` with only one
new listener and one new singular-generation stage. The listener cursor is
published before its body, and the iteration cursor plus one independent
full-shuffle result are published before the generated-card await. The
existing generated-card lifecycle then records owner history, inserts the
canonical L0 card into Hand or overflow Discard, dispatches physical-entry and
generated-card listeners, and resumes through its authenticated caller. A
Regalite/Gremlin-Horn/Draw pause therefore cannot replay either the listener
or its 18 generation draws, while the loop condition still observes live
Amount after each awaited insertion.

Creative AI's recursive pool member is a fixed point rather than an extra
callback edge: the generated canonical Creative AI is inserted and its
listeners run, but it is not played. Consequently it cannot apply another
power or enter the already-frozen current `BeforeHandDraw` listener snapshot.
If the player explicitly plays that physical generated copy later, it stacks
Amount on the existing instance without moving its first-application slot and
can affect only later loop conditions/turn snapshots as native execution
allows.

Malformed listener/stage/cursor payloads, missing application order, pool
provenance drift, unsupported owner/unlock state, or missing stream counters
refuse before publication. Coverage advances cards **529/67 to 530/66** and
aggregate accepted/refused **986/76 to 987/75**. Full audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-08-05-02-batch231-creative-ai.md`.

Deck`. Compact enumerates Discard, so every Status there passes this predicate
even if Eternal; the Status type filter is the only remaining selector.
The solver therefore freezes exact physical Status objects in current
Discard order and never substitutes the older removable-card predicate.

hook; replacements keep native indexes, get fresh monotonic UIDs, and produce

## Batch 241 / #969 — Dense Vegetation event combat

The event-choice boundary is explicit and remains outside combat

TRUDGE_ON and REST. The complete nested TRUDGE_ON body

option. `DenseVegetation::Fight` **0xcbab3** passes an empty reward sequence

The solver models only a caller-supplied exact combat id/state. It does not
choose REST, replay the heal, invent a reward, or relax the existing
historical `.run` `entry_ambiguous` refusal.

GenerateMonsters` are **0xd6d0c/0xd6d0f/0xd6d3c/0xd6d3f/0xd6d4c**. The
roster is exactly four Wrigglers in `wriggler1..4` order, and every mutable

The complete WRIGGLE body **0xc8d30/0x373e28** adds exactly one Infection to

### #987 — Mysterious Knight event combat (The Lantern Key)

The publishing event is `TheLanternKey`. `get_CanonicalEncounter` **0xd37b0**
names `MysteriousKnightEventEncounter`; `GenerateInitialOptions` **0xd37c8**
offers RETURN_THE_KEY and KEEP_THE_KEY. The complete nested RETURN_THE_KEY
body **0xd3820/0x381470** grants the event's 100-gold `CanonicalVars`
(**0xd37ba**) value and finishes without combat. `KeepTheKey` **0xd3863**
publishes a FIGHT option whose body `Fight` **0xd389c** assembles one
`SpecialCardReward` (`CreateCard<LanternKey>`) and calls
`EnterCombatWithoutExitingEvent<MysteriousKnightEventEncounter>` at
**IL 0x0052**. The solver models only the caller-supplied exact combat
id/state: it does not choose an event option, grant the reward card, or
relax the historical `.run` `entry_ambiguous` refusal.

`MysteriousKnightEventEncounter::RoomType/AllPossibleMonsters/
GenerateMonsters` are **0xd798e/0xd7991/0xd799d**: exactly one
MysteriousKnight with a null slot name. `MysteriousKnight` (**ctor 0xbd5a3**)
subclasses FlailKnight and overrides only `AfterAddedToRoom`
(**0xbd560**, nested d__0 MoveNext **0x361bb8**): after the awaited base
hook it applies `StrengthPower` 6 then `PlatingPower` 6 to itself
(`ThrowingPlayerChoiceContext`, no player choice). Plating reuses the
audited monster-side `mplating` primitive (block at own side start when
RoundNumber > 1, ordinary decrement each own side start round 1 included).

The inherited `FlailKnight::GenerateMoveStateMachine` **0xb7d64** builds
WAR_CHANT (BuffIntent), FLAIL_MOVE (MultiAttackIntent FlailDamage x2),
RAM_MOVE (SingleAttackIntent RamDamage), and one RAND. The machine's
initial state is the concrete RAM_MOVE MoveState (no MonsterAi draw);
all three MoveStates follow up into RAND, whose AddBranch calls resolve to
cooldown 0 / CannotRepeat / weight 1.0 — WAR_CHANT through the
`(state, MoveRepeatType)` wrapper **0x7cb89** (via 0x7cb00/0x7cb2e), FLAIL
and RAM through the `(state, int)` wrapper **0x7cb7a** (via
0x7cb3c/0x7cac1), both terminating in the four-argument core **0x7ca04**.
That is the SludgeSpinner shape: from turn 2 exactly one MonsterAi
`NextFloat` per roll, uniform over the moves not just used
(`GetNextState` **0x7cb98**, `GetStateWeight` **0x7cc54**).

Values (`AscensionHelper::GetValueIfAscension`): HP fixed 108 at A8+
(Min **0xb7d32** = 108/101, Max **0xb7d3e** = Min, one Niche draw through
`SetUniqueMonsterHpValue`); FlailDamage **0xb7d49** = 10 at A9+ (else 9);
RamDamage **0xb7d56** = 17 at A9+ (else 15). Complete outer/nested move
bodies: WAR_CHANT **0xb7e58/0x359114** applies `StrengthPower` 3 to
itself; FLAIL_MOVE **0xb7e9c/0x358f04** is one AttackCommand `WithHitCount`
2; RAM_MOVE **0xb7ee0/0x359010** is one single attack. Composition in
`content/encounters/event.py` `_mysterious_knight`; engine registration in
the `RANDOM_AI`/`_UNIFORM_CR_ORDER`/`_RANDOM_MOVES` uniform-CannotRepeat
family. Coverage moves Mysterious Knight from untouched to modeled:
encounter status becomes **9 certified, 70 modeled, 9 refused,
2 untouched**; aggregate accepted moves **998 to 999**; refused remains
**70**; eligible remains **1071**. Unpinned (no live capture). Full audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-08-06-01-batch242-mysterious-knight.md`.

### #988 — Punch-Off event combat

The publishing event is `PunchOff`. `IsAllowed` **0xcf644** requires
TotalFloor >= 6; `get_CanonicalEncounter` **0xcf63a** names
`PunchOffEventEncounter`. `GenerateInitialOptions` **0xcf660** offers NAB
(complete nested body **0xcf758/0x37bfa0**: `AddCurseToDeck<Injury>` and
event end, no combat) and I_CAN_TAKE_THEM (`TakeThem` **0xcf79c**), which
cancels the ambient animation and publishes FIGHT. `Fight` **0xcf7f4**
assembles one RelicReward and one PotionReward and calls
`EnterCombatWithoutExitingEvent<PunchOffEventEncounter>` at **IL 0x0054**.
The ambient `PunchEachOther` loop (**0xcf6ec**, nested d__12 **0x37c1a8**)
is strictly cosmetic — `CreatureCmd::TriggerAnim`, `VfxCmd`,
`NHitSparkVfx`, `Cmd::Wait` only, no `DamageCmd` and no HP mutation — so
fight-start HP does not depend on how long the player idles on the event
page. `CalculateVars` **0xcf72f** rolls only the event gold var on the
EventModel stream (no combat effect). The solver models only the
caller-supplied exact combat id/state and preserves the historical `.run`
`entry_ambiguous` refusal.

Because `PunchOff::get_LayoutType` **0xcf637** is 1 (combat layout),
`EventCombatSynchronizer::InitializeForEvent` **0x7102c** makes the
canonical encounter mutable and runs `GenerateMonstersWithSlots`
**0x83070** at event-room enter; `EnterCombat` **0x71318** then reuses
that same combat state (`ShouldCreateCombat` false for layout 1), so the
scene roster IS the fight roster and the generation draws happen exactly
once.

`PunchOffEventEncounter::RoomType/AllPossibleMonsters/GenerateMonsters`
are **0xd7e86/0xd7e89/0xd7e98**: two PunchConstructs, creation = slot
order. The first gets `StartsWithFastPunch = true` and
`StartingHpReduction = EncounterModel.Rng.NextInt(2, 10)` (counter-0 draw,
range [2, 9]); the second only `StartingHpReduction` (counter-1 draw).
`EncounterModel::get_Rng` **0x82f45** is the `_rng` field seeded in
`GenerateMonstersWithSlots` from seed + TotalFloor + hash(entry) — the
per-fight Encounter stream already modeled by `Rng.for_encounter`
(`ctx.encounter_rng`), so the builder needs `total_floor` and refuses
without it. Each fixed-HP creature (60 A8+, Min **0xbf473** = Max
**0xbf47f**) spends one Niche draw through `SetUniqueMonsterHpValue`.
`PunchConstruct::AfterAddedToRoom` (**0xbf4d4**, nested d__24
**0x36451c**) applies innate `ArtifactPower` 1, then when
`StartingHpReduction` (get **0xbf4bc**) > 0 sets current HP to
`Math.Max(1, CurrentHp - StartingHpReduction)` at **IL 0x00fb..0x0123**
(max HP unchanged).

The monster machine is the already-modeled #148/#802 PunchConstruct
deterministic loop (READY GainBlock 10 -> FAST_PUNCH FastPunchDamage x2 +
Frail 1 -> STRONG_PUNCH -> READY; machine **0xbf518**), with the initial
state `StartsWithFastPunch ? FAST_PUNCH : READY` (**0xbf518** at IL
0x00c8). Composition in `content/encounters/event.py` `_punch_off`; no
engine change. Coverage moves Punch-Off from untouched to modeled:
encounter status becomes **9 certified, 71 modeled, 9 refused,
1 untouched**; aggregate accepted moves **999 to 1000**; refused remains
**70**; eligible remains **1071**. Unpinned (no live capture). Full audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-08-06-02-batch242-punch-off.md`.

### #989 — The Architect event encounter: structurally excluded (I5), combat unreachable

> Coverage-accounting correction (2026-08-16): this census-only scene roster
> is now `eligible=false` with its full `exclude_reason`. It cannot block the
> playable-encounter denominator; the reachability evidence below is unchanged.

`ENCOUNTER.THE_ARCHITECT_EVENT_ENCOUNTER` is registered as an explicit
structural exclusion in `content_refusals.json`, not modeled, because no
player combat can ever occur in it on the current build.

Complete reachability read. Event combat can start only through
`EventModel::EnterCombatWithoutExitingEvent`, which awaits
`EventCombatSynchronizer::ReadyToEnterCombat` **0x71180**; that is the sole
caller of `EventCombatSynchronizer::EnterCombat` **0x71318**. Every
combat-bearing event therefore carries a
`spec:EnterCombatWithoutExitingEvent<TEncounter>` instantiation (Fake
Merchant, Battleworn Dummy, Dense Vegetation, The Lantern Key, Punch-Off
all do). A full MethodSpec-table scan of the assembly shows the ONLY
generic instantiation naming `TheArchitectEventEncounter` is
`Encounter<TheArchitectEventEncounter>` — used by
`TheArchitect::get_CanonicalEncounter` **0xd286e** and
`ModelDb::get_EventEncounters` **0x84954**. No
`EnterCombatWithoutExitingEvent<TheArchitectEventEncounter>` exists, and
`TheArchitect` defines no Fight method.

What the encounter actually is: `TheArchitect::get_LayoutType` **0xd286b**
returns 1 (combat layout), so `EventCombatSynchronizer::InitializeForEvent`
**0x7102c** instantiates the canonical encounter as the event-room SCENE at
room enter (`GenerateMonstersWithSlots` **0x83070**). The roster
(`RoomType/AllPossibleMonsters/GenerateMonsters`
**0xd8b3e/0xd8b41/0xd8b4d**; `HasCustomBackground` **0xd8b3b**) is one
`Architect` stage prop: fixed HP 9999 (**0xb217d/0xb2184**) and a single
self-looping NOTHING MoveState with `HiddenIntent`
(`GenerateMoveStateMachine` **0xb218c**, body `<>c::b__4_0` **0x350632** =
`Task.CompletedTask`). The event itself is a scripted dialogue
(`OnRoomEnter` **0xd2974** binds the scene creature and computes Score via
`ScoreUtility::CalculateScore`; `DivideWildly` **0xd30fc**;
`AnimPlayerAttackIfNecessary` **0xd30b0** / `AnimArchitectAttackIfNecessary`
**0xd31f0** are animation-only; `WinRun` **0xd306c** ends the run) whose
options are dialogue lines — the player never takes a combat turn.

Excluding is exact, not a gap: a solver "model" of this row would synthesize
a fight the game cannot produce (I5/I8). The exclusion reason in
`content_refusals.json` carries the full cite chain. The original Batch 242
ledger recorded the row as refused; the 2026-08-16 accounting correction
removes census-only structural rows from the playable denominator while
preserving that evidence.
Full audit: `invariant-walks/2026-08-06-03-batch242-the-architect.md`.

## Batch 243 — turn-start Hand-choice powers (#376 / #418)

Current-build provenance: v0.110.1 / db5d3552; installed/archive
`release_info.json` SHA-256
`cd3abf5bea78ff74db5f09f592b0ea7524be7aeb602225989204a0f8a5a16e47`;
ARM64 `sts2.dll` SHA-256
`5a8fb7eb62510a86fd03653b9210cd8f67b511b632331a1f174042de39c92bd9`.

- **MACHINE_LEARNING** — the existing shared primitive is current-build
  exact: `MachineLearningPower::ModifyHandDraw` **0xa7f2d** owner-gates
  incoming draw + Amount; `<OnPlay>d__3::MoveNext` **0x3a7cd0** applies the
  Cards variable; upgrade only adds Innate (**0xe80df**). SetupPlayerTurn
  nested `MoveNext` **0x3f3cf0** invokes `ModifyHandDraw` before the sole
  turn-start `Draw(..., fromHandDraw=true)` and does so every owner turn.
- **TOOLS_OF_THE_TRADE** — OnPlay nested **0x3c17e4** applies amount 1;
  `ModifyHandDraw` **0xad84d** owner-gates +Amount. AfterPlayerTurnStart outer
  **0xad870**, nested **0x347730**, owner-gates exact-Amount
  `FromHandForDiscard`, materializes the selected list, and awaits one plural
  Discard. Plural `Discard` delegates to `DiscardAndDraw(cards, 0)`
  (**0x3dda08 / 0x3ddad0**), preserving selected order through serialized
  discard history/hooks and the later Sly AutoPlay tail. The upgrade is cost
  1 to 0 only (**0xf2957**).
- **TYRANNY** — OnPlay nested **0x3c29b0** applies amount 1;
  `ModifyHandDraw` **0xada8a** owner-gates +Amount. AfterPlayerTurnStart outer
  **0xadab0**, nested **0x347b74**, owner-gates exact-Amount `FromHand`, then
  serially awaits `CardCmd::Exhaust(card, false, false)` in selection order.
  Exhaust nested **0x3ddf24** moves each then-live CardModel to Exhaust before
  its complete AfterCardExhausted walk; later selected references therefore
  observe earlier Dark Embrace, Feel No Pain, Joss Paper, Midnight, and other
  exact listener effects. Upgrade adds Innate only (**0xf2f93**).

`CardSelectCmd::<FromHand>d__28::MoveNext` **0x3e4de4** returns empty after
the command's ending gate, auto-returns the whole current Hand when candidate
count is at most Amount, and otherwise opens an exact Amount modal. The two
powers keep a keyed first-application-order tuple; stacking preserves the
existing token. Each hook entry freezes that tuple before the first awaited
choice, so a power applied by a Tools Sly tail cannot join the already-captured
listener walk until the next turn. Both modals enumerate every exact selected
identity order because plural Discard and serial Exhaust consume result order.
Compositions with legacy same-AfterPlayerTurnStart powers are
I5-refused at entry and dynamic application boundaries because the shared
native hook enumerates player powers in application order
(`IterateCombatHookListeners` **0x3d149c**; combat listener construction
**0x3f6700**) and that cross-family order is not represented.

Coverage moves `CARD.TOOLS_OF_THE_TRADE` and `CARD.TYRANNY` from refused to
modeled: cards **536 modeled / 60 refused -> 538 / 58**; aggregate accepted
**1000 -> 1002**, refused **71 -> 69**. No test, capture, or fight-state pin
was weakened. Full invariant audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-08-07-01-batch243-turn-start-hand-choice.md`.

`release_info.json` SHA-256

- **TAG_TEAM** — ctor/MultiplayerOnly getter/vars/upgrade are
  **0xf19ba/0xf19c7/0xf19cf/0xf1a2f**. OnPlay outer **0xf19e0**, exact nested
  MoveNext **0x3bf474**, awaits one selected-target powered Attack for 11/15,
  then applies one amount-1 TagTeamPower to that retained enemy with the
  local card owner's Creature as applier. Ordinary ending/dead/replacement,
  Lamp, and Artifact boundaries remain on the later Apply.
- **DISTINCT POWER STATE** — type/stack/instance/display getters
  **0xac869/0xac86c/0xac86f/0xac872** establish visible Type-2 Intensity,
  distinct InstanceType 1, and displayed Amount. `Monster.tag_team` therefore
  stores insertion-ordered `(amount, applier_player_key)` rows rather than a
  scalar. Rend counts every row; Misery clones each repeated acquisition token
  with Amount and applier intact; all ordinary/Illusion death cleanup removes
  rows and ordering state.
- **PLAY-COUNT HOOK** — Modify **0xac878** admits only Attacks owned by the
  power applier. AnyEnemy also requires exact target-owner equality; only
  AnyEnemy/AllEnemies target enums can change count. Every matching instance
  adds its full Amount. Hook Modify **0x108914** freezes changed listeners;
  GeneratePlayCount outer/nested **0x81898/0x318eb8** awaits the complete
  fold and changed-list callback before returning; Hook After outer/nested
  **0x10791c/0x3cc368** serially dispatches those callbacks. Tag Team After
  outer/nested **0xac8dc/0x345770** removes the whole distinct instance before
  CardPlayStarted and before any replay body. Each serial removal publishes
  its negative Type-2 AfterPowerAmountChanged event after collection mutation;
  local Sleight of Flesh therefore fires before CardPlayStarted.

Manual and direct AutoPlay entry require more than one live represented
Player, while an already-started body does not recheck teammate liveness.
Locally applied rows trigger local attacks; explicitly projected
teammate-applied rows preserve exact provenance, use teammate hook identity
when Misery clones them, and do not match a local card owner. Removal suffixes
that would suspend or become terminal under Sleight/death/Draw are
clone-preflighted and refused atomically before the play boundary mutates;
this includes Stock replacing a dead Axebot at the same slot with a fresh
Creature identity. A teammate-applied Misery clone also bypasses the local
owner-only Unsettling Lamp latch while preserving an already-latched card's
multiplicative tail.
Malformed instances, unknown appliers, and ambiguous Misery order fail closed
before relevant mutation. Coverage moves cards
**543 modeled / 53 refused -> 544 / 52**; aggregate accepted

The local-owner path reuses the existing exact physical-UID single-pile
selection continuation. Zero or one candidates auto-resolve; multiple local
candidates expose one exact selection action per physical card. The remote
projection cannot expose teammate input or infer teammate policy, so every
living remote target is admitted only with zero or one live Draw candidate.
A multi-candidate teammate Draw pile refuses the whole Tutor action context
before manual action enumeration, resource spend, AutoPlay target RNG,
activation, logs, or pile mutation. Dead teammates are not legal targets and
do not widen this choice boundary.

Manual actions enumerate self plus every living teammate Player. A living pet
retains the existing I5 refusal because its native legal AnyAlly identity is
not expressible by the player-key action vocabulary. AutoPlay validates every
possible remote target's choice-free Draw quotient before consuming its one
ordinary CombatTargets draw, then fetches from the selected living non-owner
Player. Replay re-reads the target's then-live Draw pile; a first replay that
moves a singleton leaves the next replay an empty no-op.

The raw/checked translator refusal `call Creature::get_Player` remains pinned
as historical provenance; only Tutor's exact ID/levels and private body are
admitted. Coverage moves cards **594 modeled / 2 refused -> 595 / 1** and
aggregate **9 certified / 1049 modeled / 13 refused -> 9 / 1050 / 12**. Full
invariant audit:
`invariant-walks/2026-08-13-08-batch292-tutor.md`.
